title: Lane Johnson's retirement could create a cap mess for the Eagles in 2027
summary: Eagles right tackle Lane Johnson said in August that 2026 will probably be his last year.
full_text: Eagles right tackle Lane Johnson said in August that 2026 will probably be his last year. After three games, he decided to retire now. He has an absolute right to do it. No player should continue to play pro football if he no longer wants to do it — whatever the reason(s). The move nevertheless has financial consequences, for the Eagles and for Johnson. If he had retired after the season, and if the Eagles had waited until after June 1 to process it, the cap charges would have applied in 2027 and 2028. Now, all of the dead money will hit in 2027. The Eagles also will have the prerogative to seek reimbursement of previously-received payments by Johnson. It gets complicated; they can recover unallocated signing bonus money and a portion of his 2026 option bonus of $21.7 million (only half of it has been paid). And recovery of the amounts they're entitled to pursue would be credited against the dead-money charges. First, the Eagles have to decide whether they want to try to take money back from a first-ballot Hall of Famer who has meant so much to the team. While the Lions did it with both Hall of Fame running back Barry Sanders and Hall of Fame receiver Calvin Johnson, the Eagles may choose not to alienate such an important player by asking him to give money back. Second, there's a way to finesse the situation to delay the bulk of the cap charge until 2028, in theory. If, for example, they put him on the non-football injury/illness list for the rest of the season and he officially retires after June 1, 2027, the Eagles will avoid taking the full cap charge in 2027. The fact that the Eagles have yet to make a roster move with Johnson suggests that they're coming up with a good strategy. The best could be to delay his retirement, agree not to seek repayment of money he has earned (while possibly not paying the $10.85 million due on December 1), and finessing the cap consequences to avoid a potential mess in 2027.
author: Mike Florio

title: Through four weeks of the season, zero kickoff return touchdowns
summary: The NFL may like to call kickoffs "Dynamic," but the most dynamic thing that can happen on a kickoff hasn't happened at all this season.
full_text: The NFL may like to call kickoffs "Dynamic," but the most dynamic thing that can happen on a kickoff hasn't happened at all this season. There has still not been a single kickoff return touchdown, four weeks into the 2026 NFL season. The longest kickoff return of the season was a 79-yarder by Miami's Jaylen Wright, who was knocked out of bounds at the 18-yard line at Las Vegas in Week 1. That continues a downward trend in kickoff return touchdowns that began before the 2024 adoption of the "dynamic kickoff" and hasn't changed under the new rules, which have encouraged more returns but haven't resulted in more big plays. There were only six kickoff return touchdowns all of last season, and seven in 2024. In 2023, the last season of the old kickoff rules, there were only four touchdown returns. Kickoff return touchdowns were once commonplace. From 2000 to 2010 there were at least a dozen kickoff return touchdowns league-wide every year. In 2007 there were 25 kickoff return touchdowns, the high-water mark for the 21st Century. Then, in 2011, the kickoff was moved up from the 30-yard line to the 35, and kickoff return touchdowns went into a decline as more kickoffs went for touchbacks. That decline hasn't reversed with the dynamic kickoff. For all the talk that the dynamic kickoff would make the play more exciting, it really hasn't happened. Kickoff return touchdowns are among the most exciting plays in football, but we hardly ever see them anymore.
author: Michael David Smith

title: 49ers DE Mykel Williams: "Losing my mind" with excitement for return to lineup
summary: 49ers defensive end Mykel Williams's long path back to the field after last season's torn ACL is close to the finish line.
full_text: 49ers defensive end Mykel Williams's long path back to the field after last season's torn ACL is close to the finish line. Williams is expected to be activated for this Sunday's game against the Seahawks and that would mark his first time in the team's lineup since Week 9 of last season. The 2025 first-round pick said it's been "killing me" to watch the 49ers struggle to produce a consistent pass rush with Nick Bosa out of action early this season and that he's itching to finally cut loose. “I’m going crazy. I’m losing my mind ,” Williams said, via Josh Dubow of the Associated Press. “I’m ready to go. I’m excited to play ball. I miss playing ball. It’s been like damn near a year since I played, so I just want to get back on the field.” Williams had 20 tackles, a sack and a forced fumble before the injury ended his rookie season. In addition to rehab work, he's spent his time away from the field becoming leaner and honing in on other ways to increase his burst. Williams said "we’re going to see Sunday" if that had the desired effect and the 49ers' chances of moving to 5-0 will look a lot better if Williams hits the ground running.
author: Josh Alper

title: Sean Payton: Offensive focus needs to be on details, not who calls plays
summary: When the Broncos changed offensive playcallers this offseason, it guaranteed a lot of attention would be paid to how the unit fared with offensive coordinator Davis Webb calling the shots instead of head coach Sean Payton.
full_text: When the Broncos changed offensive playcallers this offseason, it guaranteed a lot of attention would be paid to how the unit fared with offensive coordinator Davis Webb calling the shots instead of head coach Sean Payton. The early returns have not been great. The Broncos are 27th in points and yards after a 2-2 start that has featured plenty of questions about whether Payton will be taking the job back. On Wednesday, Payton was asked at his press conference whether four games are a long enough time to evaluate Webb's performance and his answer pivoted to other matters having greater importance than who sends in a play. "I think our focus needs to be more on the specific and the detail of each play regardless," Payton said. "I think Davis is very fast and quick and understands what we're doing. I appreciate the question, but I think that the most important job I have is really evaluating the whys. I think collectively, we all, after a game, and after a four-game sample size, certainly this isn't championship football, what we see. How quickly can we correct those things?" Payton returned to the importance of details several times when discussing the team's offensive performance and said at one point that the team has to "become experts in the detail" in order to perform at the "championship football" level they want to reach this season. That does not preclude a change on the operations side, but it doesn't sound like one is imminent in Denver.
author: Josh Alper

title: Cowboys will "move pieces around" in field goal protection after blocks two weeks in a row
summary: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer says changes are being made after the Cowboys have had field goals blocked in their last two games.
full_text: In Week 3 against the Ravens, the Cowboys had a field goal blocked. In Week 4 against the Texans, the Cowboys had another field goal blocked — and Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said his team exploited the same flaw in the Cowboys’ protection the Ravens did. Obviously, the Cowboys have to change something. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer says they will. Schottenheimer said that with offensive lineman Drew Shelton injured and ruled out for tonight's game against the Buccaneers, the Cowboys have to make some changes because Shelton has been part of the field goal protection unit. But Schottenheimer acknowledged that changes had to come regardless of injuries after two straight games with blocked field goals. "Moving some pieces around, we were going to move some pieces around anyway because it hasn't been very good," Schottenheimer said. "We've got a good rotation going but at the end of the day we've just got to clean some things up from a technical standpoint." The Cowboys are the only team in the NFL this season that has had multiple field goals blocked. That's something Schottenheimer and his staff need to get fixed, and something the Buccaneers will be well aware of heading into tonight's game.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Mike Macdonald on Joe Mixon: "Didn't work out"
summary: The Seahawks, who are thin at running back, brought Joe Mixon to town for a workout on Monday.
full_text: The Seahawks, who are thin at running back, brought Joe Mixon to town for a workout on Monday. It seemed to be working out, until it wasn't. The team ultimately didn't proceed with signing him to the practice squad, based ostensibly on his physical. Coach Mike Macdonald was asked about the decision not to sign Mixon during Macdonald's Wednesday press conference. “Didn’t work out," Macdonald said. "Probably the most we should say about it with respect to the process. Those things happen and it’s a part of the process.” Mixon's health continues to be shrouded in mystery. He was on the Texans' non-football injury list for all of the 2025 season. There was never a clear answer as to what the problem was. And so Mixon continues to be a free agent, available to sign with any team. And there are teams (like the Eagles) that need help at the position.
author: Mike Florio

title: Odell Beckham Jr.'s arrival could be a message to Jauan Jennings
summary: The Vikings didn't sign receiver Odell Beckham Jr. for P.R. purposes.
full_text: The Vikings didn't sign receiver Odell Beckham Jr. for P.R. purposes. They signed him to help the team win games. And they may have signed him to send a clear message to receiver Jauan Jennings. Jennings, who signed a one-year, $8 million deal in the offseason, has yet to provide the Vikings with much of a return on their investment. In three games, he has been targeted four times, making two catches for nine yards. On Sunday, with Justin Jefferson out, Jennings participated in 95 percent of the offensive snaps. He was targeted once. Beckham eventually could become the No. 3 receiver, behind Jefferson and Jordan Addison. With both of them stressing defenses (and with tight end T.J. Hockenson developing into a reliable weapon for quarterback Kyler Murray), Beckham could find favorable matchups and plenty of opportunities to make plays. If nothing else, Beckham's presence will provide a wakeup call for Jennings. Or for second-year receiver Tai Felton, who has only one catch for 14 yards on three targets in four 2026 games. Regardless, Beckham is there for a reason. And the reason seems to be that, beyond Jefferson and Addison, the receiving corps hasn't been good enough.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jesse Minter on Lamar Jackson: A lot of time between now and Sunday
summary: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson didn't practice on Wednesday because of the ankle injury that has left doubt about whether he'll play against the Falcons this Sunday, but head coach Jesse Minter isn't ruling him out at this point.
full_text: ' Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson didn't practice on Wednesday because of the ankle injury that has left doubt about whether he'll play against the Falcons this Sunday, but head coach Jesse Minter isn't ruling him out at this point. Minter said he wasn't worried about Jackson being prepared to play because of missed practice time and that the team isn't going to rush making any decision until they see how he responds to treatment in the coming days. "It’s Wednesday. There’s a lot of time between now and Sunday," Minter said. "To Lamar’s credit, he’s getting a lot of treatment and doing things. There’ll be a point later in the week where we’ll kinda figure out where it’s at. . . . When he’s ready to play, he’ll be ready to play.” Tyler Huntley will get the start for Baltimore if Jackson does not play. He was 8-of-9 for 63 yards in the second half of last Sunday's win over the Titans.
author: Josh Alper

title: Sean Payton: I "don't think" Patrick Surtain II, Pat Bryant will land on IR
summary: Broncos cornerback Patrick Surtain II and cornerback Pat Bryant suffered ankle injuries during Sunday's loss to the 49ers.
full_text: Broncos cornerback Patrick Surtain II and cornerback Pat Bryant suffered ankle injuries during Sunday's loss to the 49ers. There has been some speculation that either or both could land on injured reserve. Coach Sean Payton was asked about it on Wednesday. “That’s jumping way ahead," Payton told reporters. "I don’t think so, and if they were I wouldn’t say so, but I don’t think so.” The key words were this: "If they were I wouldn't say so." So he's not saying so. And they can delay the move until Saturday in order to start the four-game clock for their return with the Week 5 game against the Chargers. For now, it's unlikely either will play on Sunday. (Neither practiced on Wednesday.) It's even less likely that the Broncos will disclose anything more than what the injury report requires.
author: Mike Florio

author: Charean Williams

title: Drake Maye is skeptical of the moon landing
summary: Sunday's win at Buffalo was one small step for Maye, one giant leap for the Patriots.
full_text: Sunday's win at Buffalo was one small step for Maye, one giant leap for the Patriots. It's fitting, then, that New England quarterback Drake Maye spent some time the next day expressing skepticism about the moon landing. “ I don’t know about the moon , you know. I think I can see back in the day why we would put on the mask if we went there, but I’m not really sure 200 percent if we went there or not,” Maye said in an appearance on WEEI, via Boston 25. “I wouldn’t say I’m leaning one way or the other. I just know I’m a little bit skeptical.” Maye added that he took a class at North Carolina about conspiracy theories. “They studied Hitler being alive and ‘are birds real?,’ some of the classic ones that you hear about,” Maye said. The "are birds real?" conspiracy theory was a spoof on conspiracy theories generally. (Hopefully, they covered that in the class Maye took. Along with whether Tar Heels actually have tar on their heels.) As to Maye's skepticism that we put a man on the moon, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman chimed in on Twitter, saying " I quite literally have the receipts ." Maye's comments are a reflection of post-truth America. Facts no longer matter. The only thing that's relevant is what a given person believes.
author: Mike Florio

title: John Harbaugh: Giants are "just not good enough" at generating explosive runs
summary: The longest run from a Giants running back this season was a 13-yarder by Cam Skattebo.
full_text: The longest run from a Giants running back this season was a 13-yarder by Cam Skattebo. Giants coach John Harbaugh says that's not good enough. Harbaugh said today that the Giants' running game needs to generate some explosive runs and make some big gains, and so far it isn't doing that. "We're just not good enough yet," Harbaugh said. "Defenses are playing us pretty well. As we get better, we'll probably have more longer runs, also if we make them pay more with play action, I think that'll loosen them up a little probably. We've just got to keep getting better. The guys are working hard at it. We're playing very hard. We're trying to play very physically. All the elements are there, we just have to get better." Skattebo is more of a bruising power runner than a big-play explosive runner, and his 3.5 yards per carry are down this year from the 4.1 he averaged as a rookie last year. Harbaugh would like to see Skattebo do more, and the offense do more to give Skattebo the opportunity.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Odell Beckham Jr.: Kevin O'Connell wanted me to be here
summary: Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell and new Vikings receiver Odell Beckham Jr. spent time together with the Rams, and they both have a Super Bowl ring from it.
full_text: Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell and new Vikings receiver Odell Beckham Jr. spent time together with the Rams, and they both have a Super Bowl ring from it. It was O'Connell's influence that brought Beckham to Minnesota. Meeting with reporters on Wednesday, Beckham said he had other options after being released by the Giants. He chose the Vikings. " It seemed as if he wanted me to be here ," Beckham said as to O'Connell. "And that was expressed to me. And that feels good. . . . It always feels better when you're doing it for somebody who, you know, you feel like their heart is there for it as well." With the Giants, his return always felt more like a feel-good story at best, and a publicity stunt at worst. Once the games started, it wasn't sustainable. Minnesota doesn't have any marketing or P.R. reason to add Beckham. It's all about making the team better. And O'Connell, who has had opportunities to sign Beckham in the past but didn't, apparently believes that, in this specific moment, Beckham can make a difference. The first opportunity could come as soon as Sunday, in a game in his home state of Louisiana against the Saints.
author: Mike Florio

title: Falcons LT Jake Matthews, DE Za'Darius Smith did not practice Wednesday
summary: Falcons left tackle Jake Matthews made his 199th consecutive start on Monday night, the longest active streak in the NFL.
full_text: Falcons left tackle Jake Matthews made his 199th consecutive start on Monday night, the longest active streak in the NFL. The next one is in question. Matthews did not practice Wednesday, two days after leaving Monday night's win over the Saints in the first quarter. He did not return with a groin injury. His backup, Michael Jerrell, is also on the injury report as a limited participant with an ankle injury. Josh Kendall of TheAthletic.com reports that Jerrell said he's anticipating backup snaps at practice this week, potentially a good sign for Matthews' availability. Defensive end Za'Darius Smith (concussion/neck) and linebacker Yasir Abdullah (hamstring) did not practice. Defensive end Cam Thomas (shoulder) was limited.
author: Charean Williams

title: Justin Jefferson returns to practice, Jordan Addison sits out
summary: The Vikings got Justin Jefferson back at practice on Wednesday, but another wideout was missing from the workout.
full_text: The Vikings got Justin Jefferson back at practice on Wednesday, but another wideout was missing from the workout. Jordan Addison missed practice with a hamstring injury. He had four catches for 52 yards in last Sunday's win over the Dolphins. Jefferson missed that game with an ankle injury and he was limited in his first day back on the field. He addressed his outlook on playing in Sunday's road game against the Saints later in the day. "Hopefully so. That's definitely the plan ," Jefferson said, via Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com. "Being back at home, being in Louisiana, is definitely something that I want to do. So the plan is for me to play, but who knows? We going to take it day by day." Left tackle Christian Darrisaw (concussion) and cornerback Chuck Demmings (hamstring) did not take part in practice. Running back Aaron Jones (rest) and right tackle Brian O'Neill (knee) were both limited while center Michael Jurgens (elbow), tight end Ben Yurosek (ankle), and punter Brett Thorson (hamstring) fully participated on Wednesday.
author: Josh Alper

title: Sam LaPorta: Don't know if extension is off the table, but there's a stalemate
summary: A contract extension for Lions tight end Sam LaPorta may not be off the table, but it doesn't sound like the two sides are close to an agreement.
full_text: ' A contract extension for Lions tight end Sam LaPorta may not be off the table, but it doesn't sound like the two sides are close to an agreement. LaPorta is in the final year of his rookie deal and a report last weekend indicated that talks about a new deal have broken off . On Wednesday, LaPorta took some issue with that assessment while sharing his understanding of where things stand at this point. “I don’t know if it’s truly off the table , but I think there’s certainly a stalemate right now," LaPorta said, via Tim Twentyman of the team's website. "I’m really giving the reins to my agent, Jack Bechta. He’s been handling it with the front office. All the advice he’s given me so far is that we just haven’t come to terms yet." Head coach Dan Campbell called LaPorta's contract talks "the last thing on my mind right now" during his Wednesday press conference and LaPorta's play hasn't appeared to be negatively impacted by the negotiations. He has 22 catches for 228 yards and two touchdowns through four weeks, which puts him on pace for his most productive season since joining the team.
author: Josh Alper

title: Ravens expect Cam Jurgens to be ready to play in Week 6
summary: The Ravens traded for center Cam Jurgens on Wednesday, but it doesn't look like his debut for the team will come for another week.
full_text: '' The Ravens traded for center Cam Jurgens on Wednesday, but it doesn't look like his debut for the team will come for another week. Jurgens is in the concussion protocol and head coach Jesse Minter said that the team expects that he'll be cleared to return to action before they face the Browns in Week 6. "I anticipate him really being ready next week , probably," Minter said, via the team's website. "So, again, we will see who is available, what that looks like and what the best five are for this particular game." While Jurgens is progressing through the protocol, he'll also be familiarizing with a new offense. Minter said he thinks Jurgens's experience with different offensive coordinators in Philadelphia should make that easier. "I think he has just been really well-developed and well-trained. He is a good athlete. Mentally, he is at a really high level, I would say," Minter said. "We will have to catch him up. Obviously, the terminology will be different for him. But with a guy like that — with the experience of having gone through a few different offenses — that will probably end up benefiting him now, rather than a guy coming from maybe one system." Vega Ioane started at center for Baltimore in Week 4 and he's the likeliest choice to be there against the Falcons on Sunday night. Once Jurgens is ready to step into the lineup, Ioane will likely move back to his original spot at right guard.
author: Josh Alper

title: Tyler Shough limited in practice with left hand injury

title: Seahawks DT Jarran Reed: Players hit penalty issues "head on" in meeting this week
summary: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald called the team's seven personal fouls in last Sunday's win over the Chargers "unacceptable at any level" and his players didn't wait to go to work on cleaning things up this week.
full_text: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald called the team's seven personal fouls in last Sunday's win over the Chargers " unacceptable at any level " and his players didn't wait to go to work on cleaning things up this week. Defensive tackle Jarran Reed told reporters at a Wednesday press conference that some of the defensive leaders organized a meeting in order to address the issue early this week. Reed said "it wasn’t like a panic moment, but it was a moment of realization" that the team can't afford to hurt itself with penalties that extend drives for opponents if they hope to keep winning games. "We basically got together as a defense on Monday, just players only, we just had a real meeting, a real honest meeting with each other about what we expect, what we want to go through," Reed said. "We hit it head on because that was way too many penalties for us as a team." The Seahawks had 14 overall accepted penalties last Sunday and Reed said there will always be some fouls in the normal course of doing business. The Seahawks want to cut down on the more avoidable ones as they move toward this week's meeting with the 49ers.
author: Josh Alper

title: Aaron Rodgers won't comment on whether play calls are coming in fast enough
summary: After Thursday night's loss in Cleveland, Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers wasn't asked about his viral moment with coach Mike McCarthy, sparked by Rodgers's obvious frustration with the time it was taking to communicate the play call to the huddle.
full_text: ' After Thursday night's loss in Cleveland, Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers wasn't asked about his viral moment with coach Mike McCarthy, sparked by Rodgers’s obvious frustration with the time it was taking to communicate the play call to the huddle. On Wednesday, Rodgers was asked several questions about the topic. Here’s the video , as posted by DK Pittsburgh Sports . As to whether the plays are coming in "a little later than you would like," Rodgers said, "I'm not gonna touch that one." Regarding the interaction with McCarthy, Rodgers said, "Yeah, Mike and I have talked." It is ironed out? "It's always ironed out," Rodgers said. Is this the normal way they communicate? "Sometimes, yeah," Rodgers said. Has Rodgers found it to be effective? "Yeah, yeah. We've had a lot of success together," Rodgers replied. It's an issue that goes beyond the relationship between Rodgers and McCarthy. If Rodgers is behaving in a way that creates the impression that he believes McCarthy is incompetent when it comes to the simple act of quickly and efficiently telling the quarterback the next play, other players will see it. And they may view McCarthy differently. Indeed, the fact that Rodgers wouldn't comment on whether the plays are coming in fast enough means that, in his view, they're not. That's why McCarthy, quite frankly, shouldn't have wanted another year with Rodgers. Most of the rest of the locker room will be back next year. Rodgers won't. The impressions of McCarthy that are influenced by the words and actions of Rodgers will linger for as long as McCarthy is the head coach.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jalen Ramsey, Jamel Dean did not practice on Wednesday
summary: The Steelers did not have a couple of defensive backs for Wednesday’s practice as they begin to get ready to face the Colts.
full_text: The Steelers did not have a couple of defensive backs for Wednesday’s practice as they begin to get ready to face the Colts. Cornerback Jalen Ramsey (wrist) and cornerback Jamel Dean (ankle) both did not participate. While defensive tackle Cameron Heyward also didn’t practice, he was given a veteran rest day. Additionally, running back Rico Dowdle (toe) and receiver Michael Pittman (foot) were both limited. Dowdle has missed the last two games with his injury.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Patriots WR Mack Hollins hopes to practice later this week
summary: Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins did not practice on Wednesday, but he hopes to be back on the practice field later this week.
full_text: Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins did not practice on Wednesday, but he hopes to be back on the practice field later this week. He left Sunday's 29-26 win over the Bills with a calf injury. Hollins played 31 of 76 snaps and made three catches for 53 yards. “I hope so. That’s the goal ,” Hollins said of returning this week, via Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald . “That’s a decision between me, and the trainers as well. That’s why we have them because I think as players we’d go out there no matter what. So yeah, if they say it’s cleared, then for sure.” The Patriots won't have wide receiver A.J. Brown until at least next week. He's on injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain and isn't eligible to return until next week. Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams are the options if Hollins also can't play.
author: Charean Williams

title: Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins among six Bengals out of practice
summary: The Bengals had six players miss Wednesday's practice.
full_text: ' The Bengals had six players miss Wednesday's practice. Their top two wide receivers were among them. Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (groin/neck) were injured in Sunday's loss to the Jaguars. Chase played 15 of 76 snaps and Higgins 60. Their departures from the game left the Bengals to finish with three healthy wide receivers on the game-day roster. Defensive tackle Jonathan Allen (rest/knee), linebacker Swayze Bozeman (groin), safety Bryan Cook (ankle) and safety Kyle Dugger (quad) also were out. Safety Jordan Battle (hamstring), linebacker Barrett Carter (ankle), defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II (wrist), offensive guard Dalton Risner (knee) and wide receiver Colbie Young (knee) were limited. Defensive tackle B.J. Hill (Achilles) was a full participant.
author: Charean Williams

title: In joint statement, NFL and NFLPA say drinking celebrations will be permitted
summary: For "gray area" celebrations, NFL will communicate with player before fining him.
full_text: '' NFL players of the world, drink up! Celebrations may include the miming of the consumption of a beverage without fear that the league will impose discipline for the player pretending to drink the official beer of the NFL. In a joint statement issued by the league and the NFL Players Association, it was explained that celebrations including "imitating drinking a beverage" will not be considered a violation. Here's the full text of the statement: "Football is the greatest game in the world. NFL players are admired by millions of fans, including young people competing at every level of the sport. "The passion emotion, and personality players bring to the field are a big part of what makes the game special and connects them with fans worldwide. Good sportsmanship is equally important: "To clarify the line between player expression and conduct that may result in discipline, players were reminded this week that the following are prohibited and may result in a 15-yard unsportsmanlike conduct penalty, a fine, or both: "Gestures that depict violence, including the use of guns or other weapons, or gang-related signs. "Gestures that depict smoking or drug use. "Gestures that are sexual in nature. "Conversely, recent celebrations imitating drinking a beverage will not be considered violations or result in discipline. The league-wide guidance provides players with greater clarity on how they can celebrate while remaining within the rules. "When conduct falls into a gray area, the league will contact the player and provide direction before imposing discipline. The player will be advised that continued use of the identified celebration may result in future fines. "Individual and team celebrations are part of the game and help players connect with fans. Providing clear, consistent guidance allows players to express themselves while upholding the principles of sportsmanship that have long been a hallmark of NFL football." Beyond eliminating the Church Lady-style sensitivity to a drinking-based celebration, the league has adopted a new approach to celebrations that don't clearly violate the rules. In lieu of a fine, the league will communicate with the player. If the NFL decides that the celebration will not be allowed, the player will be fined only if he thereafter continues to do it. It's the right result, even if it makes the sudden rash of celebration fines after Week 2 seem even more abrupt, unexpected, and flat-out bizarre.
author: Mike Florio

title: Giants list Malik Nabers as out of practice
summary: The first Giants practice of the week was missing a key member of the offense.
full_text: ' The first Giants practice of the week was missing a key member of the offense. Wide receiver Malik Nabers told reporters on Wednesday, via SNY, that he's a " little sore " while declining to share what part of his body was affected by the soreness. He said he did "as much as I could" at practice, but the team's injury report revealed that he did not participate. It also revealed that his knee was the reason why he was off the field. Nabers didn't seem overly concerned about how he was feeling, but others may feel differently if he remains out of practice heading into Sunday's game against the Commanders. Defensive lineman Chauncey Golson (neck), running back Najee Harris (personal), defensive back Jason Pinnock (concussion), and left tackle Andrew Thomas (groin) were also out of practice. Tight end Isaiah Likely (knee, groin), tight end Chris Manhertz (shoulder), and running back Cam Skattebo (shoulder) were listed as limited participants while cornerback Dontae Banks (calf) and offensive lineman Bryan Hudson (ankle) were full participants.
author: Josh Alper

title: Super Bowl stock report for NFL Week 5: Jaguars enter peak form, Eagles trend toward rebuild
summary: We assess the NFL title race after Week 4 and identify three upcoming games that could reshape the Super Bowl picture
full_text:
The NFL International Series rolls on in Week 5 with the second of three games in London, and it marks the first of two consecutive contests in England for the Jacksonville Jaguars . Liam Coen's team returns to its "home away from home" across the Atlantic Ocean for a matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles : A contest between two teams trending in opposite directions.
If the Eagles are to save their season and return to Super Bowl contention after back-to-back losses, this is an ideal spot to prove they can beat one of the best teams in the league. If the Jaguars handle their business as favorites, they will extend their winning streak to three games and improve to above .500 all-time in games held in London.
That is not the only impactful showdown on the road to the Super Bowl this week. In fact, even more seismic collisions occur on the West Coast with an NFC West battle between the San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks and a meeting between the two Super Bowl favorites in the Los Angeles Rams and Buffalo Bills .
Here is a look inside the Super Bowl race entering Week 5.
Odds via DraftKings , +2000 or better
The next time the Jaguars play on American soil will be in November. Each of their next two games come in London as they become the first NFL team to play consecutive home regular-season games in an international market. For most teams, the departure from the friendly confines of their domestic home stadium to spend two weeks abroad could be seen as a hindrance. For the Jaguars, games in England are nothing new. They should have a logistical advantage over the Eagles and Texans , and they are simply the better team in both matchups, too.
Trevor Lawrence last week finally got a Joe Burrow-sized monkey off his back, as the Jaguars defeated the Bengals 22-17 for Lawrence's first head-to-head win over Burrow in four tries. Jacksonville now has two consecutive victories under its belt in response to its Week 2 loss and might be in the early stages of another extended winning streak. It will be favored in each of its next three games.
Lawrence is easily a top-10 quarterback , but most impressive during the 3-1 start has been the defense. The Jaguars rank second in scoring defense at just 13.3 points allowed per game. The unit stands fifth in EPA per pass despite having to match up against Burrow's high-octane aerial assault and the reigning MVP runner-up, Drake Maye , in consecutive weeks. This squad is more well-rounded than ever and looks poised to avenge last year's 35-7 loss in London with a pair of overseas wins.
The odds of Nick Sirianni bringing a second Super Bowl to the City of Brotherly Love in three years are nearly twice as long now as they were heading into Week 4. That is the product of a miserable offensive showing in which the Eagles set a franchise record with 12 third downs without a conversion en route to a 24-20 loss to the Rams. They squandered a 10-point lead in the final four minutes and have now lost two in a row after opening at 2-0. And those two wins to begin the season were hairy, one-score outcomes against bad teams.
This season is heading in the wrong direction for Sirianni. Not all of that is his fault, but he now has work to do in order to save his job , because the pressure is officially on in Philadelphia.
The Eagles closed Week 4 without 10 key players. Injuries to Saquon Barkley , DeVonta Smith , Zack Baun and numerous other starters ravaged their roster. Further depleting the squad, Lane Johnson announced his retirement from the NFL, and Philadelphia traded Cam Jurgens in an overhaul of what used to be a stout offensive line. That trade might signal that the Eagles are already prepared to pack things up and move on to next year.
With the 12-longest odds to win the Super Bowl, the market might not have caught up to the Falcons quite yet. This is no championship frontrunner, but it is a completely different team with Michael Penix Jr . running the offense, and it is one that at least deserves the respect of a division favorite .
When Cooper Rush was under center, the Falcons lost their first two games, scored a combined 16 points and coughed up seven turnovers. In the two games with Penix at quarterback, the offense racked up 80 points, managed nearly twice as many yards and turned the ball over just once. Atlanta went from 0-2 to 2-2 at the flip of a switch. Now that there is a signal-caller in the lineup capable of feeding the ball to Drake London , Bijan Robinson and Kyle Pitts , a unit that stands among the NFL's most talented collection of skill players can excel.
It is not just the offense that is getting the job done now, too. The Falcons also rank third in the league with a 43.6% pressure rate and boast the NFL's stingiest run defense by a hefty margin, having allowed just 48.3 yards per game. All of that is without Jalon Walker and James Pearce Jr . on a defensive front that was supposed to sputter in their absences.
Monday, 8:15 p.m., ABC, stream on Fubo
With respect to the Australia game between the Rams and 49ers, Week 5 presents the biggest showdown of the year thus far. Los Angeles hosts the Bills in what may be a Super Bowl preview. These two teams hold the best odds to hoist the Vince Lombardi Trophy. Both star-studded squads need a momentum-building win in this spot because the Rams did not appear nearly as strong as expected in their 2-2 start and the Bills seek to avoid a two-game losing streak on the heels of their first loss of the year.
Sunday, 4:25 p.m., Fox, stream on Fubo
The 49ers are already the top team in the NFC West with a 4-0 record and two wins in divisional play, but they can take complete command of football's best division with a win in Week 5. They already topped the Rams in their season-opening blowout, so to defeat the reigning Super Bowl champion Seahawks on the road would be the second statement win over a divisional foe in the first quarter of the season. Seattle's defense let off the gas over the last two weeks and needs to get right in this big spot, because the next four games are a gauntlet.
Sunday, 9:30 a.m., NFL Network, stream on Fubo
A loss in England would not end the Eagles' season, but it might create the kind of downward spiral that derails the rest of the campaign. A three-game losing streak amid the onslaught of injuries and coaching scrutiny Philadelphia faces at this juncture would be awful for momentum. On the flip side, this is where the Jaguars need to pounce. Squaring off against a downtrodden team, they have a chance to build early separation in a top-heavy AFC South and cement themselves as a top-tier conference championship contender.
author: Carter Bahns

title: NFL Week 5 upset alert: Why these five favorites could easily lose, including the Patriots
summary: After accurately identifying three major upsets last week, we examine five more for Week 5
full_text:
No favorite appears to be safe these days in the NFL , as underdogs have come on strong over the first month of the regular season.
In the past two weeks, a total of 23 games have been decided by one score, which is tied for the most in a two-week span in NFL history. Naturally, those coin-flip games have produced quite a bit of upsets, and we've largely been on the scent with them. In last week's upset alert, we accurately identified the Texans , Lions , and Saints as favorites ripe to fall short, with the Cowboys , Panthers , and Falcons each pulling off upsets.
Now, we turn our focus to Week 5, where there are several home underdogs, which always put our antenna up. Three of which you can find below, as they could stun the road favorites this weekend, along with two AFC East favorites possibly on shaky ground at home.
All NFL odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook.
New England is coming off its biggest win of the season after going up to Buffalo and upsetting the Bills to get to 2-2 on the year. After it felt like the sky was falling in Foxborough, that win -- at least for the moment -- stabilized things. That said, this does feel like a possible letdown spot for the Patriots after such a monumental victory. They host a Raiders team that saw its undefeated 3-0 start get snapped by the Kansas City Chiefs last week, but Las Vegas largely hung in there. The defeat didn't expose them as fool's gold. Rather, I expect them to go into Gillette Stadium and make the Patriots sweat.
Vegas ranks sixth in the NFL in pressure rate (42.5%) and fifth in sack rate (8.7%). Drake Maye was much improved against Buffalo's pressure last week, but he's still struggled overall when under duress and has had a propensity to turn the ball over. If that rears its head here, Kirk Cousins -- who is tied for the league lead in passing touchdowns (11) -- should be able to take advantage.
I don't think it's hyperbole to call this a make-or-break game for Green Bay. A loss at home to Chicago would drop them to 2-3 on the season and, more importantly for tiebreaker situations, 0-2 in the NFC North. That's the makings of a hole that'll soon be too big to claw out of, no matter if Micah Parsons and/or Josh Jacobs return. So, with that in mind, I think the Packers -- who are admittedly flawed -- could throw the kitchen sink at a Bears team that is still dinged up.
On top of Caleb Williams (hamstring) still being out and Tyson Bagent set to start at quarterback, Kyle Monangi (thumb) and D'Andre Swift (knee, hip) did not practice on Wednesday. They both could play in Week 5, but if they are limited in any way, that takes away/deminishes the identity of what this offense has been. Coming into Week 5, the Bears lead the NFL with 196.3 rushing yards per game.
It's also worth noting that the Ben Johnson-led Bears have struggled against the NFC North. Against the division, Chicago is 2-5, while they are 12-2 against everyone else.
What if the Browns are just good? Cleveland is coming off a marquee win over the Steelers in Week 4, and will have the rest advantage over the Jets after playing last Thursday. After a season opener where it looked like the Browns were going to sink to the bottom of the league, they've ripped off three straight, and Deshaun Watson has looked solid. In fact, he's been clutch. Over this winning streak, he's orchestrated three game-winning drives and has completed 15-of-20 passes, averaged 6.9 yards per attempt, and has two passing touchdowns with no interceptions in those drives.
Watson and the Browns now face a Jets team that has gone in the opposite direction from them. After winning its first game of the year, New York has lost three straight. As it relates to this matchup, it's the Jets defense that should be of central focus and possibly the reason for an upset. Sure, they got an interception last week, but the unit has struggled in the two games prior to Week 5. The Jets' defense ranks last in the NFL in yards per game allowed at 436.5. Watson also won't have to deal with a ton of pressure as New York ranks 28th in the NFL in pressure rate this season.
New York is 0-12 in its last 12 games against above-.500 teams.
The Saints were embarrassed on Monday night in a 45-24 loss to their division rival, the Atlanta Falcons, at home in primetime. Typically, a team playing on a short week might be at a disadvantage, but I'd guess New Orleans is foaming at the mouth to get back out there to get rid of the sour taste of that defeat.
Minnesota is 4-0 on the year, but that undefeated record has come despite some questionable play on offense. They've registered the third-fewest yards per game (262.8) during a 4-0 start to a season by any team since 1940. Meanwhile, Kyler Murray hasn't looked like the second coming of Sam Darnold by any stretch of the imagination to this point. Of the 28 quarterbacks who've thrown at least 70 pass attempts this year, Murray is 24th in passer rating, 25th in yards per attempt, and 27th in EPA per dropback.
Really, it's been the play of the Vikings defense that has spearheaded this undefeated start. Brian Flores' unit has allowed the fewest points per game (12.8) in the NFL this season and has by far the highest blitz rate (71%) in the league. Against the blitz this season, Saints quarterback Tyler Shough has a 105.8 passer rating (11th among QBs) and five passing touchdowns (tied for third-most in the NFL), so he has been solid in the face of added pressure.
If he can find some success against this Vikings blitz, that could be enough to pull out the win, especially if the Murray-led offense continues to struggle to get off the ground.
The Detroit Lions simply cannot be trusted as a road favorite with their current defense. They just let Bryce Young and the Carolina Panthers torch them for 32 points and 329 passing yards, despite it largely just being a two-man show between Young and wideout Tetairoa McMillan (14 catches, 192 yards, and two touchdowns). Detroit's secondary is giving up a league-worst 423.8 total yards per game, and their 31.8 points per game allowed is the second-worst in the NFL.
While the Cardinals won't be mistaken for a Super Bowl contender, they have enough playmakers on offense to take advantage of the Lions' poor defense. Jacoby Brissett is coming off his worst statistical game of the season, tossing three interceptions against the Giants , but he is capable of bouncing back and throwing it around the yard, especially with the likes of Trey McBride and Michael Wilson at his disposal.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Cowboys vs. Buccaneers preview: Can Tampa Bay slow down CeeDee Lamb and high-powered Dallas offense?
summary: Dallas brings a historically efficient scoring attack into Thursday night against an 0-4 Tampa Bay squad turning to rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels
full_text:
In the Week 5 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Dallas Cowboys play host to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Dallas rebounded last week from its heartbreaking loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Rio de Janeiro the week before, storming back from a double-digit deficit to defeat the Houston Texans with a furious fourth-quarter rally. The Cowboys have arguably the NFL's best offense through the first four weeks of the season, and it could get a lift here with the potential return of guard Tyler Smith . But the Cowboys also have arguably the league's worst defense, and that unit is still dealing with various injuries even after trading for Joey Porter Jr .
Tampa is coming off a dispiriting loss to the Green Bay Packers in the first game of the Jalon Daniels era. The Buccaneers have turned to Daniels in the wake of Baker Mayfield's thumb injury, and the offense sputtered in his first game under center, totaling just 275 yards while Daniels was intercepted twice. The Bucs are now 0-4 after that loss and already in danger of falling out of the playoff picture entirely just a month into the NFL season.
Will Dallas get over .500 for the first time, or will Tampa capture its first win of the season? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
The Bucs went fairly run-heavy against the Packers in Daniels' first start, with the undrafted rookie throwing 27 passes while the team totaled 31 rush attempts despite trailing for most of the afternoon. Daniels went 19 of 27 for just 148 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, while also rushing eight times for 55 yards. Six of those runs were scrambles, and he totaled 46 yards on those plays.
The Cowboys have faced mobile quarterbacks three times this year and given up a ton of rushing yards to them. Jaxson Dart ran 11 times for 54 yards, Jayden Daniels ran for 69 yards on seven carries in just one half and Lamar Jackson ran six times for 50 yards.
Dallas does not have a strong pass rush to begin with (the Cowboys are 21st in pressure rate and 29th in sack rate), and the Cowboys have also allowed the highest scramble rate in the NFL while yielding 9.1 yards per scramble, according to Tru Media. Daniels, if he can maintain his composure when he does see pressure (and he was pressured on 42.9% of his dropbacks last week), should have opportunities to take off.
Tampa's offensive line has surprisingly not played all that well this year. The Buccaneers check in 22nd in ESPN's pass-block win rate and 23rd in run-block win rate. The team's running backs (mostly Bucky Irving ) have averaged just 1.07 yards before contact per attempt, indicating that the line isn't getting much push up front. And that's despite the fact that they've run into eight-man boxes at the second-lowest rate in football.
The Cowboys, of course, have gotten clocked on the ground, yielding 4.8 yards per carry to enemy backs. They check in 24th in yards before contact per attempt with 25th in yards after contact, per Tru Media. Irving should have room to run here if the Bucs can get their line in order.
The questions for Tampa's attack center on the passing game, where it's unclear whether Daniels can lead a competent attack. The Cowboys have gotten lit up through the air so far this season. Porter should help on that front, and he can probably follow Emeka Egbuka around the formation here and force Daniels to work the passing game through his other targets, but the Dallas secondary outside of him is eminently burnable right now.
Daniels didn't look like a player who could push the ball downfield with any degree of consistency against a subpar Green Bay defense, though, and there are still questions about whether he'll be able to do it even against this decrepit Cowboys unit.
So far this season, the Cowboys have an offense that is not just one of the best in the league but one of the best in recent memory. Consider this: Dallas has run the fewest drives of any team in the NFL (36), yet still ranks tied for second in points (122), just five behind the league leader (the Buffalo Bills at 127).
That's because the Cowboys have been historically efficient, averaging 3.39 points per drive. According to Tru Media, that makes them the sixth-most efficient offense through four weeks since the 2000 season. (The full-season record for points per drive during that span was just 3.19 by the 2007 Patriots .) When Dak Prescott called this unit the Greatest Offense There Is during the preseason, it's possible that he was not lying.
It's been Prescott himself doing the lion's share of the work, too, because the running game has yet to really get untracked. Javonte Williams has five rushing touchdowns, but he's averaged only 3.7 yards per carry and gained five-plus yards on his runs at the fifth-lowest rate among the 26 backs with at least 50 carries so far this season, per Tru Media. Rather than Williams getting consistent gains, it's just been Prescott methodically working the ball downfield with short and intermediate passes and then occasionally hitting defenses over the top with a shot to CeeDee Lamb or, more occasionally, George Pickens .
Tampa's defense has done an excellent job of stopping the run (opponents have averaged 3.2 yards per carry, the second-worst mark in the NFL), largely because that's what Todd Bowles tends to focus on. Those efforts have been successful, but the Bucs have been somewhat less successful against the pass, and they'll be shorthanded here thanks to the absence of Antoine Winfield Jr . They'll get Rueben Bain Jr . back to help the pass rush here; he hasn't been particularly effective so far, but Terence Steele has been friendly to opposing linemen who rush off the left side of the defensive line, so it's possible he could get going on Thursday night.
The Bucs probably don't have anybody who can deal with Lamb, mostly because it seems like nobody can actually guard Lamb when he's healthy. It's easy to forget what he did the last time he was full strength and had Prescott for a full season: he was a First Team All-Pro and totaled 135 catches for 1,749 yards and 12 touchdowns. He leads the league in both receptions (37) and yards (498) so far this year.
Pickens, by comparison, has yet to really make an impact, but that is probably coming soon enough given that defenses will presumably begin paying even more attention to Lamb. Pickens could have a significant size advantage against Tampa's corners on Thursday, and this could be the game where he gets loose.
Dallas' offense is too much for Tampa — or anyone else — to handle. Perhaps if the Buccaneers still had Mayfield under center, they could win a shootout, but even the version of Mayfield that was out there to start this season would have made that pretty unlikely. I suppose it's possible the Bucs could muscle and run their way to a win, but given how the offensive line has started the season, I don't see it happening in this one. Pick: Cowboys 34, Buccaneers 17
author: Jared Dubin

title: NFL Week 5 injury report: Lamar Jackson, Ja'Marr Chase among several stars uncertain for Sunday
summary: Commanders' Jayden Daniels logged a full practice on Wednesday and could return
full_text:
The early NFL season has been dominated by high-profile injuries, and if anything, that unfortunate trend only picked up in Week 4. Lamar Jackson , Ja'Marr Chase , Saquon Barkley , Tee Higgins and Rashee Rice were just a few of the big names to leave their respective contests early, and that's only on the offensive side of the ball.
Quarterback has been especially hard-hit this season, with Jaxson Dart done for the season and Jackson, Jayden Daniels , Caleb Williams , Baker Mayfield , Sam Darnold , Kyler Murray have all missed time with injuries suffered this season. Health can be one of the biggest factors, especially as injuries pile up throughout the rugged 17-game, 18-week schedule.
Two teams -- the Chiefs and the Panthers -- get their bye and a chance to heal up in Week 5, and the Rams face the Bills on "Monday Night Football," so they're not practicing Wednesday. As such, we're taking a look at the initial injury reports for the 28 teams playing on Thursday and Sunday.
Odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook
Not only are the Buccaneers down their starting quarterback -- they'll turn to Jalon Daniels for the second straight week -- but they're down two key members of their secondary, too, against one of the league's best passing attacks. Morrison got hurt early in Week 3 and hasn't played since, and Winfield fractured a rib in Week 4. In better news, Rueben Bain Jr . (groin, shoulder) carries no injury designation into the game after missing Week 4.
The Cowboys are dealing with plenty of defensive injuries as well, but the most noteworthy development is the potential season debut of Tyler Smith, the team's top offensive lineman. He's officially questionable.
Several notable Eagles , including RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring), LB Jihaad Campbell (knee) and OLB Jonathan Greenard (ankle), did not participate Wednesday. WR Marquise Browns (ankle), S Marcus Epps (groin) and C/G Drew Kendall also didn't practice. LB Zack Baun (concussion), TE Dallas Goedert (knee), T Fred Johnson (knee) and CB Quinyon Mitchell (knee) were limited.
S Eric Murray (concussion) was the only Jaguars player not practicing. CB Montaric Brown (hamstring), DT DaVon Hamilton (foot), T Anton Harrison (elbow), DE Josh Hines-Allen (groin), CB Jarrian Jones (foot), CB Jourdan Lewis (hamstring) and G Cole Van Lanen (knee) were all limited.
The Bears were again without QB Caleb Williams (hamstring), who hasn't played since Week 2. Their top two running backs Kyle Monangai (thumb, toe) and RB D'Andre Swift also didn't practice Wednesday, and neither did OL Jonah Jackson (ankle), DL Grady Jarrett (NRI/rest), OL Joe Thuney (pec) and OL Darnell Wright (ankle). LB Keyshaun Elliott (quad), LB Noah Sewell (Achilles) and DL Shemar Turner (knee) were limited.
For Green Bay, G Aaron Banks (knee, toe), RB Chris Brooks (ankle), G Jager Burton (back) and G Jacob Monk (quad) did not practice. T Anthony Belton (knee), DT Anthony Campbell (ankle), LB Lukas Van Ness (shoulder), WR Savion Williams (ankle) and DT Devonte Wyatt (ankle) were limited.
DE Will Anderson Jr . (ankle), T Trent Brown (NIR/rest) and LB Jamal Hill (knee) did not practice Wednesday for the Texans . LB Azeez Al-Shaair (groin), DE Jadeveon Clowney (knee), WR Nico Collins (NIR/rest), WR Tank Dell (knee), DE Logan Hall (knee), DT Kayden McDonald (ankle) and T Braden Smith (foot) were all limited. Dell, McDonald and Smith all had their practice windows opened.
For the Titans , DT Jeffery Simmons (back), DL John Franklin-Myers (back), RB Tony Pollard (foot), S Amani Hooker (concussion) and CB Marcus Harris (knee, ankle) did not practice. S Kevin Winston Jr . (shoulder) was limited.
Neither of the Bengals ' top wide receivers -- Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) nor Tee Higgins (groin, neck) -- practiced Wednesday. Also not practicing were DT Jonathan Allen (NIR/rest, knee), LB Swayze Bozeman (groin), S Bryan Cook (ankle), S Kyle Dugger (quad). DT Dexter Lawrence (wrist), S Jordan Battle (hamstring), LB Barrett Carter (ankle), G Dalton Risner (knee) and WR Colbie Young (knee) were all limited.
Four Dolphins did not practice Wednesday: DE Rob Beal Jr. (hamstring), WR Caleb Douglas (ankle), DB Reese Taylor (quad) and LB Jackson Woodard (ankle). The limited participants were LS Tucker Addington (shoulder), WR Chris Bell (knee), CB Julius Brents (heel), DT Kenneth Grant (toe), T Austin Jackson (knee) and S Dante Trader Jr . (shin).
The Raiders were without WR Jalen Nailor (concussion) at Wednesday's practice. TE Brock Bowers (knee), G Spencer Burford (knee), DT Folorunso Fatukasi (shoulder), G Jackson Powers-Johnson (groin), WR Cody White (ankle) and G Trey Zuhn III (knee) were all limited. RB Ashton Jeanty (ankle) was a full participant.
CB Carlton Davis (neck), CB Christian Gonzalez (shoulder), WR Mack Hollins (calf) and CB Karon Prunty (hamstring) did not practice for the Patriots on Wednesday. RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee), DT Christian Barmore (shoulder), LB Dre'Mont Jones (shoulder), T Morgan Moses (foot), CB Channing Canada (hamstring), LB Christian Elliss (chest), FB Reggie Gilliam (ankle, knee), CB Charles Woods (shoulder) and S Craig Woodson (shoulder) were all limited participants.
