title: NFL overreactions or reality? Sorting fact from fiction after the first quarter of the 2026 season
summary: We sort through what's real and what's an overreaction, from the Chiefs' resurgence to Bryce Young's breakout
full_text:
There is no longer an official one-quarter mark of the NFL season now that the league operates with a 17-game schedule, but with four games in the books, the campaign is about 25% complete. That is a large enough sample size to begin to draw conclusions about teams, players and coaches, even if some of those takeaways will age poorly over the remaining three-fourths of the year.
In some cases, it is not too early to write the book on a team's season. For instance, the five winless teams can effectively wave goodbye to their postseason hopes because it will be nearly impossible to climb out of the deep trenches they dug themselves into over the season's first month. Even the Houston Texans , who entered the year as Super Bowl hopefuls, look like an afterthought in the race to the playoffs.
The rest of the campaign will prove that some four-game starts are nothing more than hot streaks and cold stretches. But for now, all we can run with is what we have seen in a month's worth of action.
Let's separate overreactions from reality as the NFL's regular season reaches its quarter-way mark.
The Kenneth Walker III signing might have been the most impactful free agency move of the offseason. The Kansas City Chiefs are a completely different beast in 2026 than they were a year ago, and it all stems from the reintroduction of a prolific rushing attack. The $14.35 million the Chiefs are paying the reigning Super Bowl MVP suddenly looks like a steal, because Walker leads the NFL in rushing through four games with his 537 yards. That is 116 more than the second-most-prolific ballcarrier and last year's rushing title winner, James Cook.
Because the Chiefs boast the No. 3 rushing attack in the league, Patrick Mahomes does not have to shoulder an immense load with his arm as he did in years past. This not only helps him ease back into action following his ACL tear, but it should also aid in his career longevity. The passing offense is so much more impactful than it was one year ago, it was the only thing that worked. Just look at Travis Kelce's resurgence this season as a top-tier receiving tight end.
Kansas City needs help at wide receiver, but even with the depth concerns there, it is one of three undefeated teams and has the look of the same unstoppable force that won three Super Bowls in five years and went to two others since 2019.
There was no more disappointing individual player in the first three weeks of the season than Drake Maye . Last year's MVP runner-up was the second-worst quarterback in the NFL by passer rating through three games. That is an unfathomable fall from grace. Even after a bounce-back performance on Sunday against the Buffalo Bills , Maye leads the league in interceptions with seven and fumbles with five. His mistakes cost the New England Patriots mightily in their two early-season losses.
Week 4 was a reminder not to fall victim to the moment, though, and to recognize that this is the same player who orchestrated a 10-win turnaround and a trip to the Super Bowl a season ago. Maye showed tremendous growth in the Patriots' 29-26 upset of the Bills, especially under duress. According to ESPN Insights , Maye completed 50% of his passes for 76 yards and a touchdown across a career-high 21 pressures against Buffalo. That is in contrast to the 42% completion rate, zero touchdowns and three interceptions under pressure in Weeks 1-3.
Drake Maye's huge day led the Patriots to a win in Buffalo 🙌 @FedEx pic.twitter.com/BZe1LtAkVP
A lot of Maye's struggles to open the year may have come from between the ears. His disastrous Super Bowl performance seemed to linger as he walked into the same kinds of trouble in the first three games of 2026. Losing his top target, A.J. Brown , to a high ankle sprain did not help. Sunday's win was the kind of confidence-building moment that could pull Maye out of his slump for good, and Brown should be back before long. A return to MVP-caliber play in the weeks to come is not out of the question.
The Chicago Bears are 3-1, and each of their victories came with a different starting quarterback. Caleb Williams won the season opener, Case Keenum delivered a surprising win over the Eagles after Williams went down with a hamstring strain in Week 2 and Tyson Bagent stepped in on Sunday to deliver a triumph over the New York Jets . This says something about the strength of the Bears' quarterback room, but it says even more about coach Ben Johnson and his offensive prowess.
Johnson was already renowned as a rising offensive mastermind heading into the year. His work as the Detroit Lions ' offensive coordinator was evidence enough, and a prolific debut season with the Bears backed it up. This is his most dazzling effort yet, though. The ability to put second- and third-string quarterbacks in positions to not just win games but also excel in the process says everything about Johnson's stardom.
Before the season, Johnson said that he wanted to field the highest-scoring offense in NFL history. That looked like a legitimate possibility after Week 1. It will not happen now, but when Williams returns to the lineup, there is a real chance Chicago will dominate the league as the most unstoppable unit in football.
Trading for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie , signing Jaylen Watson and pulling Aaron Donald out of retirement made the Los Angeles Rams the winners of the offseason. No team generated more positive buzz this spring and summer, and for good reason. The additions to the defense included two future Hall of Famers and two impact cornerbacks, and that pairs with an offense that features the reigning MVP in Matthew Stafford , a superstar wide receiver in Puka Nacua , another potential Hall of Famer in Davante Adams and other high-impact standouts.
But then the season arrived, and the Rams laid an egg in Australia with a 27-7 divisional loss to the San Francisco 49ers . They blew a 16-0 lead to the Denver Broncos two weeks later, dropping to 1-2. And it took a miraculous late-fourth-quarter comeback to get past the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 4. Those are not the kinds of results expected of a super team.
It is still too early for major concern, though. Garrett has not played since Week 1 and was not at full strength in his lone outing. Donald is nursing a back issue. The offense has not had time to gel because of Nacua's early absence. Once these superstars get onto the field together at the same time, the Rams should hit their stride. Los Angeles' schedule is incredibly manageable outside of NFC West play, so the wins should pile up even if it takes longer than anticipated for the full system to fire on all cylinders.
It is extremely difficult to go an entire season without winning a single game, especially now that the campaign is 17 games long. No team has gone winless since the NFL expanded its schedule in 2021, and before that, the Cleveland Browns were the last 0-16 squad all the way back in 2017. There will eventually be a team that drops all 17 games, however, and this year's Miami Dolphins are the strongest candidate to date.
The Dolphins already held the worst roster in the league, and that was before they lost De'Von Achane for the season. The star running back tore his ACL in Week 3, which stripped Miami of its best player and the only Pro Bowler in town. Without Achane, the franchise is incredibly young and inexperienced and rid of high-upside talent.
Miami showed some fight defensively in Week 4 when it held the Minnesota Vikings out of the end zone, but if the Dolphins cannot win a game in which they hold the opposing team to five field goals, then who will they beat? The also-winless Los Angeles Chargers and reeling Green Bay Packers present the two best opportunities, and there are two matchups with the Jets up ahead. But the Dolphins could be underdogs in each of those games, and the rest of the schedule is grueling.
For the first two years (and even into the third season) of Bryce Young's career, the former No.…
author: Carter Bahns

title: Russell Wilson says Chiefs should call Tyreek Hill amid WR injuries: 'Why would you not do it?'
summary: On this week's episode of 'Set Hut,' the former Super Bowl-winning quarterback explains why a Hill reunion is best for business in Kansas City
full_text:
Should the Kansas City Chiefs call Tyreek Hill ? Super Bowl champion Russell Wilson and former Chief Kyle Long think so.
In this week's installment of CBS Sports' "Set Hut," the two former players discussed how K.C. looks right now and why they should pick up the phone to call Hill in for a workout.
"I'm going after Tyreek Hill right now if I'm the Chiefs. ... Think about the yards," Wilson said. "If he's healthy, why would you not do it? ... Chiefs Kingdom would go crazy for it."
Wilson noted how the offense would open up, and because the Chiefs didn't have the run game they do now years ago, they'll be that much more elevated.
"They've got explosive plays in the pass game, they've got explosive plays in the running game. I don't know how you're going to beat these guys," Wilson said, in a world where the Chiefs have Hill.
Long was a 2021 Chiefs teammate of Hill. That season, Hill posted 111 receptions for 1,239 yards and nine touchdowns in 17 games, 16 of which were starts. Having a front-row seat to the connection between Hill and Mahomes, Long says the "unspoken communication" and chemistry they share "can be huge and so priceless for the Chiefs."
Some are hesitant about the 32-year-old because he is returning from such a gruesome leg injury. Even if he can't do all the things he used to be able to on the field, Long still thinks the WR can make an impact.
"If you're worried about the ins and outs cuts that Tyreek Hill can do with his newly reconstructed leg, how about you say, just go run straight down the field and force that safety to cover you, and it opens up so much of the middle of the field," Long said.
The Chiefs are coming off a win over the Las Vegas Raiders , who were 3-0 going into the divisional contest. This week, they are on a bye, and in Week 6, Kansas City will face the Los Angeles Chargers .
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Best NFL futures bets to make after the first month of the 2026 season: Buy Dallas Cowboys, Bijan Robinson
summary: Don't sleep on Kyle Shanahan to win Coach of the Year either
full_text:
Four weeks of NFL action are now in the rearview mirror. The rust has been shaken off, and clubs are now getting into a groove as we continue to barrel down the road that'll eventually lead us to Super Bowl LXI. Of course, before we get to that matchup, there's plenty that still needs to be determined, so how about we roll up our sleeves and call some shots?
Below, we're going to roll through a handful of futures bets to make now that we've seen these teams up close for four games. In this very story a year ago , we clued you in on a number of winners, including the Jaguars winning their division, New England going over their then-8.5 over/under win total, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba leading the league in receiving yards. Each of those paid out at plus money, with Smith-Njigba being our biggest winner at +600.
With 14 weeks left in the 2026 regular season, let's jump on some early value on the futures market while we still can.
NFL odds as of Oct. 6 and courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook
This is just as much of a play against the rest of the division as it is buying Dallas. While the Giants were my preseason dark horse to burst onto the scene in the NFC East, the Jaxson Dart season-ending knee injury imploded that prediction. Meanwhile, the Commanders have QB injuries of their own, with Jayden Daniels again dealing with a left elbow injury. He's slated to return at some point, but they've dug themselves into a 1-3 hole through the first month and are already 0-2 in the division, including a head-to-head loss to the Cowboys .
Then there's the Eagles . Despite sitting at 2-2, they look lost offensively. Even before dealing with an onslaught of injuries to the likes of DeVonta Smith , Saquon Barkley and Dallas Goedert , it just hasn't looked right. Through the first month, their yards-per-play average is tied for the third-lowest in the NFL, with teams like the Tennessee Titans and Los Angeles Chargers moving the ball at a more efficient clip. While the injury luck could eventually flip in the Eagles' favor, this just doesn't feel like Philadelphia's year.
That brings us to Dallas. Sure, their defense hasn't looked much improved from last year despite a slew of new faces being injected into that side of the ball. But they still feel like the most complete team in the division. They also just traded for corner Joey Porter Jr. , and his arrival could help bring the defense to a more serviceable level.
Even if they get there, the strength of this team will remain its offense, and it's that unit that gives us confidence in this future. The Cowboys are tied for the second-highest scoring offense in the NFL (30.5 points per game), fourth-best on third down (51.02%) and the third-best in the league in the red zone (81.25%). They also protect the football well with just two turnovers through the first four games.
Their upcoming schedule is pretty soft, which will be an opportunity to pile up some wins. Over the next seven games, they'll face the likes of the Buccaneers , Packers , Cardinals , Colts , and Titans, which could all be looked at as penciled-in wins.
If you want to play this more conservatively and look at the Cowboys to simply make the playoffs, that sits at -114.
Let's take advantage of the uncertainty surrounding Caleb Williams ' return from his hamstring injury and jump on this value with Chicago to win the NFC North.
Minnesota currently is the betting favorite to win this division at +125, but I think its 4-0 record is a bit hollow. It beat up on bad competition in the Packers, Bucs, and Dolphins . While the Vikings claimed a head-to-head win over the Bears , that was when Williams went down. They might be able to win games solely based on their lethal defense, but I think rubber will eventually meet the road, and they'll need their offense to muster something. So far, I don't know if Kyler Murray is the best fit for Kevin O'Connell's system, which has me questioning their ability to hang onto their division lead.
Beyond the Vikings , this division doesn't feel as fearsome as it did heading into the year. The Lions ' defense leaves them vulnerable, and the Packers haven't instilled any faith , so I think this is Chicago's division to lose. Williams will be back sooner rather than later, and, when he does, I'd expect this number to shrink. That'll be especially true if their defense continues to play at a high level after allowing less than 13 points in each of its last three games.
I think Jacksonville is hiding in plain sight as the best team in the AFC. Sure, Kansas City's revival with its 4-0 start has the NFL buzzing, but the Jaguars feel like a sleeping giant. Dating back to 2025, the club is 11-1 over its past 12 regular season games. There's a lane for them to possess the top seed and first-round bye when the dust settles on the regular season.
The Jaguars, who are 3-1 and currently atop the AFC South, have the easiest remaining strength of schedule in the NFL. They'll be in London over the next two weeks and face a depleted Eagles team in Week 5 before their first divisional matchup of the year against the current 0-4 Texans in Week 6. They'll be favored in both of those games, meaning they could be 5-1 as they enter the Week 7 bye week.
After that, their toughest remaining games are arguably at the Ravens in Week 9, at the Bears in Week 13, and at the Cowboys in Week 16. It wouldn't surprise me if they go into any of those environments and pull out the victory. But let's say they lose all three of those games and take care of business elsewhere; that'd put them at 13-4 for the second-straight year, which would certainly put them in prime position to claim the No. 1 seed.
Robinson is looking up to both Jahmyr Gibbs (+400) and Kenneth Walker III (+380) in the race currently, but I think this is a fantastic price for the Falcons star back. He's currently second in the NFL in rushing and total yards from scrimmage, trailing Walker by just 43 rushing yards and 7 scrimmage yards. Robinson has caught up in the standings after going nuclear over the last two games, once Michael Penix Jr . returned at quarterback.
While it's hard to imagine Robinson keeping up his current pace with Penix under center, let's just have some fun and project out what these numbers would look like over a full 17-game season. That'd come out to about 2,881 rushing yards and 34 rushing touchdowns. LOL!
That's just an extreme projection to illustrate that Robinson has the ability to light it up now that the Falcons are getting stable quarterback play with Penix. He's just as — if not slightly more — talented than both Gibbs and Walker, and if the Falcons go on to win the NFC South (currently tied with the Panthers after the first month), I believe he'll be given the large chunk of the credit in the form of OPOY votes.
Let me lay out some of the current odds surrounding the 49ers . After Week 4, they are the betting favorite to have the most regular-season wins at +350, meaning that they are also the favorites to be the No. 1 seed in the NFC (+190) as well as win the NFC West (+100). If all that comes to fruition and they are the top dogs in the conference with a big win total (currently 4-0), why wouldn't Kyle Shanahan be the favorite to win Coach of the Year?
Shanahan would have once again navigated his team through another pile of injuries and firmly have them in the Super Bowl conversation. This is almost exactly what he did a year ago, only the Niners fell to the Seahawks in Week 18, which spurned them the opportunity to be the No. 1 seed. Had they won that game, I think Shanahan would've won COY then. Now, he has a similar opportunity and, given the +1200 price point, it's maybe the best value on the entire futures board.
The only candidate that truly makes me nervous in this race is Todd Monken (+700). He has the Browns at 3-1 on the year, and Cleveland is tied for the third-easiest remaining strength of schedule in the NFL. Given how low the bar has been with that…
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: NFC team grades: 49ers top of class through four games, Rams, Eagles slip to middling marks
summary: Plus, the reigning Super Bowl champs still look the part
full_text:
The first month of the NFL season can play tricks on us. Last year through four games, Baker Mayfield was looking like an MVP candidate, and the Buccaneers were 3-1. The Colts were also 3-1, and Daniel Jones was not only putting up even better numbers than Mayfield, but putting up some of the best numbers in the league — one of the most out-of-nowhere quarterback surprises in recent memory.
On the other side, the Panthers were 1-3 and coming off a 26-10 shellacking courtesy of the Jaguars . The Texans were also 1-3. Both of those teams made the postseason.
Of course, there are plenty of early signs that turn out to be true, too. The Bills and Eagles were the only undefeated teams through four weeks last year, and both were playoff teams. The Saints , Titans and Jets — all 0-4 at this point last year — ended up continuing their poor play and landing top-10 picks.
What we can say for sure is that it's early. The standings of today will look very different one month from now, let alone three months from now when the regular season wraps up. Still, with four games down, we've seen enough to hand out first-quarter grades to every team, taking into account not just their record, but how they've looked getting there and how that projects moving forward.
After hitting the AFC yesterday , we move to the NFC.
If Jaxson Dart and Brian Burns were healthy and the Giants were 3-1, this would be an "A" or "A-" easily. Instead, both suffered season-ending knee injuries. Dart is the one that really, really hurts. Based on the tiny sample size we saw, he looked excellent. Yes, the Giants lead the NFC East, but their last two wins were 12-7 over the Titans and a win over the Cardinals that came down to a goal-line stand in the final seconds. Any team wondering whether to start Jameis Winston or J.J. McCarthy can't really get a grade much higher than this, especially given the short- and long-term implications of Dart's injury.
The defense deserves a "B-" or a "C+." The offense deserves a "D" ... or maybe worse. Hence, the "C-" mark. The Eagles are 29th in offensive success rate and 31st in EPA per play, only ahead of the Buccaneers. Yikes. Jalen Hurts looks completely lost, and Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith are both dealing with injuries. The offensive line, due to injuries and significant skill decline, is a shell of its former self. The defense has been much better, but still disappointing given its lofty expectations. The Eagles' wins are narrow ones over the Commanders and Titans. They got blown out by the Case Keenum-led Bears and blew a 10-point lead with under five minutes left against the Rams , who made so many mistakes they were practically begging the Eagles to win the game. Nick Sirianni, Sean Mannion, Hurts and many others are drawing the ire of Philadelphia faithful.
The Cowboys currently have the fifth-highest-scoring offense on a per-drive basis of the 21st century. Dak Prescott has been outstanding, and CeeDee Lamb and/or George Pickens can dominate any defense, as seen against the Texans in Week 4 . Plus, the Cowboys are about to get their best offensive lineman, Tyler Smith , back. For as good as the offense is, though, the defense is just as bad. Dallas' defense is 20th in EPA per play, 31st in success rate and 31st in explosive play rate. They're allowing a league-worst 6.4 yards per play. The Joey Porter Jr . addition should help, but he's just one of the 11 players on the field.
In Week 1, the Commanders' defense looked good, but the offense looked bad. In Week 2, the offense started to come around, but then Jayden Daniels got hurt again, and Washington got blown out. Week 3 remains one of the most surprising results in the NFL this season, a 33-31 win over the Seahawks . But any chance at building hope and momentum dissipated in Week 4, where Marcus Mariota got hurt, forcing the Commanders to turn to seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis . Other than first-round rookie Sonny Styles looking very good, it's hard to find good news for a team that very much looks like last year's 5-12 outfit. Washington is 30th in offensive success rate and 23rd in defensive success rate.
How does a 4-0 team receive a "B" mark? Well, how about this: Over the last three weeks, the Vikings have scored one offensive touchdown. Every other team in the NFL has at least three. The Vikings beat the Bears 9-3 in a downpour in Week 2, a game Caleb Williams left early. They beat the winless Buccaneers 23-16 in Week 3, a game Baker Mayfield left early. They nudged past the winless Dolphins 15-10 in Week 4. That does not inspire much confidence. The defense is the best in the league in both EPA per play and success rate. Brian Flores is simply superb. That's an "A+" unit. The offense is a "D" at best, ranking dead last in yards per play. Kyler Murray and co. have to figure something out. The 4-0 record bumps the grade up a hair, but this style of winning doesn't seem sustainable.
The Bears have won three games using three different quarterbacks, a remarkable feat in and of itself. The offense looked magnificent in Week 1 with Williams at the helm, and then it looked bad in a rainstorm in Week 2, even before Williams left early. The Bears' domination of the Eagles despite playing third-string quarterback Case Keenum is one of the more impressive performances of the season. There are still major questions about the defense, but it has at least somewhat started heading in the right direction, albeit against weak competition. Williams' hamstring injury knocks this grade down a bit, mostly because of the long-term implications. Yes, he's expected back sooner rather than later, but how healthy will he truly be? His mobility, escapability and scrambling are crucial parts of his game and the Bears' offense as a whole.
The Lions ' defense ranks dead last in EPA per play and explosive play rate. It's hard to be much worse than that, right? Everyone is frustrated, Dan Campbell is fielding questions about defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard , and the talent in the secondary simply isn't up to par. The eventual return of Brian Branch will help, but he can't fix everything — and he shouldn't be expected to — especially coming off an Achilles tear. The offense is generally very good: second in EPA per play and third in success rate and points per drive. But there's so much pressure for Jared Goff , Jahmyr Gibbs and co. to score a touchdown every time they touch the ball. Week 4's loss to the Panthers was a prime example: Detroit scored on six of its 10 drives and lost.
The Packers ' two wins this year are a three-point overtime win against the Jets (in a game they very easily could have and perhaps should have lost) and a three-point win over the Buccaneers, quarterbacked by undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels . That doesn't exactly inspire confidence. Neither do huge losses to the Vikings (a Carson Wentz-led comeback) and the Falcons . There are gigantic issues running the ball (31st in success rate) and stopping the run (28th in success rate). The Packers are scrambling at the offensive line. Jordan Love already has three interceptions; he threw six all of last year. The defense just lost Edgerrin Cooper to a torn Achilles. Micah Parsons ' looming return will help, but there are just so many issues here.
Here's a sentence you probably didn't expect to read four weeks into the season: Bryce Young leads the NFL in passing yards. It's not just the counting stats, either. He's sixth in EPA per dropback and seventh in yards per attempt. He has taken a gigantic leap forward in every aspect , though it hasn't been against the world's best competition. Regardless, Carolina should be thrilled. The defense has been less thrilling. If we take out a Week 2 game against the Cooper Rush-led Falcons, Carolina has a -0.15 defensive EPA per play, which would rank 29th. Without starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson , it could get worse before it gets better, too.
Atlanta leads the NFL in…
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Prisco's Week 5 NFL picks: Cowboys rout Buccaneers on Thursday, Packers upset Bears
summary: Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 5 picks, including the Texans getting their first win and the Jets over the Browns
full_text:
So much for starting October the right way.
My picks stunk last week. I was OK straight up, going 9-7, but the late-game shenanigans cost me a chance at a decent week against the spread. I went 4-11-1 ATS last week as many back-door covers got me.
My straight-up record for the season is 38-26-0 and my ATS record is a dismal 25-37-2. How can I be that bad?
No time for sulking. It's time to turn it around and this week I think I have a chance to move closer to .500 for the season. Then we can build on things from there.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
The Bucs are 0-4 and playing a rookie at quarterback in Jalon Daniels . He will be making his first road start. On a Thursday night? That's tough. The Cowboys are coming off a big win at Houston and the offense was dynamic. Dak Prescott keeps it going in this one.
The Eagles are so banged up and coming off a tough loss to the Rams . Then, right tackle Lane Johnson retired on Tuesday. They have so many key players out, which has to help the Jaguars . The Jaguars are second in scoring defense and have stopped the run all year long. They will limit the Eagles' offense in this one. The Jaguars go to 4-1.
Pick: Jaguars 28, Eagles 16
These two don't like each other. The Bears have been great running the ball, but this could be the game where playing without Caleb Williams shows up. Look for Jordan Love to have a big day throwing it on the other side — finally. The Packers win it in an upset.
Pick: Packers 27, Bears 24
Both of these teams are 0-4, which is surprising when it comes to the Texans . The Titans have played a lot of close games, which they will again here. But C.J. Stroud will make the plays late to win this one.
Pick: Texans 23, Titans 17
The Bengals are hurting at receiver with both Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase suffering injuries last week against the Jaguars. But there is a chance they can play. Even if they don't, the Bengals will move the football. Miami plays hard, but they are undermanned.
Pick: Bengals 23, Dolphins 13
This is a long trip for the Raiders , coming off a tough division loss. The Patriots seemed to right things against the Bills , which meant Drake Maye came alive. Look for that to continue here as the Patriots get to 3-2.
Pick: Patriots 28, Raiders 24
The Saints looked awful in their loss to the Falcons on Monday night and now face an undefeated Vikings team. That Minnesota defense is special. The Saints are really banged up on defense. Maybe Kyler Murray can get it going against them. I think he does.
Pick: Vikings 24, Saints 17
The Browns are 3-1 and have won three straight, while the Jets have lost three straight. But they are back home after two on the road. That matters. Look for a better showing here from their offense as they upset the Browns.
The Colts have won two straight as they head to face the Steelers on the road after beating the Commanders in London last week. That's a tough turnaround, while the Steelers have extra days of rest. That matters. The Steelers will get back on track with a victory led by Aaron Rodgers .
Pick: Steelers 33, Colts 23
There is a chance Jayden Daniels will play for the Commanders. That's the good news. But he will be wearing a brace on his elbow. How much will it restrict him? The Giants are 3-1, but this is a big road test. I think they will be up to it. Give me Jameis Winston playing well as the Giants get to 4-1.
Pick: Giants 26, Commanders 24
The Broncos are playing consecutive road games after losing at San Francisco last week. The Chargers haven't won. They will here. Desperation will be in play for the Chargers. The Broncos have offensive issues right now that will show up. Look for Los Angeles to quiet the critics for a week.
Pick: Chargers 23, Broncos 17
The Lions are playing on the road off a Sunday night loss. They can't stop anybody on defense. But the Cardinals have some defensive issues as well. Look for the Lions to outscore Arizona in a shootout as Jared Goff puts up big numbers.
Pick: Lions 40, Cardinals 31
This is an enormous division game that will be a physical war, as they always are between these two. The 49ers are undefeated, but this is a tough road test. The Seahawks are the healthier team, but the 49ers have played better. The 49ers have played well in Seattle, but I think the Seattle defense will come up big late to win it.
Pick: Seahawks 28, 49ers 21
This could be a Ravens team without Lamar Jackson after he suffered an injured ankle last week. If he can't go, Tyler Huntley will start. That means this will be a Derrick Henry game. The Falcons impressed Monday night, beating up the Saints, but this is a short week and a better opponent. The Ravens will rally if Jackson doesn't play and be thrilled if he does.
Pick: Ravens 24, Falcons 17
This is one of the best games of the week. The Bills are coming off a tough loss to the Patriots, while the Rams rallied to beat the Eagles. Look for a lot of points in this one as Josh Allen and Matt Stafford have big games. In the end, the Rams will make the plays late to win it.

title: Week 4 3up and 3 down: Falcons run away with the win
summary: The Atlanta Falcons came up big in primetime once again, throttling their rivals in New Orleans. When the hardest part of writing an article is finding “down” players to nitpick, you know it was a good week. Here’s the Week 4, 3 up and 3 down. 3 up Harold Perkins Jr Perkins celebrated his homecoming […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 05: Drake London #5 of the Atlanta Falcons celebrates a first down against the New Orleans Saints during the second quarter of the game at Caesars Superdome on October 05, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons came up big in primetime once again, throttling their rivals in New Orleans . When the hardest part of writing an article is finding “down” players to nitpick, you know it was a good week. Here’s the Week 4, 3 up and 3 down. 3 up Harold Perkins Jr Perkins celebrated his homecoming in style, securing 6 solo tackles and a sack, along with multiple impressive coverage reps. He had his most snaps of the season and finished with the 6th-highest snap count on the team. Many, myself included, wondered what Perkins’ role would be with this team; most envisioned a situational rusher, but he’s playing like a legit 3-down linebacker. Jeff Ulbrich has excelled at putting his players in position to succeed, and Perkins’ growth over four weeks is one of the best examples. What a homecoming for Harold Perkins Jr. He was a jack of all trades last night. Blowing up the puller and stuffing the run, getting after the QB, and breaking up passes. He's been more than just a situational rusher, he's playing like a legit LB. — Tre’Shon (@treshon.io) 2026-10-06T21:00:45.963Z The Robinsons It was impossible to only pick one running back from this backfield after the duo combined for 5 touchdowns and 187 yards, leading the way to the Falcons win. These two go together like Owen Wilson and Ben Stiller. Watching Bijan carry the football is poetry in motion, and Brian brings the slam- poetry energy. Every week, analysts say, “If you stop this run game, then you can win the game,” but that is easier said than done. Even if you manage to blow up the blocking, the duo has combined for 571 yards after contact. Chris Lindstrom The All-Pro was an unstoppable force against the Saints. This revitalized run scheme showcased their best player all night. Lindstrom is finally getting the opportunity to pull across the formation, and it’s leading to touchdowns. He’s still one of the best in the league at getting to the second level and puts out teach tape on how to take proper angles to cut off would-be tacklers. He finished the game as the highest-graded player on the field per PFF , and the film backs it up. Bill Callahan’s influence can be felt across the entire line, but we’re seeing him maximize Lindstrom’s talents in ways we haven’t seen the team do before. Chris Lindstrom had one of the best performances of his career last night. He's doing it all in this revitalized run scheme. Elite at climbing to the 2nd level. Finally getting opportunities as a puller. Had multiple 2 for 1s & consistently moved the Saints DL off their spots pic.twitter.com/SNxddB0MIG — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) October 6, 2026 3 down Divine Deablo Deablo doesn’t look like himself. The linebacker nursed a hamstring injury all week , but he looked sluggish before he hit the injury report. His coverage instincts haven’t been there, and he’s regressed in the run game too. If we’re being honest, his 2025 season is an outlier in his career, but there’s no need to panic yet. The linebacker clearly isn’t healthy and should get the benefit of the doubt before being written off; in the meantime, the Falcons have two rookie linebackers who have shown they can be leaned on for support. Jessie Bates III Similar to Deablo, Bates’ regression has been noticeable this season. The gambles in coverage aren’t paying off, and we’ve seen a few busts and explosive plays happen on his watch. For years it felt like Bates had to make a play to help cover up issues on his side of the ball, but that isn’t the case anymore. Sometimes when you only know one speed, it’s hard to adjust, but if Bates focuses more on doing his job on any given play, the turnover opportunities will come. He’s still an above-average safety in this league, but he doesn’t need to win the game on his own anymore. ESPN’s MNF Production First off, the Saints “Domecoming” is worth celebrating and revisiting. Katrina was a travesty that forever altered the lives of New Orleans citizens, and the Superdome’s reopening was a historic moment. That doesn’t mean the Falcons should be billed as a villain or secondary product; at the end of the day, these are two NFL teams that deserved equal coverage when the game broadcast started. However, it felt like Troy Aikman and Joe Buck ran out of lines quickly for the Saints and had none prepared for the Falcons. The Manning cast was also a one-sided affair, with no Falcons guests. It is what it is. The Falcons got the W, and that’s all that matters. The Falcons are now at 2-2, resetting the early-season narratives around the team. This staff deserves a lot of credit for keeping this group engaged after both a poor start and a dominant Week 3 win. The sky’s the limit, and next week is a battle of the birds as the Falcons return home to host the Baltimore Ravens .

title: The Falcoholic Reacts Survey: The trajectory of Michael Penix Jr.
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bengals fans and fans across the country. After two composed performances in leading the Falcons to definitive road victories, conversations are changing about Michael Penix Jr. Many were skeptical that he would play […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 05: Michael Penix Jr. #9 of the Atlanta Falcons celebrates during the first quarter of an NFL football game against the New Orleans Saints at Caesars Superdome on October 05, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bengals fans and fans across the country. After two composed performances in leading the Falcons to definitive road victories, conversations are changing about Michael Penix Jr. Many were skeptical that he would play at a high level again after another devastating knee injury last season. The new regime was noncommittal about him. As high as his highs were in 2024 and 2025, his lack of dependability and erratic play at his worst didn’t inspire great confidence in him becoming a franchise quarterback. That has changed in two difficult environments to play in, especially on primetime. He is getting the ball out quicker and crisper. The decisiveness and processing of coverage alignments have been hugely impressive. While plenty has been said about his ability to thrive operating under center, it should also be noted that he’s become much more comfortable playing under duress. That is pivotal for a young quarterback in their maturation process to play fully in command in the pocket. While two games can only reveal so much, there is plenty to be excited about Penix Jr.’s recent performances. The question is do you think the strides he is making can translate into being the franchise’s long-term quarterback? The locker room is fully behind him. His throwing velocity is impressive. Penix Jr. has played a major role in helping turn the Falcons’ fortunes around in 12 days. Can he do that for years to come? Has Michael Penix changed your outlook? Are you confident in the Falcons? Whoever overcomes theirs will be the last team standing. This week, those teams were the Falcons and Panthers, who put on a display of offensive firepower. On the other end of the spectrum, you have the Saints and Buccaneers, who are now multiple games under .500. Here’s the Week 4 NFC South Review. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-4) Week 4 Result: Buccaneers 14 – Packers 17 Week 5 Opponent: Dallas Cowboys The Buccaneers are off to their worst start since 2013. New offensive coordinator Zac Robinson has been unable to get anything going, and Todd Bowles’ seat looks hotter than ever. UDFA Jalon Daniels looked like a UDFA, and Bucky Irving and company have looked quite pedestrian after having success in prior seasons. Fans are sick of Bowles, but his defense hasn’t been the main issue; with Antoine Winfield Jr. expected to miss 2-4 weeks with a broken rib, that could change quickly. There is no rest for the wicked, as the Buccaneers have a quick turnaround against the Cowboys on Thursday Night Football. Carolina Panthers (2-2) Week 4 Result: Panthers 32 – Lions 26 Week 5 Opponent: Philadelphia Eagles Coming into the game, the Panthers injury report had to be posted on two pages. Luckily for Carolina, all they needed was Bryce Young and Tetairoa McMillan. The duo was unstoppable, racking up 14 completions for 192 yards and 2 touchdowns. The defense did just enough to hold off the Lions, and they kept Jahmyr Gibbs in check on the ground. This team hasn’t been able to stack these performances multiple weeks in a row, but they are in position to win this division. Their next test will be on the road in Philadelphia against an Eagles team that looks like a shell of its former self. BRYCE YOUNG pic.twitter.com/5dq6OdFqrN — Ian Hartitz (@Ihartitz) October 5, 2026 New Orleans Saints (1-3) Week 4 Result: Saints 24 – Falcons 45 Week 5 Opponent: Minnesota Vikings The Saints have been a volatile product through the first quarter of the season, but they had no high moments in this rivalry game. What started as a celebration ended as a travesty. They had no answer for Atlanta’s run game and surrendered big plays when the Falcons dialed up the deep ball. Kellen Moore’s seat is heating up as the team falls two games below .500. Their season isn’t over, but it will be soon if they can’t sort out their struggles. They’ll host the undefeated Vikings next Sunday. Atlanta Falcons (2-2) Week 4 Result: Falcons 45 – Saints 24 Week 5 Opponent: Baltimore Ravens Week 2 feels like it happened a year ago. The Falcons have been a completely different team with Penix under center. Atlanta spoiled the Saints’ “Domecoming” and dominated from the opening snap. The Robinsons are the league’s best running back duo and accounted for 5 rushing touchdowns and nearly 200 yards. Penix is doing his part by taking care of the football and hitting shots when called upon. You can’t say enough about what Jeff Ulbrich is getting out of this hobbled defense. They pressured Tyler Shough all night and maintained the lead through all four quarters. Everything looks like it’s finally coming together. The Falcons return home for their 3rd straight primetime game and will face off against the Ravens. Bijan Robinson ➖19 carries ➖145 yards ➖2 TDs That guys rocks. pic.twitter.com/ZUCAStw1GJ — That Guy Rocked NFL (@NFLRocked) October 6, 2026 The division is starting to take shape, and the early favorites for the division crown are the Falcons and Panthers. If both teams keep things going, the rest of the league will have to respect the South.

I don’t know why Pitts was largely parked very early on in this one, but thankfully he was more frequently targeted and productive too. title: Has the Ravens defense really been bad?
summary: Jesse Minter and the Ravens defense have taken a lot of heat through four weeks. Minter was supposed to be the savior of this defense, the guy who would end two years of struggles under Zach Orr. Most people expected a dominant unit right away. That hasn’t happened yet, but they haven’t been nearly as […]
full_text: Jesse Minter and the Ravens defense have taken a lot of heat through four weeks. Minter was supposed to be the savior of this defense, the guy who would end two years of struggles under Zach Orr. Most people expected a dominant unit right away. That hasn’t happened yet, but they haven’t been nearly as bad as people seem to think. Let’s start with where they rank. In 2024 and 2025, the Ravens were 18th and 30th in penalty-adjusted defensive EPA through four weeks. This year they’re ninth. Those 2024 and 2025 units finished eighth and 22nd, so this defense has historically gotten better as the season goes on, and this year it’s starting from a much better spot. I’m using a penalty-adjusted metric for a reason. Penalties have been a real problem for this team, and they’ve been going almost entirely one way. With penalties included, the Ravens rank 15th in defensive EPA per play. Sunday’s game against the Titans got out of hand: Baltimore was flagged 13 times for 131 yards, compared with 5 for 32 for Tennessee. And that one-sided pattern goes beyond one game. Opposing offenses have been flagged against the Ravens just nine times, tied for the fewest in the league, and Baltimore ranks dead last in EPA gained from those penalties. Short version: the defense is getting no help from the refs. They’ve drawn exactly one offensive holding call through four games, against Dallas, which is again tied for last. The defense hasn’t been clean either, but it’s getting nothing back in return. The offense is in the same spot: it has drawn only four defensive penalties, 31st in the league, while consistently shooting itself in the foot with procedural flags. If opposing offenses were being flagged at even a league-average rate, this defense would jump to 11th in EPA per play. Remove all penalties and it’s 9th. All of this is to say the defense hasn’t been bad; it just needs some penalty luck to swing its way. One holding call or DPI can completely change a drive and turn a three-and-out into a touchdown drive. Fans, players, and coaches have harping on the penalties for weeks because they’re doing so much damage. As a team, the Ravens have lost 329 yards and 40 expected points to penalties, both second-worst in the NFL. Remove the penalties and they’re also 2nd in offensive EPA per play. Without the flags, this team has a top-two offense and a top-10 defense. I said after the Saints game that the Ravens were getting flagged at an unprecedented rate, and that’s turned into a broader NFL story. Teams are getting flagged at the highest rate in a decade, refs are getting suspended, and fans are fed up with how much officials are shaping games. This general pushback against the penalties could lead to a regression to the mean. Add it all up: the penalties, a new head coach, injured players still working their way back and finding their chemistry, and a defense that has historically improved as the year goes on. I have no doubt this will be a top unit over the back half of the season. The defensive line has been a bit of a carousel, but Nnamdi Madubuike and Mike Green have both looked very good – Green in particular looks like he is ready for a sophomore breakout. Trey Hendrickson missed last week after a procedure on his finger and should be back this week or next. The one area that needs immediate improvement is the run defense. The Ravens rank 21st in EPA per rush allowed with penalties removed, and they no longer have time to sort it out. With Lamar Jackson now injured, the defense needs to play up to its potential right away, starting with Bijan Robinson and a red-hot Falcons team.
author: Stephen Bopst

title: Roundtable Reactions: Ravens trade for Cam Jurgens
summary: The Baltimore Ravens made a surprise trade this afternoon, acquiring offensive lineman Cam Jurgens from the Philadelphia Eagles in exchange for draft capital. The Ravens are trading a 2027 fifth-round pick and 2028 second-round pick to the Eagles, while also receiving a 2027 seventh-round pick in addition to Jurgens. Here are the Baltimore Beatdown staff’s […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - OCTOBER 04: Philadelphia Eagles center Cam Jurgens #51 gets set during the game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Los Angeles Rams on October 4th, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens made a surprise trade this afternoon, acquiring offensive lineman Cam Jurgens from the Philadelphia Eagles in exchange for draft capital. The Ravens are trading a 2027 fifth-round pick and 2028 second-round pick to the Eagles, while also receiving a 2027 seventh-round pick in addition to Jurgens. Here are the Baltimore Beatdown staff’s instant reactions to the move: The Ravens were simply running out of options on a depleted offensive line. Jurgens has not played well this season at guard, but the hope is that a move back to the center position will help him. Jurgens is an athletic center, making him a stylistic fit for Dwayne Ledford and Baltimore’s zone run scheme. Time will tell if the Ravens overpaid simply out of desperation, but if Jurgens is able to return to solid form at center and remain relatively healthy after dealing with injuries in recent years, then Baltimore could have their answer to the position for the next several years alongside Vega Ioane. — Dustin Cox The Ravens moving a future second-rounder definitely raises an eyebrow with a front office that has been traditionally stingy about keeping their draft picks. I’ve seen the word “desperate” floating around, and I don’t necessarily think it’s the wrong word to use for this situation, but maybe just a reminder that a move made in desperation doesn’t mean it was a panic move. The Ravens were very depleted along the O-line at this early stage of the season and now once again face the specter of Lamar Jackson missing time with an injury. To keep the season on its trajectory, they had to make a move to solidify the trenches, so they paid a premium price for Cam Jurgens. Jurgens has struggled playing out of position for Philly, but moving back to Center could be the thing he needs to have the best parts of his game restored (we hope). History has shown it’s bad business to deal with Howie Roseman, but then again, Baltimore got something for nothing from Philly in the Jaire Alexander move, so who knows how this one shakes out. I’m glad they have another O-lineman in the room that’s not just a body, but a guy who has shown a high level of competence. — Kevin McNeils Eric DeCosta is not messing around. It’s rare that the Ravens trade a Day 2 pick, but this is no rental. Cam Jurgens is signed through 2029, making him Baltimore’s long-term successor to Tyler Linderbaum. Vega Ioane played well at center when called upon, but he is no doubt a more natural guard and moving back to RG will be best for his immediate play and future development. This is the kind of move the Ravens refused to make to fix their OL issues in years past, so their urgency to get a deal done before Week 5 is commendable. Jurgens is a good player, too, on an affordable deal for the next four(!) seasons – which is probably worth more than the second-round pick Baltimore gave up in the trade. — Cam Jurgens It’s a risk, but one that was needed. Ravens fans are happy, Eagles fans are happy. Who wins this trade will obviously take time to figure out but in the short term, the Ravens fill an immediate need at center that has been in flux ever since Tyler Linderbaum signed with the Raiders this offseason. Cam Jurgens has been named to the Pro-Bowl twice as a center but was recently moved to guard after Landon Dickerson got hurt. The results have not been good. If Jurgens can come in and get back to his old form at his natural position, the 2028 second-rounder will be justified as it will drastically raise the floor on this shaky offensive line. I have to tip the cap to Eric DeCosta here, the offensive line has been a weakness for two years and he’s clearly taking action to at least try to fix it. — Stephen Bopst The Ravens needed a solution on the offensive line, whether it was at guard or center. DeCosta opts to find a long-term solution for their center problem after trying to find stopgaps this year following Linderbaum’s departure. Jurgens has been arguably a top-3 or top-5 center for multiple years and has a rather team friendly contract that runs through the 2029 season. While Jurgens has struggled this year, he’s playing out of position at left guard due to injuries the Eagles have and in a bad offense that simply doesn’t suit him. Getting him back in a wide zone scheme, next to Vega Ioane, coached by Dwayne Ledford should hopefully return Jurgens to his peak. If it does, this line could suddenly be strength. Now the Ravens need to figure out if John Simpson is the right answer at left guard after two struggling games against Dallas and Tennessee or if Emery Jones should get a look somewhere. Remember that Ioane’s position at Penn State for two years was left guard and Jones is a right side fit. — Zach Canter The Ravens have had horrible injury luck at center, where all three of their offseason additions suffered season-ending (likely) injuries. That only compounded further when Andrew Vorhees, starting at right guard because Vega Ioane slid over to center, left their Week 4 matchup early with a foot injury. Simply put, Eric DeCosta’s is forced as the Ravens badly need stability on the interior of their offensive line. At this juncture in the season, acquiring Cam Jurgens is a best-case scenario for the Ravens in terms of talent and upside. A future second-round pick is not an insignificant price and Jurgens has struggled thus far in 2026. However, he was an above-average starting center for multiple years before sliding over to left guard this season. Moving back to center in a new environment, playing back at his natural position, could see Jurgens thrive. On paper, he is a seamless scheme fit for the Ravens. He’s also only 27 years old and under contract until 2029, so he’s far from merely a one-year rental. DeCosta is clearly not willing to sit on his hands and hope the coaching staff can patch together a workable combination of starting interior offensive linemen. — Frank Platko
author: Stephen Bopst

title: Ravens vs. Titans: Rookie Report
summary: The Baltimore Ravens improved to 3-1 in Week 4, with their rookies involved in back-to-back wins after defeating the Tennessee Titans, 24-18. It wasn’t a pretty victory, but the NFL is filled with learning how to win ugly and the rookies did just that. OG Vega Ioane Ioane continues to show why he was the […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - OCTOBER 04: Olaivavega Ioane #71 of the Baltimore Ravens prepares to snap the ball before a play during the second half against the Tennessee Titans at M&T Bank Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) The Baltimore Ravens improved to 3-1 in Week 4, with their rookies involved in back-to-back wins after defeating the Tennessee Titans, 24-18. It wasn’t a pretty victory, but the NFL is filled with learning how to win ugly and the rookies did just that. OG Vega Ioane Ioane continues to show why he was the best pick for the Ravens at 14th overall in the draft. After a couple of really good games as the right guard, Ioane stepped up and made his first career start at center for the Ravens. The Ravens are now missing all three of the guys they brought in to compete for the center job. So, the rookie drafted to be a perennial Pro Bowl guard slid over to play center for the first time since 2024, across from All-Pro Jeffery Simmons. All Ioane did in the start was give up zero pressures and be one of the highest-rated players on the Ravens offense, according to PFF. No big deal. Vega Ioane first career start at center 0 pressures allowed on 34 pass block snaps Smooth hips and initial punch, strong core and pass protection chops pic.twitter.com/hSaql2VVml — Yuri (@Yuri_Ravens) October 6, 2026 OLB Zion Young After a great game against the Cowboys and with Trey Hendrickson out, many were hoping for a big game from the second-round pick. While it wasn’t a bad day for Young, he didn’t flash at all in the pass game against Tennessee after making an impact versus the Cowboys. He ended the game with zero pressures and a 0% win rate on his pass rushes. He did play well against the run, grading out at 62.9 according to PFF, and used his power on the inside multiple times to knock back linemen. Young will have a big opportunity next week against Atlanta, where the Ravens will surely try to utilize his skill set to help neutralize Bijan Robinson. WR Elijah Sarratt Sarratt saw the first snaps of his NFL career and grabbed his first catch while he was at it. It was also a day filled with mistakes for Sarratt. He had multiple penalties and, at one point, ran the wrong route, which put him in the way of a ball meant for Zay Flowers that Sarratt reached out for but couldn’t catch. There’s a very good chance that a lot of the mistakes were rookie jitters after waiting four weeks to finally get snaps. However, with Lamar Jackson looking like he’s going to miss some time, plus Ja’Kobi Lane’s likely lining up when Jackson will get back, it’s hard to see Sarratt getting another extended chance anytime soon as the offensive game plans will get more condensed with Tyler Huntley in. TE Matt Hibner Hibner caught another two passes on two targets yesterday for 34 yards and is becoming trusted more as time goes on. His role will likely expand as veteran tight end Durham Smythe’s season ended early with a torn Achilles. Hibner is going to be asked to replace a lot of what Smythe did as a run blocker. We will have to see how quickly the Ravens can develop their rookie tight ends, but Hibner has already been doing well in the run game. Now, we will see what he can do with even more snaps. The Ravens are going to need him to do a bit of everything as the main partner to Mark Andrews. Mark Andrews hard selling the bootleg, splashing the water as Hibner pops wide open on the Leak. Even like how the OL drift to create a quasi-screen in case the ball is checked down. pic.twitter.com/sgd0Np7Wsk — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) October 5, 2026 TE Josh Cuevas Cuevas didn’t get much action in this one till Smythe went down, but his role against the Titans was exclusive to run blocking. That’s going to have to change with Smythe’s injury. The Ravens are going to need their rookie tight ends to grow up quick, but Cuevas has a skill set to be utilized. He’s an excellent chip blocker, excelling at squaring his target and releasing quickly to become a quarterback-friendly target fast. He can block well when he stays in as a pass blocker, being capable of setting an anchor, but he struggled more as a run blocker to dig out and push defenders. He’s also underrated as a vertical threat when I watched his Alabama tape. He runs excellent vertical routes and gets to top speed quickly, especially when designed targets go his way. The Ravens are going to have to find his role fast with Smythe down for the season. CB Chandler Rivers Rivers’ snap count remained around same as previous weeks. That didn’t change despite Marlon Humphrey’s disappearance due to injury. Nearly all of his snaps came against the pass, where PFF wasn’t kind to him (55.3 grade). PFF coverage games don’t add up to much because they don’t know the play calls and chart reception responsibilities to simply whichever defender was the closest, whether it was their guy to cover or not. By my eye test, River’s hasn’t been a liability or picked on despite being a fifth-round rookie surrounded by starting talent veteran corners. Expect his role to grow as Minter continues to install his defense. P Ryan Eckley Eckley had six punts against the Titans, averaging 47.3 yards on them and pinning four of them inside the 20. Eckley’s stats haven’t been out of the world, but the biggest thing is the rookie punter seems to be both consistent and avoiding mistakes that put his defense in bad situations, which is all you can ask. His holding for kicker Tyler Loop also seems to have been consistent, though his hold on the Loop’s miss in the game may have contributed to the wide left miss. Wide receiver Ja’Kobi Lane and running back Adam Randall remain on injured reserve, with defensive tackle Rayshaun Benny on the practice squad. Randall is capable of returning from IR starting this week.

title: Ravens trade for Eagles Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens
summary: The Ravens entered the season with major questions at the center position, and injuries quickly morphed the situation into a dire emergency. As opposed to past years, when Eric DeCosta declined to address their offensive line during the season, Baltimore’s general manager is making a splash, trading for two-time Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens from […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - NOVEMBER 28: Philadelphia Eagles center Cam Jurgens (51) prepares to seal the ball during the game between the Chicago Bears and the Philadelphia Eagles on November 28, 2025 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA.(Photo by Andy Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Ravens entered the season with major questions at the center position, and injuries quickly morphed the situation into a dire emergency. As opposed to past years, when Eric DeCosta declined to address their offensive line during the season, Baltimore’s general manager is making a splash, trading for two-time Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens from the Eagles. Trade: Eagles are sending two-time Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens and a 2027 7th-round pick to the Ravens in exchange for a 2027 5th-round pick and a 2028 2nd-round pick, sources tell ESPN. pic.twitter.com/AaGL3MYqS7 — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 7, 2026 The Ravens are sending a 2027 5th-round pick and a 2028 2nd-round pick to Philadelphia in exchange for Jurgens and a 2027 7th-round pick. The 27-year-old has been a highly regarded center in the NFL for multiple years and earned a four-year contract extension in 2025 that keeps him under control through the 2029 season. “We are excited to acquire a two-time Pro Bowl center, Cam Jurgens, from the Eagles in a trade,” DeCosta said in a statement provided to Baltimore Beatdown. “Cam is a player we have long admired going all the way back to the draft process. He’s a young foundational piece along our offensive line – a great scheme and cultural fit who will contribute quickly in Baltimore. We are confident that Cam will significantly impact our team and community.” Jurgens has struggled in 2026. He was playing left guard following an injury to Landon Dickerson in a struggling offense that does not fit his skill set. He did play one game at center this season where he allowed zero pressures, indicating he could show improvements in Baltimore. The Ravens are planning on moving Jurgens to his natural position, and hopefully coaching from Dwayne Ledford will help Jurgens get back to his peak. He is an excellent fit to lead Derrick Henry in Declan Doyle’s wide zone scheme. Similar to former Ravens center Tyler Linderbaum, Jurgens will need help in pass protection, but he should not struggle as much as Jovaughn Gwyn. Snapping should not be an issue, either. Currently, Jurgens is under concussion protocol, so it’s unlikely Ravens fans will see him Sunday as he works back to getting healthy and focuses on learning the offense to debut Week 6 against the Browns. Cam Jurgens currently is in concussion protocol and not expected to make his Ravens debut Sunday. He is expected to make his Ravens’ debut in two weeks against the Browns. https://t.co/0MPoqQOHz7 — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 7, 2026 Jurgens’ contract is a hugely appealing part of this trade for the Ravens. The Eagles already paid out his option bonus this year, so the Ravens will owe him just under $1 million in base salary for the rest of the season. He is set to earn $16 million in fully guaranteed money next year with non-guaranteed compensation of roughly $17 million in 2028 and 2029. At present, his cap hits for 2027 through 2029 are scheduled to be about $4.5 million, $7.5 million, and $11.8 million. Dead money from the options bonus prorations will hit Baltimore’s cap in 2030.
author: Zach Canter

title: Ravens Week 4 film study: Vega Ioane could be a long-term center
summary: The Ravens’ gritty Week 4 win over the Titans gave us another opportunity to evaluate several players in the trenches on both sides of the football. Mike Green stepped into a larger role as Baltimore’s primary edge rusher on passing downs, Nnamdi Madubuike continued to show that he has returned to form, and rookie first-round […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - OCTOBER 04: Olaivavega Ioane #71 of the Baltimore Ravens prepares to snap the ball before a play during the second half against the Tennessee Titans at M&T Bank Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Ravens’ gritty Week 4 win over the Titans gave us another opportunity to evaluate several players in the trenches on both sides of the football. Mike Green stepped into a larger role as Baltimore’s primary edge rusher on passing downs, Nnamdi Madubuike continued to show that he has returned to form, and rookie first-round pick Vega Ioane provided some much-needed stability along the interior offensive line in his first start at center. OLB Mike Green 40 snaps | 26 pass rush | 13 run defense | 1 coverage | 5 pressures With Trey Hendrickson out, Mike Green was expected to take on a larger role as a pass rusher, and he delivered. Green finished with five pressures while posting a 29.4% win rate on true pass sets, but one of the more interesting developments was the power he flashed throughout the game. On one rep, Green held a firm edge before using a rip move to work around the offensive tackle and make the tackle. On another, he struck the tackle with heavy hands, stood him up at the point of attack and worked off the block to make the play. Those reps were encouraging because Green’s game has largely been built around his quickness, hand usage and ability to win around the edge. Mike Green had 5 pressures, 3 qb hits and a 29.4 % win rate on true pass sets vs the Titans One interesting development has been his power usage, he’s trying to convert speed to power multiple times. He’s also a little more sawed off vs the run, synching into the ground. pic.twitter.com/3ErPw6k43W — Yuri (@Yuri_Ravens) October 5, 2026 As a pass rusher, Green continued to flash the cross chop that has become one of his most dependable moves. The timing of that move has gotten close to automatic, but he also showed some development within his pass-rush plan. On one rep, Green used a hesitation into a cross chop to open the offensive tackle’s hips before countering with an inside spin and generating pressure on the quarterback. On another, he converted speed to power, got inside the tackle’s chest and drove him backward into the quarterback’s lap. The encouraging part of Green’s performance was the variety. We already knew he could win with quickness and his cross chop, but adding legitimate power and counters gives tackles more to think about when trying to protect against him. As the season progresses, Green becoming a dependable pass-rush option will be important if the Ravens want to consistently generate pressure without Trey Hendrickson on the field. DT Nnamdi Madubuike 46 snaps | 16 run defense | 30 pass rush | 6 pressures Nnamdi Madubuike has started to pick things up over the last few weeks, and considering where he was physically a year ago, his return to form has been impressive. For a player who was facing the possibility of medical retirement, Madubuike looks as strong and explosive as he has at any point in his career. He finished the game with six pressures and recorded a 20% win rate on true pass sets. His ability to convert speed to power remains one of the most dangerous parts of his game. Madubuike has the athleticism to threaten offensive linemen off the snap before turning that momentum into power and collapsing the interior of the pocket. Nnamdi Madubuike lead the Ravens with 6 pressures vs the titans. He’s also had a 20% win rate on true pass sets and 2 QB hits The power and explosiveness are the best it has ever been, does not look like a guy who was about to medically retire. His upper body/ hand usage and… pic.twitter.com/LEzGWIye85 — Yuri (@Yuri_Ravens) October 5, 2026 That strength also showed up against the run. One of the more important aspects of Madubuike’s game has always been his ability to handle combination blocks, engage double teams and find ways to split offensive linemen. On one rep, he established inside leverage against the blocker before working his way into the backfield and helping force the running back into a minimal gain. Madubuike’s return has been great to see, but more importantly, his presence changes what Baltimore can do up front. Interior pressure forces quarterbacks off their spot and prevents them from simply stepping up when Baltimore’s edge rushers win around the corner. If Madubuike continues playing at this level, he will be a major piece of the Ravens developing a more consistent pass rush as the season progresses. C Vega Ioane 64 snaps | 30 run blocking | 34 pass blocking | 0 pressures allowed Vega Ioane made his first start at center this season, and there was a lot to like about what he showed. Ioane played all 64 offensive snaps and did not allow a pressure despite matching up with Jeffery Simmons multiple times throughout the game. One of Ioane’s biggest strengths is his ability to operate in close quarters. He does a good job preventing defensive linemen from getting clean access to his chest, while his punch timing and hand fighting allow him to maintain leverage and keep defenders at length. That showed up repeatedly against Simmons, where Ioane was able to absorb contact without surrendering significant ground in pass protection. His ability to quickly flip his hips also translates well to center. Ioane has the core strength to absorb power while maintaining his balance, and his movement skills allow him to redirect defenders once he establishes contact. Vega Ioane first career start at center 0 pressures allowed on 34 pass block snaps Smooth hips and initial punch, strong core and pass protection chops pic.twitter.com/hSaql2VVml — Yuri (@Yuri_Ravens) October 6, 2026 One rep in particular highlighted the combination of technique and athleticism that makes Ioane intriguing inside. Ioane used a snatch technique to throw the defensive lineman to the ground before immediately working downfield on a screen. It was a good example of his ability to win the initial engagement and then transition into his next assignment. The biggest takeaway from Ioane’s first start at center was stability. Baltimore’s interior offensive line has desperately needed reliable play, and allowing zero pressures over 34 pass-blocking snaps against a defensive front featuring Jeffery Simmons is an encouraging start. If Ioane can continue providing that level of pass protection while developing the finer details of playing center, the Ravens may have found an answer at a position that entered the season with plenty of uncertainty. title: AFC North Week 4 recap: Browns take the lead
summary: An unfamiliar face sits atop the competitive AFC North after four weeks of the season. Here are the latest updates from around the division: Cleveland Browns (3-1) The Cleveland Browns won their third consecutive game with a 27-24 victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers, taking the lead in the division in the process due to tiebreakers. […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - OCTOBER 1: Denzel Boston #12 of the Cleveland Browns reacts after completing a catch against the Pittsburgh Steelers during an NFL football game at Huntington Bank Field on October 1, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images An unfamiliar face sits atop the competitive AFC North after four weeks of the season. Here are the latest updates from around the division: Cleveland Browns (3-1) The Cleveland Browns won their third consecutive game with a 27-24 victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers, taking the lead in the division in the process due to tiebreakers. Deshaun Watson’s resurgence on the field continued into Week 4 as he led the Browns’ offense to set up a career-long 56-yard field goal from Andre Szmyt to take the lead with 10 seconds remaining in regulation. Watson finished the game 24 of 33 for 268 yards, a touchdown, and an interception while also losing a fumble. The story of the game for Cleveland’s offense, however, was the play of their two rookie wide receivers. Second-rounder Denzel Boston led the team with 89 yards on four catches while first-rounder KC Concepcion was second with 64 yards on five catches. Harold Fannin Jr. caught Watson’s lone touchdown. Quinshon Judkins led the team in rushing, but found little success with just 53 yards on 17 carries. The second-year back did find his way into the end zone once, though. The Browns’ defense made life difficult for Aaron Rodgers, sacking him five times while coming down with two interceptions against the future Hall-of-Fame quarterback. Denzel Ward snagged the first interception in the second quarter, while the second came from Grant Delpit on the final play of the game. Cleveland lost Mason Graham early in the game with what was later revealed to be a sprained MCL and ankle. The timeline for the 2025 fifth-overall pick is currently unknown. Baltimore Ravens (3-1) The Ravens improved to 3-1 with a 24-18 home win over the Tennessee Titans, but an ankle injury to Lamar Jackson overshadowed the victory. Jackson was stellar in the first half, completing 15 of 20 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns before an ankle injury on a sack sidelined him for the remainder of the game. The NFL world now awaits clarity on the status of Jackson’s injury and how much time, if any, he may miss. Tyler Huntley replaced Jackson for the second half as the offense came to a screeching halt. Zay Flowers was on his way to another dominant outing before Jackson exited the game, finishing the day with a team-high 118 receiving yards and a touchdown on eight catches. Mark Andrews caught Jackson’s other touchdown as he found the end zone for the first time this season. Derrick Henry struggled to find running room against his old team, racking up 73 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries for just 3.2 yards per carry. Alongside Jackson, Baltimore also lost Durham Smythe to a torn Achilles, Andrew Vorhees to a foot injury, and Marlon Humphrey to a calf injury during the game. The Ravens’ defense has been under heavy scrutiny to start the season, and that was not helped by an up-and-down performance against a weak Titans’ offense. The game started strong with a Trenton Simpson interception on the first drive, but many of the same issues popped up throughout the game, including an inability to finish sacks and missed tackles. Undrafted rookie Ethan Burke recorded the team’s lone sack on Cam Ward. Kyle Hamilton forced a fumble on rookie first-rounder Carnell Tate, which was recovered by Malaki Starks. Starks also recovered an onside kick to ice the game. Pittsburgh Steelers (2-2) The Steelers dropped to 2-2 with a 27-24 loss on the road to the Browns. Pittsburgh rallied from a 21-10 hole at halftime, falling three points short in the end. Rodgers completed 22 of 40 passes for 299 yards and three touchdowns with two interceptions, although the second came with just 10 seconds remaining in the game. DK Metcalf had by far his best game of the season with five catches for 115 yards. Roman Wilson, Darnell Washington, and Pat Freiermuth were the recipients of Rodgers’ three touchdowns. Jaylen Warren had another strong performance with 93 rushing yards on 17 carries to go with three catches for 33 yards. The Steelers’ defense forced two turnovers on the night, a fumble forced and recovered by T.J. Watt, and an interception by Robert Spears-Jennings. Watt and Payton Wilson had the team’s two sacks on Watson. Pittsburgh lost Derrick Harmon during the game to a foot injury and Jamel Dean to an ankle injury. Harmon has since been placed on injured reserve, meaning he will miss at least four games. Dean is not expected to join Harmon on injured reserve. Cincinnati Bengals (2-2) After starting the season 2-0, the Bengals have now dropped back-to-back games following a 22-17 home loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Joe Burrow had a tough outing while losing his top two wide receivers during the game. Burrow finished 39 of 54 for 428 yards, a touchdown, and two picks. Tee Higgins had a team-high 157 receiving yards on 11 catches before a groin injury knocked him out of the game in the fourth quarter. Ja’Marr Chase left the game much earlier with a concussion, leaving Burrow possibly without his top two weapons next week against the Miami Dolphins. Cincinnati had next to nothing in the run game, with Chase Brown leading the team with just 10 yards on nine carries. The Bengals finished the game with only 23 total rushing yards. Cincinnati’s defense sacked Trevor Lawrence four times, with Dexter Lawrence, Boye Mafe, Myles Murphy, and Kris Jenkins Jr. all getting a sack.

McMillan’s performance came at just the right time, allowing the Panthers to even up the win-loss record to 2-2 before entering the bye week.
