title: Panthers bye week injury update: The answer is on the (injured reserve) roster
summary: The Carolina Panthers are on a bye this week. Normally the having the earliest bye week in the season would be frustrating, but it actually kind of worked out in the Panthers’ favor this time. The team has gotten off to a decent start to their 2026 campaign, including an upset win over the Detroit […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - SEPTEMBER 20: A Carolina Panthers football helmet on the turf prior to the start of the NFL game between the Carolina Panthers and the Atlanta Falcons on September 20th, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Carolina Panthers are on a bye this week. Normally the having the earliest bye week in the season would be frustrating, but it actually kind of worked out in the Panthers’ favor this time. The team has gotten off to a decent start to their 2026 campaign, including an upset win over the Detroit Lions on Sunday Night Football. Amidst the excitement of a fun start to the season, there’s been some uneasiness about mounting injuries all over the roster. The bye week will help some players with nagging short term injuries, like Jalen Coker, Jaelan Phillips, and Monroe Freeling, get back to full health for the (long) stretch run of the season, and it will also provide some runway for possible long term absentees to make their returns. In his press conference with the media on Monday , Panthers head coach Dave Canales actually had some good injury news to report for what’s felt like the first time all year. He deemed the injuries that Freeling and Phillips suffered against the Lions to be minor, with both having a chance to be back for the Eagles game after the bye week. On top of that, three players that started the season on the PUP list have a chance to return to the roster. Trevor Etienne, Taylor Moton, and Tershawn Wharton all have imminent returns, and the Panthers already shuffled the roster around to create some open roster spots for them. Etienne looks good to go, and he’ll reprise role as the team’s go to kick returner. Moton and Wharton are awaiting medical clearance, but Canales seems to think they’re both ready and should receive those clearances sooner rather than later. Moton will be a welcome addition to an offensive line that’s struggled to give Bryce Young consistent time in the pocket, while Wharton will give the Panthers some more depth on the defensive interior. In a less positive but unsurprising bit of news, Canales said that Ikem Ekwonu is further away from making his return, though he is making good progress and there’s still hope that he’ll be ready before the end of the season. He’s progressed to jumping but still has a few more hurdles to clear before he’s ready for game action. As for the rest of the Panthers injuries, we don’t have a lot of concrete information, but here’s what we know. On the bright side, most of the players currently out seem likely to return at some point during the season. Jaycee Horn: Avoided needing surgery on his torn quad. We don’t know the full severity of the tear, but it seems that the goal is for Horn to be back for the last month or so of the season. Mike Jackson: Had to have surgery for his groin injury, but the team is hopeful he’ll be back sometime in November. Damien Lewis: Injured the UCL ligament in his elbow. He has not been placed on injured reserve, which means the team is hopeful that he’ll be back within the next couple of weeks. Xavier Legette: It’s hard to know what to make of his injury. He hurt his knee when it banged into the turf on his 55 yard catch against the Falcons. He didn’t get placed on injured reserve until last week, so whatever it is seems to be lingering longer than expected. That said, it’d be surprising if he still wasn’t ready to go after his minimum of four weeks on injured reserve. Jonathon Brooks: Underwent surgery for a core muscle injury with a roughly six week timetable for return. That was two weeks ago, so we should hear some update on his progress in about a month. The team has been cautious with Brooks given his injury history, so it’s possible they handle this injury the same way. Brady Christensen: Little news on his progress after he suffered a hamstring injury during the preseason. Without knowing the nature of his injury, there’s no way to predict when he’ll return, though he’ll be eligible to come off injured reserve next week. Bam Martin-Scott: Martin-Scott was the team’s other IR designated to return player (along with Christensen) during final roster cuts. Like Christensen, we haven’t heard anything about his progress since he was placed on injured reserve, but he’ll be eligible to come off injured reserve next week if he’s healthy.

title: Panthers vs. Lions game review: M-V-P, M-V-P
summary: When you get your first opportunity to host a Sunday Night Football game in over a decade, you want to make the most of it. If the chants ringing out through the stadium at various points of the broadcast were any indication, I’d say that mission was accomplished. Bryce Young may not have heard it, […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 4: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers reacts as he takes the field against the Detroit Lions prior to an NFL football game at Bank of America Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images When you get your first opportunity to host a Sunday Night Football game in over a decade, you want to make the most of it. If the chants ringing out through the stadium at various points of the broadcast were any indication, I’d say that mission was accomplished. Bryce Young may not have heard it, or was too humble to acknowledge it, but the millions of people watching the only game on TV did. For this week’s game review, let’s take a look at his performance and how it’s worthy of the chants. While Young has had games with 300+ passing yards, it’s the considerable jump in consistency that’s new and is adding some weight behind the MVP buzz. Not only that, but the ‘lows’ aren’t as low and he still puts up well over 200 yards instead of well under. The raw passing production also comes with several notable more advanced metrics that add more context to just how well Young performed. On 41 attempts, Young completed 8.5% more passes than expected, including the 3rd and 14 strike to Teteiroa McMillan that’s the 18th most improbable completion of the season so far, according to Next Gen Stats. Young still manages to generate an EPA of 0.47 even while pressured at a rate that’s (depending on which site you look on) more than any other quarterback in the NFL. Now, I do believe that there is some inflation to that statistic. While there is definitely no doubt that the offensive line has left much to be desired while being down several starters and losing Monroe Freeling during the game, some of those pressures are caused by the Panthers leaving defenders intentionally unblocked as the read defender in the Panthers run-pass-option concepts. A huge uptick in those plays caught the Detroit Lions off guard, and isolated their defenders in space and put them in conflict; do they take the bait and crash down on Young? On several occasions an unblocked player was credited with a pressure while Young threw the ball to an open receiver running through a passing lane that the defender just vacated. JT does an outstanding job diagramming the Panthers RPO that crushed the Lions multiple times @theqbschool (I'm going to assume Darrell Bevell brought this with him from the Dolphins) https://t.co/ecwVuuh5Sc pic.twitter.com/fpBxhl6UWL — Josh Norris (@JoshNorris) October 7, 2026 But it’s Young’s development and ability as a passer that allows the offense to operate this way. Few quarterbacks in the NFL can handle that much onus being put onto them; to handle an unblocked defender speeding at them and choosing between 3 different routes that his stature likely doesn’t even allow him to fully see. It’s not just adequate, in many aspects it’s elite. According to TruMedia, Young has a 72% precision pass rate in the middle of the field, the highest mark in the league. When you make an argument for Young as an MVP, or say his Week 4 performance is the quality you’d expect from an MVP candidate, it’s those aspects that should be considered. When things aren’t going as expected (see: injuries to Jalen Coker, Xavier Legette, Ikem Ekwonu, Taylor Moton, Damien Lewis, Monroe Freeling, Brady Christensen, Jonathon Brooks, Trevor Etienne and Chris Brazzell) what can he do to make it work? In other words…. how does Young still provide value? Right now, Young is putting himself in the line of fire and producing at a level that rivals the best quarterbacks in the NFL. Can it continue like this? If it does, don’t be surprised if those chants are heard throughout Charlotte in December.

summary: Though Case Keenum technically started at quarterback for the Bears in their Week 4 victory over the Jets, Tyson Bagent was the one who led them to 23-12 win on Sunday. The win brought Chicago up to a 3-1 record to begin the 2026 season, and it was a pretty decisive win which saw them […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 04: Tyson Bagent #17 of the Chicago Bears throws a pass against the New York Jets at Soldier Field on October 04, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Though Case Keenum technically started at quarterback for the Bears in their Week 4 victory over the Jets, Tyson Bagent was the one who led them to 23-12 win on Sunday. The win brought Chicago up to a 3-1 record to begin the 2026 season, and it was a pretty decisive win which saw them dominate the time of possession clock. It wasn’t the flashiest performance for the Bears on either side of the ball, but they did more than enough to get the job done and pick up the win. Going into their Week 5 matchup against the Packers, they have plenty to look back on and be proud about from last week’s tape. Each week, I’ll review how Chicago’s eligible performers graded by Pro Football Network’s Impact Scoring model. Here’s how Week 4 looked. Offense Tyson Bagent: 80.8 (7th of 32 QBs) Kyle Monangai: 84.6 (5th of 45 RBs) D’Andre Swift: 67.8 (40th of 44 RBs) Rome Odunze: 78.9 (15th of 65 WRs) Luther Burden III: 72.9 (39th of 65 WRs) Colston Loveland: 74.6 (14th of 32 TEs) Theo Benedet: 69.5 (75th of 91 OTs) Joe Thuney: 81.4 (14th of 48 OGs) Garrett Bradbury: 72.4 (20th of 28 Cs) Jonah Jackson: 78.3 (21st of 48 OGs) Darnell Wright: 80.6 (15th of 91 OTs) The usual suspects performed quite well along the Bears’ offensive line, as each of Joe Thuney, Jonah Jackson, and Darnell Wright graded as above-average starters at their respective positions. Rome Odunze was the Bears’ most efficient weapon through the air, as he placed No. 11 in the NFL with 0.95 EPA gained per play in Week 4. Kyle Monangai finished sixth in the league last week with 16 rushing yards over expected, along with his second-place ranking of 150 scrimmage yards. Through the air, Tyson Bagent had a +8.0 CPOE and led the league with a 61.1% success rate. Defense Montez Sweat: 56.9 (68th of 91 EDGEs) Jordan van den Berg: 59.9 (79th of 103 DTs) Grady Jarrett: 56.2 (93rd of 103 DTs) Neville Gallimore: 53.9 (103rd of 103 DTs) Austin Booker: 77.2 (23rd of 91 EDGEs) Dayo Odeyingbo: 77.5 (21st of 91 EDGEs) Devin Bush: 75.3 (35th of 70 LBs) T.J. Edwards: 73.1 (47th of 70 LBs) Malik Muhammad: 81.7 (13th of 87 CBs) Tyrique Stevenson: 62.5 (84th of 87 CBs) Dillon Thieneman: 77.5 (20th of 70 SAFs) Much of the Bears’ pass rush came off the edge, as they generated four pressures from edge rushers and only one pressure from a defensive tackle. Both Dayo Odeyingbo and Austin Booker got home for sacks against the Jets, continuing what’s been a surprisingly solid season from Chicago’s defensive end group. The Bears’ linebackers weren’t particularly productive in run support, but they each held their own in coverage, with Devin Bush allowing a 66.7 passer rating in coverage and T.J. Edwards allowing just a 73.1 average. Rookies Malik Muhammad and Dillon Thieneman both excelled, with each allowing only a 39.6 passer rating. That said, Tyrique Stevenson was picked on pretty often in coverage by New York, and that provided the Jets some success. Special teams (for the sickos) Cairo Santos: 77.3 (16th of 30 Ks) Cairo Santos hit all three of his field goal attempts on Sunday, but none of them were from further than 30 yards out, so he only finished the game with +0.1 field goals over expected. With an average grade, he isn’t punished for doing his job and making the easy kicks, but he isn’t necessarily rewarded for it, either. Conversely, the Bears didn’t punt at all in Week 4, so Tory Taylor doesn’t have a grade this week.

title: Chicago Bears Pass Protection Analysis on the Sack Allowed vs Jets
summary: The New York Jets pressured Tyson Bagent 13 times, according to Next Gen Stats, but the Chicago Bears allowed only one sack and two quarterback hits. While head coach Ben Johnson did dial up a few more longer developing plays than in the Week 3 game plan for Case Keenum, Bagent’s average air yards per […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 4: Tyson Bagent #17 of the Chicago Bears is sacked by Kingsley Jonathan #57 of the New York Jets during the second quarter at Soldier Field on October 4, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Jets pressured Tyson Bagent 13 times, according to Next Gen Stats, but the Chicago Bears allowed only one sack and two quarterback hits. While head coach Ben Johnson did dial up a few more longer developing plays than in the Week 3 game plan for Case Keenum, Bagent’s average air yards per attempt of 5.8 was even lower than Keenum’s against the Eagles (6.4). For those curious, Caleb Williams averaged 10.4 in Week 1. Head coach Ben Johnson said in an ESPN 1000 interview that Bagent’s performance featured, “Some good and some that I think he wants back, and so it was a little bit of a mixed bag.” He added, “The best part was how he controlled the operation. I thought we had good tempo in and out of the huddle. I thought our guys played with a lot of confidence because of how he conducted himself, and you know, he found completions. I thought he played an efficient football game. But you know, we put the ball in jeopardy too much, and fortunately we did have a couple negated due to penalties, and yet, the one (interception) that we had was still a significant turnover because we were giving them momentum, and you know, between the fact that we weren’t scoring in the red zone, the game was a lot closer than what it needed to be. So, we got to do a better job protecting that football.” The pass protection was there for Bagent most of the afternoon, and even with some pressure leaking through, I felt he could have avoided it with a subtle movement in the pocket instead of being so quick to check it down. He’s a good athlete, so I also wonder if Johnson will ask him to take off if the opportunity arises. “Then there’s a couple times where we had some other opportunities down the field that we’re going to challenge him to go ahead and pull the trigger on, when we have our pass catchers playing the way that they played yesterday. You got to keep them guessing this week.” Let’s get down to the nitty-gritty and one of the most uncharacteristic sacks allowed I’ve had to break down. Sack 7: 2nd Quarter – 1-10-CHI 33 (:59) (No Huddle, Shotgun) T.Bagent sacked at CHI 25 for -8 yards (D.Davis) The Bears were in hurry-up mode as the end of the half was nearing, and watching live, my immediate thought was that Bagent missed where the free blitzer was coming from after setting the protection. But then I saw the replay and realized he never had a chance. I assume right tackle Darnell Wright missed a check or misheard the play, because he wasn’t pass-blocking here. Wright realized his error before he was ineligibly downfield, but he was in no position to help, and no one was there to pick up linebacker Demario Davis. Running back D’Andre Swift looked to be heading to the edge for a check release into the flat, so he overshot Davis, who never should have been free anyway. Bagent also wasn’t aware of Davis because he assumed Wright had that gap locked down and Swift was moving right in case the Jets sent a third player. Could Bagent have felt the pressure? Perhaps, but he trusted the protection in front of him and knew that any free blitzer would have come from his left since Swift and tight end Cole Kmet were both on the right. This sack is on Wright. But he is playing at an All-Pro level. 🛡️ The highest-graded NFL offensive tackles entering Week 5, per PFN's OL Impact metric: 1. Darnell Wright, CHI – 97.1 2. Garett Bolles, DEN – 88.4 3. title: NFL Power Rankings: Quarter Pole Edition
summary: Well, you did it. I told you not to; I tried to warn you, but you did it anyway. You blinked. You blinked, and now 25% of the NFL season is already over. As we did last year, we are going to update our team and QB power rankings every 4 weeks (or thereabouts) throughout […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 04: Head coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers looks on from the sideline during the game against the Denver Broncos at Levi's Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, you did it. I told you not to; I tried to warn you, but you did it anyway. You blinked. You blinked, and now 25% of the NFL season is already over. As we did last year, we are going to update our team and QB power rankings every 4 weeks (or thereabouts) throughout the season. As we did last year, we will keep the previous rankings in parentheses next to the team name. These rankings are not based on record; they are based on how well the team is playing compared to the rest of the league. Here’s a look at the rankings 25% of the way into the season. 1. San Francisco 49ers (6) Made a statement in Week 1 in Australia against the Rams and haven’t slowed down since. If they stay healthy (enough), they should be playing in late January, probably February. 2. Seattle Seahawks (1) A trip up against the Commanders cost them their top spot in the rankings, but this is a formidable team and continues to show it. 3. Buffalo Bills (3) Josh Allen is on a mission. Can Buffalo get home-field advantage this year and slay the dragon that is Patrick Mahomes? 4. Baltimore Ravens (4) For the last 7 or 8 years, the Chiefs, Ravens, and Bills have dominated the AFC; it doesn’t look like we are getting a different outcome this year. 5. Kansas City Chiefs (10) I’m not sure if the Chiefs are all the way back, but they are most of the way back at a minimum. 6. Chicago Bears (9) If Dennis Allen can keep getting this out of this defensive unit, this team has a chance to reach the big dance in February. 7. LA Rams (2) The Rams should probably be higher on this list, but you make stupid travel plans and blow a game the way they did against the Denver Broncos, and you need to get punished. Had they managed to beat Denver, they’d probably be 3rd. 8. Jacksonville Jaguars (14) The Jaguars move up 6 spots, and if I’m being honest, you can make the argument they should be even higher on this list. They have it on both sides of the ball. 9. Dallas Cowboys (13) The Cowboys have some holes, but they are showing flashes of having this come together. We will see how much Joey Porter boosts this defense. 10. Minnesota Vikings (15) The Vikings defense is doing what it needs to under Brian Flores. The offense isn’t playing well enough to get a spot higher than this on the list despite being undefeated. 11. Denver Broncos (5) The Broncos have had a tough schedule so far this season. All 4 of their opponents are ranked in the top 8 of the power rankings. It might have been too harsh to drop them this far, but Bo Nix’s inconsistent play has me concerned for their future this season. 12. Cincinnati Bengals (16) A lot of people wanted to applaud the Bengals and their improved defense, and it does look better, but their two wins were against Tampa and Houston, and perhaps they weren’t as back as we thought they were. 13. Philadelphia Eagles (12) The Eagles look a lot like the 2025 version, which is a pretty good team that will shoot itself in the foot and probably make the playoffs but not have any January success. 14. Las Vegas Raiders (26) This Raiders team is good, and Klint Kubiak seems like the real deal. I don’t know if Kirk Cousins can keep the clock turned back for 17 games, but it’ll be fun to see how far they ride this wave. 15. New England Patriots (7) Drake Maye looked a little better on Sunday, but things have been off with this team this season. That was a monster win in Buffalo. Too early to say it saved their season, but it could swing the momentum in the right direction for them. 16. Carolina Panthers (23) Bryce Young is operating this offense quite well. He may never be an elite quarterback, but if he plays like this, he’s a QB you can win with. The defense has given up some points, but they’ve also made some big plays. This team is trending in the right direction. 17. Cleveland Browns (28) The Browns are sitting at 3-1 and are playing really well. Can Deshaun Watson continue to play well enough to get them victories? They may fade over the course of the season, but Todd Monken will have this team fighting for 60 minutes. 18. Detroit Lions (17) The Lions can still score points, but they just can’t stop other teams from scoring. Dan Campbell just looks like a man searching for answers, and I’m not sure he’s going to find any. 19. New York Giants (22) The Giants are a well-coached team, and that’s going to get them more wins than they’ve had in recent years. But their QB situation has already ended this season, whether they win a few games or they don’t. 20. Atlanta Falcons (29) I was ready to bury the Falcons after two games, but they look like a different team under Michael Penix. He’s not great, but he can operate an offense, and it’s been a world of difference. 21. Houston Texans (8) This is more of a respect spot. They have an extremely talented defense and a few talented pieces on offense as well. They shouldn’t be this bad, but there’s nothing they’ve put on tape at this point that says they aren’t this bad. There are no moral victories when you fall to 0-4. 22. Pittsburgh Steelers (19) This Steelers team is an aging group that always had a low ceiling. They look exactly like they were expected to look: a near .500 team that’s not going to be bad enough to get a great QB in the draft and not good enough to make an impact in the playoffs. It’s another Mike Tomlin year even if he isn’t there. 23. Green Bay Packers (18) This team might be 2-2, but they look absolutely awful. They won a game that Aaron Glenn handed to them on a platter and barely beat a UDFA rookie QB. Something is missing with this team. Can Micah Parsons elevate the team and make them contend again? That seems like their only hope. 24. Los Angeles Chargers (11) The Chargers should probably be even lower on this list, but again, we give them a little bit of a respect ranking as we did with the Texans. This team looks absolutely lost, and this is headed to a massive reset after this season if they don’t turn this thing around quickly. 25. Indianapolis Colts (24) The Colts’ two wins are against teams with a combined 1-7 record. Daniel Jones isn’t playing well, and the Colts have a lot invested in this team, and it doesn’t look like they are going to get much in terms of the results they are looking for. 26. New Orleans Saints (20) I really thought the Saints were going to show some life and potentially push for the NFC South division title. They still have a chance to do it, but they are going to have to figure out how to protect Tyler Shough to do it. 27. New York Jets (30) The Jets are definitely bad. They are largely bad because of their head coach. But the team is paying hard, seemingly because of their head coach. The Jets are going to play hard, but they aren’t going to win a lot of games. 28. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (21) The Bucs aren’t it. They are headed towards the basement of possibly the worst division in the league. Todd Bowles probably should have lost his job last year, and this is a team that doesn’t have an obvious path out of mediocrity. 29. Washington Commanders (25) Jayden Daniels can’t stay on the field, and this team simply doesn’t have enough talent or strong enough coaching to overcome that. The Commanders are going to face a lot of tough decisions this offseason. 30. Arizona Cardinals (31) The Cardinals are a bad team. We knew they were a bad team. They’ve played like a bad team. The Cardinals are a bad team. 31. Tennessee Titans (27) Cam Ward is frustrated. The Titans franchise has been a mess for years. This is a car stuck in the mud, and they don’t have any tools in the trunk to help them out. 32. Miami Dolphins (32) With the first pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, the Miami Dolphins select…

title: Chicago Bears Stock Watch: Monangai rising as Swift falls
summary: Sunday morning, I found myself getting nervous. As the Chicago Bears game approached, I found myself doubting the optimism and enthusiasm I saw online from fellow Bears fans. I’ve seen the Bears start backup quarterbacks so many times, I thought. And Tyson Bagent is far less experienced than Case Keenum. Surely, there was a chance […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 04: Kyle Monangai #25 of the Chicago Bears reacts after rushing for yards during the fourth quarter of the game against the New York Jets at Soldier Field on October 04, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Jessie Alcheh/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sunday morning, I found myself getting nervous. As the Chicago Bears game approached, I found myself doubting the optimism and enthusiasm I saw online from fellow Bears fans. I’ve seen the Bears start backup quarterbacks so many times, I thought. And Tyson Bagent is far less experienced than Case Keenum. Surely, there was a chance he would play badly enough for the Jets to hang around and possibly win. Then the game started. I have long been a “hope for the best, expect the worst” fan. Beaten down by years of high offseason expectations, only to be disappointed by the on-field result. It’s time I adjust my expectations. This is the Ben Johnson era. He is one of the best at scheming and game planning. He almost always has his team ready to play. The Bears have one of the best coaches in the league. And that means they’re going to be in way more games than they’re out of. Get used to it. Stock up Kyle Monangai, RB – 4.9 yards per rush, 146 rushing yards and two touchdowns. The seventh-round pick has endeared himself to many Bears fans. He is a driving force of Chicago’s rushing attack. Rome Odunze, WR – After a week of chatter about how disappointing he’s been, Rome came out with his best game of the young season. He caught six of seven targets for 94 yards. And they were at all levels — a long of 37 yards and even just short routes and quick screens. Hopefully, he builds on this. Colston Loveland, TE – Finally, the guy fans have been longing to see all summer got involved in the passing game. His blocking highlights were still there, as he helped pave the way for Chicago’s 232 yards on the ground. But he also caught six of his nine targets for 57 yards. Stock down D’Andre Swift, RB – We’ll see how long Swift remains in Johnson’s doghouse following his second lost fumble of the season. Swift didn’t return to the game after he lost a fumble in the third quarter. However, he’s too important to stay on the bench. I imagine the message was sent, but now it’s up to Swift to bounce back. Tyson Bagent, QB – He won; he was efficient (completed 73.5 percent of his passes), but it’s never good when your team wins by 11 and some amount of fans and pundits think you should be benched. Bagent doesn’t have the arm strength for some of the over-the-middle throws. But the coaches believe in him, and he’s going to get another start this weekend. I just don’t know if I feel as comfortable with that as I was maybe two months ago. Tory Taylor, P – He got no action this week. Poor guy. He must’ve been super bored. Who was up and down in your opinion? Let us know in the comments.

title: Bears-Jets Upon Further Review: A Closer Look at the Referees
summary: Hello Chicago Bears fans! This one is a fun one, as the Chicago Bears dominated the New York Jets and the laundry was one-sided in our favor. Tyson Bagent started for Caleb Williams and threw four interceptions – only one of which counted as a result of Jets penalties. Kyle Monangai ran for 146 and […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 04: Jowon Briggs #91 and Will McDonald IV #9 of the New York Jets tackle D'Andre Swift #4 of the Chicago Bears during the first quarter of the game at Soldier Field on October 04, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello Chicago Bears fans! This one is a fun one, as the Chicago Bears dominated the New York Jets and the laundry was one-sided in our favor. Tyson Bagent started for Caleb Williams and threw four interceptions – only one of which counted as a result of Jets penalties. Kyle Monangai ran for 146 and two scores, in the wake of two controversial goal-line reversals by the eye-in-the-sky that turned away two Swift touchdowns and gave the ball back to the Jets. Chicago held the ball for 42:45 on their way to a 3–1 record and a date with the Pack. New York had 157 yards, seven first downs, and one touchdown. Carl Cheffers’ crew accepted 16 flags: Chicago 4–29 , Jets 12–76 . However, that flag disparity hides some unseen calls if we only look at the yellow cloth on the field. The flags killed three Jets interceptions (two of which would not have been interceptions but for the flags), and “upon further review” two Bears touchdowns were deleted from the scoreboard. Same scale for judging flags: Correct, Arguable, Incorrect, Horrible. Impact weight is scaled 1–4: housekeeping, drive disruption, scoring or automatic first, wiped score or takeaway. First Quarter NYJ 0, CHI 0 Elijah Hicks (CHI), illegal block above the waist, 6 yards — 15:00. Opening kick. Zach Thomas returns to the 15; enforced back to the 6. Correct. Wt 1. Darrell Jackson Jr. (NYJ), face mask, 15 yards — 10:39. 2nd-and-8 at the NYJ 31. Monangai for 1. Jackson grabs the facemask. Ball to the NYJ 15. Chicago reaches the 1 and has a Swift touchdown reversed. Correct. Wt 3. Replay — Swift, runner broke the plane, reversed — 9:31. 2nd-and-3 at the NYJ 4. Swift right guard is ruled a touchdown on the field. Booth looks at it and brings it back: Swift to the NYJ 1 for 2 yards. This one is a pile at the goal line. You can sell the short of the plane. You can also sell that the ball got there. Clear and obvious is not met either way. Arguable. Wt 3. It is a taken-off score, but the down is not dead yet. Replay — Swift, runner broke the plane, reversed — 9:14. 4th-and-1 at the NYJ 1. Swift left guard is ruled a touchdown on the field. The replay official stops it. Reversed: no gain, short of the goal line. Turnover on downs. This is the one that fails the standard. The call on the field was a score. To take a touchdown off the board you need a frame that makes the ruling indisputable, not a better guess from upstairs. The available look is a body at the goal line with the ball at the hip. That is not clear and obvious. Incorrect. Wt 4. A touchdown that would have made it 7–0 becomes Jets ball at their own 1. New York (team), delay of game, 0 yards — 9:12. Goal-line stand just held. Enforced at the NYJ 1 before the first snap of the ensuing series. Process. Correct. Wt 1. Qwan’tez Stiggers (NYJ), illegal touch kick, 5 yards — 7:47. Wipes Austin McNamara’s 62-yard punt. Re-kick. Correct. Wt 2. Cole Kmet (CHI), false start, 5 yards — 6:42. 2nd-and-3 at midfield. Dead-ball. Correct. Wt 1. Theo Benedet (CHI), offensive holding, 10 yards — 4:58. 2nd-and-6 at the NYJ 29. Monangai’s 15-yard run comes back. Enforced at the 25: 2nd-and-12 at the NYJ 35. Arguable. Wt 2. Azareye’h Thomas (NYJ), illegal use of hands, 5 yards — 4:34. The snap of the game. 2nd-and-12. Bagent throws for Loveland. T’Vondre Sweat intercepts at the NYJ 36. Flag on Thomas. No play. Automatic first at the NYJ 30. Eight plays later Monangai scores from the 1. 0–7. Correct if the hands are on the receiver before the ball — and the crew treated it as a live foul that kills the pick. Wt 4. This is the flag that turned a Jets takeaway into the first points of the afternoon. NYJ 0, CHI 7 at 0:23. Second Quarter NYJ 0, CHI 7 New York (team), delay of game, 5 yards — 14:07. 3rd-and-10 at the NYJ 32 becomes 3rd-and-15. Geno Smith sacked by Austin Booker. Punt. Correct. Wt 2. Harrison Phillips (NYJ), defensive holding, 5 yards — 5:59. Automatic first. Arguable. Wt 2. Minkah Fitzpatrick’s interception of Bagent stands. Jets’ first pick in 21 games. They start at the CHI 34 and get a Sanders 36-yarder. 3–7. D’Angelo Ponds (NYJ), illegal contact, 5 yards — 0:43. 3rd-and-6. Second wiped interception on the Jets’ own postgame account. Automatic first. Arguable until All-22 says the contact is early and obvious. Wt 3. Santos from 30 as the half expires. 3–13. Third Quarter NYJ 3, CHI 13 New York (team), delay of game — declined — 10:12. 4th-and-12. New York (team), delay of game, 5 yards — 7:05. 4th-and-4. They still kick Sanders from 30. 6–13. Correct. Wt 1. Brandon Stephens (NYJ), face mask, 15 yards — 6:23. 2nd-and-4. Fifteen yards and a first. Correct if the hand is in the cage. Wt 3. Monangai’s 5-yard score at 2:26 makes it 6–20. title: Chicago Bears Midweek Musings: Dennis Allen, Magician
summary: Some random thoughts about the Chicago Bears and other things, mostly football-related as we count down the hours until we get to watch this team play football again: I had to chuckle just a bit at the Dennis Allen love this week – not that he doesn’t deserve it, just how some Bears fans and […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Offensive coordinator Press Taylor and defensive coordinator Dennis Allen of the Chicago Bears look on prior to the game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Some random thoughts about the Chicago Bears and other things, mostly football-related as we count down the hours until we get to watch this team play football again: I had to chuckle just a bit at the Dennis Allen love this week – not that he doesn’t deserve it, just how some Bears fans and analysts are presenting it. Many came into the year saying the Bears had a bottom three defense and they were wasting the season by not doing enough on that side of the ball. Because the defense has looked sharp the last three weeks, and it can’t be a misevaluation of the talent, it’s clearly that Dennis Allen is a magician. Many of those same fans and analysts were openly questioning whether or not Allen would last in Chicago at times last year. So it goes. For my part, I was a big fan of Dennis Allen hire, and I’m a sucker for a “second year in the system” bump. I’ve also talked about the potential for the Bears defense to continue their thieving ways in 2026 with more positive game scripts. So far, so good. I get that the lack of investment made many nervous, but it’s always a good idea to let actual football be played before making a final determination. Still a long way to go, but early returns are positive. I do like the magician talk because Allen is truly good at what he does. Someone good at Photoshop, get me Dennis Allen in a magician outfit, stat. Cue Final Countdown, please. At my local gym, 95+% of people are wearing earbuds or headphones, but there’s usually loud music playing. Then the new trainer brings out a boom box turned up to 11 for his small group sessions. Plus, the one guy talking on his phone trying to shout over all the background noise. I think I need to invest in another pair of noise-canceling headphones. I’m going to hold out hope that Jaylon Johnson rounds into form and recaptures some of his old magic before hitting the panic button, but the clock is running out on Tyrique Stevenson. When Kyler Gordon returns and ramps up to a full-time role (I know, I know), Malik Muhammad is going to take over the boundary corner snaps and Tyrique will be relegated to a part-time role. All the talent in the world but can’t put it together. That dropped pick, which looked like it had a chance to be a pick-six if he drove on the ball, seemed emblematic of his season. I saw Band of Brothers released a 25th anniversary documentary. The only question is do I watch the documentary before or after my 12th rewatch of the series? We’re probably not giving enough love to Jonah Jackson. Every time we say something good about him it’s usually after talking about Darnell Wright or Joe Thuney. He deserves his own vase of flowers because he’s killing it. Kudos to Ben Johnson for knowing how to best use Jackson where his previous play caller couldn’t figure it out… My best friend drove two hours to watch the game with me last weekend. We set up a TV in the garage, grilled out on a beautiful October day, and watched our favorite team dogwalk the poor Jets. The highlight might have been his plea for some Roschon Johnson, which was immediately answered with an explosive run. Loudest cheer of the day… I thought Tyson Bagent played an excellent game. He threw an interception, yes, and he got bailed out on another by penalty, but overall he played on time and threw catchable passes. (Yes, I know there were four total, but one was clearly a free play and the other was aided by the hold that was called as Bagent was throwing it. The screen pass into the mountain defensive tackle is the one he was bailed out on.) With the offensive infrastructure, he’s good enough to beat bad teams and keep the Bears competitive against mediocre ones. I’m not sure he can beat good teams. We’ll find out where the Packers sit in that spectrum on Sunday. I’m starting to hear rumors about Khalil Mack drawing trade interest from teams and you’d have to believe the Bears would be interested in adding him back. For Mack’s sake, you wonder if he’d be most interested in continuing his Hall of Fame career by circling back to Chicago and helping in a playoff run. He could use some post season success on his resume and might just be the perfect way to gild his fabulous career. Plus, it would give me an excuse to break out the Mack throwback jersey I bought years ago… Is Kyle Monangai the most fun Bears running back to watch since Walter Payton? I’m not saying best, I’m saying the most fun. Tarik Cohen was a lot of fun but not necessarily as a running back. Forte was smooth, Thomas Jones will always hold a special place in my heart, but neither brought me the pure joy I get from watching Monangai. He’s the perfect Bears running back. You got any musings? Hit the comments and let me know what’s up.

title: Bengals Film Room: New defensive line additions doing their part
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals dropped to 2-2 after a frustrating loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. While players like Jordan Battle continue to struggle on defense, the new additions to that defensive line played really well once again. The trio of Boye Mafe, Dexter Lawrence, and Jonathan Allen combined for 12 pressures during the game on Sunday. […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals dropped to 2-2 after a frustrating loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. While players like Jordan Battle continue to struggle on defense, the new additions to that defensive line played really well once again. The trio of Boye Mafe, Dexter Lawrence, and Jonathan Allen combined for 12 pressures during the game on Sunday. Mafe and Lawrence each recorded a sack during the game. Jonathan Allen led the defense in pressures, recording five on Sunday. He was also the highest-graded player on the defense that game with an 80.7 overall grade. He finished with an 82.7 pass rush grade. While he was the only one of the trio of guys to not record a sack this week, he was an impact player all game long, rushing the passer. His pressure was part of the reason his teammates were able to come away with sacks during the game as well. He had notable pressure when Mafe and Murphy both had their sacks on Sunday. The three new defensive line additions have certainly been doing their part early in the season. pic.twitter.com/m4xSyVSAX2 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Myles Murphy running right through talented young left tackle Anton Harrison for the sack. pic.twitter.com/NYpeoUOHPg — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 It wasn’t just his pass-rushing ability that impressed this week either; it was what he was able to do against the run. While he finished with just three tackles, his presence was felt along that defensive line. He and Dexter Lawrence have quickly established a chemistry playing beside one another. Barrett Carter quickly closing off the running lane with Jonathan Allen getting there to finish off the tackle. pic.twitter.com/PEiA20T9Un — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Jonathan Allen with the tackle for loss pic.twitter.com/DJKMiXyKcO — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Speaking of Dexter Lawrence, he was his usual dominant self again this week. Lawrence finished the game with three pressures, three tackles, and a sack during the game. It isn’t just the numbers on the stat sheet either, as Dexter is constantly freeing up the linebackers to make plays against the run. He also does a dang good job of making plays against the run himself. Knight and Carter in on another run stop, this time with some help from Dexter Lawrence. That was the best game the young linebackers have both played at the same time this season. pic.twitter.com/4zUb0LhGNh — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Dexter Lawrence, Myles Murphy, Boye Mafe, and the linebackers getting the stop on 3rd down. pic.twitter.com/DvuESVuemU — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Dexter Lawrence, Demetrius Knight, and others in on the gang tackle of Tuten late in the game. pic.twitter.com/1yLasVfi39 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Dexter is such a handful for teams to deal with. Oftentimes they will have a handful of jersey when trying to block him. His power just tossed Robert Hainsey out of the club on one play, with Hainsey having no choice but to get an obvious holding penalty to protect his quarterback. That play ended up helping lead to the Jaguars only coming away with a field goal, after initially having 1st and 10 inside of the five-yard line. 1st and goal around the 2 yard line for Jacksonville and the dominance of Dexter Lawrence draws a holding call to push them back. pic.twitter.com/9e3oMtf8ci — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Not only is Dexter Lawrence a sheer force of nature with his power, but he also is giving a ton of effort out there for a guy that is 350 pounds. Lawrence was able to get his sack by chasing down Trevor Lawrence from behind. That type of effort goes a long ways in setting the tone for your teammates on that defensive line. Boye Mafe with the pressure on Trevor Lawrence, and Dexter Lawrence with the hustle to chase him down. pic.twitter.com/6MnZFs2GfX — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Boye Mafe was highly impressive rushing the passer again this week for Cincinnati. He finished the game with four pressures and a sack. He started the game off with a bang by getting to Trevor Lawrence and knocking the ball up in the air. Myles Murphy was close to intercepting the ball. Mafe with the pressure, and look how close Murphy was to picking that ball off. Also, good lawd Jonathan Allen. pic.twitter.com/swH6eobpzX — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Mafe had another pressure during the game that led directly to a Kris Jenkins Jr. sack. Mafe beat talented left tackle Anton Harrison around the edge and was almost able to come up with a strip sack on the play. Boye Mafe with the pressure, and the sack is finished off by Kris Jenkins Jr. pic.twitter.com/E7jA1ceHdS — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Mafe was buzzing around during the final possession for the defense when they absolutely had to have a stop. He set the tone for getting one by combining with Jordan Battle for a tackle behind the line of scrimmage to start the possession. Mafe and Battle combining for the tackle for loss pic.twitter.com/TdvsoqzNhT — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 On a day with a frustrating loss, it is still very apparent just how much this defensive line has improved. If they can fix some of the issues in the secondary during the season, this defense should have a chance to finish the year in a much better place than they did last season. If they do, it will be because of guys like Lawrence, Mafe, and Allen getting the job done all season long up front.

title: Zac Taylor rising up NFL Hot Seat Rankings
summary: After a thrilling 2-0 start, the Cincinnati Bengals have dropped back-to-back games against the Steelers and Jaguars and are now 2-2 going into Week 5. The Bengals also lost Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins during the loss to Jacksonville and will be working through those injuries going into the next game. After two straight losses, […]
full_text: After a thrilling 2-0 start, the Cincinnati Bengals have dropped back-to-back games against the Steelers and Jaguars and are now 2-2 going into Week 5. The Bengals also lost Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins during the loss to Jacksonville and will be working through those injuries going into the next game. After two straight losses, head coach Zac Taylor is facing heat again, and Sports Illustrated has him back on the hot seat. Connor Orr now has Taylor ranked No. 5 in his latest NFL hot seat rankings. Taylor is still riding off the fumes of a surprise Super Bowl berth in 2021, which was followed by a conference title game appearance in 2022. Since that season, the Bengals have yet to make the playoffs. Last year, we ran up against a bizarre situation in which it was revealed that the Bengals quietly extended Taylor, though the team and the coach declined to address it. This is fair criticism considering the Bengals have no business being 2-2 with this roster, and the in-game management, game planning, and offensive playcalling are still frustrating to watch. Yes, the season is still incredibly early, but similar issues from the past few seasons are coming to the surface again, and winning is the biggest cure when that happens. One of the biggest issues right now is that Taylor’s offense is still incapable of establishing the run with a healthy Joe Burrow, and that created so many problems for this unit against Jacksonville. Burrow reassured everyone in his press conference that no one is panicking and the season is still incredibly early, but with these injuries stacking up and issues coming back around, it is fair for everyone to have concerns.

title: Bengals Film Room: Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight play well vs. Jaguars
summary: I thought the Cincinnati Bengals defense played well enough to win the game on Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars. A couple of untimely turnovers by the offense did not help their cause. Ultimately, the Bengals were unable to pull out the victory. They lost 22-17 to the Jaguars and fell to 2-2 on the season. […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals linebacker Barrett Carter (49) celebrates a stop after tackling Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten (33) in the first quarter of the NFL Week 4 game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Jacksonville Jaguars at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati on Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co I thought the Cincinnati Bengals defense played well enough to win the game on Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars. A couple of untimely turnovers by the offense did not help their cause. Ultimately, the Bengals were unable to pull out the victory. They lost 22-17 to the Jaguars and fell to 2-2 on the season. There are still things to be fixed on the defense. Most notably, they are battling a tackling issue with one of their starting safeties. Overall though, this was a much better performance from the defense than we saw the week before in Pittsburgh. Specifically, I thought Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight Jr. had the best game combined of the season for the linebackers against Jacksonville. Demetrius Knight Jr. finished the game with 6 tackles and played much more aggressively at times than we have seen in some previous weeks. When he is aggressively attacking downhill, it is typically when he is playing at his best. We saw him shoot a gap early in the game, ending up with a tackle for loss against Bhayshul Tuten as a result. Explosive tackle for loss from Demetrius Knight Jr. pic.twitter.com/GFjFXhtpSg — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Knight and Carter combining for another run stop pic.twitter.com/zeI1paSyDg — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Knight and Carter in on another run stop, this time with some help from Dexter Lawrence. That was the best game the young linebackers have both played at the same time this season. pic.twitter.com/4zUb0LhGNh — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Things were not perfect for Knight on the day, as there were still a couple of questionable angles taken during the game. In particular, the touchdown run in the second half was a play that Knight looked out of position coming up near the line of scrimmage. He wasn’t the only one to question on that play, but it was probably his most notable negative play. A lot of guys you can call out on this touchdown run. Knight and Mafe near the line of scrimmage being out of position and then Ivey missing a tackle with Jules getting blocked and Battle taking a poor angle toward the ball carrier. pic.twitter.com/2OWD1psm7o — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 As solid as Knight was during the game overall, I think Barrett Carter might have been even more impressive. Carter finished the game with a team-high 11 tackles, a tackle for loss, and a pass defensed against Parker Washington. Carter was in a really good position on the talented slot receiver for the Jaguars. He did a good job of not turning him at all on the play, which would have certainly drawn a flag from Sunday’s flag-happy crew. Good pass defensed by Barrett Carter. We know what Ron Torbert would have done if this was with the Super Bowl on the line. pic.twitter.com/LHo3PsNekz — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Carter looked very instinctive during the game on Sunday. He was decisive, quick to react against the run, and wasn’t credited with a single missed tackle during the game. Barrett Carter quickly closing off the running lane with Jonathan Allen getting there to finish off the tackle. pic.twitter.com/PEiA20T9Un — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 5, 2026 Any game where your linebackers do not record a single missed tackle combined seems like a win to me. The biggest question will be consistency going forward. We need these guys to start doing this week-in and week-out for this defense. If there is a glaring weakness on this defense, it isn’t the linebacker play right now. It is the play of Jordan Battle. The Bengals will have to get healthy to consider replacing Battle in the starting lineup. I don’t think that should be in question for these linebackers. We just need more performances from them like we saw on Sunday against Jacksonville.

title: Bengals News: Chad Johnson believes in the backup wide receivers
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are heading into Week 5 riding a two-game losing streak, and both Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) are nursing injuries. The Bengals are facing the Dolphins in Miami on Sunday in a game they need to win to go into the bye week on a high note. It’s currently unclear […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are heading into Week 5 riding a two-game losing streak, and both Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) are nursing injuries. The Bengals are facing the Dolphins in Miami on Sunday in a game they need to win to go into the bye week on a high note. It’s currently unclear as to whether or not Chase and Higgins, the best wide receiver duo in the NFL, will be able to play in Miami. If they don’t, it’ll be Mitchell Tinsley, who was signed off the Texans’ practice squad and rejoined the team last week, and rookie Dohnte Meyers (it’s also possible Colbie Young could play as well) catching passes from Joe Burrow at wide receiver while Mike Gesicki fills in the gaps. One guy who has confidence in the Bengals’ backup receivers is Cincinnati great Chad Johnson, who told Geoff Hobson he’s excited to see the game from his home city of Miami. “And for them, that’s a good thing because if (Ja’Marr) Chase and Tee (Higgins) can’t go., I have the utmost confidence in Tinsley and Myers being able to make plays,” he said, per Hobson . “It’s all up to Zac Taylor understanding their skill sets and what their strengths are, and putting them in positions to be able to make those plays. Even if Tee and Chase can’t go, I mean it’d be a blow, but I still won’t feel that bad understanding how good Tinsley and Meyers are.” Here’s what else is going on: Though there is a small sample size, the Bengals have never lost when wearing orange jerseys, white pants with orange stripes and orange socks. That’s what they’re wearing on Sunday in Miami when they look to bounce back against the Dolphins. They’re 2-0 in that combination, and they’re 28-11-1 in orange jerseys since they were unveiled for the first time in 2004. Bengals’ offensive approach could change. What might be tweaked after 2 straight losses “A very honest and brutal Monday. Which we deserved,” Karras said. “We need to get ourselves back. Wake up. It doesn’t feel like it was a crazy game because we had a chance to win, but I have a pit in my stomach similar to Minnesota last year as an offensive line. That was not very good.” While it isn’t confirmed, it’s possible Colbie Young could suit up on Sunday in Miami. Zac Taylor didn’t rule him out. With Andrei Iosivas on IR, Ja’Marr Chase in concussion protocol and Tee Higgins dealing with an adductor injury that could keep him on the sidelines for an unknown period of time, Young being able to suit up on Sunday could help make sure the Bengals don’t extend their losing streak to three. full_text: As the Cleveland Browns were busy losing a ton of games the last two years, their defense was playing at an elite level led by DC Jim Schwartz and DE Myles Garrett . When the Browns decided to hire Todd Monken as their next head coach , instead of Schwartz, and the veteran coordinator decided to walk away instead of coaching the team, eyes were raised about a possible defensive turndown. Then Garrett was traded to the Los Angeles Rams and everyone expected Cleveland’s defense to get worse by a lot. After a Week 1 destruction, fans were calling for Schwartz to return . Instead of falling apart, the Browns defense came together with a lot of pass rush pressure and a team effort to three straight victories, leading to the top spot in the AFC North . In a video podcast about preseason expectations that were completely off, Cleveland’s defense received a lot of praise: The Browns defense is far from perfect, but they are far less predictable with DC Mike Rutenberg than they were with Schwartz and seem to be playing a more unified approach without the “easy button” of Garrett. With teams no longer double teaming one guy, running away from Garrett, and scheming against one player, different Cleveland defenders have been able to make an impact. After Week 1, where Rutenberg failed to play to his defensive backs’ strength in man coverage, not only did the Browns play in 73% man versus the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 4, but Cleveland is lapping other teams in the coverage style for the season: Highest % of defensive man coverage this season Browns 61.0% Bears 49.4% Chiefs 46.6% Patriots 46.0% Giants 45.2% pic.twitter.com/2EiJoUoYz2 — PFF (@PFF) October 6, 2026 Even the best units usually run zone coverage more than 50% of the time, for a variety of reasons. Man coverage is physically hard for players to run consistently, receivers know their routes and have the ability to separate often, and consistent man coverage can get beat with specific route combinations and often leads to quarterback scrambles being wide open. None of that has been a major problem for Cleveland because the defensive backfield is very talented, and the pass rush pressure, starting with Jared Verse and Mason Graham , along with blitzers, has sped up the clock on quarterbacks. Speedy linebackers Carson Schwesinger and Quincy Williams have helped contain the quarterback as well. No Schwartz and no Garrett led to strong convictions that the Browns defense would fall off in 2026. Instead, Rutenberg and the talented players have played at an elite level since Week 1, with more challenges to come.

title: Trade whispers: 2 pass rushers might be available if the Browns are interested
summary: After the Cleveland Browns traded off EDGE rusher Myles Garrett in the offseason, the fanbase was given a dialogue that his replacement, Jared Verse, could fill in nicely. After all, he had two Pro Bowls in each of his years in the league, plus won the “NFL Rookie Defensive Player of the Year” award after […]
full_text: After the Cleveland Browns traded off EDGE rusher Myles Garrett in the offseason , the fanbase was given a dialogue that his replacement, Jared Verse, could fill in nicely . After all, he had two Pro Bowls in each of his years in the league, plus won the “NFL Rookie Defensive Player of the Year” award after a very good rookie season. The narrative was that Alex Wright and Isaiah McGuire would hold down the fort on the right side while Verse would wreak havoc on the left. RELATED: MACK’S CONTRACT, SALARY CAP HIT Yet, none of that is happening. The pass rush so far has been very anemic, to say the least, though sacks are not everything . Currently, the Browns rank #23 in overall defense. How can they improve their pass rush? There are two pass rushers who are rumored to become available before the NFL trade deadline on November 11: Josh Sweat of the Arizona Cardinals and Khalil Mack of the Los Angeles Chargers . Should Cleveland GM Andrew Berry attempt to bring in a proven pass rusher this season? Sweat (6’-5”, 265 pounds) was drafted in the fourth round of the 2018 NFL Draft by the Philadelphia Eagles. When the Eagles’ DC, Jonathan Gannon, became the head coach of the Cardinals, his contract extension expired, and Gannon had his team go after Sweat. The talented defensive end then inked a four-year deal worth up to $76.4 million with $41 million guaranteed. Sweat, age 29, came through last year with 12 sacks. He also had 17 QB hits, 30 total tackles, 13 tackles for loss, I fumble recovery, 2 pass defenses, 4 forced fumbles, 7 knockdowns, 9 hurries, 28 pressures, and zero missed tackles. He played alongside DT Calais Campbell, who was an excellent pass rusher as well, and had 6.5 sacks, 16 QB hits, and 18 pressures, to go along with other stats. The inside/outside pass duo of Sweat and Campbell worked extremely well for Arizona. After losing a franchise-record 14 games, the Cardinals fired Gannon. The two men were close. Sweat was placed on the PUP list early due to a knee injury that was never disclosed. He did not practice at all during training camp or play in any of the preseason games. His first action since the final game of the 2025 season was the Week 1 contest against the Chargers. So far this year, he is a shell of himself. Sweat rarely generates any actual pass rush, although he is going after it every play he is inserted. In 2026, he has just one sack. And that occurred in the last game when the defensive tackle forced the quarterback out of the pocket and into the arms of Sweat. In four games, Sweat has 7 total tackles, 2 tackles for loss, 2 QB hits, 5 pressures, 1 knockdown, 3 hurries, and zero missed tackles. He is being paid $9.78 million this year with a cap hit of $16.4 million. Mack (6’-3”, 269 pounds) is on his third team with the Chargers. Everywhere he has played, the fanbase acts like they just signed Lawrence Taylor. He was selected with the fifth overall pick in the 2014 NFL Draft by the Oakland Raiders, and by his second year in the league, he was destroying every offense he faced. In Mack’s final three seasons with the Raiders, he had sack totals of 15, 11, and 10.5, QB hits of 24, 26, and 22, plus double-digit pressures each year. The Raiders then traded Mack, now age 35, to the Chicago Bears in 2018 for two first-round picks, a third, and a sixth. In return, Chicago also received a second-round pick, plus a conditional fifth-round pick. He responded with getting 12.5 sacks in 2018 and 36 during his four years in Chicago. The Bears then traded Mack to the Chargers in 2022 after a foot injury concluded his final year with the Bears. Chicago received a second-round draft pick while Los Angeles received the player plus a sixth-round selection. In his first game with LA, Mack had three sacks plus a forced fumble. He had a career high in sacks in 2023 with 17 sacks. So far this season, he had three sacks, 14 total tackles, 5 QB hits, and 8 pressures, among other stats. For his 13-year career, Mack has played in 183 games and started 181, 676 total tackles, 153 tackles for loss, 116 sacks, 13 fumble recoveries, 36 forced fumbles, 43 batted passes, 201 QB hits, 49 knockdowns, 110 hurries, 239 pressures, and 41 missed tackles. Mack is currently on a one-year $18 million fully guaranteed contract extension. For the Browns, after four games, the pass rush isn’t what it should be. There may be other pass-rushing defensive ends that could be pried from a team’s roster, but these two are rumored to be on the trading block before the NFL trade deadline. 2026 Browns Defensive End Stats: Sacks Isaiah McGuire – 2 Jared Verse – 0 Sam Williams – 1 Derek Barnett – 0 QB hits Isaiah McGuire – 2 Jared Verse – 2 Sam Williams – 2 Derek Barnett – 2 Knockdowns Isaiah McGuire – 0 Jared Verse – 2 Sam Williams – 1 Derek Barnett – 2 Hurries Isaiah McGuire – 2 Jared Verse – 0 Sam Williams – 0 Derek Barnett – 1 Pressures Isaiah McGuire – 4 Jared Verse – 2 Sam Williams – 2 Derek Barnett – 3 Should the Browns trade for either veteran pass rusher? full_text: Cleveland Browns fans have been waiting for several seasons for the team to reach a point where it seems like it could be a true contender in the division. While it’s still early, the Browns currently sit atop the AFC North alongside the Baltimore Ravens. There is still a lot to prove in the coming weeks , but this team certainly deserves to be part of the conversation. They have one division win thus far, coming against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday Night Football. With upcoming division matchups against the Baltimore Ravens, who could be without QB Lamar Jackson , and the Steelers for the second time, these games will really start to set the scene for what Cleveland can accomplish in the division. Baltimore will likely be their biggest competition, as the Ravens are also 3-1 and have a history of being the best team in the division. The Browns’ much easier schedule gives them a leg up , but they will have to continue to execute. Deshaun Watson does not have to be perfect, but the offense will need to continue giving the team a chance to stay in these games. title: Scouting Browns Week 5 opponent: These aren’t the same old New York Jets
summary: As the Cleveland Browns prepare to try to extend their winning streak, the schedule brings them an AFC East opponent in the New York Jets. These two teams played last season, with New York coming out with the victory. Similar to the Browns, the Jets are undergoing a rebuild of their own. Veteran quarterback Geno […]
full_text: As the Cleveland Browns prepare to try to extend their winning streak , the schedule brings them an AFC East opponent in the New York Jets . These two teams played last season, with New York coming out with the victory. Similar to the Browns, the Jets are undergoing a rebuild of their own. Veteran quarterback Geno Smith is back at the place he started his career. Offensively, the unit has young talent led by wide receiver Garrett Wilson and running back Breece Hall, who could miss Week 5 with an injury. Defensively, the unit has some form of veteran presence after lacking in that department previously. Cleveland is a road underdog heading into Week 5 preparations. Scouting New York ahead of this week’s matchup looks like this Like the Browns, the Jets received a facelift on offense On paper, the Jets offense is much improved from a year ago. For starters, having a veteran quarterback like Smith helps. This unit lacked competent quarterback play, but seems to have it now with Smith, who was in a rough situation last season with the Las Vegas Raiders. Offensively, the unit has a competent offensive line and good receiving talent. Wilson is a top 20 receiver, Hall is underrated, and rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq gives New York some versatility in their tight end room. Offensive coordinator Frank Reich isn’t necessarily the best, but he has somehow kept this offense playing at a competent level. HC Aaron Glenn could be coaching for his job It’s hard to say that this is the same Jets team from last year. Head coach Aaron Glenn has gone through the ups and downs, but it’s fair to question whether this will be his last season in Gang Green. On paper, New York is better than last year. However, the team should be 2-2 instead of 1-3. The loss to the Green Bay Packers was more about how the Jets gave the game away instead of the Packers outright winning it. This past Sunday, New York came out flat and were outmatched against a Chicago Bears squad missing superstar quarterback Caleb Williams. People questioned why the Jets chose to bring back Glenn after last season considering how it went, but if New York doesn’t show any improvement as the season goes on, the team will likely make a change with Glenn, perhaps sooner rather than later. The Jets defense is improved (?) Last season, the New York Jets were pretty abysmal on the defensive side of the ball. Before Week 4, the Jets defense had the longest streak without an interception until it was broken by safety Minkah Fitzpatrick on Sunday against the Bears. This season, the unit has veterans on that side of the ball in linebacker Demario Davis and Fitzpatrick, someone Browns fans have high on their dislike list. The secondary has talented pieces in cornerback Azareye’h Thomas and rookie D’Angelo Ponds, however as a collective, the secondary has issues. In terms of their pass rush, it’s lacking. Despite attempting to improve the area in the offseason, the unit is 29th in terms of pressure rate, and rookie David Bailey hasn’t shown the abilities that made the Jets draft him second overall. On paper, the unit appears to be improved, but their on-field performance tells a different story. Whether the defense turns it around is something that is worth monitoring. Overall, the Jets have talent to make things tough on the Browns in Week 5, especially with more veterans on the roster. How concerned are you about the Jets in Week 5 versus the Browns? summary: All-Pro guard Tyler Smith could make his 2026 debut on Thursday against the Tampa Buccaneers, which will give the Cowboys’ offensive line a major boost. Dallas could still use some upgrades to their roster, and team owner Jerry Jones says he’s still open for business. Left tackle Tyler Guyton had a lot to prove coming […]
full_text: Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images | Getty Images All-Pro guard Tyler Smith could make his 2026 debut on Thursday against the Tampa Buccaneers, which will give the Cowboys’ offensive line a major boost. Dallas could still use some upgrades to their roster, and team owner Jerry Jones says he’s still open for business. Left tackle Tyler Guyton had a lot to prove coming into his third season, and he’s showing why he was a first-round pick. Here’s the latest news for the Cowboys. Jerry Jones on Tyler Smith’s status, CB room, another potential trade and more – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com Cowboys’ owner Jerry Jones made an appearance on 105.3 The Fan to discuss many things, including Tyler Smith. “How he feels about that hand,” Jones said of what Smith would need to determine. “Now that’s a big deal, that hand. And we all understand it in an offensive lineman boy, he’s got a punch, and I mean that thumb or that hand has to really be ready to take a beating out there because without it, you can’t do much.” “But it’s up to him. He’ll have a feel for it. He’ll have a feel as the game is going. He’ll see if he’s reluctant in any way because of the mental aspects of it, but he’s ready to play. He can play, and I mean play at that level that we’re used to see him right now. We’ll just let him feel it out and see if he wants to go.” Tyler Guyton’s growth as Cowboys’ LT is prominently displayed in viral moment vs. Texans – Calvin Watkins, Dallas Morning News Tyler Guyton has turned the corner in his development at left tackle. One play in particular proved that last week against the Texans. It’s one of those plays that symbolizes what Guyton has become in the first month of the season: terrific. Tyler Guyton. I believe coaches refer to this as “finishing your block.” pic.twitter.com/jk7daV3NV6 — Babe Laufenberg (@BabeLaufenberg) October 6, 2026 And to think, Guyton’s job status was a question in training camp . Now, with the Cowboys about to face the Buccaneers on Thursday night , there are no worries about the left tackle position. ‘That’s what he does’ – Dallas Cowboys know exactly what weaknesses to exploit on the Bucs defense come Thursday night – Mauricio Rodriguez, AtoZ Sports The Buccaneers will undoubtedly bring a lot of pressure against the Cowboys’ offense. However, that fits right into Dak Prescott’s hands. Not only is Dak Prescott known as one the most dangerous quarterbacks against the blitz, but the Bucs defense isn’t getting its money’s worth for sending 5+ defenders. Despite their high blitz rate, they’re dead last in the league in pressure rate. And Bowles knows how it goes when you blitz Prescott, too. He’s seen it firsthand. In the 2022-2023 playoffs, the Bucs blitzed the Cowboys in 35% of his dropbacks. The result? Dak completed nine of 12 pass attempts for 109 yards and one touchdown. Dallas Cowboys list two players questionable, three out for Thursday night game – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram Dallas releases latest injury news ahead of NFC battle with Tampa Bay. Cornerback Cobie Durant, linebacker DeMarvion Overshown and offensive tackle Drew Shelton will not be available as they all recover from hamstring injuries. Durant and Overshown are closer to a return for the team’s Week 6 matchup against the Green Bay Packers, while Shelton is “week to week” after suffering the injury in Week 4, according to head coach Brian Schottenheimer. All-Pro left guard Tyler Smith is aiming to make his season debut after a thumb injury on his right hand required surgery just days before the season began. Quinnen Williams on quick turnaround for Cowboys vs. Buccaneers: ‘I’m not tired’ – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com The Cowboys only had three days to prepare for the Buccaneers. However, defensive tackle Quinnen Williams welcomes the challenge. Thursday night will mark the third game that the Cowboys have played in 11 days, the first of which was 10 hours away in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said that his team is “tired” and “sore” heading into the quick turnaround as a whole. Williams, personally, disagreed. “I’m not tired,” Williams said. “I love football, I look more forward to the opportunity and getting a chance to play again, get to play at prime time against a great team, against Todd Bowles. It’s an amazing opportunity for us.”

title: Cowboys looking to capitalize against a Baker-less Bucs team
summary: The last time the Dallas Cowboys faced the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at home (Week 16 of 2024), it was a quarterback battle between Baker Mayfield and Cooper Rush for the home team. The time before that, it was the 2022 Wild Card game in Tampa Bay – Dak Prescott versus Tom Brady. Now in Week […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The last time the Dallas Cowboys faced the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at home (Week 16 of 2024), it was a quarterback battle between Baker Mayfield and Cooper Rush for the home team. The time before that, it was the 2022 Wild Card game in Tampa Bay – Dak Prescott versus Tom Brady. Now in Week 5 of 2026, we get yet another different QB matchup of Dak Prescott against undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels. The one constant for the Buccaneers over this time has been head coach Todd Bowles, now in year five. Last season was Bowles’ first time not making the playoffs in Tampa, and already his chances of doing so this season have taken a massive hit with the team losing their first four games, as well as Mayfield as their starting QB. The Bucs have failed to take to the identity a Todd Bowles team should have, with the third fewest sacks of any defense so far this season with six. The Giants, Chiefs, Eagles, and Dolphins have less, as well as the Cowboys with four. Despite this, their defense is the second best in the league behind only Seattle in percentage of receptions given up that result in a first down. They are third in rushing yards allowed and second in yards per carry, and as a result of all this have been in four straight one-score games. The only opponent to score over 30 points on the Bucs so far this season was the Bengals in Week 1, and Tampa themselves have not scored more than 27 (also in that game) so far. For this year’s Cowboys, playing against Todd Bowles marks yet another defensive-oriented head coach for Brian Schottenheimer to scheme against at the start of this season. It has been four straight to reach this point already, and the results are a split down the middle at 2-2. How the Cowboys offense figured things out on the fly to avoid a 1-3 start despite being down 16-6 last week in Houston against DeMeco Ryans and the winless Texans could be encouraging when it comes to signs of progress against these defense-first coaches, and something Dallas would welcome in their return home for Thursday Night Football . Setting expectations as fans for a decisive win is almost always a bad idea that leads to nothing but disappointment, but there is buzz around Cowboys fans this week that this game could be a classic example of an AT&T Stadium runaway where the offense piles on points, the defense gets takeaways as a result, and the Cowboys cruise. The Bucs will have some clear reasons to think this won’t happen to them, though. In Daniels’ first start last week against the Green Bay Packers, the Bucs fixed their season-long red zone woes on offense and went 2-2 scoring touchdowns. Even with throwing two interceptions, the Bucs played their closest game of the season, only losing 17-14. A bit like the Cowboys, the Packers came into this game needing a win where they not only came out on top but looked really good doing so, but did not get it in Florida. The Cowboys offense is putting up chart-breaking numbers on points and efficiency despite having the fewest possessions in the league, so if this is indeed the week they get their first interception of the season, those extra possessions could go a very, very long way. The more tangible thing to look for in this game would be if the second half momentum from the comeback in Houston carries over against Tampa Bay. Coming into that game, we pointed out how Dallas has historically struggled with teams playing in desperation mode, which the Texans already were at 0-3. That certainly showed itself for large stretches of that game. A combination of the Texans relying on their four man rushes, which were getting home in the first half but not so much as the game went on, and then getting exposed by Prescott when bringing extra rushers in the second half, led to the Cowboys offense figuring things out to go on a game-winning drive. The pressures should come early, often, and everywhere in between from an even more desperate Bucs team. The Cowboys will need a sound protection plan against a team that will be hellbent on doing everything they can to hold Prescott’s play down in order to have another shot to steal a game. The Dallas offensive line is getting better news coming into this game on Thursday, looking to have left guard Tyler Smith back in the lineup. The extra peace of mind that the pocket will be clean for Prescott will allow the Cowboys to go after starting cornerbacks Jacob Parrish and Zyon McCollum for the Bucs. The Cowboys will be hoping their four game body of work against similar defensive challenges up to this point gives them a chance to stack two wins in five days, and put a bow on three games in 12 days with a winning record. After two long field goals were missed in the Texans game, scoring touchdowns would be the best way to do so, especially given how their last home game against the Buccaneers went. Dallas started the scoring with a 58-yard Brandon Aubrey field goal, went up 13-7 on a 49-yard field goal, and ended the first half by going up 23-14 with another 58-yarder. Another Aubrey make from 53 yards was their only score of the second half. As simple and borderline silly as it is to say, touchdowns will win this game for the Cowboys, which would be a third straight against the Bucs. The Cowboys have not won three straight against the Bucs since winning five in a row from 2006-2012. You have to go back even further though to find the last time the Bucs won in Arlington with a quarterback not named Tom Brady. This was 2001 when Brad Johnson ran in a one-yard touchdown against a Quincy Johnson-led Cowboys team to turn a 6-3 Dallas lead in a slugfest into a 10-6 Tampa win. This was the first loss of the season for a Cowboys team that started 0-4 themselves. Despite never making the playoffs as head coach of the Jets from 2015-2018, this 0-4 start to a season is the worst any Todd Bowles coached team has ever had, and chance for the Cowboys coaching staff to prove a little bit more they’re the right fit for the job of taking this Cowboys team back to the playoffs by reaching 3-2 and sending the Bucs to 0-5.
