title: Cowboys have a big opportunity against the winless Buccaneers
summary: Momentum can change very quickly in the NFL. A week ago, the Dallas Cowboys were 1-2 and coming off a heartbreaking last-second defeat in Brazil. Now they are back at .500 after a dramatic 34-30 comeback victory over the Houston Texans, and have an opportunity to move above .500 on Thursday Night Football. Standing in […]
full_text: Photo by Matthew Pearce/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Momentum can change very quickly in the NFL. A week ago, the Dallas Cowboys were 1-2 and coming off a heartbreaking last-second defeat in Brazil. Now they are back at .500 after a dramatic 34-30 comeback victory over the Houston Texans, and have an opportunity to move above .500 on Thursday Night Football . Standing in their way are the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, but we have some reasons to be positive this week. Tampa Bay arrives at AT&T Stadium at 0-4, without its starting quarterback and without one of the best players on its defense. Meanwhile, Dak Prescott is playing some of the best football in the league, CeeDee Lamb is absolutely on fire, and Javonte Williams just scored three touchdowns. The biggest reason for confidence remains Dak Prescott. Through four games, Prescott has thrown for 1,065 yards, eight touchdowns and only one interception while completing 70% of his passes. He has now gone three straight games without throwing an interception. That matters with the Cowboys having scored at least 31 points in each of their last three games. On the opposite side, Tampa Bay quarterback Baker Mayfield will not play because of a thumb injury. Instead, undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels will make only his second NFL start. Daniels completed 19 of 27 passes against Green Bay last week but managed only 148 passing yards. He also threw two interceptions and was sacked three times. Now he has to make his second start on the road at AT&T Stadium on a short week. Dallas should make that as uncomfortable as possible. Superstar receiver CeeDee Lamb is coming off an incredible 17-catch, 189-yard performance against Houston. He now has 498 receiving yards through four games. Making that matchup even better for Dallas is the absence of Antoine Winfield Jr, one of Tampa Bay’s best defensive players. Without him in the secondary, Prescott should have opportunities to attack with Lamb, Jake Ferguson and George Pickens. Javonte Williams is another big reason to be positive for Cowboys fans. He scored three rushing touchdowns against Houston and now has four rushing scores over the last two games. This shows that Dallas does not need Prescott throwing 45 times every week. Using Williams can help control the clock and protect the quarterback. The Buccaneers have already allowed 16 sacks in four games. Dallas has struggled to finish pressures with sacks this season, but this is a good matchup for the pass rush to finally break through and get some momentum. If Quinnen Williams and the defensive front can make Daniels uncomfortable, mistakes should follow along with a multiple sacks. The Cowboys are finally back at AT&T Stadium after playing in Brazil and then travelling to Houston. Dallas won its only true home game so far this season, beating Washington 37-20 in healthy fashion. That environment should be difficult for a rookie quarterback making only his second career start. The Buccaneers are 0-4, but every one of their games have been competitive. They lost 33-27 to Cincinnati, 23-19 to Cleveland, 23-16 to Minnesota, then lost 17-14 to Green Bay. The positive here for Dallas is that Tampa Bay hasn’t shown it can finish those close games, but Dallas just did. The Cowboys were behind late in Houston, took the football with 2:15 remaining and drove down the field for the winning touchdown. One team has just proved it can finish. The other is still looking for its first win. Tampa will be without its starting quarterback, and star defensive player, plus early practice reports have listed cornerback Benjamin Morrison and linebacker SirVocea Dennis as non-participants. Rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter was also limited with a knee injury. For Dallas, Tyler Smith is back in practice, so things are looking up. That’s a lot here that’s massively positive heading into Thursday Night Football .

title: Dallas Cowboys injuries: Status updates on Tyler Smith, DeMarvion Overshown
summary: It’s the final injury report for the Dallas Cowboys and Tampa Bay Buccaneers ahead of their game tomorrow night. We have good and bad news about the Cowboys’ health status before tomorrow night’s game.  Tyler Smith was upgraded to full participation on Wednesday and has been listed as questionable to play in tomorrow’s game. Dallas […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images It’s the final injury report for the Dallas Cowboys and Tampa Bay Buccaneers ahead of their game tomorrow night. We have good and bad news about the Cowboys’ health status before tomorrow night’s game. 📝 #Cowboys final injury report vs. Bucs: 🚨 Tyler Smith upgraded, was a FULL participant for the first time since undergoing thumb surgery — listed as questionable for TNF. pic.twitter.com/kbrQavAlax — Patrik [No C] Walker (@VoiceOfTheStar) October 7, 2026 Tyler Smith was upgraded to full participation on Wednesday and has been listed as questionable to play in tomorrow’s game. Dallas likely gets a major boost to their offensive line with the return of their Pro Bowl guard. After not practicing this week, the team opted to shelve DeMarvion Overshown with his lingering hamstring injury. The decision to sit him is wise given Dallas will have an extended break between Thursday’s game and next Sunday night at Green Bay. Also ruled out are cornerback Cobie Durant (hamstring) and rookie offensive lineman Drew Shelton. For the Buccaneers, there are no surprises. Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib) and cornerback Benjamin Morrison (quad), who have not practiced all week, have been ruled out. Also ruled out is starting quarterback Baker Mayfield (thumb), which means it’ll be undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels taking the start for the winless Buccaneers.

title: Digging into the numbers to predict Cowboys vs Buccaneers
summary: Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. We’ll look at the recent numbers and trends for each team. At the end, we’ll add it all up to see what Dallas needs to do to secure a win and which team may have the edge. Cowboys key stats from last […]
full_text: Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. We’ll look at the recent numbers and trends for each team. At the end, we’ll add it all up to see what Dallas needs to do to secure a win and which team may have the edge. Cowboys key stats from last week Dak Prescott threw for 335 yards, one touchdown and zero interceptions against the Texans. He finished with a 99.8 quarterback rating. Javonte Williams was limited on the ground to just 62 yards on 19 carries. He did have an impressive three touchdown performance, however, with all of the scores coming in the second half. CeeDee Lamb showcased why he’s one of the premier receivers in the NFL. The All-Pro receiver finished with a season high 189 yards on a career high 17 receptions. He also caught the game winning touchdown against the Texans. The Dallas defense continues to impress on third down, allowing only three first downs on ten attempts against the Texans. But that’s only one part of the tale. Explosive plays were the Achilles heel all game long. The Texans recorded a 16% explosive play rate, gashing Dallas for 20+ yard gains throughout the day. Buccaneers key stats from last week The Buccaneers took on the Packers last Sunday and took home the loss, 17-14 . Tampa Bay has now started the season 0-4 for first time since 2013. This was also their fourth straight loss by seven points or less. Rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels received his first start, going 19-of-27 for 148 yards through the air. He would finish with one touchdown and two interceptions on the day. On the ground, the mobile quarterback would run for 55 yards, including a long of 21 . In Baker Mayfield’s stead, this offense needs to run through running back Bucky Irving. He racked up 61 yards on 16 carries against the Packers. According to SumerSports, the Buccaneers defense ranks fourth in EPA/play allowed this season and finished as the 14th ranked unit in the same category against the Packers in Week 4. Defensive line: Start your engines Last week was somewhat of a disappointment for the Cowboys pass rush when considering the weakness of the Texans offensive line. Rashan Gary and Quinnen Williams each recorded one sack, but the pass rush took entirely too long to get started and was inconsistent at best. But Dallas has another shot at a get right matchup this week. Coming into this game, Tampa Bay has surrendered the most sacks in the NFL, including three last week against the Packers. Facing a rookie quarterback in his second start, Dallas will get another shot at jump starting the pass rush of their defensive front. While mobile quarterbacks had made the Cowboys pay for the first three weeks, this is a much less proven passer as compared to the other three. Dallas can’t break contain because Jalon Daniels will be more than happy to take off and pick up 15 yards at any moment. At the same time, this front will need to figure out a way to consistently put pressure on the young quarterback to force mistakes. Christian Parker should lean into the blitz more this week as well with the same goal in mind. What do the numbers mean? On offense, this should be another game where Dak Prescott and the receivers shine. The Tampa Bay defense doesn’t sack the quarterback often, with just six on the season. And their pass defense ranks 22nd in quarterback rating allowed. In addition, safety Antoine Winfield Jr. is set to miss this game. The Buccaneers won’t allow CeeDee Lamb to go unchecked like the Texans did last week, so this could very well be the 2026 coming out party for George Pickens and Ryan Flournoy. Defensively, the Cowboys have to get after Daniels. This is another week where the Cowboys face an opponent that has not been good at protecting their quarterback. It’s time this defense takes advantage of it. And if we discover that the front four is not getting it done, Parker should be unafraid to send extra blitzers. Young quarterbacks are typically susceptible to disguised coverages and blitzes, and Daniels has already shown that to be the case last week. The first order of business is to stop Irving and the run game, of course, but the defense should also be able to force Daniels into some errors throughout the day. As of right now, the line on the game sits at Cowboys -8.5. That seems like a lot at first glance, but the Dallas offense has been historically good through four weeks. Through four games, the Cowboys offense ranks fifth in points per drive out of every offense since 2000 pic.twitter.com/Ad9jM44pDt — Anthony Dabbundo (@AnthonyDabbundo) October 5, 2026 Going up against a struggling Buccaneers offense and a backup quarterback should equate to an easy day for the Cowboys. This is a week for the Cowboys defense to take a step forward, should they be willing and able to do so. You never really can get too comfortable around these parts though. We also have to consider the rough schedule Dallas has had: getting beat up in Brazil to then come back to Texas to win a buzzer beater against the Texans. The Cowboys should clearly win this game against the Buccaneers. But until we can put more consistent trust in the defense, games that should be blowouts are likely to end up closer than they would initially appear on paper.
author: Dyllan Rivers

title: Cowboys point/counterpoint: Still looking for answers against the Buccaneers
summary: In the NFL, you take any win, no matter how many warts it has. And make no mistake, there were warts all over the Dallas Cowboys’ 34-30 win over the winless Houston Texans. From the way the defense struggled at so many points in the game to the anemic run offense outside of the redzone, […]
full_text: Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images | Getty Images In the NFL, you take any win, no matter how many warts it has. And make no mistake, there were warts all over the Dallas Cowboys’ 34-30 win over the winless Houston Texans. From the way the defense struggled at so many points in the game to the anemic run offense outside of the redzone, there clearly is much to work on. Now they face another winless team, the 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers. This comes on a short week as it is on Thursday Night Football . With so many questions still to be answered, here are some areas Sean Martin and Tom Ryle have concerns. Tom – Some context is important here. By beating the Texans, the Cowboys kept themselves in the thick of the NFC East race. The New York Giants are somehow keeping at the head of the division without Jaxson Dart, the Washington Commanders are trailing everyone else but hope to have Jayden Daniels back this week, and it is with great sadness that I observed what can only be called a meltdown by the Philadelphia Eagles against the Los Angeles Rams that may bode ill for them. The playoffs are hardly out of reach for Dallas at this point. But some things really need to change. And forgive me for venting a bit about something. I didn’t like the whole ‘Greatest Offense There Is’ idea from the start. Not only was it unoriginal and clumsy, it seemed to have been created while willfully ignoring something very important. Yes, the Cowboys offense was tearing it up all offseason and leading up to the regular season. But it appears Dak Prescott put out of his mind it was looking so good working against a defense that was simply pitiful last season. And the first four games have shown that the supposed improvements during the offseason have not panned out as well as we were hoping. It leaves the offense still having to carry this team. That was certainly the case in Houston, but it was just half the offense, or more precisely, it was the Dak-to-CeeDee Lamb connection being on absolute fire. Yes, Javontae Williams scored three touchdowns, but he still mustered a paltry 3.3 yards per carry. That, to me, is not a sustainable formula for making any kind of a playoff run. Sean – Well, it’s good to be talking to you after a win Tom. I wish I could say it was 2-2 over the weekend, but I’m sure we’ve all seen what happened at this point to my Bobcats at Idaho. You make a great point about the GOTI offense for the Cowboys, and Prescott pushed that further by saying he expected a blowout win against the Texans. All we can say about that now, is that at least he came up clutch when it mattered and the ball was firmly in the offense’s court. We have CeeDee Lamb’s historic day to thank for that. I think we learned with the Cowboys this week, and in many other places around the league, that we’re at a point where it’s important to not get too high or too low. This win had all of the thumbprints the Cowboys would like on it, Schottenheimer redeeming himself and calling the right plays in crunch time, the defense getting some key pressures, overcoming two missed field goals and a deficit, and winning late. There’s going to be talk of the “culture” being fixed because of this, of the Cowboys righting all their wrongs, almost as if Brazil didn’t happen. We have to pair these last two games together, all of the crazy highs and lows, and try to paint a more realistic picture of where this team is at with a short week to get back to work. Mix it all together and a winning record before we even get to the weekend is still in sight, so sign me up for that. Having the intensity to hand a winless, desperate team another loss was nicely done though, and exactly what the Cowboys will need to do again as the headline for the Buccaneers is that they also fell to 0-4 on Sunday. Tom – The problem is that I’m not sure what it really proves to get wins over winless teams, especially close ones like Sunday. I know that on any given Sunday something something, but Dallas needs to really assert itself. Tampa Bay offers a great opportunity for just that. But if they don’t breeze to a comfortable win, then we have to worry very much about what will happen when the competition is more formidable. And after facing the Texans and Buccaneers back to back, that is exactly what is coming. A win is a win, of course, but unless we see the offense really clicking without Prescott and Lamb, or maybe George Pickens have to be superheroes, and the defense shows it can put the clamps on a team that is having its own struggles, we should have a sense of trepidation. A strong showing against Tampa Bay would not only make us feel better about the overall performance of the team. It could set Dallas up to be a real challenger to win the division and get back to the playoffs. Sean – I am going to disagree with the general premise of style points mattering right now, but the thing I can’t possibly disagree with is that this team still has a lot of work to do. Luckily, so does every team right now as we’re a long way from knowing who will be the last one standing in February. We’ve seen Cowboys teams that won with style points in the regular season before not even make it to January, and the league is on a heater when it comes to games being decided by one score across the board right now. The Texans win can’t ease all of our woes about playing better competition, but the level of competition the Houston defense gave the Dallas offense in the first half sure was challenging, and they built a ten-point lead off of it. Within the same 60 minutes, the Cowboys turned it around and won, so maybe that will be something we look back on for evidence of getting it done against top defenses. I also think the easiest room for improvement to play even better on offense is the play-calling consistency right now, which is fixable if there’s still trust to be had in Schottenheimer. That trust will be back down to near-zero if the Cowboys are upset by the Bucs. The cruel reality is that it also won’t skyrocket back up with a win against this very depleted Tampa squad, but that Todd Bowles defense is going to bring pressure and play a bit reckless I think. The offense will need to show poise yet again. It’s a bye week on Saturday for the Bobcats, and a free Sunday for us Cowboys fans to watch other teams. Should be a nice weekend if they handle business on Thursday!
author: Sean Martin

title: Cowboys roundtable discussion: Houston comeback, Nick Sorensen, defensive sacks
summary: Every week, we gather to discuss the latest news about the Dallas Cowboys and seek our writer’s perspective on each headline. Welcome back to the roundtable. This week we have Jorge Guajardo, Dyllan Rivers, Tom Ryle and Sean Martin.  What was most convincing about the comeback win?  Mike – The most convincing part was Brian Schottenheimer. Dallas looked flat, stuck, and […]
full_text: Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images | Getty Images Every week, we gather to discuss the latest news about the Dallas Cowboys and seek our writer’s perspective on each headline. Welcome back to the roundtable. This week we have Jorge Guajardo , Dyllan Rivers , Tom Ryle and Sean Martin. What was most convincing about the comeback win? Mike – The most convincing part was Brian Schottenheimer. Dallas looked flat, stuck, and out of answers in the first half, but Schottenheimer helped flip the game after halftime. The play-calling became much better, the offense found rhythm, and the team clearly still believed it could win even when Houston had control. Credit has to go to the head coach when adjustments work and the team responds. This was not just Dak Prescott or CeeDee Lamb dragging Dallas out of trouble. It was a coaching staff finding answers, and Schotty did that. Dyllan – If teams choose to eliminate the quick death by focusing on George Pickens, Dallas is happy to methodically beat you with CeeDee Lamb the entire game. And don’t forget about Flournoy, by the way, who is completely capable of key chain moving grabs. This WR room reminded the NFL why they’re so dangerous. Jorge – The offense genuinely looks like a force of nature, and I still don’t think it’s firing on all cylinders yet. To Dyllan’s point, the WR room may be the deepest and most capable in the league, and they are getting the job done when called up and asked to deliver in the clutch. Oh, and QB Dak Prescott ain’t playing too bad either. Tom – I’m not sure there was anything convincing besides the obvious potency of the passing attack, and a nice bit of evidence that CeeDee is indeed among the elite at his position. But a couple of other things were at least encouraging. The red zone offense found a way every time. And the Cowboys had half the penalties, not their normal result. Oddly, those two are kind of interconnected, because on one touchdown the Texans just refused to get off the field without getting a flag. Sean – The offense not being denied in crunch time. The margin for error on some of Dak’s biggest throws of the game was slim to none, and every point the Cowboys put up ended up being needed. We can keep hoping and dreaming to see this offense with a little less pressure on their backs to score almost every time they touch it, but for now they’re scoring at an elite rate anyway, and it’s good enough to be right in the thick of things going into mid-October. Are we happy with how Nick Sorensen is coaching the special teams unit? Mike – In my opinion he needs to go. Brandon Aubrey is elite, but Aubrey’s leg should not cover up the wider special teams problems. The unit has too many messy moments, too many avoidable mistakes, and too many situations where Dallas either loses hidden yards or puts unnecessary pressure on the rest of the team. Special teams should be the cleanest, most reliable phase, not something that constantly feels like it is one mistake away from hurting the Cowboys. At some point, the coordinator has to own that. Dyllan – The FG unit needs to learn how to block things up in a hurry. They nearly had a second kick blocked on the PAT at the end of the game. But I do love their mastery of the dirty kick. The hidden yards in field position is extremely important for the growing defense. And Turpin is quietly putting up solid return numbers. I’m fine with Sorensen but they do need to figure out how to block on the FG attempts. Jorge – No. Special teams was an issue last year, and continues to be this year. The kickoff penalties are unacceptable, and blocked field goals played a hand in a loss this year. Aubrey’s special ability to nail those long kicks will be neutralized if the Cowboys can’t shore up protection on these field-goal attempts. Tom – It is more tolerable than satisfying. Those blocks and near blocks are potential game changers and must be avoided. Return yards are a plus, but we still haven’t seen the big return for a score or to get on the doorstep of the end zone. Sean – The Texans hurt themselves more than the Cowboys with special teams penalties in this game, but the Cowboys left an opportunity to push this differential even further with some sloppiness in the third phase themselves. For a coach that’s been here for a minute now, that’s a tough thing to swallow, and they’ll need to get it corrected. Is this the game where the defensvie line have to turn pressures into sacks? Mike – Yes, absolutely. Tampa Bay has allowed 16 sacks in four games, so if there is ever a week for the Cowboys’ defensive front to arrive, it is this one. Pressures are nice, but against a struggling protection unit, Quinnen Williams, Kenny Clark, Rashaan Gary and the rest of the edge rushers have to finish plays this week. If the Buccaneers offensive line gives them chances and the Cowboys still cannot turn those chances into sacks, then the concern level goes way up. Dyllan – The game against Houston was the one where I thought they’d rack up the sacks. And they did finish with two. But I thought it’d come together sooner and more frequently. I’m losing confidence that the current room will be able to get after passers this season. Jorge – I agree with Dyllan; I’m not sure this group has what it takes to consistently bring the opposing quarterback down. They looked much better at the end of the game and on third down, but we still aren’t seeing much in the rush. I think that Christian Parker has to start maximizing their ability to rush the passer beyond asking them to beat their blockers with their skill/athleticism, so I’m talking more vigorous rush plans, and maybe even more blitzes. Tom – The lack of sacks is only concerning when paired with the failure to get a single interception. One can offset the other, but when neither is happening, it just increases the concern about whether this team can ever put it all together on D. Sean – To Tom’s point, rookie starter Jalon Daniels was sacked three times by the Packers on Sunday, but also threw two interceptions, so the impact plays could go either way, and both would be welcome from Parker’s defense. I would lean towards forcing this quarterback to throw into coverage as much as possible, so the chance for edge rushers to win matchups straight up will be there. I think they’ll get some, but not enough for us to feel drastically better about the EDGE group coming out of the game. RAPID FIRE Who scores first for Dallas? Dyllan – George Pickens gets on the board first the week. Jorge – CeeDee Lamb Tom – Javonte Williams, rapidly becoming a red zone machine Sean – I think it’s time for me to start picking Pickens until it hits, so Pickens. CeeDee Lamb receptions, over/under 9.5 Dyllan – Under. This is the week Pickens faces more solo coverage and comes alive. Jorge – Yeah, under. Tom – Ditto Sean – Ride the hot hand, over for me. Javonte Williams rushing yards, over/under 79.5 Dyllan – Over. I think Dallas gets up early and it becomes kill the clock time. Jorge – Over, for the reasons Dyllan mentioned. Tom – I’ll stick with the under until this team proves it can run the ball effectively outside the red zone Sean – Under. Dallas sacks on Jalon Daniels, over/under 3.5 Dyllan – Under. The pass rush is still very suspect regardless of opponent. Jorge – Under Tom – Ditto again Sean – Under Cowboys margin of victory, over/under 9.5 Dyllan – Over. 10 points is a huge line in the NFL but I think Dallas piles on the points and the defense nets them extra possessions. Jorge – Under, I’m still not convinced with this coaching staff. Tom – Over, just because they are about due for a blowout of an outmanned opponent Sean – Over would sure be nice True or false? Dallas forces multiple turnovers this week on defense. Dyllan – True. And I see your multiple turnovers and raise you one defensive touchdown. Jorge – False Tom – False until proven otherwise Sean – Probably false.
author: Mike Poland

title: Cowboys offensive plan: Attack the Buccaneers corners early and often
summary: Coming off the most exciting win of the 2026 season, the Dallas Cowboys offense has a quick turnaround in week five, hosting the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in a pivotal NFC conference matchup. The Cowboys offense started out slow in their 34-30 win over the Houston Texans, but unleashed on a quality Texans defense in the […]
full_text: Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Coming off the most exciting win of the 2026 season, the Dallas Cowboys offense has a quick turnaround in week five, hosting the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in a pivotal NFC conference matchup. The Cowboys offense started out slow in their 34-30 win over the Houston Texans, but unleashed on a quality Texans defense in the second half to seal the victory. A lot of went right for the Cowboys offense in the second half against Houston should be heavily leaned on in this Tampa Bay matchup. The Cowboys took a more conservative approach in the first half against the Texans and that led to struggles putting up touchdowns and sustaining drives. In the second half, they came out and played their typical style of football. They aggressively pushed the ball downfield while getting better pass protection. The Tampa Bay defense has played pretty well to start their season, despite their 0-4 start. Their defense currently ranks fifth in EPA/play and sixth in success rate. With that said, the Cowboys passing game should look to attack the Tampa Bay corners early and often. The Buccaneers starting three corners showcase rookie Keionte Scott in the slot, and Jacob Parrish and Zyon McCollum on the outside. Scott and Parish have played well to start the season, but both players are young and undersized compared the Cowboys trio of wide receivers. Scott is feisty nickel who does most of his damage as a run defender and blitzer, but he can be had in coverage and will lineup across from CeeDee Lamb on a high percentage of snaps. That is a clear advantage for the Cowboys and they should look to involve Lamb in all areas of the field, just like last week, and take advantage of the rookies inexperience against arguably the best wide receiver in football through four weeks. On the outside, George Pickens will also have an advantage over Parrish and McCollum. To make matters worse for Tampa Bay, they will be without their best secondary player in Antoine Winfield Jr., limiting their ability to control the middle of the field. While we should expect the Cowboys top two receivers to feast in this game, the matchup for all the pass catchers favors the Cowboys. Rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter has been fantastic to start the season, but getting tight ends Jake Ferguson and Brevyn Spann-Ford matched up on him in coverage with Winfield out gives the Cowboys more size advantages against the Buccaneers coverage defenders. Through four weeks, the Cowboys have seemingly needed to score 30+ points to win these games. Even with Baker Mayfield not expected to play, the Cowboys passing game will likely need to carry the weight of this game again, but they should have a much easier matchup in week five than they had in week four.
author: Connor Livesay

title: Cowboys Week 5 opponent: Looking at the 2026 Tampa Bay Buccaneers
summary: The Dallas Cowboys don’t have much time to enjoy their comeback victory over Houston. After Dallas erased a 10-point halftime deficit to beat the Texans 34-30 on Sunday, they immediately started prepping for a Thursday night matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Tampa Bay enters the game at 0-4 after a 17-14 loss to the […]
full_text: Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys don’t have much time to enjoy their comeback victory over Houston. After Dallas erased a 10-point halftime deficit to beat the Texans 34-30 on Sunday, they immediately started prepping for a Thursday night matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Tampa Bay enters the game at 0-4 after a 17-14 loss to the Green Bay Packers, while Dallas comes in at 2-2. The Buccaneers’ record doesn’t tell the whole story of where this team stands, though. Tampa Bay has dealt with injuries, inconsistent quarterback play and an offense that has struggled to turn opportunities into points, while its defense has kept the team competitive through the first month of the season. And now, with just three days between games, Tampa Bay will arrive in Dallas without the quarterback it expected to lead it through the season. So what exactly are the Cowboys getting on Thursday night? Baker Mayfield won’t be there Baker Mayfield was supposed to be the centerpiece of Tampa Bay’s offense this season, and through the first three games, he had thrown for 615 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions while completing 63.5% of his passes. He also added 65 rushing yards and a touchdown on the ground. Those numbers haven’t produced the kind of offensive explosion Tampa expected, but Mayfield’s absence still changes the complexion of this game. He suffered a dislocated right thumb in Week 3 and is expected to miss at least three games, meaning he will not be available Thursday night against Dallas. That leaves rookie Jalon Daniels as the Buccaneers’ starter. Daniels made his first NFL start against Green Bay in Week 4, completing 19 of 30 passes for 148 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. He also ran nine times for 64 yards, giving Tampa a slightly different look when their QB scrambles. There were some encouraging moments for Daniels against Green Bay, but the Buccaneers ultimately couldn’t capitalize on their opportunities. He also threw an interception that helped set up a Packers field goal, and Tampa’s final possession ended without the game-winning drive the team needed. That makes Thursday a very different quarterback challenge for Dallas than the one it would have faced against Mayfield. Instead of dealing with an experienced veteran who has played more than 100 NFL games, the Cowboys will be facing a rookie quarterback making his second career start on a short week and on the road. Jalon Daniels' first career TD! 🙌 @GBvsTB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/MKQijt4XeA — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 Tampa still has plenty of weapons The quarterback situation may have changed, but Tampa hasn’t suddenly become an offense without playmakers. Bucky Irving remains one of the Buccaneers’ most important offensive pieces. Through four games, Irving has rushed for 241 yards on 56 carries, averaging 4.3 yards per carry, and has added 61 receiving yards. Chris Godwin Jr. is another veteran Dallas will have to account for. Godwin has 16 catches for 142 yards through four games, while second-year receiver Emeka Egbuka has emerged as another important part of the passing attack with 15 receptions for 154 yards and a touchdown. Then there is Cade Otton. The Buccaneers’ tight end currently leads the team in receiving yards with 157 on 15 receptions, averaging 10.5 yards per catch. He has become an increasingly reliable target for Tampa’s quarterbacks, and his involvement could become even more important with Daniels now running the offense. The Buccaneers have also gotten production from receiver Ted Hurst III, who has eight catches for 128 yards and a touchdown. His 16.0 yards per reception average is actually the highest among Tampa players with multiple receptions. So while Tampa’s offense has struggled to score consistently, Dallas can’t afford to approach Thursday as though it is simply facing a struggling offense with a rookie quarterback. There are too many legitimate weapons available for the Buccaneers to create problems if the Cowboys’ defense isn’t disciplined. Jalon Daniels hole shot to Ted Hurst pic.twitter.com/jNdNK0n5mP — Josh Norris (@JoshNorris) October 6, 2026 Tampa’s defense has quietly kept the team alive If there is one thing the Buccaneers have done well through the first four weeks, it is keeping games within reach. Tampa has allowed fewer than 300 total yards in three consecutive games, including just 283 against Green Bay in Week 4. The Buccaneers also forced multiple turnovers against the Packers, recovering a fumble and intercepting Jordan Love during the fourth quarter. The Buccaneers have only allowed their opponents to score nine touchdowns in the first four games. David Walker leads the team with two sacks, while Alex Anzalone and Anthony Nelson each have one. Tampa has also gotten strong early contributions from linebacker Josiah Trotter, cornerback Keionte Scott and cornerback Zyon McCollum, who lead the team in tackles with 17, 16 and 15 respectively. The defense has essentially kept giving Tampa opportunities to win games that the offense hasn’t consistently been able to finish. The Cowboys just demonstrated against Houston that they can overcome defensive problems by scoring 34 points, but Tampa’s defense has shown that it can make opponents work for every possession. Tampa’s defense will also be missing one of its most important players. Safety Antoine Winfield Jr. suffered a rib fracture during Sunday’s loss to Green Bay and is expected to miss two to four weeks. Winfield had recorded 24 tackles through the first four games and has been one of the Buccaneers’ most important defensive players since entering the league. Tampa Bay’s defense does it again! #WeAreTheKrewe pic.twitter.com/Hq5dtapFvM — Matty B (@mattthew_jordan) October 4, 2026 A Thursday night game with two very different teams The Cowboys and Buccaneers enter Thursday night in very different places. Dallas is 2-2 and coming off its highest-scoring comeback of the season. CeeDee Lamb is coming off a historic performance, Dak Prescott just threw for 335 yards against Houston, and the Cowboys have scored at least 20 points in every game this season. Tampa Bay is 0-4 and has already had to change quarterbacks because of injury. Even still, the Buccaneers have a legitimate running back in Irving, productive receiving options in Godwin, Egbuka and Otton, and a defense that has consistently kept opponents under 300 total yards. The Buccaneers have been close in every game, and their defense has proven capable of keeping them within striking distance. If Dallas wants to improve on its 2-2 record, Thursday night is an opportunity to do exactly that. Now the Cowboys get a Tampa Bay team that may not be able to match them offensively, but has spent the first month of the season proving that it can make a game uncomfortable for anybody.
author: Jorge Guajardo

title: Cowboys news: Dak Prescott says team will be ready for quick turnaround
summary: In the words of head coach Brian Schottenheimer, the NFL blessed the Dallas Cowboys with three games in 11 days after they returned from a ten-hour flight to Rio, Brazil. So far, they are one of two teams to beat the Houston Texans on the road, but they lost to the Baltimore Ravens on the […]
full_text: Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images | Getty Images In the words of head coach Brian Schottenheimer, the NFL blessed the Dallas Cowboys with three games in 11 days after they returned from a ten-hour flight to Rio, Brazil. So far, they are one of two teams to beat the Houston Texans on the road, but they lost to the Baltimore Ravens on the road. The Cowboys have their first Thursday night game of the season, and after two physical, down-to-the-wire matchups, Dak Prescott is confident his team will be ready for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Dak Prescott promises Cowboys will be ‘100’ percent for TNF vs. Buccaneers – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com The Cowboys need to win Thursday night if they want to keep pace with the New York Giants—what a world. “Oh, it’s gonna be 100. It’s gonna be 100,” said All-Pro Dak Prescott when asked if the Cowboys will be ready in a short week after two emotionally and physically draining matchups. “That’s how much I love this game, how much I put in this game throughout my life. Through the offseason, you prepare and you condition, and you do a lot of things for these types of moments. How Jerry Jones helped a Cowboys’ player make it to the birth of his first child – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram Congratulations to Shemar James and his entire family. At halftime of the win, James was informed by the Cowboys’ director of security, Cable Johnson, that James’ wife was going into labor. The team and James quickly talked through options, and the way that got him to the delivery room the quickest was actually to wait until after the game and ride back on Jerry Jones’ private jet. title: NFL picks and predictions: Broncos vs. Chargers and the rest of Week 5
summary: Welcome back to the fifth installment of Hart’s Picks for the 2026 NFL regular season. A big thanks once again to Bixbys Hooman in the comments for riding along with me this year to see who picks the best. For Week 4—if my math is right this time—I was 8-8—only predicting the Rams, Bears, Packers, […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 4: Fred Warner #54 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates on the field after an NFL football game against the Denver Broncos at Levi's Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome back to the fifth installment of Hart’s Picks for the 2026 NFL regular season. A big thanks once again to Bixbys Hooman in the comments for riding along with me this year to see who picks the best. For Week 4 —if my math is right this time—I was 8-8—only predicting the Rams, Bears, Packers, Ravens, Vikings, Seahawks, Chiefs, and Falcons correctly. Let’s see how well I do in Week 5. Keep in mind, there are only fifteen games with the Carolina Panthers and Kansas City Chiefs on their BYE. Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Dallas Cowboys — Thursday Night Football The Buccaneers are 0-4 to start the season. They’ll be without Baker Mayfield again on Thursday Night Football against the Cowboys. Dallas is struggling on defense, but I’m pretty sure Dak Prescott and their offense will be able to score a lot more points than Tampa Bay with Jalon Daniels. I’m going with the home team. Winner: Cowboys Philadelphia Eagles at Jacksonville Jaguars — Sunday (Morning Game) This Week 5 matchup for the morning game will be played in London. After two straight losses, the Eagles are trying to find a way to get back on track. Though they may be without Saquan Barkley and Tank Bigsby. If so, that means Will Shipley is their starting running back. I don’t think that will bode well for them. Jalen Hurts isn’t playing well and Lane Johnson just retired. Meanwhile, the Jaguars are playing good football, and I expect them to take care of business at home. Winner: Jaguars Indianapolis Colts at Pittsburgh Steelers — Sunday (Early Game) The Colts and Steelers are both 2-2 to start the season. Pittsburgh has struggled to put points on the board and Indianapolis has a few issues on defense. I don’t think any team has a clear advantage in this matchup. My gut is telling me to go with the Steelers here—so I’ll do that and take the home team. Winner: Steelers Cleveland Browns at New York Jets — Sunday (Early Game) Can you believe it? The Browns have reeled off three victories in a row. On the flip side, the Jets have lost three in a row after starting off the season with a victory. Cleveland does have some injuries on their offensive line that give me some concerns. Nevertheless, Deshaun Watson is playing decent, and rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston seems to make a big play every week. I’ll take the Browns here. Winner: Browns Cincinnati Bengals at Miami Dolphins — Sunday (Early Game) The Dolphins aren’t doing much on offense and their defense is one of the worst in the NFL. I don’t think Joe Burrow and his playmakers will have a problem scoring points against Miami. Easily one of the easiest picks for me in the Week 5 slate of games. Winner: Bengals Minnesota Vikings at New Orleans Saints — Sunday (Early Game) Surprise! The Vikings are 4-0 to start the season. Their offense has been hit or miss, but Brian Flores may be coaching the best defense in the NFL thus far. Given that, I think they will find a way to make it five in a row on the road against New Orleans. Winner: Vikings New York Giants at Washington Commanders — Sunday (Early Game) Somehow, even with all their injuries, the Giants are the top team in the NFC East. A lot of folks seem to be picking the Commanders in this one, but that defense is terrible and has allowed at least thirty points or more the past three contests. It’s hard to pick them with that in mind. I’ll be taking the G-Men. Winner: Giants Las Vegas Raiders at New England Patriots — Sunday (Early Game) After three quarters, it sure looked like the Raiders had the Kansas City Chiefs beat. However, Patrick Mahomes and Kenneth Walker II were able to work some fourth quarter magic and score 20 points to remain unbeaten. Meanwhile, the Patriots were able to edge the Buffalo Bills in a thriller. I didn’t expect that. Drake Maye performed quite a bit better against the Bills but needs to stop turning the ball over. All things considered, I’ll take New England at home. Winner: Patriots Houston Texans at Tennessee Titans — Sunday (Early Game) Oof. These two AFC South teams are winless to start the season. I honestly can’t believe Houston’s four-game skid to start the year. I thought they’d be doing much better than that. But somebody has got to win this one, right? Who will that be? I’m betting on the Texans. Winner: Texans Chicago Bears at Green Bay Packers — Sunday (Early Game) This is a classic NFC North matchup. Virtually nothing has gone right for Green Bay this year. They have some major issues on both sides of the ball. The Bears will be starting Tyson Bagent at quarterback who performed decently against the Jets last week. I’ve been impressed with Kyle Monangai. He has really stood out to me the past few weeks for the Bears. I’ll be taking Chicago on the road because they have a much better defense and can run the ball well. Winners: Bears Denver Broncos at Los Angeles Chargers — Sunday (Afternoon Game) The Broncos are coming off a tough loss to the San Francisco 49ers while the Chargers keep spiraling downward and are winless to begin their 2026 season. Both teams are struggling mightily on offense, but I have confidence in Denver’s ability to bounce back and earn their third win of the season. Winner: Broncos Detroit Lions at Arizona Cardinals — Sunday (Afternoon Game) The Lions defense is an absolute mess right now. You can say the same for the Cardinals who also have allowed over 110 points through four games. That being said, I feel confident in Detroit’s ability to outscore Arizona on the road and earn their third win of the season. Winner: Lions San Francisco 49ers at Seattle Seahawks — Sunday (Afternoon Game) This NFC West affair will determine who has the early lead in the division after Week 5. Both are really good teams that are scoring well and have solid defenses. The Seahawks may have the homefield advantage, but I’m a big fan of how Brock Purdy has been playing to start the season. I’ll roll the dice here and take the 49ers as road victors. Winner: 49ers Baltimore Ravens at Atlanta Falcons — Sunday Night Football The Falcons have earned back-to-back victories after starting out the season 0-2. Their recipe for success? Running the ball well and being the best run stopping defense in the NFL. The Ravens’ defense doesn’t look too great, but they can run the ball with authority with future Hall of Famer Derrick Henry. Winner: Ravens Buffalo Bills at Los Angeles Rams — Monday Night Football This game might be my favorite of the week. The Bills are coming off a loss to the Patriots, and the Rams were able to edge out the Eagles. Both teams have a few key injuries, but I like the Rams as the home favorites in this one. The Bills defense has struggled to keep their opponents at bay, but with Davante Adams and Puka Nucua will be back in the fold for the Rams’ offense. Winner: Rams

title: Courtland Sutton confident Broncos will find their way on offense
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country. Entering Week 5 of the NFL regular season, the Denver Broncos are 2-2. It’s certainly not where they hoped to be four games in. Yet being a .500 ball club given their tough slate of opponents isn’t a terrible spot. Moving forward, the Broncos have a lot to work on. That […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 27: Courtland Sutton #14 of the Denver Broncos warms up prior to the game against the Los Angeles Rams at Empower Field at Mile High on September 27, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country. Entering Week 5 of the NFL regular season, the Denver Broncos are 2-2. It’s certainly not where they hoped to be four games in. Yet being a .500 ball club given their tough slate of opponents isn’t a terrible spot. Moving forward, the Broncos have a lot to work on. That much is certain. It’s safe to say they haven’t played a complete game in all three phases thus far. They’ve struggled stopping the run on defense. After back-to-back franchise record setting seasons sacking opposing quarterbacks, Denver’s fearsome front seven haven’t been as potent rushing the passer. On special teams, the only bright spot has been Jeremy Crashaw and decent coverage units. Unfortunately, there have been several missed field goals, a big turnover that proved to be a backbreaker against the San Francisco 49ers, and few kick or punt returns that have given them quality field position. However, the lack of production and consistency on offense may be the most worrisome development to date. Prior to the season, many fans believed Nix and Denver’s offense was poised for a breakout campaign. The team added Jaylen Waddle to upgrade their wide receiver corps, drafted Jonah Coleman to bolster their rushing attack, and brought back their entire offensive line that ranked as one of the best in 2025. Those were all adequate reasons for fans to be bullish on their potential. Alas, the Broncos have started off slow—much like in years past. That has led to rightful criticism and concerns on how things will shake out as the season continues. Nevertheless, longtime wide receiver Courtland Sutton remains confident Denver has the players and coaching staff to get things back on track. “It is all right in front of us. We still have the utmost faith in our players and our abilities that we have and the coaches to put us in the right position. It’s just maximizing those opportunities when they do arise,” stated Sutton. Sutton placed the onus on himself and the rest of his teammates on offense to get things right. They know the talent is there; they just have to focus on the details and minimize the self-inflicted wounds and mistakes that have got them in an early-season rut. “From a player perspective, we can always do more. There are things here and there that we may not be fully dialed in on. There is a little bit of attention to detail that we need to tighten up as players. As a collective, we need to find a way to maximize the opportunities when they do pop and minimize the lack of attention to detail that may transpire over the course of a full game,” added Sutton. The opportunity to put their best foot forward presents itself on Sunday when the Broncos head to Los Angeles to take on the winless Chargers. There is no doubt that they have a lot of talent offensively. The question is can they finally live up to it? We are fixing to find out shortly. As always, thank you for reading. summary: The Broncos’ pass rush could have a boost this weekend. Well, the bad news continued on Wednesday when NFL Network’s lead league insider Ian Rapoport […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Joe Alt #76 of the Los Angeles Chargers in action against the Las Vegas Raiders at SoFi Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Inglewood, California. Well, the bad news continued on Wednesday when NFL Network’s lead league insider Ian Rapoport reported that their starting right tackle Joe Alt could miss Sunday’s game vs. the Broncos with a neck injury. #Chargers Pro Bowl OT Joe Alt is expected to miss this Sunday’s game against the #Broncos with a neck injury, sources say. Alt continues to rehab the injury suffered last week at Seattle, and there are no plans for IR. pic.twitter.com/qOVKtSmht7 — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 7, 2026 The Chargers have already lost their starting center; their starting left guard did not practice today with a fibula injury, and reserve Trevor Penning did not practice due to a concussion, while reserve Branson Taylor was limited with a neck injury. In other words, their offensive line, which was already struggling, is very banged up heading into Sunday’s game. It has been a tough start to the season for the Chargers, who sit at 0-4 and are the NFL’s most disappointing team to start the 2026 season. The addition of former offensive guru Mike McDaniels has not worked out, and the Chargers’ offense has not looked good at all. Now, with the annual offensive line injuries piling up, things could begin to snowball for the Chargers. This is where the Broncos’ pass rush needs to come alive. They have had a tough start facing Patrick Mahomes, Trevor Lawrence, Matthew Stafford, and Brock Purdy (who still hasn’t been sacked) and seem to be missing John Franklin-Myers and Jonathon Cooper. Nik Bonitto, Zach Allen, Jonah Elliss, Que Robinson, and the rest of the Broncos pass rushers need to dominate the Chargers’ offensive line and get back to their league-leading sack ways. They have had their struggles against the Chargers when Justin Herbert is starting, so hopefully, they can get things rolling on offense and defense this Sunday and improve to 3-2

title: Broncos HC Sean Payton tells reporters that he doesn’t believe that CB Pat Surtain II or WR Pat Bryant will be placed on the IR
summary: Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton met with the media today and gave an update on some notable injuries. He provided some good news and told reporters that neither cornerback Pat Surtain II nor wide receiver Pat Bryant is expected to land on the season-ending or short-term injured reserve. Both players left Sunday’s loss to […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - SEPTEMBER 20: Pat Surtain II (2) of the Denver Broncos prepares for the Jacksonville Jaguars offense during the second quarter at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Sunday, September 20, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton met with the media today and gave an update on some notable injuries. He provided some good news and told reporters that neither cornerback Pat Surtain II nor wide receiver Pat Bryant is expected to land on the season-ending or short-term injured reserve. Sean Payton doesn’t believe Pat Surtain or Pat Bryant will be placed on IR. Huge for the Broncos. pic.twitter.com/RrUEYG34hz — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) October 7, 2026 Both players left Sunday’s loss to the 49ers, and it did not look good. Surtain II left after a non-contact injury to his ankle, and many thought he suffered an achilles injury, while Bryant left on the cart, which is never good. Thankfully, we learned late Sunday Night and early Monday that both ankle injuries are not season-ending and are considered more short-term injuries. However, this did not rule out an eventual short-term IR stint for one or both players. Thankfully, despite the worst-case scenario seeming likely at one point, neither player is currently expected to land on the IR, which seems to point to them being back in a few weeks. The Broncos play their division rival, the Los Angeles Chargers, this Sunday before hosting the reigning champs, the Seattle Seahawks, on a short week on Thursday Night Football. I would assume both players will be out for these games, especially with the short week, but could be back for their road game vs. the Cardinals in Week 7. That is me just guessing, but that mini bye week after their Thursday Night game could be beneficial for these two. With Surtain and potentially Moss sidelined for Sunday’s game vs. the Chargers, look for former first-round pick Jahdae Barron to get the start, with reserve Kris Abrams-Draine seeing playing time as well. The defense will need both players to step up against Justin Herbert and the struggling Chargers offense. As for Bryant, look for veteran Lil’Jordan Humphrey to see some added playing time as a blocking receiver, while Marvin Mims Jr. and Troy Franklin see more snaps at the WR3 role. The Broncos’ passing offense has struggled, so they will need these three to step up. Overall, this is good news for the Broncos, who will need to get by and rely on their depth for a few weeks before these two key players return to the field.

title: Should the Broncos try to extend Brandon Jones?
summary: I was looking at the Denver Broncos salary cap situation heading into 2027 and realized there are two rather important decisions they need to make. One very soon and another before 2028. The first is safety Brandon Jones. So much emphasis was put around whether or not they should extend cornerbacks Riley Moss or Ja’Quan […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 04: Deebo Samuel Sr. #19 of the San Francisco 49ers is brought down by Brandon Jones #22 of the Denver Broncos after making a catch for a first down in the second quarter at Levi's Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images I was looking at the Denver Broncos salary cap situation heading into 2027 and realized there are two rather important decisions they need to make. One very soon and another before 2028. The first is safety Brandon Jones. So much emphasis was put around whether or not they should extend cornerbacks Riley Moss or Ja’Quan McMillian that I missed Jones being in the final year of his contract in 2026. He has played really good ball through the first four games and Denver is rather thin at safety behind the two starters. Of all of the position groups, safety is looking scary after this year with Jones potentially leaving and Talanoa Hufanga entering the final year of his deal. Honestly, I would say both of them should get extended. Jones is 28, so he is entering age wall territory, but I could see a three-year deal working out. Hufanga is just 26 and entering his prime. He has certainly proved he should be in Denver beyond 2028. What do you think? Should Denver just roll the dice and save the cap room or should they make safety a priority knowing the two starters they have really do lock down the back end of that defense? Broncos daily recap Broncos at Chargers preview: Denver hunts for first divisional win The Broncos head to LA on Sunday looking to rebound from a loss to the 49ers. Denver looks to keep the Chargers winless. Stats for the Broncos and the NFL after week four The Denver Broncos have somehow made it to 2-2. If you listen to the doomsayers, we have a terrible offense, a terrible defense, AND a QB who needs to be replaced. The combined record of the Bronco’s four opponents is 13-3 (2x 4-0, 3-1, and 2-2). Both losses were on the road. Both wins were at home. So let’s look at the team from a unit perspective at the quarter point of the season. Potent quotables Sean Payton Opening statement “Obviously just finishing up our first day here with the Chargers. Any questions?” On if WR Pat Bryant or CB Pat Surtain II could be placed on injured reserve “That’s jumping way ahead. I don’t think so, and if they were I wouldn’t say so, but I don’t think so.” On if he has noticed any issues with QB Bo Nix “No, listen and respectfully I understand. It’s hard for someone who just gets the All-22 and generally speaking, we’re all… Relative to the details of each play, that position’s performance will go up as we all are and the thing that I saw in the film was, yes, are there certain throws that from a timing standpoint he wants back? Yes. But I think collectively when you’re playing well on offense, you’re doing a lot of little things well, and then that job for him becomes somewhat easier. So that’s really the focus this week is the little things, detailing the little things and we’ll see that in the end product.” On what improvements he expects to see in the offense’s overall performance “I think running the ball efficiently, the play action passing game and then the route specifics relative to protection. That player… There’s so much that goes into making his job easier and then if you’re having trouble, for instance, with early-down efficiency, second-and-9 or third down-and-long, those would be a few that come to my mind right away.” On the importance of timing in a quarterback’s drop “There are some that are coming out quick with the three rhythm. I’m talking about if we’re in gun, some are more extended. We look all the time in great footwork on each play and depending on the depth of the route, that can change what the footwork of the route is.” On what stood out on film about CB Kris Abrams-Draine and CB Jahdae Barron “They’re savvy players, they both have good football instincts and IQ. One of the reasons you draft at that position is because it’s hard to find in free agency. So both were ready when they needed to be and that’s encouraging.” On whether young quarterbacks’ struggles are normal “I can’t speak for anyone else. In other words, I watch film of other teams and yes, we’re four weeks in and I think that I kind of get back to that these next two, three weeks are critical relative to our team as we looked at this from the beginning. The only way from my experience that I know how to improve, whether it’s the QBs play or the runners, is out here, but really with the specifics.” On RB RJ Harvey recording 10 receptions while WR Courtland Sutton had one “Some of it’s the soft zone coverage that went underneath. There are probably five different reasons to the team we played. Certainly, you come away from that game as a coach and you’re like, ‘All right, we have to find more touches for Courtland for “X” amount of receivers, even when they’re in these deeper zones. We’ll be able to do that, but we start with a mirror right away with ourselves. So we know he can be a factor for… He doesn’t have to be just outside, he can be inside depending on the route.” On the areas he believes need to be corrected “The things we’re just discussing now, the inconsistencies, the details of little things. It’s easy to say, ‘Look, we want a fast start.’ Well, who doesn’t? So let’s focus on the attention to detail and then the other stuff will come.” On what he attributes the slow starts to “It’s probably a combination of a bunch of things, but I’m not going to say it’s a script issue or… Some people have a long amount of openers, some not so. I think overall we’ve got to become experts in the details.” On if he changes the approach each week to address slow starts or continues emphasizing the same details “No, a lot of it depends on the defense we’re playing relative to the things we’re doing.” On what he sees from the Chargers and the challenge of facing a team playing with desperation “I buy into the notion in the NFL each week, you’re going to see teams that week-in and week-out, when you watch them play a number of their games… For me, it’s the scheme study, the personnel study and not as much the end result. They had five takeaways in Buffalo, they’ve been ahead in a number of games, they’ve started actually really well. So the focus really becomes on the personnel of the opponent and how they’re playing their defense and offense and kicking game.” On if Chargers Defensive Coordinator Chris O’Leary has maintained elements of former Defensive Coordinator Jesse Minter’s scheme “I would say they’re probably… Fair question. With two changes, I would say it’s probably a little bit more similar on defense than maybe than some of the stuff on offense.” On studying film of the Chargers’ defense from last season “Yes, I think they’re looking at that cut up. We’re looking at this year, but we’re looking at last year, yes.” On the similarities between Chargers Offensive Coordinator Mike McDaniel’s offense and 49ers Head Coach Kyle Shanahan’s “Yes, I would say the one common philosophy is you see that fullback and 21 personnel on the field like [49ers Head Coach] Kyle [Shanahan] likes. You see him in not just the traditional spots, you see him in a bunch of different spots. So I think there are some similarities there.” On if four games provide an accurate sample size to evaluate a play caller “I think our focus needs to be more on the specifics and the detail of each play regardless. I think [Offensive Coordinator] Davis [Webb] is very fast and quick and understands what we’re doing. So I appreciate the question, but I think that the most important job I have is really evaluating the why’s. I think collectively we all after a game… After a four-game sample size… All right, certainly this isn’t championship football or what we see, how quickly can we correct those things?” On if he reviewed film from the 2023 Broncos-Dolphins game to prepare for…

title: Broncos at Chargers preview: Denver hunts for first divisional win
summary: Your Denver Broncos sit at 2-2. Yet based on most of the commentary following the loss to the San Francisco 49ers, you’d think the Broncos are 0-4. Nope, but that’s the current state of affairs for Justin Herbert and the Los Angeles Chargers. That’s who’s on the docket for Bo Nix and Denver this Sunday. […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 04: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks on prior to the start of the game against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Your Denver Broncos sit at 2-2. Yet based on most of the commentary following the loss to the San Francisco 49ers, you’d think the Broncos are 0-4. Nope, but that’s the current state of affairs for Justin Herbert and the Los Angeles Chargers. That’s who’s on the docket for Bo Nix and Denver this Sunday. And much like the season-opening loss to the Kansas City Chiefs when they beat the Jacksonville Jaguars in the following game, the Broncos will look to rebound in Week 5 in LA. Denver is the current -3.5-point road favorite over the Chargers at FanDuel Sportsbook. The total sits at over/under 42.5 points, with a lean toward the over at -112. Offensive Rankings LA Chargers : Twenty-first in total offense (306.8 yards per game), ninth in rushing offense (121.5 YPG), 24th in passing offense (185.3 YPG), 29th in scoring offense (16.8 points per game). Denver : Twenty-seventh in total offense (280.3 yards per game), 29th in rushing offense (81.3 YPG), 20th in passing offense (199 YPG), 27th in scoring offense (18.5 points per game). Defensive Rankings LA Chargers : Sixteenth in total defense (333.5 yards per game), 22nd in rushing defense (121.8 YPG), 14th in passing defense (211.8 YPG), 24th in scoring defense (26.5 points per game). Denver : Twenty-eighth in total defense (375.0 yards per game), 29th in rushing defense (142.8 YPG), 21st in passing defense (232.3 YPG), 17th in scoring defense (23.5 points per game). Here are the MHR staff’s keys to Sunday’s game. Control the line of scrimmage on offense This is probably the biggest cliche when it comes to football, but it’s the truth. And goes back to the sport’s beginning. For Nix and the Broncos to have success on offense, the offensive line needs to control the line of scrimmage. Whether it’s run blocking or protecting Nix in the passing game, or “opening the playbook,” the guys up front must set the tone on Sunday. — Ian St. Clair Dial up the heat on Justin Herbert Justin Herbert has had a rough start to his 2026 season. He has more interceptions (six) compared to touchdowns (four) and has made a lot of bad decisions. With several key injuries to the secondary, the Broncos need their defensive front seven to rattle Herbert early and often. The Chargers have allowed twelve sacks in four games and could be without both their left tackle and left guard on Sunday. If Denver’s pass rush can force Herbert into bad decisions and cause turnovers, I really like Denver’s chances of earning its third victory of the season. — Christopher Hart Open up the offense I’m less interested in run/pass splits if the offense is moving the ball, but a key component of moving the ball is variety and dictating to the defense. If the run game is sucking up the linebackers, hit some play action leaks or digs and crossers behind them. Don’t be afraid to push the ball down the field. Shell coverage and two-high safeties aren’t a magic bullet and automatic check down. Go watch Dak Prescott dropping hole shots vs 2-man. It’s possible. The QB and OC just need to be on the same page and aggressive with the plan. You can’t win football games with screens and swings. Challenge the defense and dictate to them. — Jeffrey Essary Hunt with the football As Tim Jenkins likes to say, “Hunt with the football.” This is what I want to start seeing Bo Nix do in games. The Broncos have too much speed at wide receiver not to be taking shots downfield. The checkdowns work out a lot, but they stop working when teams don’t think you’ll put a dagger through the heart of their defense with chunk plays. — Tim Lynch Score more points than LA Advanced analytics show the Broncos are 2-0 when they score more points than their opponent and 0-2 when they do not. If they can score more points than the Chargers, my advanced analytical formula concludes that they have a 100% chance of winning and improving to 3-2. Pretty simple if you ask me! — Scotty Payne What are your keys to Sunday’s game?
author: Ian St. Clair

title: Stats for the Broncos and the NFL after week four
summary: The Denver Broncos have somehow made it to 2-2. If you listen to the doomsayers, we have a terrible offense, a terrible defense, AND a QB who needs to be replaced. The combined record of the Bronco’s four opponents is 13-3 (2x 4-0, 3-1, and 2-2). Both losses were on the road. Both wins were […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - SEPTEMBER 27: Kolbe Katsis #81 of the Denver Broncos runs with the football after receiving a punt during the third quarter against the Los Angeles Rams at Empower Field at Mile High on September 27, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos have somehow made it to 2-2. If you listen to the doomsayers, we have a terrible offense, a terrible defense, AND a QB who needs to be replaced. The combined record of the Bronco’s four opponents is 13-3 (2x 4-0, 3-1, and 2-2). Both losses were on the road. Both wins were at home. So let’s look at the team from a unit perspective at the quarter point of the season. Offense The Broncos are 27th in scoring. 26th in passing (by passer rating). 21st in passing EPA. 21st in ANYA. 21st in TD percentage. 19th in INT percentage. Suffice it to say that the passing offense overall has been in the bottom third or bottom quartile of the league. The offense is also the only offense in the NFL to get zero first downs on its first drive in every game this season (INT, punt, punt, and punt). The rushing offense has been comparable. 27th in YPC. The run game also has had almost no explosive plays. Denver run game has been pedestrian and mostly inept. 30th in % of runs that gained 6 or more yards. pic.twitter.com/0gUPZkeBWd — Joe Mahoney (@ndjomo76) October 5, 2026 Only 21.5 percent of the Broncos actual runs (removing kneel downs) have gained six yards or more. The Chargers have had the highest percentage at 33.9 percent so far this season. This does not bode well for our defense, which has given up a large percentage of runs for six or more this year. We’ll get to that in a bit. The defenses that the Broncos have faced so far are 2nd, 3rd, 7th, and 10th in points allowed. So at least offense is failing against good defenses. The Chargers defense is currently 24th. If the Bronco offense fails on Sunday, it’s completely the fault of the offense and not a result based on the strength of the opposing defense. The Broncos are tied for third worst with eight fumbles through four games. Only the Packers and the Chargers have more. This counts all fumbles so Kris Abrams-Draine’s and Talanoa Hufanga’s fumbles are counted in this. The Broncos only have five turnovers through four games. The Lions and the Jets lead the league in both only having one turnover so far. The Patriots and the Chargers are tied for the worst at 10. Defense The defense is currently 17th in scoring. 9th in ANYA. 5th passer rating allowed. 9th in QBhits. 20th in sack percentage. 3rd in completion percentage allowed. 30th in pressure rate on opposing passers. 15th in TD percentage. 10th in INT percentage. The Cowboys are the only defense in the NFL without an INT so far this season. The Bronco defense is 23rd in EPA, but 10th in pass defense EPA and 30th in run D EPA. The run defense has been bad. 27th in YPC allowed. 18th in TFL. The run D has allowed 32 gains of 6 or more yards. That is tied for 25th. The Cowboy defense has been the worst allowing 40 runs of 6 or more through 4 games. The Falcon defense has only allowed 11. The defense was really good last year at forcing 3-and-outs, forcing 61 during the regular season which was second on to the Texans defense in 2025. The Bronco D forced 61 3-and-outs in 17 games in 2025 which was second most in the NFL last season. They have only 7 in 4 games this season which is second to last. One pace for 30, which was the least last szn – WAS. pic.twitter.com/OmF2RqiAVK — Joe Mahoney (@ndjomo76) October 5, 2026 With seven through four games so far this season, the Bronco defense is on pace for 30. That would have made them dead last in 2025. One reason for this is that the Bronco defense is 27th in 3rd down percentage allowed so far this season – allowing conversion on 47.5 percent. The Lions are currently the worst at 52.8 and the Vikings are the best at 22.6 percent. The saving grace so far for the Bronco defense is the red zone defense. The Broncos have only allowed TDs on 50 percent of red zone drives. That’s tied for 7th best with the Browns. The Vikings are currently the best at 22.6 percent while the Packers are the worst at 85.7 percent. They have allowed TDs on 12 of 14 RZ drives so far this season. Special Teams Will Lutz has made five of seven FG attempts which is tied for 27th. The accuracy of NFL kickers has been good to start the season – 85.7% success. That includes 68 percent on attempts from 50+. Twelve teams have yet to miss a FG this season. Punting has been one of the bright spots for the Broncos (outside of late game heroics) so far this season. Jeremy Crawshaw has pinned opponents inside the 10 seven times through four games. That is two more than the nearest punters (three are tied with 5). Crawshaw getting 7 of 19 punts inside the 10 is mind-blowing – 37%. What’s crazy is that he only has two between the 10 and the 20 so his inside the 20 percentage is 11th. Matt Araiza has an inside the 20 percentage of 75 percent (9 of 12). None of Crawshaw’s punts have pinned opponent’s inside the five yet, although he was really close in the last game when the coverage team stepped on the goal-line for a touchback instead of getting one downed inside the one. Crawshaw has one other touchback. Two is not great, but one is the fault of the coverage team. I can’t remember the other. Nine punters have avoided a touchback so far this season. None of the seven of the opponent drives that started inside ten led to scores (2 INTs, 4 punts, 1 end of half). The punt coverage team is currently 5th allowing 7.5 yards per return. The KO coverage team is is 7th allowing 24.6 per return. The KO coverage team forced a fumble last game. The Bronco return game has been decent – 15th in punt return average at 9.6 yards and 8th in KOR average at 27.6 yards. There has been one punt and zero kickoff returns for a TD this season. Penalties Last season there were 3585 penalties in the 285 games during the regular and post season. That is 12.58 penalties per game. So far this season there have been 64 NFL games and there have been 963 penalties called. That’s 15.0 penalties per game. That’s a 20 percent increase in penalties in 2026 relative to 2025. There were 3565 penalties called in the 285 games in the full NFL season in 2025 – 12.58 per game. There have been 963 penalties called so far this season – 15.04 penalties per game. That's a 20% increase over last season. https://t.co/XfaeFlBZOe — Joe Mahoney (@ndjomo76) October 6, 2026
