title: Detroit Lions TE Sam LaPorta ‘optimistic’ about new contract despite stalemate
summary: Over the weekend, ESPN reported the Detroit Lions and tight end Sam LaPorta had cut off contract extension talks after failing to come an agreement in the first four weeks of the season. The report wasn’t clear on whether the two sides had a chance to re-enter talks before the season ends, or if the […]
full_text: Detroit Lions tight end Sam Laporta (87) talks to media members after practice during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Wednesday, July 29, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Over the weekend, ESPN reported the Detroit Lions and tight end Sam LaPorta had cut off contract extension talks after failing to come an agreement in the first four weeks of the season. The report wasn’t clear on whether the two sides had a chance to re-enter talks before the season ends, or if the sides would stand down until the offseason. On Wednesday, LaPorta offered his first public thoughts on the contract negotiations, offering a fair amount of optimism moving forward. Much of that optimism appears to come from the fact that he knows the Lions organization appreciates him. “I would like to think that I’m optimistic,” LaPorta said. “I say that with a smile because this is the organization that took a chance on me and drafted me and took me in. There was a very deep tight end class the year that I came out in 2023, and there’s been a lot of great tight ends that have come out of that class, some of which have gotten paid, some of which are younger than me and gotten paid, and that’s about all I can comment on other than, I’m going to keep doing my thing, keeping my head down and working hard.” This offseason, several tight ends from the 2023 draft class signed contract extensions with the team that drafted them, including Michael Mayer (three years, $45 million), Tucker Kraft (four years, $75 million), and Darnell Washington (four years, $42 million). LaPorta told reporters that he is not necessarily looking to become the highest-paid tight end in football, which is currently George Kittle (four years, $76.4 million). “I’ve never hung my hat on, like, being the highest paid tight end, being the first tight end to get drafted in my class, making the Pro Bowl, being first-team All-Pro,” LaPorta said. “I’ve always put all my chips in the pile of, ‘What can I do for the team?’ And those chips are still all there. And, like I said, I’m letting my agent and the front office handle the financial side of things, and when I feel like we’re a go, you guys will know. And I’m sure the news will break and everybody will shoot confetti in the air. It’ll be the whole thing.” Earlier in the day, Lions coach Dan Campbell said contract talks were the last thing on his mind. But he also made sure to again express his appreciation for what LaPorta brings to the table. “Just because there’s a report of that doesn’t mean that that’s some big issue, big deal,” Campbell said. “I love LaPorta. We love LaPorta. He’s a heck of a football player and I though he played his best game the other day. His work ethic, his production speaks for itself.” Still, there is obviously some road block in negotiations. LaPorta opened the door for conversations to continue during the season, but described the current status as a “stalemate.” “I don’t know if it’s truly off the table, but I think there’s certainly a stalemate right now,” LaPorta said. “I’m really giving the reins to my agent, Jack Bechta. He’s been handling it with the front office. All the advice he’s given me so far is that we just haven’t come to terms yet.” Despite what is likely a frustrating situation, LaPorta said it will not impact his game on the field, where his focus remains resolute. “That’s about all I can comment on other than I’m going to keep doing my thing, keeping my head down and working hard,” LaPorta said.
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: Brian Branch provides some optimism on Kerby Joseph
summary: On Wednesday, Brian Branch returned to practice after being sidelined for 10 months with an Achilles injury, giving the Detroit Lions one half of their Pro Bowl safety duo. Branch will likely take some time to acclimate, but he’s eager to get back on the field. “I want to be back my damn self, so […]
full_text: Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph (31), left, and safety Brian Branch (32) walk off the field after practice during mini camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Wednesday, June 17, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co On Wednesday, Brian Branch returned to practice after being sidelined for 10 months with an Achilles injury, giving the Detroit Lions one half of their Pro Bowl safety duo. Branch will likely take some time to acclimate, but he’s eager to get back on the field. “I want to be back my damn self, so I’m ready to be out there,” Branch said in the locker room on Wednesday. Lions coach Dan Campbell said “it’ll take a minute” for Branch to kick off the rust, considering he hasn’t had any practice reps in almost a full year. However, Branch feels like he’s already starting to acclimate just one practice in. And after learning from toe surgery rehab two years ago, he’s much more locked in mentally, too. “Shoot, I’m getting the rust off now in practice,” Branch said. “I feel good. Honestly, when I had surgery on my toe two years ago, coming back I was kinda in my head. But this time, I don’t know what transpired or what’s been going on with me, but I ain’t in my head. I’m ready to go.” Branch also offered some optimism about the other half of the Lions’ safety duo, Kerby Joseph. Joseph has been battling a knee injury for over a year, and his timeline for a return continues to get pushed back. But Branch believes Joseph will be back. “Kerb’s my dawg. We’ve been—we ain’t quitting, man,” Branch said. “Injured, we’ve been in this thing together for, what, 10 months, man? It’s been a long road. We’ve been fighting every day. He gonna be alright. He gonna be back. We’re gonna be back.” There is still no timeline for Joseph’s return. The last time coach Dan Campbell offered an update on Joseph’s condition, he only reiterated that they won’t put him out on the field until they’re confident his knee is healthy and protected. “I just know we were strengthening the knee and it wasn’t a setback, but there was a little time there where we weren’t able to do everything we needed to do. And so now we’re back at it,” Campbell said on Sept. 21. “And until we can get the knee to a certain point to where it feels strong, as strong as we can possibly get it, and he feels comfortable. We’re not going to put him out there until he’s ready.” In the meantime, the Lions’ safety room consists of Chuck Clark, Christian Izien, Jalen Mills (practice squad), and Bishop Fitzgerald. Earlier on Wednesday, Campbell indicated that they may lean more on Mills this week vs. the Cardinals.
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: Lions, Cardinals Week 5 injury report: Brian Branch, Cade Mays return to practice
summary: The Detroit Lions (2-2) will take on the Arizona Cardinals (1-3) in Week 5, and both teams took to the field on Wednesday to prepare. The Lions officially got some great news with two starters officially returning to practice to start their 21-day evaluation windows, while the Cardinals are dealing with a few injuries suffered […]
full_text: Detroit Lions safety Brian Branch (32) practices during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Thursday, August 21, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions (2-2) will take on the Arizona Cardinals (1-3) in Week 5, and both teams took to the field on Wednesday to prepare. The Lions officially got some great news with two starters officially returning to practice to start their 21-day evaluation windows, while the Cardinals are dealing with a few injuries suffered last game. Let’s take a look at Wednesday’s injury report and get you up to date with what we know. Note: Any changes from the most recent injury report will be bolded . Injured list updates RB Isiah Pacheco (MCL/Back) — IR, expected to be out until December C Cade Mays (Wrist) — IR, eligible to begin practicing at any time OL Giovanni Manu (Undisclosed) — NFI, eligible to begin practicing at any time S Brian Branch (Achilles) — PUP, eligible to begin practicing at any time S Kerby Joseph (Knee) — PUP, eligible to begin practicing at any time S Thomas Harper (ankle) — IR, eligible to begin practicing in Week 7 On Monday, coach Dan Campbell informed the media that Branch was in the final stages of medical clearance to return to practice , and on Tuesday during his weekly radio appearance on 97.1 The Ticket, Campbell disclosed that Cade Mays was also likely returning to practice this week . “He’s doing great,” Campbell said of Mays. “He and Branch are on the same plan right now. So the plan is to get them worked into practice. We’re waiting on the final call from the doctor on both to say, ‘Yes, they can practice.’ We’d love to get them going this week. Doesn’t mean they’re going to play (vs. Cardinals).” On Wednesday, both Branch and Mays indeed opened their 21-day evaluation windows by suiting up and practicing. The Lions now have 21 days to evaluate Branch and Mays’ health, and while they remain on PUP during this timeframe, Detroit is free to activate them to the 53-man roster at any time. “Well, it’d be good to get him out there running around and actually doing football work,” Campbell said of Branch on Wednesday. “He and Cade (Mays) both start their clocks and let them get back on the grass. And so yeah, it’s good. Anytime we can get some of our guys back off injury, that makes everybody happy.” N o practice G Ben Bartch (foot) DL Tyleik Williams (foot) — injured in Week 4 CB Rock Ya-Sin (Hamstring) — injured in Week 4 After starting in Week 2 for then-injured Christian Mahogany, Bartch hasn’t practiced since, missing a total of six practices and two games. By not practicing on Wednesday, and with the bye week looming in Week 6, it’s very possible the Lions won’t want to push his recovery process. Williams was injured late in Week 4 and was seen in the locker room wearing a protective walking boot, but told media in attendance that it was only for precautionary reasons. On Monday, Campbell was less optimistic, noting that “Tyleik is touch-and-go. He’ll be day-to-day.” He still has time to return to the field and play in this Sunday’s game, but this situation will be worth monitoring. Ya-Sin was injured on special teams in Week 4 and was ruled out after only a handful of snaps. Based on Campbell’s comments, Ya-Sin’s injury is a bit more concerning, as the Lions coach noted that he doesn’t “think Rock looks good right now.” If Ya-Sin can’t play, it should open the door for depth players, like rookie Keith Abney or veteran safety Jalen Mills, to potentially see more playing time. “Yeah, I think Abney will probably help us out a little bit more here this week,” Campbell said on Wednesday. “So, will Mills. I can see both those guys taking on a bigger role.” Limited practice C Cade Mays (Wrist) — Days remaining in evaluation window: 20 EDGE DJ Wonnum (back) S Brian Branch (Achilles) — Days remaining in evaluation window: 20 Wonnum missed last Wednesday’s practice but returned in full and played against the Panthers. He didn’t appear to suffer an aggravation during the game, so signs are pointing in a positive direction, despite a limited practice on Wednesday Full practice None listed No longer on the injury report CB D.J. Reed (rib) Reed was a limited participant at practice all last week but was able to play in Week 4. His injury could linger a bit, but with him being removed from the injury report, there’s no real reason for concern at this time. title: Dan Campbell reveals 2 Detroit Lions defenders who may play more vs. Cardinals
summary: Throughout the week, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell has talked about tweaks and adjustments they plan on making to their defense to pull them out of their current rut. Again, he has teased some personnel changes, and on Wednesday, he revealed two players who may get more playing time this week against the Arizona Cardinals. […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 04: Jalen Mills #27 of the Detroit Lions looks on before a football game against the Carolina Panthers at Bank of America Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Throughout the week, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell has talked about tweaks and adjustments they plan on making to their defense to pull them out of their current rut. Again, he has teased some personnel changes, and on Wednesday, he revealed two players who may get more playing time this week against the Arizona Cardinals. “I think (Keith) Abney will probably help us out a little bit more here this week. So, will (Jalen) Mills. I can see both those guys taking on a bigger role,” Campbell said. Abney, one of the team’s fifth-round picks this year, has only played 25 defensive snaps all season, all in the team’s season opener. In training camp, he was comfortably behind both Roger McCreary and Christian Izien at the nickel position. However, Detroit has already made several shakeups to the secondary that have opened this opportunity for him. Izien has been playing more at safety after the injuries to Avonte Maddox and Thomas Harper. Meanwhile, McCreary has been getting more opportunities at outside cornerback after the Lions benched Rock Ya-Sin two weeks into the season. If Abney takes over at nickel, it will be interesting to see what they do with the rest of their cornerback room. Campbell has also talked about giving more opportunities to Ennis Rakestraw after two promising situational roles in the last couple weeks. Could that mean pushing McCreary to the bench in favor of Rakestraw? Or is it possible the Lions are considering benching D.J. Reed and riding with Rakestraw and McCreary on the outside, with Abeny at nickel? Or this may just mean getting Abney some situational play at nickel, and nothing more. As for Mills, the team signed the veteran safety just two weeks ago after the injuries to the safety position. He played four snaps late in the Lions’ loss to the Panthers, working in both the box safety and nickel roles. He could take reps from Christian Izien, who has shown some struggles in both the run and pass game. Or he could also be a part of the nickel conversation. It’s probably worth mentioning there’s an outside chance that Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch could play on Sunday after returning to practice from an Achilles tear on Wednesday. However, coach Dan Campbell noted that it will take time for him to knock off rust, and Detroit typically gives players coming off a long-term injury at least a couple weeks of practice before playing them. We’ll have to wait until Sunday to see exactly what the Lions will trot out there in their secondary, but it certainly promises to be a significantly different lineup than in previous weeks.
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: Lions coach Dan Campbell hasn’t considered adding defensive assistant… yet
summary: As the pressure continues to mount on the Detroit Lions and defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard, one popular solution proposed by fans is to add a senior defensive assistant. On Wednesday, coach Dan Campbell said he hasn’t considered adding someone to the coaching staff. “Not at this moment, no I have not,” Campbell said. However, Campbell […]
full_text: Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell, left, talks to defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard during OTAs at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Friday, May 29, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co As the pressure continues to mount on the Detroit Lions and defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard, one popular solution proposed by fans is to add a senior defensive assistant. On Wednesday, coach Dan Campbell said he hasn’t considered adding someone to the coaching staff. “Not at this moment, no I have not,” Campbell said. However, Campbell did leave the door open for that possibility, noting that next week’s bye week could be an opportunity to re-assess everything. “Look, we’ve got another game here, and then I’m going to have a bye to be able to sit down for a minute, and not drink out of a fire hydrant,” Campbell said. “And that’ll help just a tic.” While adding a defensive assistant coach midseason is not a very common elixir to fixing problems, there is precedent of it working. Back in 2024, the Baltimore Ravens were struggling mightily under second-year defensive coordinator Zach Orr. In early October, Baltimore hired Dean Pees as a senior advisor, and the Ravens defense was drastically different down the stretch of the season. After allowing 25.2 points per game through five weeks, Baltimore allowed just 19.6 points per game after the hiring of Pees. In the meantime, the Lions head to Arizona this week to face a Cardinals team that is currently 17th in points scored, 31st in yards per play, and 17th in EPA/play. If Detroit’s defense—which currently ranks 31st in points allowed, 29th in yards per play, and 32nd in EPA/play—can’t hold them in check, it could mean changes are coming during their break.

(Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images After being significant players in the trade talks for Joey Porter Jr.—but ultimately missing out—the Detroit Lions must go back to the drawing board if they want to upgrade their struggling secondary. Last week, we offered our own suggestions that Lions general manager Brad Holmes should consider . On Wednesday, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler offered two more trade targets Detroit should consider . “One potential option is Kansas City’s Kristian Fulton , who is in and out of the Chiefs’ lineup,” Fowler wrote. “He is owed real money — $5 million of his $9.75 million base salary is guaranteed — but perhaps the Chiefs and Lions could split the bill to facilitate a deal. Is it worth calling Pittsburgh for Jalen Ramsey ? Not sure he’s available, but the Lions’ defense seems far from settled.” Let’s handle these one by one. Fulton was the Titans’ second-round pick in 2020. After starting 37 games over four years in Tennessee, he signed a one-year deal with the Chargers in 2024. There, he produced a strong season: 51 tackles, seven passes defended, an interception, and a 68.9 PFF grade, ranking him 32nd out of 80 qualifying cornerbacks. Fulton parlayed that success into a two-year, $20 million deal with the Chiefs last year, but it turned out to be a failed year for him. A knee injury caused him to miss most of the offseason program, he dealt with a Week 2 ankle injury, and then essentially lost his job. He was a healthy scratch for about a third of the season, playing in just eight games and starting two. This year, Fulton has played more, but is not a full-time player. He’s logged 115 defensive snaps through four games, including a Week 3 contest against the Dolphins in which he did not play a single snap for reasons that are unclear. Despite the part-time gig, Fulton has held up well. He’s produced a 76.0 overall PFF grade and a 76.4 coverage grade. He’s been targeted eight times and allowed just four catches for 19 yards and an interception—though he does already have two penalties. KRISTIAN FULTON PICKS OFF DANIEL JONES 🤯 The Chiefs CB jumps the route and wins the ball for the interception 🔥 pic.twitter.com/xnqtquheTE — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) September 21, 2026 Fulton’s usage is certainly peculiar, but it could suggest the Chiefs would be willing to move on. Fulton is a physical, handsy cornerback with average size (5-foot-11, 197 pounds) and acceptable speed (4.46 40-yard dash). As for Ramsey, his history of success is well documented. Since entering the league in 2016, he’s an eight-time Pro Bowler and three-time All-Pro. He’ll turn 32 later this month and certainly isn’t in the prime of his career, but he’s still producing at a strong level. From 2024-25, he produced 148 tackles, 19 pass breakups and three interceptions. But if you’re hoping that helps the Lions’ outside cornerback situation, he may not be the guy you’re looking for. Ramsey has mostly played as a nickel corner or safety with the Steelers this year—a transition he’s been making over the last two seasons. Could the Lions still use help at those positions? Absolutely. But if you want an upgrade on the perimeter, Ramsey is probably not the answer. As for financials, Ramsey wouldn’t come cheap. He’s currently sporting a $17.5 million salary—and that number jump to $19.7 in 2027 and $22 million in 2028—so it would likely be just a one-year rental for Detroit.

title: Detroit Lions scouting report: Arizona Cardinals better than their record shows
summary: Last week was called the “Petzing Bowl,” as Detroit Lions offensive coordinator Drew Petzing squared off against his brother, Dean Petzing, of the Carolina Panthers. This week, Drew Petzing plays his former team, the Arizona Cardinals, adding a little more drama to the matchup. After a Week 1 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers, the […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 04: Elijah Higgins #84 of the Arizona Cardinals celebrates with teammates after scoring a touchdown against the New York Giants during the third quarter at MetLife Stadium on October 04, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last week was called the “Petzing Bowl,” as Detroit Lions offensive coordinator Drew Petzing squared off against his brother, Dean Petzing, of the Carolina Panthers. This week, Drew Petzing plays his former team, the Arizona Cardinals, adding a little more drama to the matchup. After a Week 1 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers, the Cardinals have lost three straight, but don’t let the record fool you. This team has improved and has been playing good football, so don’t be surprised if this game turns into a shootout as both defenses struggle and the offenses keep it close. Let’s take a deep look at the Cardinals and how much they’ve changed ahead of Week 5. Arizona Cardinals 2025 season 3-14 record (4th in NFC West) 23rd in points for, 29th in points allowed Overall DVOA: 27th (24th on offense, 21st on defense) The Cardinals fell quickly in 2025. Quarterback Kyler Murray suffered a foot injury in Week 5, joining running back James Conner, who also suffered a foot injury in Week 3. Murray was replaced by veteran Jacoby Brissett, who did well under the circumstances he was in. Brissett threw for 3,366 yards, 23 touchdowns, and eight interceptions. He had to do a lot of the heavy lifting because he wasn’t getting help in the backfield, and he was constantly on his back, getting sacked 43 times; the Cardinals’ offensive line allowed 59 sacks overall, the fifth most in the NFL. The Cardinals had a lot of running backs start, with Michael Carter the most successful, leading the team with 333 yards and a touchdown. The team got a spark from Zonovan Knight, who ran for 269 yards and four touchdowns, but his season ended early as he suffered an ankle injury in Week 15 and was put on IR. With Brissett having to air it out, he leaned on tight end Trey McBride to carry the offense, finishing as the team’s leader in catches (126, setting an NFL record for tight ends) for 1,239 yards and 11 touchdowns. Wide receiver Michael Wilson had a breakout season, posting 78 catches for 1,006 yards and seven touchdowns. Second-year wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. finished with only 41 catches for 608 yards and four touchdowns. While the offense struggled, the defense tried its best to help. The Cardinals signed EDGE Josh Sweat in the offseason, and he was their best defender on the field, leading the team in sacks (12) and forced fumbles (four). He had a solid partner in crime in EDGE Calais Campbell, who, at 39, still got 6.5 sacks and was a presence on the defensive line. The secondary had some woes, but cornerback Denzel Burke led the team in interceptions (three) and pass deflections (11). Overall, once the wheels fell off the Cardinals offense, the rest of the season felt like a slow demise as they finished the year on a nine-game losing streak. Despite starting 2-0, the team finished 3-14, pushing their hopes to compete in the NFC to 2026. 2026 offseason Key additions: G Isaac Seumalo, RB Tyler Allgeier, DT Roy Lopez, WR Kendrick Bourne, LB Jack Gibbens, HC Mike LaFleur Key losses: QB Kyler Murray, S Jalen Thompson, DL Dalvin Tomlinson, DL Calais Campbell, OC Drew Petzing, HC Jonathan Gannon 2026 NFL Draft picks Round 1: RB Jeremiyah Love Round 2: G Chase Bisontis Round 3: QB Carson Beck Round 4: DT Kaleb Proctor Round 5: WR Reggie Virgil Round 6: LB Karson Sharar Round 7: OT Jayden Williams There was some drama for the Cardinals in the offseason. First, with the team falling flat on it’s face, head coach Jonathan Gannon was fired after finishing his career at 15-36 for three seasons. The Cardinals would move on and hire Los Angeles Rams offensive coordinator Mike LaFleur to be their new head coach. With Gannon gone, Petzing left Arizona to be the offensive coordinator for Detroit. Next, they moved on from Murray and had a contract standoff with Brissett, which ended with Brissett getting a reworked one-year deal for $21 million, $15.5 million guaranteed. The offensive line got some help at guard with the signing of Isaac Seumalo and the second-round draft pick of Chase Bisontis. With Conner still dealing with an injury, the team drafted running back Jeremiyah Love in the first round and signed Tyler Allgeier as a backup to add solid depth at the position. Arizona’s offensive shakeup didn’t stop there, as they signed wide receiver Kendrick Bourne and drafted wide receiver Reggie Virgil. Before signing Brissett to his reworked deal, the team drafted quarterback Carson Beck to help prepare for the future at the position. The defense took the biggest hit, losing safety Jalen Thompson and defensive linemen Dalvin Tomlinson and Campbell in free agency. Arizona countered those moves by signing defensive tackle Roy Lopez and drafting Kaleb Proctor. 2026 season thus far (1-3) Week 1: Defeated the Los Angeles Chargers 26-14 Week 2: Lost to Seattle Seahawks 31-7 Week 3: Lost to San Francisco 49ers 36-30 Week 4: Lost to New York Giants 36-24 Stats: 17th in points scored, 29th in points allowed Overall DVOA: 18th (12th on offense, 29th on defense, 4th on special teams) The season started with a bang for the Cardinals, who beat the Chargers on the road. They came down to earth the following week against the defending Super Bowl Champion Seattle Seahawks, losing by 24. Arizona didn’t let that loss deter them much, as they kept up with one of the three undefeated teams left in the NFL, the San Francisco 49ers, and almost pulled off another upset. Finally, against the New York Giants, they lost on the final play when Brissett attempted a fourth-down touchdown pass, but it was picked off and returned for a touchdown. Brissett has had a decent start to the season, throwing for 818 yards, six touchdowns, and four interceptions. Three of those interceptions came against the Giants, so he was doing well protecting the ball until last week. He’s been asked to carry the load as the running game hasn’t taken off yet, but it’s showing signs of improvement while Conner is still on the sidelines. Love leads the team in rushing yards with 223, averaging 4.1 yards per carry and a touchdown. Allgeier has 112 yards, averaging 3.5 yards per carry and a touchdown. The run game could certainly be better and ease some pressure off Brissett as he tries to carry the offense with his arm. The team’s current leading receiver is Wilson with 25 catches for 258 yards and a touchdown, but McBride is still Brissett’s go-to option. He leads the team in targets (46) and catches (33) for 242 yards and two touchdowns. Teams know McBride is the lifeblood of the passing game, and limiting his production forces Brissett to go elsewhere. Harrison got his first touchdown of the season against the Giants in Week 4, but he still has only five catches for 85 yards. While the offense has shown signs of life and moving the football, the defense hasn’t gotten that memo since Week 1. After the win over the Chargers, the Cardinals have allowed over 30 points in their last three games. Their last in the NFL in passing yards per attempt with 9.1, tied with the Lions and Washington Commanders for most passing touchdowns allowed (11), and have the second-highest QBR rating allowed at 114.9. Their best defensive player, safety Budda Baker, is everywhere for them this season, leading the team in sacks (1.5), tied for most interceptions (one), and tied for most pass deflections (three). He is the heartbeat of this defense and is playing what he is worth, while others haven’t been up to par. Sweat is off to a slow start (seven tackles and 1.0 sack) this season. Arizona’s defense is similar to Detroit’s, where opposing quarterbacks seem to have their way. Heck, they allowed Giants backup quarterback Jameis Winston to throw for…

title: 5 Lions vs. Cardinals thoughts after watching Arizona’s loss to Giants
summary: To help turn the page from the Detroit Lions’ previous game and set up expectations for the upcoming matchup, I spend some of my Tuesday watching the Lions’ next opponent’s most recent game. While it’s only a small snapshot of the team’s season, it provide a look at how they’re playing right now. I take […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 04: Basil Okoye #99 of the New York Giants sacks Jacoby Brissett #7 of the Arizona Cardinals during the second quarter at MetLife Stadium on October 04, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images To help turn the page from the Detroit Lions’ previous game and set up expectations for the upcoming matchup, I spend some of my Tuesday watching the Lions’ next opponent’s most recent game. While it’s only a small snapshot of the team’s season, it provide a look at how they’re playing right now . I take notes during the watch, then I compare those notes with some statistical outputs from the entire season to see if what I’m watching is congruent with how this team has been regularly playing or perhaps an outlier. So here are my thoughts on the 2026 Arizona Cardinals, and what it may mean for Sunday’s matchup with the Lions. Cardinals run game is only finding success on the perimeter… but that’s not good for Detroit This offseason, Arizona invested in their running game by signing RB Tyler Allgeier, drafting Jeremiyah Love, and signing guard Isaac Seumalo. But the overall impact of those additions have yet to be felt. The Cardinals sport a 3.9 yards per carry average (20th) and rank 13th in rush EPA. Against the Giants, they did finish with 123 rushing yards and 4.7 yards per carry, but almost none of that success was up the gut. However, stretch running plays to the outside were wildly successful, and if you look at their season-long numbers, they match what we saw in this game. They’re producing an impressive +0.26 EPA/rush outside the left tackle (fourth best) and +0.36 EPA/rush outside the right tackle (second) —while producing negative numbers pretty much everywhere else. Meanwhile, the Lions have been terrible at defending perimeter runs . They’re allowing +0.36 EPA/rush outside left tackle (second worst) and +0.17 EPA/rush outside right tackle (fifth). Detroit will need their defensive backs to play much more disciplined run defending on the edge. I’m looking at you, Christian Izien. Also, be on the look out for QB sneaks and tush pushes in short-yardage situations. Jacoby Brissett is 6-foot-4, 235 pounds, and it makes him very effective at that play. Jacoby Brissett crumbling under pressure I thought the Cardinals’ offensive line did a pretty good job when the Giants sent just four defenders in their pass rush. Considering New York has a pretty formidable front (albeit without Brian Burns in this game), I thought Brissett had fairly comfortable pockets. The Giants managed just a 17.6% pressure rate without blitzing, ranking 29th in Week 4. However, the Giants opted to crank up the blitz rate (51.3%, fifth), and the Cardinals didn’t have an answer. New York produced a 55.0% pressure rate when blitzing (eighth highest). Brissett is simply not a very good quarterback when the blitz is coming. He either checks down far too quickly (6.2 average depth of target, 27th out of 29 qualifying QBs) or is too risky with the football. Against the Giants, Brissett produced this statline under pressure: 6-of-12 for 53 yards, 1 TD, 2 INTs, and 50.3 passer rating. For the season, it’s even worse. Doesn’t matter whether the pressure is coming from a blitz or just a four-man runs: -0.32 EPA/dropback vs. blitz (25th out of 29) +0.01 EPA/dropback vs. no blitz (17th) -0.67 EPA/dropback vs. pressure (25th) +0.17 EPA/dropback vs. no pressure (17th) The Lions have been an abysmal defense in any situation, but particularly when blitzing. If Detroit can continue to generate pressure with just four—especially with Cardinals left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. now out for the year—I wouldn’t be surprised if they can generate some negative plays or turnovers. Cardinals defense found some pressure answers after rough start Going into the Giants game, the Cardinals’ defense was getting dragged publicly for their terrible pressure rate . For the season, the Cardinals still rank just 29th in pressure rate (30.3%). But against the Giants, they started to find some answers, and sacked Jameis Winston four times. The biggest solution was relatively simple: get more aggressive. The Cardinals upped their season-long blitz rate of 23.8% (23rd in NFL) to 30.3% and produced pressures on 40.0% of those blitzes (19th best). Detroit didn’t handle the blitz particularly well against the Panthers, but if they can, that is the key to beating this Cardinals defense. When Arizona cannot produce pressure, opposing quarterbacks are killing them. With no pressure, the Cardinals are allowed +0.50 EPA/pass (30th) and 9.6 yards per play (32nd). That’s because their primarily zone defense starts to fall apart when quarterbacks have time to process the coverage. With pressure, the Cardinals still aren’t great, but they’re better—ranking 29th in EPA/pass (-0.10) and 24th in yards per play (4.4). Run defense could give Detroit problems The Lions have run the ball very consistently this year, and the Cardinals present one of the tougher matchups thus far. They held the Giants to just 87 yards on 28 carries (3.1 YPC), and New York didn’t have a rush of over 9 yards. Now, New York has one of the worst rushing attacks in football through four weeks, ranking 24th in EPA and success rate, but for the season, the Cardinals have done a pretty good job. Arizona ranks fourth in rush EPA defense and 11th in success rate. Although the better rushing teams in football didn’t have a ton of issues against them (Seahawks: 162 yards, 4.1 YPC; 49ers: 140 yards, 6.1 YPC). The Lions aren’t ever going to go into a game expecting to abandon the run, but it’s clear to me that the bigger mismatch is through the air this week. Tight ends aren’t just about Trey McBride Yes, Trey McBride is arguably their biggest weapon in the passing game. He currently has 33 catches for 242 yards and two touchdowns. That is going to be a problem for a Lions defense that is surrendering 407 receiving yards (31st) and six touchdowns (32ng) to tight ends through four games. However, the Cardinals use 13 personnel (one running back, three tight ends) at a higher rate than everyone other than the Rams and Bills. That’s because they’ve got some dudes at that position beyond McBride. PFF’s highest-graded tight end in football through four weeks is actually Elijah Higgins (89.3 grade) because of his outstanding run blocking (77.0, second among TEs). Hunter Long has been their third tight end, and he’s also been a big asset in the running game (72.0 run blocking grade, 10th). Unfortunately, he was placed on IR this week, leaving Teagan Quitoriano to be the TE3 this week. Quitoriano has yet to play a game for the Cardinals this year, and his history suggests he’ll be a pretty significant downgrade.

title: Lions vs. Panthers Song of the Game: ‘War’ by Townland
summary: After every Detroit Lions game this season, someone on staff will select a song that incorporates the general feeling and vibes from the win or loss. By the end of the season, we will have a Spotify playlist that tells the full story of the 2026 Detroit Lions season. In Week 4, the Lions fell […]
full_text: Detroit Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard reacts to a play against Washington Commanders during the second half at Northwest Stadium in Landover, Md. on Sunday, November 9, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co After every Detroit Lions game this season, someone on staff will select a song that incorporates the general feeling and vibes from the win or loss. By the end of the season, we will have a Spotify playlist that tells the full story of the 2026 Detroit Lions season. In Week 4, the Lions fell to the Carolina Panthers in humiliating fashion. Buckle up, we’re going to war. Week 4 Detroit Lions Song of the Game: ‘War’ by Townload So put up your dukes, we’re goin’ to war Ready the nukes, it’s DEFCON 4 When the Lions’ defense kicked off the season, they were declaring war on opposing offenses. Kelvin Sheppard’s initial vision of the defense was going HAM on quarterbacks. The defensive front was stunting, twisting, creating havoc. Detroit was sending aggressive blitzes and disguising their coverages. Unlike previous years, Detroit wanted to be assertive, unpredictable, and dictate the game on both sides of the ball. So armed with a 43.0% blitz rate, the Lions hoped to bring a nuclear attack to Tyler Shough and the Saints offense, and for the first half, it worked. But then the holes in the defense started to appear. Shough and the Saints came blazing back, and some uneasiness started to seep in. Was the first half a mirage, or the second? DEFCON 3 Assemble the troops, send in the corps To hell with détente, all I want is war We cranked up the panic meter after Josh Allen dismantled Sheppard’s defense from kickoff to handshakes. It shook us to our core, and it sent the Lions scrambling into their mini bye week. But also… it’s Josh Allen, wadda ya gonna do? Dan Campbell promised to come out of the break with a new plan, some new soldiers, and a reinvigorated spirit. It was far too early in the season to declare defeat. You better watch out, New York Jets. The Lions are ready to put a hurting on your obviously inferior squadron. You broke the rules of engagement and Rebuilt your ranks without so much as a thanks And now we’re at it hand-to-hand But I don’t want to fight anymore DEFCON 2 The Lions came out of the mini-bye with a fairly reformed defense (reformed does not necessarily mean better). They put down their fancy weapons of overly complicated blitzes to help their missile defense, shuffled their servicemen, and just tried to attack the Jets with plain, sound, hand-to-hand defense. Again, it worked until it didn’t. If it weren’t for a late sneak attack from Sergeant Clark, we may have already reached DEFCON 1. DEFCON 1 You’ve broken the sanctions that we swore But I reap what I sow ’cause all I know I reap what I sow ’cause all I know I reap what I sow ’cause all I’ve known is war Six months ago, Sheppard bragged of his offseason project . He spent all offseason watching the 2025 film and promised sweeping changes. Gone would be the explosive plays. The run defense would rise from the ashes of the Rams and Steelers games. He even watched tape from the best defenses to steal and incorporate their tactics . But a month into the season, those promises have already been properly dashed . Detroit’s defense has given up the highest rate of explosive plays (9.2%) , the second-highest rate of explosive run plays (15.5%), and the 12th-highest explosive pass rate (5.6%). And I fell for it all. I liked what they did at safety and defensive line this offseason to improve those units. I was intrigued by the new things they were doing in training camp. I was encouraged by how well they performed in practice. I should have known better. Ever since Ndamukong Suh chose Miami money over a hometown discount, this franchise has known nothing but pain and suffering on defense. For a dozen years, Detroit has been fighting a war just to climb to defensive mediocrity, and I fear it’s an endless one. If you want to relive previous Lions seasons, you can find the playlists we curated below: 2016 , 2017 , 2018 , 2019 , 2020 , 2021 , 2022 . And if you want to read previous versions of our Song of the Game columns, you can find those here .

The good news here? If the Packers are out all of those offensive linemen, the team […]
full_text: (Photo by Adam Bettcher/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers had four players listed as non-participants on their first injury report of the week: left running back Chris Brooks (ankle), guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe), offensive lineman Jager Burton (back) and offensive lineman Jacob Monk (quadricep). The good news here? If the Packers are out all of those offensive linemen, the team can still play dress eight players at the position on game days, as they’re “oversigned” at the position currently . In other good news, receiver Savion Williams began practicing on Wednesday and his 21-day window to return from the injured reserve has now opened up. Williams, listed with an ankle injury, was a limited participant in practice. Joining Williams as a limited participant were right tackle Anthony Belton (knee), defensive lineman Anthony Campbell (ankle), defensive lineman Devonte Wyatt (ankle) and edge defender Lukas Van Ness (shoulder). All of those limited players were able to finish the game against Tampa Bay last week, except Campbell — who was inactive last week due to injury. Cornerback Brandon Cisse, who left the Buccaneers game with a neck injury, was a full participant on Wednesday. Assume that he’ll return to his starting role at right cornerback, where he played during his rookie season. The Chicago Bears were a bit more banged up for their Wednesday practice, as offensive lineman Jonah Jackson (ankle), running back Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe), running back D’Andre Swift (hip/knee), offensive lineman Joe Thuney (pectoral), quarterback Caleb Williams (hamstring) and offensive lineman Darnell Wright (ankle) were all non-participants today. The Bears have opened up the practice windows on three players: cornerback Kyle Gordon (calf), linebacker Noah Sewell (Achilles) and defensive lineman Shemar Turner (knee). Gordon was a full participant, Sewell was a non-participant and Turner was a limited participant on Wednesday. full_text: (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Green Bay Packers worked out five linebackers on Wednesday, after working out two on Tuesday who were not signed by the team. This time around, the batch produced a signing: former Cincinnati linebacker Jack Dingle has joined the Packers’ practice squad. Green Bay no longer had an off-ball linebacker on their practice squad, as they brought up special teams contributor Kristian Welch to the 53-man roster when the team moved Edgerrin Cooper, who tore his Achilles tendon, to the injured reserve for the remainder of the season. As of now, there is no word on which practice squad player has been released to make room for the signing of Dingle. Previously, the Packers’ 17-man practice squad was full, following the re-signing of running back Damon Bankston on Tuesday. Here’s a current count of Green Bay’s practice squad, which will need to be cut down by one player by tomorrow: QB: Kedon Slovis RB: Pierre Strong Jr. and Damon Bankston WR: Isaiah Neyor, Quincy Skinner Jr and Coleman Owen TE: Drake Dabney OL: Mekhi Becton Sr., Dalton Cooper, Josh Gesky and Dillon Wade DL: David Blay Jr. ED: Nyjalik Kelly and Arron Mosby LB: Jack Dingle CB: Domani Jackson S: Kahlef Hailassie K: Lenny Krieg (international exemption) P: None LS: None Jack Dingle is a LB prospect in the 2026 draft class. He scored a 9.82 RAS out of a possible 10.00. This ranked 65 out of 3460 LB from 1987 to 2026. https://t.co/FvjagUF5bb pic.twitter.com/gGoxszCYea — RAS.football (@MathBomb) April 6, 2026 Dingle was undrafted in the 2026 class and signed with the local Cincinnati Bengals as a UDFA. title: The Packers’ running back problems are on full display
summary: In an enjoyable turn of events this past Sunday, the Green Bay Packers’ offensive line was completely fine. Through three games, the Buccaneers ranked fourth in the NFL in opponent rushing success rate, creating what should have been a very steep challenge for the running game. This was of little surprise as for much of […]
full_text: (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images In an enjoyable turn of events this past Sunday, the Green Bay Packers’ offensive line was completely fine. Through three games, the Buccaneers ranked fourth in the NFL in opponent rushing success rate, creating what should have been a very steep challenge for the running game. This was of little surprise as for much of nose tackle Vita Vea’s career, the Buccaneers have been a very stout run defense. But on Sunday, Green Bay’s offensive line was fine. They weren’t good, but they were fine. The Packers had a 56th percentile rushing success rate against Tampa, but it frankly should have been higher, and the EPA-per-rush was destroyed by a self-induced red zone fumble as the Packers were about to put the final nail in the coffin. The running backs remain a massive problem. On the fumble, these are just really poor fundamentals from Kaleb Johnson. Near the goal line, you have to be going through the traffic with two hands on the ball. The only way Tampa has a chance in the game is if they force a turnover here. And instead he just keeps it in one, and has it stripped out from the side where there is the greatest threat. These are mistakes that just can’t be made at the college level, let alone in the NFL. lmao pic.twitter.com/2IUqaAlKHD — rcon14 (@rcon14) October 7, 2026 Here is Chris Brooks’ big carry on the day, and one where the front really does make it easy. The alley is clean, and then Brooks is able to get a big chunk play. You can see once he gets into space, though, he just doesn’t have any juice. Winfield is not particularly fleet of foot as a safety, but there’s really no threat that he’s going to lose the angle. Brooks is a lot of things, but he’s not a value-add as a ball carrier. no meep pic.twitter.com/QDTZx9dgtB — rcon14 (@rcon14) October 7, 2026 Here is just another example of Marshawn Lloyd’s persistent tendency to want to bounce everything at the first sign of conflict. when it doubt, always try to bounce pic.twitter.com/LSGaALSAgK — rcon14 (@rcon14) October 7, 2026 In Lloyd’s defense, this is a really poor rep from Jordan Morgan, who gets pushed into the backfield. It’s not helped by the tight ends not cleaning up the backside of the play where Lloyd eventually tries to bounce. But also… stop bouncing everything. Morgan is pushed, but he’s not beaten. If Lloyd drives this play-side, there actually is a hole that the right side created. It has Antoine Winfield Jr. at the end of it, but that’s the job. Lloyd is a stoutly built running back. Attack the defensive back near the goal line. Stop [redacted] bouncing everything. In defense of Lloyd’s bouncing, it did come in handy once. Tucker Kraft completely blew this play, getting beat across his face. It’s not an easy block for a tight end against an edge defender, but it’s one that has to be made for the play to work. Lloyd actually bounces this back weak-side and turns it into a decent gain. Tucker, pal pic.twitter.com/G9QQ64ENlj — rcon14 (@rcon14) October 7, 2026 The thing that may drive me most nuts about the running back room right now is that while they are taking a bunch off the table when it comes to vision and fundamentals, they’re also not putting anything on the table. This here is a pretty basic duo play. The whole reason Jonnu motions to the wing is to carry the cornerback into the hole. The play is designed to get Johnson one-on-one with a cornerback. And he doesn’t do anything with it. He doesn’t even really try to. Kaleb, that's a cornerback. Please. pic.twitter.com/younrERCIr — rcon14 (@rcon14) October 7, 2026 The Packers are clearly just waiting for Josh Jacobs to return from the exempt list/suspension, but I don’t know how long they can keep rolling this out. This isn’t replacement-level running back play; it’s sub-replacement level, and it’s really stretching how you can even build a coherent offense.

title: Kevin Zeitler takes starting right guard reps for Packers on Wednesday
summary: Last Sunday, Travis Glover did an admirable job filling in as the Green Bay Packers’ right guard in the team’s win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The offensive line as a whole looked more cohesive than it had through the first three weeks of the season with Glover and veteran acquisition Laken Tomlinson as the […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - SEPTEMBER 20: New York Giants offensive guard Kevin Zeitler (70) battles with Chicago Bears defensive tackle Akiem Hicks (96) in action during a game between the Chicago Bears and the New York Giants on September 20, 2020 at Soldier Field in Chicago, IL. (Photo by Robin Alam/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Last Sunday, Travis Glover did an admirable job filling in as the Green Bay Packers’ right guard in the team’s win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The offensive line as a whole looked more cohesive than it had through the first three weeks of the season with Glover and veteran acquisition Laken Tomlinson as the starting guards, though the bar to clear was extraordinarily low. Heading towards the Packers’ Week 5 matchup with the Chicago Bears, however, it appears that another veteran is preparing to start at right guard. On Wednesday, Kevin Zeitler lined up in that position with the Packers’ number one offensive line unit , a clear signal that the team expects him to be the starter on Sunday afternoon. This tracks with Matt LaFleur’s comments after his signing, when the head coach said “ as soon as (Zeitler) feels good and ready to go, he’ll be in there ” as the starter. Zeitler starting against the Buccaneers would have been a particularly big ask of a player who is both fresh off the street and recently finished rehab on a quad injury. Not only did he only sign last Wednesday, limiting the time he had to pick up the Packers’ playbook, but the game was taking place in extremely warm weather and on the road. All of the cards were stacked against him playing last week, but those factors are now all gone. With his insertion into the number one offensive line, Zeitler will have all week to prepare to start against Chicago. The weather is expected to be unseasonably warm in Green Bay this weekend — as of the time of this publication, the expected high according to the Weather Channel on Sunday is 80 degrees Fahrenheit — but the game is at home, limiting any travel complications. If there were any additional question about who the team sees as its starting right guard, the depth chart on the team website should put that to rest. Zeitler is listed on the starting line, with Jacob Monk as the backup and Donovan Jennings on the third string. Zeitler’s arrival may have already paid dividends in the classroom. A line that looked much more stable against the Buccaneers has already seemed to benefit from him passing along some veteran experience in meetings last week. Putting him on the field this Sunday should only further benefit the offense as a whole.

title: Packers WR Savion Williams returns to practice Wednesday
summary: One of the two players who the Green Bay Packers placed on injured reserve before the season with a return designation is officially on his way back. On cutdown day in August, the Packers put second-year wide receiver Savion Williams on injured reserve to open up a roster spot; on Wednesday ahead of week five, […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 13: Savion Williams #83 of the Green Bay Packers in action during the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Acrisure Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the two players who the Green Bay Packers placed on injured reserve before the season with a return designation is officially on his way back. On cutdown day in August, the Packers put second-year wide receiver Savion Williams on injured reserve to open up a roster spot; on Wednesday ahead of week five, Williams has returned to practice. Head coach Matt LaFleur announced Williams’ return during his morning press conference, confirming that his three-week practice window will begin immediately. Under the NFL’s roster rules, the Packers now must activate Williams and move him to the 53-man roster within the next 21 days or else he will revert to injured reserve and will be ineligible to return for the remainder of the season. LaFleur added that the Packers may consider activating Williams as soon as this week for Sunday’s game against the Chicago Bears. What role Williams will play if and when he returns is uncertain, however. The Packers have a firmly entrenched pair of boundary receivers in Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, while Skyy Moore has settled in as the primary slot receiver since Jayden Reed was lost for the season in Week 2. The team’s current depth chart lists J. Michael Sturdivant as Golden’s backup and Bo Melton as the backup behind both Watson and Moore. However, given Williams’ size-speed combination and his potential blocking ability, he may be in line to serve as Watson’s backup with Melton focusing on returning more to a slot receiver role. Green Bay seems content to roll with their top three options at this point, however. Of the 120 total snaps given to wide receivers in Week 4, Melton and Sturdivant combined for just 12. What is also unlikely is Williams getting the number one kick returner job back. Moore has done an admirable job on punt returns (8 attempts for 128 yards, a 16-yard average) and has been reasonably solid on kickoff returns with a 27.5-yard average. That kick return average ranks Moore 14th out of 50 qualifying players in the NFL, a number that certainly suggests that no change is imminent. Given Williams’ numbers from a year ago, Moore should have a firm handle on this job moving forward; as a rookie, Williams averaged 25.6 yards per kickoff return, nearly two yards fewer than Moore’s average. The Packers may try to find ways to get Williams onto the field on offense as a different look. Last season, he caught 10 passes for 78 yards and one touchdown while rushing the football 11 times for 37 yards. But don’t expect his eventual return to shake up the depth chart or the distribution of snaps among the wide receivers very much.

title: Packers vs. Bears Week 5 TV Broadcast Map
summary: At the beginning of the 2026 NFL season, the Week 5 matchup between the Green Bay Packers and Chicago Bears looked set to be one of the biggest regular season games on the schedule. The two teams played three thrilling games in 2025, including a Wild Card matchup that went Chicago’s way after a late […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - DECEMBER 20: A FOX Sports broadcast camera operator prepares to perform their duty before a regular season game between the Green Bay Packers and the Chicago Bears on December 20, 2025, at Soldier Field in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Joseph Weiser/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images At the beginning of the 2026 NFL season, the Week 5 matchup between the Green Bay Packers and Chicago Bears looked set to be one of the biggest regular season games on the schedule. The two teams played three thrilling games in 2025, including a Wild Card matchup that went Chicago’s way after a late comeback. As a result, FOX claimed the game and seemed confident that it would remain one of the premier matchups this season, likely set to feature it as the Game of the Week in the late afternoon time slot. Fast-forward a few weeks and we find that this game has been flexed out of the featured time slot and back to an early kickoff at 12 Noon Central Time. The Packers stumbled out to a 2-2 start while Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is injured and will miss the game. Instead, FOX will feature 49ers-Seahawks, another divisional battle but one between two hot teams, as the main game in the late window instead. Still, a large portion of the USA will still be able to see Packers-Bears, particularly areas in the Central, Mountain, and Pacific time zones. Fans living in the Eastern time zone, however? You may be out of luck; Giants-Commanders and Bengals-Dolphins will take up much of the Eastern seaboard and Appalachia respectively, while Vikings-Saints claims a good portion of the southeast (as well as Minnesota and the Dakotas in the Central Time zone). Here’s this week’s broadcast map from 506sports.com, showing Packers-Bears in red: The Packers do get a bit of an upgrade on the commentators from their last two noon games, however. Both of those games (against the Jets and Saints) got FOX’s “C” team, both with Jonathan Vilma on the call as the color commentator. This week they get the “B” squad, which features Kenny Albert and Greg Olsen on the call. Albert is normally paired with Vilma, but he gets bumped up a notch again this week due to Olsen’s usual play-by-play partner, Joe Davis, covering baseball playoffs as FOX’s top commentator for that sport. Still, Olsen is a massive upgrade over Vilma for the ears of Packers fans this week. As usual, Packers fans whose home TV markets get other games will need to find alternate options to watch this week’s contest. NFL Sunday Ticket is the primary option, with the service still offering a 7-day free trial for new subscribers.

title: Green Bay Packers News: Zaire Franklin takes center stage
summary: You can count me among the people who were initially skeptical of the Zaire Franklin acquisition. Brian Gutekunst seems to have had an over-obsession with linebackers ever since De’Vondre Campbell’s out-of-nowhere All-Pro season in 2021, and his move to add Franklin as a replacement for Quay Walker, then reward him with a reworked contract, seemed […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - SEPTEMBER 24: Zaire Franklin #44 of the Green Bay Packers looks to defend during the first half of the NFL game against the Atlanta Falcons at Lambeau Field on September 24, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images You can count me among the people who were initially skeptical of the Zaire Franklin acquisition. Brian Gutekunst seems to have had an over-obsession with linebackers ever since De’Vondre Campbell’s out-of-nowhere All-Pro season in 2021, and his move to add Franklin as a replacement for Quay Walker, then reward him with a reworked contract, seemed like putting too many eggs in an aging and undersized basket. You can also count me as very glad that Gutekunst pulled the trigger on that move, especially since he only had to give up Colby Wooden, always a poor fit in Green Bay, to do it. Franklin has been a more-than-solid running mate for Edgerrin Cooper to this point. He’s played literally every snap of the Packers’ four games so far and he’s currently third on the team in tackles behind Evan Williams and Cooper. And Franklin donning the green dot had freed up Cooper to focus on doing Edgerrin Cooper things, always a plus when you’ve got a playmaker of his caliber. But now, Franklin is even more important to the Packers’ defense. With Cooper done for the year (and, unfortunately, at least part of 2027), Franklin’s contributions become all the more crucial to a defense that was just trying to get by until Micah Parsons came back. And with Parsons’ return apparently slightly slowed, someone’s going to have to make up for Cooper’s playmaking ability until the Packers’ best defender is back in the lineup. So yeah, I’m glad the Packers nabbed Zaire Franklin when they could. At least we’re not heading into a game against the Bears with Isaiah McDuffie and Ty’Ron Hopper as the starting linebackers. title: Packers Film Room: Random fun moments from a Week 4 win
summary: I know the vast majority of people have already moved past the Green Bay Packers’ Week 4 win over the Buccaneers and are looking forward to Week 5, but I’m not quite ready to do that yet, because there are still fun things to talk about from Week 4. So let’s take a couple minutes […]
full_text: Oct 4, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Green Bay Packers running back Kaleb Johnson (26) runs with the ball past Tampa Bay Buccaneers linebacker Christian Rozeboom (52) at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jonathan Dyer-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect I know the vast majority of people have already moved past the Green Bay Packers’ Week 4 win over the Buccaneers and are looking forward to Week 5, but I’m not quite ready to do that yet, because there are still fun things to talk about from Week 4. So let’s take a couple minutes and talk about them. Play 1: 3rd & 2, 10:32 remaining in the 1st quarter This is the Bo Melton [16] drop. It’s a real shame to refer to it that way, but I just assume it’s the way everyone will remember it so it’s a nice (sad?) little shorthand. The Packers are in 11 personnel (1 RB, 1 TE, 3 WR) in a 2×2 spread look. MarShawn Lloyd [32] is the running back, but, with the Bucs in a mugged-up look in the A gap, Lloyd is in the Sniffer role (aligned between the QB and the line). The Bucs are showing two-high safeties pre-snap with a lot of bodies up at the line. I mentioned the mugged-up A gap, but the slot defender over Matthew Golden [0] is inching towards the line, showing a blitz. Melton short-motions before the snap and Zyon McCollum [27] bumps over Golden. With Melton releasing out of the slot, that is showing Melton uncovered off the line. The Packers are running vertical routes – with Melton running right down the middle of the field – so Jordan Love [10] is going to check the safety movement post-snap but is already thinking about Melton as the first read on this play. At the snap, the slot defender drops into a hook zone (allowing Melton to fly by), the safeties are staying in their two-high look and one of the mugging linebackers is dropping off the line into zone, looking to pick up anything vertical from the slot. With Melton breaking vertical, the LB turns to run with him while the safeties turn to take a deep half of the field for each of them. It plays out like Tampa 2, with the LB covering the deep middle 3rd of the field. So that’s essentially Melton vs a linebacker, with that linebacker dropping from the middle of the line. Love checks the safeties, looks at the drops underneath and takes a shot on what is a very favorable match-up. Nice throw, but Melton just can’t hang on. Nice call. Good read. Good throw. Everything was perfect right up until the moment that it wasn’t. Still, in terms of everything that went into this, a fun call. I just wish it was a different outcome. Play 2: 2nd & 6, 6:32 remaining in the 1st quarter It’s been tough sledding for the Packers in the run game through the first few weeks of the season, but they broke off a couple explosive runs in this game so I wanted to look at them. Both of these runs come out of 13 personnel (1 RB, 3 TE, 1 WR). I mentioned this in my numbers breakdown after the game , but this was the heaviest usage of 13 personnel we’ve seen from the Packers this season, and it worked well for them. The Packers have all three of their TEs in-line. Jonnu Smith [18] is on the left, while Tucker Kraft [85] and Mark Redman [86] are in a YY Wing formation on the right. Redman goes in motion to the left pre-snap, which causes the linebackers to bump over. They snap the ball just before Redman crosses the center. On the left side of the line, Smith is kicking out the EMOL (End Man On the Line), Jordan Morgan [77] and Laken Tomlinson [72] are double-teaming the man over Morgan, and Sean Rhyan [75] takes a step to his left before turning back to block inside. Redman is working as a lead blocker for Chris Brooks. Everyone on the left side of the line does their job, with Redman taking on a LB in the hole. It looks like there’s a hole to the outside, but McCollum is lurking. Tomlinson comes off the double-team and releases over to give Redman a helping hand. Brooks does a nice job of seeing this and makes a great cut back inside, ultimately breaking through the line and picking up 27 yards. Play 3: 2nd & 5, 12:04 remaining in the 3rd quarter Another run out of 13, another explosive. Same formation as the last time, with the same players in the same spot. This time it’s a run to the right, and I really like how they get to it. Rhyan and Tomlinson work a double-team on the nose tackle to seal him inside. Travis Glover [79], Anthony Belton [71] and Tucker Kraft all block out, while Redman loops inside to work as a lead blocker. The key blocks up front are the Rhyan/Tomlinson double-team and the one-on-one with Glover. They all do their jobs wonderfully, creating a great running lane up front. Redman takes on the only other threat in the box. Kaleb Johnson [26] works behind that block and gets into the open field for a gain of 31. There are at least a dozen more plays I’d like to highlight here, but it’s late and I’m tired. Albums listened to: Zola Jesus – Conatus

title: Houston Texans NFL Power Rankings: Week 5
summary: Is this it for the Houston Texans in 2026? Is this the unceremonious closing of their Super Bowl window? These may be questions you find easy to answer now, but were you expecting that to happen so early into this season? Some believe that’s it’s hard to get a read on any NFL teams until […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - OCTOBER 04: Kamari Lassiter #3 of the Houston Texans reacts after a penalty in the second half against the Dallas Cowboys at Reliant Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Is this it for the Houston Texans in 2026? Is this the unceremonious closing of their Super Bowl window? These may be questions you find easy to answer now, but were you expecting that to happen so early into this season? Some believe that’s it’s hard to get a read on any NFL teams until a quarter of the way into the season. Of course, you can often glean which teams are truly great and which are awful right away, but the majority of teams fall between those two extremes and require a sample size of a few games to figure out. Now that we’re four games into the regular season, it’s a bit easier to determine which teams are trending in the right and wrong direction…and Houston is going in about as wrong of a direction as you could possibly imagine. Four losses in a row is a new low for this new era of Texans football, the last time it occurred was the 2020 season and resulted in head coach/general manager Bill O’Brien being fired when he was arguably at the peak of his powers within the organization. Unlike 2020, however, there’s a head-spinning mishmash of newfound problems that haunt the 2026 Texans: the insistent, exhausting struggling of the offensive line and rushing attack now in their third year of failing to improve, the surprising development of significantly worse defensive coverage (partially caused by playing more zone rather than man outside the numbers), and, of course, the injuries. The injuries to the offensive line, wide receiver, and linebacker position groups have been truly disastrous to the team’s cohesion, and the depth of the roster has not been able to pick up the slack in the way I’m sure general manager Nick Caserio intended. So, what does this all mean for the Texans’ spot on the power rankings? It means that they’re going down, way down, and it will require a miracle for Houston to break into the top half of the list by season’s end. The only NFL team to go 0-4 and still make the playoffs was the 1992 San Diego Chargers, and after last month’s showing, I strongly doubt any pundits will be betting on the Houston Texans from repeating that remarkable feat. Here’s where the Houston Texans are ranked following their 34-30 loss to the Dallas Cowboys: NFL.COM : 23. Houston Texans (0-4) I think it’s safe to remove the “elite” tag from the Texans’ defense. For a second straight week, C.J. Stroud gave Houston a late lead, and the defense failed to protect it. Kamari Lassiter had an especially terrible day, giving up eight receptions for 136 yards on 11 targets as the closest defender, per Next Gen Stats. Houston’s defense didn’t generate organic pressure, resorting to blitzes against a quarterback ( Dak Prescott ) you certainly should not blitz often. The Texans paid the price and have wasted a rather strong stretch from Stroud, who is no longer the problem in Houston. – Nick Shook ESPN: 24. Houston Texans (0-4) Week 4 result: Lost to the Cowboys 34-30 Week 4 ranking: 21 Four words to describe the first four weeks: Pass defense is struggling. The Texans’ pass defense has fallen off a cliff in 2026. Last season, Houston was fifth in passing yards allowed (179 per game). So far in 2026, it’s 28th (260). For a team with three Pro Bowlers in the secondary, that’s inexcusable. There are a bunch of reasons, but a noteworthy one is that Houston hasn’t pressed as much as last season. The Texans have the second-lowest press rate (25%), per ESPN Research, compared to the 12th highest in 2025 (56%). That has been a little confusing, as All-Pro cornerback Derek Stingley Jr . and Pro Bowl corner Kamari Lassiter are best when pressing – DJ Bien-Aime SPORTS ILLUSTRATED: 20. Houston Texans (0–4) Last week’s ranking: No. 16 Last week’s result: lost to Cowboys, 34–30 This week: at Titans Of the teams whose seasons are theoretically dead in the water, Houston provides the faintest glimmer of hope. Braden Smith, Tank Dell and Kayden McDonald are on the way, the Titans are up next on the schedule and 1–4 looks far better (with three examples of playoff teams in the last 25 years, by the way). – Conor Orr BLEACHER REPORT: 28. Houston Texans (0-4) Last Week: 27 Week 4 Result: Lost vs. Dallas 34-30 The Houston Texans understand what it means to start poorly then rally to earn a postseason appearance. However, the team has never started 0-4 and made the playoffs. Only one team in NFL history has. What makes Houston’s situation particularly concerning is the team could rely on its defense last season. This year is a different story. Houston went from fielding the league’s best defense to sitting outside of the Top 20. Houston currently ranks among the bottom five pass defenses. Derek Stingley Jr. and the Texans’ secondary couldn’t slow CeeDee Lamb. Instead, Lamb set a new Dallas Cowboys franchise record Sunday with 17 receptions in a single game. Ironically, Houston’s offense was the bigger concern entering the 2026 campaign. It’s currently ranked sixth overall. – Brent Sobleski CBS SPORTS; 26. Texans (0-4) (Last Week: 27) They’ve made the playoffs after opening 0-3. But this year it’s 0-4. Can they climb out from that hole to make the playoffs? Good luck. – Pete Prisco USA TODAY: 27. Houston Texans (25): Even if an 0-4 outfit wanted to wave the white flag , the contracts of players like DE Danielle Hunter and WR Nico Collins are basically untradeable due to their salary cap ramifications. – Nate Davis YAHOO! SPORTS: 26. Houston Texans (0-4, LW: 24) With 2:23 left on Sunday, the Texans scored to take a 30-27 lead. A defense that was expected to be one of the best in the NFL could win the game with one stop, or at least make sure the game went to overtime by holding Dallas to a field goal. The Cowboys went downfield and scored a touchdown. Dallas has a good offense but Houston was supposed to have a good defense. The Texans don’t. They are surprisingly average: 14th in DVOA after Sunday’s games and 26th in EPA ( expected points added ) allowed per play. Defensive dominance can vary more season to season than offensive excellence, but it’s still surprising that the Texans are winless and a middle-of-the-road defense is a big reason for that. “It sucks, because we know we’re the ones out there on the field,” Texans cornerback Derek Stingley Jr. said, via the Houston Chronicle . “The coaches put us in the right position to win and we’ve got to do it. They can’t do it, we’ve got to do it. We’ve got great coaches, we’ve got great everybody. We’ve got to go out there and do our job.” – Frank Schwab THE ATHLETIC 24. Instead, a defense that we thought had a chance to be an all-time great has looked awfully mediocre through the first four weeks. It’s the main reason for the Texans’ winless start.
