(Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders’ offense is getting a boost on the practice field Wednesday as the team begins the work week for Sunday’s game at the New England Patriots. Las Vegas head coach Klint Kubiak said both starting right guard Jackson Powers-Johnson and reserve wide receiver Dont’e Thornton will participate in Wednesday’s session. Powers-Johnson missed the Raiders’ Week 4 home loss to the Kansas City Chiefs with a groin injury he suffered date in a Week 3 win at New Orleans. Monday, Kubiak said he hoped Powers-Johnson, who was spelled by Caleb Rogers on Sunday, would be able to practice Wednesday. He was limited in practice Wednesday. Thornton was a full practice participant, so potentially he could be activated this week. That would mean someone would have to be removed from the 53-man roster. The 2025 fourth-round pick was quiet in training camp before being injured after a slow rookie season. But with Jack Bech on the injured reserve, Thornton should get some opportunities when he’s ready to play. Another Las Vegas receiver, Jalen Nailor, won’t practice Wednesday because he is in the concussion protocol after getting hurt Sunday. So, his availability for Sunday’s game is in question. Running back Rhamondre Stevenson was limited.

title: Raiders at the quarter pole
summary: We’re basically a quarter into the 2025 NFL season (this 17-game thing messes with the math), so let’s take a quick review of the 3-1 Raiders and where they stand with three quarters of the season remaining. Quick summary of the first quarter: It was a spectacular start for the Silver and Black. They were […]
full_text: (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’re basically a quarter into the 2025 NFL season (this 17-game thing messes with the math), so let’s take a quick review of the 3-1 Raiders and where they stand with three quarters of the season remaining . Quick summary of the first quarter: It was a spectacular start for the Silver and Black. They were dominant in their three wins and competitive in their one loss. Klint Kubiak has opened eyes around the NFL in his first year as a head coach. The league is watching the Raiders. Offensive MVP: Quarterback Kirk Cousins. When he was signed he was expected to be a mentor and temporary placeholder before No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza took over. But Cousins, 38, isn’t showing any signs of giving up his starting job. He has thrown 11 touchdown passses and is a perfect fit for Kubiak’s offfense and he is having success with the coach like he did in Minnesota. Defensive MVP: Linebacker Nakobe Dean. The free-agent is flourishing in the middle of the Raiders’ defense. He has been described as the “glue” of the unit. He is a heat-seeking missile and he is a forced fumble machine. He’s always around the ball. Rookie of the quarter: Cornerback Zeke Masses. The fifth-round draft pick became a starter in Week 2 and hasn’t looked back. Masses has three interception and could be a candidate to be the NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year. He’s a playmaker. Best surprise: The whole operation. The Raiders went from bad to extremely competitive in a heartbeat. They are a competent, dangerous team very quickly under Kubiak. Worst surprise: The running game has not been good after a strong showing in Week 1. It was expected to be be improved. Bold prediction for next quarter: The Raiders play at the New England Patriots, host the Buffalo Bills and the Los Angeles Rams and play at the New York Jets in this quarter. I see the Raiders going 2-2 in this mostly tough stretch to be 5-3 and very much in the playoff mix at midseason.

title: Tonka Hemingway becoming key figure on defense
summary: Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2025 draft class fared in a 30-27 Week 4 home loss to the Kansas City Chiefs and what to look for Sunday at the New England Patriots: Ashton Jeanty: The No. 6 overall draft pick played a season low 666 percent of the snaps Sunday. […]
full_text: (Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2025 draft class fared in a 30-27 Week 4 home loss to the Kansas City Chiefs and what to look for Sunday at the New England Patriots: Ashton Jeanty: The No. 6 overall draft pick played a season low 666 percent of the snaps Sunday. Jeanty, who appeared to be bothered by his ankles, finish fairly strong after a slow start. He had 58 yards on 15 carries and he added six catches for 68 yards, his highest receiving yardage output. The Raiders’ ground game has struggled, but at least, Jeanty made an impact in the receiving game. Jeanty is leading the NFL with 10 runs for negative yardage. Jack Bech: The second-round pick is on the injured reserve with a fractured forearm and will likely be out for several more weeks. Darien Porter: The third-round pick, a former starting cornerback, played three defensive snaps and 20 on special teams. Caleb Rogers: The third-round pick started at right guard when Jackson Powers-Johnson out with a groin injury. He struggled against the Chiefs’ star defensive tackle Chris Jones, Rogers gave up five pressures. Charles Grant: The offensive lineman, taken in the third round, didn’t play on offense, but logged six snaps on special teams. Dont’e Thornton: The wide receiver, taken in the fourth round, is on the injured reserve. The team is hopeful he can return soon. Tonka Hemingway: The fourth-round pick played 65 percent of the defensive snaps, the most of any Raiders’ defensive tackle. He had three tackles, a quarterback hit and knocked down pass. He is making plays. JJ Pegues: The defensive tackle, taken in the sixth round, was active for the first time this season and for the 10th time in his career. He played seven snaps on defensive and seven on special teams. Cody Lindenberg: The seventh-round pick played 19 snaps on special teams.

title: Jeff Hafley remains confident in direction of Miami Dolphins
summary: The Miami Dolphins have started the 2026 NFL season with four straight losses, but despite the team’s hardships, head coach Jeff Hafley still believes in the direction of his organization. On Tuesday, Miami’s rookie head coach spoke with the South Florida media and discussed why he believes his squad will turn things around moving forward. […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Head coach Jeff Hafley of the Miami Dolphins looks on during the first quarter against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins have started the 2026 NFL season with four straight losses, but despite the team’s hardships, head coach Jeff Hafley still believes in the direction of his organization. On Tuesday, Miami’s rookie head coach spoke with the South Florida media and discussed why he believes his squad will turn things around moving forward. “Everything that we do is towards winning, but if we have the right guys in the building, and they keep improving, and if they keep trusting in their teammates and trusting in themselves, and develop, they’ll continue to go forward and give their best, and do everything they can, because they respect and love their teammate, and go after it, and get better and win a game.” Hafley continued: “It’s what I just told them downstairs in the team meeting. I told the guys very clearly that this was going to be a tough journey that we were all going to go on. I told them that if they weren’t up for it, then they can go talk to [Jon-Eric Sullivan]. This is the time to find out, as we build this thing and grow, who are the real guys? Like, who are the guys that we can trust — that want in the boat — because when we flip this thing — and we will flip this thing — that we want to have around? The only way you find out those things is going through adversity together. And we’re going to find a lot about the guys.” Does Hafley believe he already has the right guys in the building? “The way we’re building this thing and the way we are talking about the process and the way we’re playing together, and the way we’re getting better, and the energy that we’ve played with, and the toughness that we’ve played with, I do believe we have the right guys, more or less, that will help us get to that point.” It’s clear that Miami’s coach believes in his team and trusts they aren’t too far away from being a consistently competitive squad. Though the Dolphins remain winless on the season, they are trusting in their process and have faith that the results will start to show in the win/loss column soon. Their next opportunity to finally claim a victory will come this Sunday when Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals visit Hard Rock Stadium.

The guard has responded to the move, but it may not be the only reason he looks like the player Miami hoped to get when they selected him in the second round of the 2025 NFL Draft. According to Savaiinaea, the move actually has nothing to do with his growth and improved play. According to a report from Miami Herald reporter Barry Jackson, Savaiinaea identified several other areas that have led to his improvement, which includes not having allowed a sack so far this season after leading all guards in sacks allowed last year: Even though Dolphins coaches have said he seems more comfortable playing right guard (his position at Arizona) after playing left guard as a rookie, Savaiinaea said changing sides has had “zero impact” on his growth. So what has been the difference? He cited a few factors: game experience, increased confidence, helpful tips from offensive line coach Zach Yenser and a determination not to get beat inside, which was perhaps his biggest of several problems last season. “Most of my beats, when I got beat, were [on] the inside” last season, he said. “My plan this year is to not get beat inside. That’s the minor change I’ve put into my game this year. There are a lot of good rushers out there who know how I’m setting. It’s minor improvements like not getting anywhere with my first step.” Savaiinaea would go on to talk about new offensive line coach Zach Yenser and the game slowing down for him. title: Vikings-Saints First Injury Report
summary: The Minnesota Vikings and New Orleans Saints released their first injury reports in advance of their Sunday afternoon matchup at Caesar’s Superdome in New Orleans. Here they are. Minnesota Vikings New Orleans Saints Injury Report Terms and Glossary Injury designation definitions: Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 4: Jordan Addison #3 of the Minnesota Vikings warms up before the game against the Miami Dolphins at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings and New Orleans Saints released their first injury reports in advance of their Sunday afternoon matchup at Caesar’s Superdome in New Orleans. Here they are. Minnesota Vikings Player Name Position Injury Wednesday Thursday Friday Injury Designation Jordan Mason* RB Thumb DNP IR-OUT Jordan Addison* WR Hamstring DNP Christian Darrisaw* LT Concussion DNP Charles Demmings CB Hamstring DNP Justin Jefferson* WR Ankle LP Aaron Jones* RB NIR-Rest LP Brian O’Neill* RT Knee LP Michael Jurgens C Elbow FP Brett Thorson* P Hamstring FP Ben Yurosek TE Ankle FP New Orleans Saints Player Name Position Injury Wednesday Thursday Friday Injury Designation Kelvin Banks* OT Ankle DNP IR-OUT Bryan Bresee* DT Knee DNP IR-OUT Travis Etienne* RB Hamstring DNP IR-OUT Julian Blackmon* S Shoulder LP Barion Brown WR Thigh DNP Kaden Eliss LB Calf DNP Noah Fant TE Abdomen LP Jaylan Ford LB Ankle FP Davon Godchaux* DT Groin FP Carl Granderson LB Ankle LP Anfernee Jennings LB Knee DNP Alvin Kamara* RB Back DNP Chris Olave* WR NIR-Rest DNP Mike Reid S Ankle LP Tyler Shough* QB Left Hand LP Lorenzo Styles CB Calf FP Injury Report Terms and Glossary FP = Full participant in practice. LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. NIR = Not injury related. PUP = Physically unable to participate list. IR = Injured reserve. Note: only starters on IR are listed. Player Name* = Starter. Injury designation definitions: Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. Notes on Injured Players For the Vikings, Jordan Addison did not participate for what Kevin O’Connell described as a minor hamstring injury, “if it is anything at all” so that doesn’t appear to be something that would cause him to miss Sunday’s game- but you never know. Justin Jefferson was back at practice on a limited basis, which is encouraging. I don’t get the impression, based on Kevin O’Connell’s comments on Tuesday with Paul Allen, that the Vikings are looking to rush him back, however, with a bye-week following the Saints game. But his returning to practice on Wednesday would seem to open the possibility of Jefferson playing on Sunday. Christian Darrisaw is in concussion protocol, so difficult to say if he’ll make it out in time to play Sunday or not. It didn’t seem like the worst hit I’ve ever seen, but you never know. I wouldn’t be surprised if they were cautious with him as well. Kevin O’Connell said he expects Brett Thorson to return as punter/holder for the Saints game and his full status for Wednesday’s practice would seem to confirm that. The Vikings also released Johnny Hekker from the practice squad, which is another indication that Thorson will be back on Sunday. Michael Jurgens and Ben Yurosek had their 21-day windows to return from injured reserve opened on Wednesday and the fact that both were full participants in practice is a good sign. However, whether they will be activated for Sunday’s game or not make come down to other roster considerations. Lastly, Brian O’Neill is dealing with what appears to be a minor knee injury he is likely to play through. For the Saints, Alvin Kamara not practicing due to back soreness following the Monday night game against the Falcons is something to monitor. Lorenzo Styles and Jaylan Ford have been designated to return from IR and have their 21-day window opened, but unclear at this point whether they will be activated for Sunday’s game or not. Saints starting QB Tyler Sough is dealing with a hand injury suffered on Monday night to his non-throwing left hand, so something that is not likely to keep him out of Sunday’s game. The Saints also have three starters on IR which hurts. Other than that, there is a long list but probably not of great consequence for Sunday’s game. We’ll have two more updates tomorrow and Friday. Stay tuned. Follow me on X/Bluesky @wludford
author: Warren Ludford

title: Week 4 Observations – Definitely Maybe
summary: The Minnesota Vikings’ 15-10 victory over the winless Miami Dolphins at U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday prompted a range of emotional reactions. If you had told me to turn off the game at the end of the 3rd quarter and asked for my thoughts, my response would be vastly different from how I feel now, […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 4: Dallas Turner #15 of the Minnesota Vikings pressures Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins as he throws the ball during the first quarter of the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings’ 15-10 victory over the winless Miami Dolphins at U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday prompted a range of emotional reactions. If you had told me to turn off the game at the end of the 3rd quarter and asked for my thoughts, my response would be vastly different from how I feel now, writing this article. Fortunately, the 4th quarter happened, offering some hope that the struggling Vikings’ offense may have finally turned the corner. The key word in that last sentence is “may.” Time will tell, but it was a much-needed boost of hope after a dismal stretch. Kyler Murray was 13 of 14 for 120 yards and took no sacks on the Vikings’ final two drives. In a shocking development, that also coincided with the decision to put Murray in an environment where he has long been more comfortable. The Vikings took 54 snaps from shotgun Sunday vs. the Dolphins. Most in a game since Kevin O'Connell got here in 2022. — Alec Lewis (@alec_lewis) October 5, 2026 Two things can be true simultaneously. I’m not going to sit here and pretend that injuries and the awful weather in Chicago in Week 2 didn’t play a role in the offense’s poor showing so far. That’s absolutely a contributing factor. But it’s also fair to say Kevin O’Connell hasn’t done Murray and company any favors early in the season. They clearly haven’t put the offense in the best position to succeed. Receivers haven’t been effectively schemed open, a traditional KOC strength, and Murray has been trying to play in a system that hasn’t maximized his strengths. It’s rather baffling, to be honest. But better late than never, I guess. Despite all of this, the Vikings are 4-0, 3-0 in the NFC, and 2-0 in the division. If the Murray we see for the rest of the season is the improved, more comfortable version we saw in the 4th quarter on Sunday, with Justin Jefferson and Jordan Mason returning, this offense has tremendous potential. We’re definitely not out of the woods yet, but it did seem like something may have clicked with KOC that could finally get this offense off the ground. We can hope. Let’s break down the other highs and lows of an (unexpected) nail-biter, shall we? THE GREAT Will Reichard, the real Most Interesting Man in the World. The baby-faced assassin with luxurious, Fabioesque hair went viral for an on-air visual during the broadcast showing that, since Week 2, he accounted for 32 (!) of the 44 points scored. Minutes later, that number was 35. Nothing more really needs to be said about Will the Thrill. The guy is amazing. Dallas Turner, Lawrence Taylor Impersonator. Turner’s early Defensive Player of the Year resume grew even stronger on Sunday, with two sacks, five pressures, and a turnover. He now has 5.5 sacks, 28 QB pressures, and 14 QB hits in just four games. I certainly thought Turner would improve this year, but being on pace for 23 sacks after the first month exceeded even the loftiest expectations. T.J. Hockenson, Reception Machine. In my Vikings’ fantasy preview article before the season, I noted that I expected Hockenson to exceed the experts’ incredibly modest consensus expectations comfortably. The main reason was simple: History shows that Kyler Murray likes to throw to tight ends. That’s it. He really liked it on Sunday, pulling in 13 receptions for 119 yards. If he stays healthy, he’ll have his best season since 2023. Myles Price, All-Pro. If September and early October are any indication, Price will run away with first-team All-Pro honors. The only question is whether it will be at kick returner, punt returner, or both. This Team’s Luck, So Far. You’re exactly what your record says you are, but that doesn’t mean you must ignore the breaks that have come your way. The Vikings have benefited from a disproportionate number of high-leverage, game-changing penalties by opponents, along with an abundance of incredibly lucky breaks on Sunday. Chris Bell’s foot out of bounds by about 1/8 of an inch that cost the Dolphins a touchdown. Blake Cashman grazing Ollie Gordon II’s jersey to get a down by contact, negating another huge play. Ivan Pace Jr. deciding not to trim his fingernails before the game to prevent a costly roughing-the-kicker penalty. We’ve seen similar movies before, for example, in 2022 and 2017. The idea is that by the end of the season, the offense will find its footing and be far more dangerous than the Case Keenum-led unit, while the defense will be in a different galaxy from Ed Donatell’s version. We won’t just need these breaks; we will be good enough to overcome them even when they fall the opponents’ way in decent numbers. That’s the hope, at least. THE GOOD Vikings Defense. I know it feels weird to put a unit that allowed just 10 points to an NFL team only in the “good” category, but the bar was set so ridiculously high over the past two weeks against much better offenses that I had to dial back the excitement a bit. That was mainly because the run defense allowed Ollie Gordon II to hit 100 yards on only nine carries. This came after holding D’Andre Swift and Bucky Irving to 2.8 and 3.1 yards per carry, respectively, the previous two weeks. Not sure what the deal was there, since they also didn’t have to deal with an explosive passing game. And, as noted, there was also the down-by-contact running play and the long touchdown reception that was called back. Long-term concern level: .001 out of 10. Isaiah Rodgers and James Pierre. The under-the-radar signings over the past two offseasons have been fantastic. When you don’t really notice a cornerback and their name isn’t mentioned often, it can be a very good thing. PFF graded them 70.9 and 76.1, respectively, against the Dolphins. That ranked #2 and #3 on the defense behind Dallas Turner. Ryan Van Demark and Joe Huber. Both called into action unexpectedly and had strong showings. In his 46% snap share replacing Christian Darrisaw, Van Demark logged a 69.4 PFF grade. Huber played nearly the entire game (91%) and earned a 50.0 PFF grade, which didn’t seem to match what I was seeing. Looked fine to me. Hopefully I’m right, because while Van Demark will likely need to make one more start, Huber is (for now) penciled in as the starter at left guard for the rest of the regular season, because… THE INCREDIBLY UNFORTUNATE The Donovan Jackson Injury. Horrible news. Jackson has played at an elite level in Year 2, especially in pass protection, where PFF ranked him 7th among 74 qualifying guards. The good news is that, as of this writing, it appears he could return for the playoffs. Either way, it’s an enormous loss. Not sure what the plan is moving forward, whether Huber’s job is for the rest of the season or a trade is on the horizon, similar to Cam Robinson in 2024. Either way, I wish Jackson the speediest of recoveries so he can continue his promising career as soon as possible. THE BAD The Freakin’ Penalties. After Week 2, I commended KOC for getting the Vikings to play smart, clean football. I officially retract that statement. The last two weeks have been an unmitigated disaster. After logging nine penalties for 95 yards against the Buccaneers, the Vikings weren’t quite done stepping on rakes, committing 11 (!) for 85 yards in the friendly confines of U.S. Bank Stadium against the Dolphins. Way too many were inexcusable false starts and formation errors. If you’re in practice, starter or not, you should do better. This stuff may fly against teams with a combined 0-8 record, but it’ll bite you in the ass against better competition, which is coming up very soon. Harrison Smith. This one hurts because he’s one of my favorite Vikings ever, but you gotta call it like it is. Smith had a rough day against the Dolphins.…
author: Shawn C

title: Vikings Autopsy: Daily Norseman Week 4 Postgame Roundtable (A 15-10 win over the Dolphins)
summary: Hello everyone, and welcome to the Week 4 Minnesota Vikings postgame roundtable here at Daily Norseman. The Vikes are coming off another ugly one, this time a 15-10 win at home over the Dolphins, and remain alone atop the NFC North at 4-0. How much longer can the offense ride the defense’s coattails? Did the […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 04: T.J. Hockenson #87 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrates against the Miami Dolphins in the fourth quarter at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. The Vikings defeated the Dolphins 15-10. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello everyone, and welcome to the Week 4 Minnesota Vikings postgame roundtable here at Daily Norseman. The Vikes are coming off another ugly one, this time a 15-10 win at home over the Dolphins, and remain alone atop the NFC North at 4-0. How much longer can the offense ride the defense’s coattails? Did the fourth quarter show an offense starting to figure some things out? Let’s talk to it: Question 1: Let’s freestyle for a minute — get your initial thoughts out about the Vikings beating the Dolphins in Week 4, 15-10. Brandon Warne : I’m going to take a little bit of a different tack here. While many are saying “they can’t keep winning like this” and things of that nature, I’m going with this: They have four wins — and those aren’t going anywhere. Good, bad or otherwise, they won those four games and nobody can take that from them. If you assume a team needs to go 10-7 to be in the playoffs this year, then if they can go 6-7 the rest of the way, they should be good to go. In a division that is by no means insurmountable with games against the Saints, Commanders, Colts, Jets and Falcons remaining, I’m choosing positivity. Now, that’s not to ignore the elephant in the room that they can’t keep winning games this way — which is likely more true than false — I also fall back on one of my most-used sports adages: No matter what, things will not stay the same. They’ll get better, or they’ll get worse — but they will not remain the same. It’s easy to fall into a thought process of “this won’t work if things don’t change,” but that’s rooted in a concept that I’ve never felt was true in sports — that things won’t change. Warren Ludford : It was another somewhat ugly win over a struggling team, so it was frustrating. On the other hand, the offense showed signs of improvement later in the game, especially with Kyler Murray. Defense and special teams continue to be great; the offense is still anemic, but there are some positive signs for the future. Craig Williams : Painful to watch. The Vikings could be the 2000 Ravens if they had average QB play. I wish Murray was mid. Shawn C. : Fortunate (again). Between the lucky breaks and penalties, we’re really playing with fire if the offense doesn’t turn the corner. Kyler Murray found his rhythm in the 4th quarter, which hopefully signals the consistent success many envisioned all offseason. Performances like these may be enough to get past the combined 0-8 Bucs and Dolphins, but teams like the Bills and 49ers will eat our lunch if the offense can’t hold up its end of the bargain. ————— Question 2: Who was your Vikings MVP? BW : I have to go with T.J. Hockenson. Love ‘em or hate ‘em, a 93.2 PFF score really tells the story here. A safety valve is so vital with a quarterback still trying to find his identity within an offense, and that’s exactly what Hockenson provided — and not only in general, but with the top wide receiver in the NFL sidelined, besides. WL : T.J. Hockenson. He had his best game post-knee injury. The Vikings will need him with Jauan Jennings being a non-factor at this point. CW: Will the Thrill Reichard is the best kicker in Vikings history and this team’s biggest weapon. Aaron Jones and Dallas Turner are in consideration as well. SC : Dallas Turner. Another amazing day for Turner, who is now on pace for like 23 sacks. I expected improvement, but this is just ridiculous now. It seems like his name is being called on every pass play ————— Question 3: Who was your Vikings LVP? BW : I’m going to go with Jauan Jennings. With Jefferson sidelined, it stood to reason that someone would have to find their way in the passing game to pick up the slack. And if I’m honest, I think Hockenson was third on my pecking order behind Jordan Addison — who was fine but not great with four receptions and 52 yards — and Jennings, who caught his only target for eight yards and graded out poorly in pretty much every facet of the game. WL : Johnny Hekker. He shanked two punts… CW : Wes Phillips. Waste of salary. SC : This one is tough, but I gotta go with Harrison Smith, who had a rough outing. Hoping it’s simply a matter of getting back into football shape after missing the entire offseason. ————— Question 4: For the second week in a row…where do you stand on Kyler Murray right now? BW : Baby steps — pun unintended. I think we expect an awful lot out of quarterbacks on a weekly basis, and there’s a lot of nuance that a signal-caller has to pick up on in the playbook, within the offense/communication with the coaching staff, and also with the supporting cast (both the pass-catchers and also the line, as well). I’ll also lean on his fourth-quarter stats as a reason for optimism: In the final stanza Sunday, Murray went 12-for-13 for 112 passing yards (92.3 percent), zero touchdowns/interceptions, zero sacks (!), 8.6 yards per attempt and a passer rating of 102.6. It’s…. something. WL : Kyler Murray is getting more acclimated and improving. His accuracy against the Dolphins was 90%, which is elite. And no turnovers. Sacks are still an issue, not 100% his fault in every case, but he built a rapport with T.J. Hockenson, which will serve him well down the road. The Dolphins played cover-2 most of the game (which they hadn’t done much this season), which limited the deeper passing game. But overall, he showed signs of getting more acclimated to the offense and becoming a bit more comfortable in his second full game. CW : We’re standing shoulder to shoulder with Donovan McNabb…in Minnesota, not Philly. SC : Optimistic. Murray played out of the shotgun much more this week, and I don’t think it’s a coincidence that he finally looked like the quarterback I thought he’d be since the spring. The fourth quarter looked like a completely different player. Getting Justin Jefferson back will be fun to watch. ————— Question 5: T.J. Hockenson — Is he “back” or do you still need to see more? BW : He’s BACK back. I think the most impressive thing to me is that he secured all 13 of his targets, making him the first pass-catcher with a 100.0 percent reception percentage on at least that many throws since CeeDee Lamb caught 13 of 13 targets for 98 yards and two scores on Jan. 7, 2024 against the Commanders. He’s also the first Vikings player to do so in team history. That’s right, a team with as rich a history as the Vikings when it comes to pass-catchers. That’s pretty special. WL : I think he’s back. He may not be targeted as much as he was against the Dolphins, but he showed he can be more dynamic than he has been in the past couple of years, and I don’t think he pulled that out for just one game. It may be as much mental as physical for him. But once he got it back, I don’t think he’ll lose it again in future games barring injury. CW : He’s never truly lived up to the expectations. A very nice game; let’s see if he can keep it up. SC : Oh, he’s back. If he stays healthy, he could have a 2023-type season. Murray loves throwing to tight ends, and a healthy, elite WR group will force defenses to pick their poison. It’s the perfect storm for Hockenson to thrive the rest of the way.

title: Will Reichard Named NFC Special Teams Player of the Week
summary: While the Minnesota Vikings’ offense can’t seem to find its way into the end zone, the National Football League has recognized the one guy on the roster who doesn’t seem to have any problems putting points on the board. On Wednesday, the league named kicker Will Reichard the NFC’s Special Teams Player of the Week. […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - OCTOBER 04: Will Reichard #16 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrates after defeating the Miami Dolphins during an NFL football game at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images While the Minnesota Vikings’ offense can’t seem to find its way into the end zone, the National Football League has recognized the one guy on the roster who doesn’t seem to have any problems putting points on the board. On Wednesday, the league named kicker Will Reichard the NFC’s Special Teams Player of the Week. This means that a member of the Vikings has been named the Special Teams Player of the Week for three weeks in a row after Isaiah Rodgers won the award in Week 2 and return specialist Myles Price took home the honors in Week 3. Reichard accounted for all of the Vikings’ scoring in the team’s 15-10 victory over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday afternoon at U.S. Bank Stadium, connecting on field goals of 50, 47, 41, 33, and 29 yards on the day. It’s the second time in his career he’s hit five field goals in a game, equaling the feat he accomplished in Week 7 last season against Philadelphia. Going back to last season, Reichard has now hit 31 consecutive field goals, which is the currently longest streak in the NFL and ties him with Fuad Reveiz for the third-longest streak in Vikings history. Counting extra points, he has converted 56 consecutive kicks, with his last miss* coming on a field goal attempt against the Los Angeles Chargers last season. (Yeah, I put a * next to “miss” there for a reason.) Reichard was also named the NFC’s Special Teams Player of the Month for the final month of the 2025 season. Reichard’s award makes the Vikings the fifth team in NFL history to bring home three consecutive Special Teams Player of the Week awards, and the first to do it since the San Francisco 49ers did it in 2011. The other teams to have done so are the 2007 San Diego Chargers, the 2004 New Orleans Saints, and the 2003 Kansas City Chiefs. Congratulations to Will Reichard on being named the NFC’s Special Teams Player of the Week for Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season!
author: Christopher Gates

title: Vikings Sign Odell Beckham Jr., Jeshaun Jones to Practice Squad
summary: With a couple of open spots on the practice squad, the Minnesota Vikings filled them on Wednesday with a pair of wide receivers, one of which you may have even heard of before. Well, if you’re a Vikings fan, you’ve heard of both of them, but one of them. . .yeah, didn’t see this coming. […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 21: Odell Beckham Jr. #13 of the New York Giants walks off the field after losing the game against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on September 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images With a couple of open spots on the practice squad, the Minnesota Vikings filled them on Wednesday with a pair of wide receivers, one of which you may have even heard of before. Well, if you’re a Vikings fan, you’ve heard of both of them, but one of them. . .yeah, didn’t see this coming. The Vikings have announced the signings of wide receivers Jeshaun Jones and Odell Beckham Jr. to the practice squad. The Vikings brought Jones back after he served his three-game suspension for violating the league’s substance abuse policy and waiving him earlier in the week, but you don’t care about that at the moment, do you? Beckham Jr. really needs no introduction. He was drafted by the New York Giants out of Louisiana State in the first round of the 2014 NFL Draft, after which he won the NFL’s Offensive Rookie of the Year Award and has twice been named a Second-Team NFL All-Pro (2015, 2016). In his career, he has 575 receptions for 7,987 receiving yards and 59 touchdowns. His career has dropped off significantly since 2020, when he suffered a torn ACL midway through the season as a member of the Cleveland Browns. He returned to Cleveland for the 2021 season but had disagreements with the way he was being used in the Cleveland offense, leading to his release. He landed with the Los Angeles Rams and was a part of their Super Bowl championship team. He scored a touchdown in that Super Bowl, but he suffered another ACL injury during that game as well, one that caused him to miss the entire 2022 season. In 2023, Beckham signed with the Baltimore Ravens and had 35 receptions for 565 yards and three scores. He was released by the Ravens ahead of free agency in 2024 and signed with Miami. He started the season on the Physically Unable to Perform List and wound up being released in December, appearing in nine games and making just nine catches. He did not play in 2025, and for part of the 2025 season served a six-game suspension for violating the league’s performance-enhancing drug policy. Beckham attempted a comeback with the Giants this season and made the 53-man roster out of training camp, but was released after three games without recording a catch. I’m not sure how high the expectations should be for OBJ at this point in his career or how much juice he has left in the proverbial tank. But he’s a member of the Vikings now, so what does everyone think about this development?

title: Patriots treating Raiders TE Brock Bowers like a wide receiver this week
summary: As New England Patriots practice squad wide receiver Kyle Dixon took the field Wednesday, he donned the No. 89 jersey, signaling his practice responsibilities for the week: Raiders tight end Brock Bowers. It’s a sign of how the Patriots plan to treat the All-Pro tight end ahead of their Week 5 matchup. “Really, Brock is […]
full_text: As New England Patriots practice squad wide receiver Kyle Dixon took the field Wednesday, he donned the No. 89 jersey, signaling his practice responsibilities for the week: Raiders tight end Brock Bowers. It’s a sign of how the Patriots plan to treat the All-Pro tight end ahead of their Week 5 matchup. “Really, Brock is a receiver; that’s impressive,” head coach Mike Vrabel said. “What he does at his size, the speed, the route craft, and being able to catch at the catch point. He’s like a big slot receiver. He has downfield speed, he runs outward breaking routes, he runs routes like a receiver, but then also he’s got the ability to double guys up inside.” After missing the first two games with a knee injury, Bowers has paced the Raiders’ offense in two games since his return. His 25 targets are a team-high for the season, while his 16 receptions and 202 receiving yards ranks third and second on the team, respectively. Most of that damage has come from the wide receiver position. Through two games, Bowers has played just 16 snaps inline this year compared to 61 out wide and 45 in the slot. “He’s the number one receiver. I wouldn’t even call him a tight end,” captain Kevin Byard said. “He’s the number one receiver, one of the best tight ends in this league. So, tough matchup.” “He’s really like a receiver,” fellow safety Craig Woodson echoed. “I mean, he has speed, good hands, good route craft. So, we’ll have to be on our technique all week. Just make sure we’re prepared for this guy.” In just two games, Bowers’ eight third-down conversions are tied for the third-most in the NFL and are tied for the most among tight ends. New England saw just how dangerous the 23-year old can be in last year’s Week 1 matchup, when he posted 5 catches for 103 yards while playing just half of the Raiders’ offensive snaps. The Raiders are also not afraid to get Bowers’ tight end counterpart, Michael Mayer, involved, either. Mayer leads the team with 20 receptions. The Patriots defense did a strong job against Bills tight end Dalton Kincaid in last week’s matchup. Kincaid, who entered the week with the most receiving yards at the position was held to just one catch for seven yards. New England will look for a similar result this Sunday. The Patriots’ defense did a strong job against Bills tight end Dalton Kincaid in last week’s matchup. Kincaid, who entered the week leading all tight ends in receiving yards, was held to just one catch for seven yards. New England will look for a similar result this Sunday. “They’re feeding their tight ends,” Vrabel said. “They have a great group. Certainly different play styles, but Brock is as elite as they come at that position. So, we’ll have a huge challenge.”
author: Brian Hines

title: Patriots vs. Raiders series history ahead of Week 5 game
summary: For the New England Patriots, Sunday will be a celebration. The franchise will honor the 25th anniversary of its first ever Super Bowl-winning team as well as recent Pro Football Hall of Fame inductee Adam Vinatieri. It is a fitting day to do so given that the Las Vegas Raiders are in town. The Raiders, […]
full_text: For the New England Patriots, Sunday will be a celebration. The franchise will honor the 25th anniversary of its first ever Super Bowl-winning team as well as recent Pro Football Hall of Fame inductee Adam Vinatieri. It is a fitting day to do so given that the Las Vegas Raiders are in town. The Raiders, of course, were one of the teams beaten by the Patriots on the way to that championship — one of 39 total meetings between the two organizations over the years. Let’s take a look back. Patriots vs. Raiders series history Overall history: Two charter members of the original AFL, the Patriots and Raiders have played 36 regular season games since back in 1960. The series has been fairly even through the years, resulting in an 18-17-1 advantage for New England in those games. The playoffs have been similar, with the Patriots holding a 2-1 edge in postseason play. The first such meeting came in 1976, when then-Oakland won 24-21 in the divisional round. The Patriots got their revenge in 1985, winning 27-20 in Los Angeles. They then celebrated a 16-13 overtime divisional victory in Foxborough en route to their victory in Super Bowl XXXVI. First game: Almost exactly 66 years ago, on October 16, 1960, the Patriots and Raiders met for the very first time at Kezar Stadium in San Francisco. It was a sloppy affair, to say the least. The visitors turned the ball over seven times, including thrice through Butch Songin interceptions, while the de facto home team threw five picks itself — three of them landing in the arms of Gino Cappelletti. Cappelletti’s efforts were for naught, however. The Raiders managed to jump to a 21-6 halftime lead and never looked back, eventually winning the game with a final score of 27-14. Most memorable game: The Patriots honoring Adam Vinatieri on Sunday makes perfect sense, because of all the kicks he made in his NFL career, none was better than the 45-yarder that sent the 2001 divisional game to overtime. Driving the ball through a snow storm, Vinatieri capped what was a 10-point fourth-quarter rally by his team: New England was down 13-3 entering the final period against the Raiders, but a Tom Brady touchdown run and Vinatieri’s kick — which was preceded by the famous Tuck Rule overturning an apparent lost fumble by Brady — tied proceedings. In extra time, the Patriots received the kickoff and marched 61 yards in 15 plays to set up the game-winning field goal from 23 yards out. Brady went 8-for-8 for 45 yards on the series, while Vinatieri’s final kick proved to be the last play at the old Foxboro Stadium. | Highlights Most recent game: Mike Vrabel led the Patriots to the Super Bowl in his first year as head coach, but his tenure actually started with a loss last September. Hosting the Raiders in Week 1, Vrabel’s team struggled to string positive plays together and was outscored 13-3 in the second half to turn a 10-7 halftime lead into a 20-13 defeat. Drake Maye threw a touchdown and an interception, Kayshon Boutte had 103 receiving yards, Jaylinn Hawkins caught a pick, and DeMario Douglas finished with more touchdowns (1) than yards (-2). | Highlights The 2-2 Patriots will take on the 3-1 Raiders at Gillette Stadium on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Patriots vs. Raiders preview for NFL Week 5
summary: Coming off a big win in Buffalo, the New England Patriots are returning back home in Week 5. The team of head coach Mike Vrabel, now in possession, of a 2-2 record, will host the Las Vegas Raiders at Gillette Stadium. The Raiders have been one of the surprise teams of the season thus far. […]
full_text: Coming off a big win in Buffalo, the New England Patriots are returning back home in Week 5. The team of head coach Mike Vrabel, now in possession, of a 2-2 record, will host the Las Vegas Raiders at Gillette Stadium. The Raiders have been one of the surprise teams of the season thus far. What can the Patriots therefore expect? Let’s find out. Raiders key stats The Raiders have opened the season with a 3-1 record, their best start since 2021. Unsurprisingly, their numbers look the part. EPA/play 0.034 (11th) -0.043 (22nd) Off. EPA/dropback 0.225 (7th) 0.039 (21st) Off. EPA/run -0.238 (29th) -0.168 (23rd) Def. yards/game 337.3 (19th) 293.8 (6th) Def. Offensively, the Raiders have been particularly good moving the ball through the air. Led by veteran Kirk Cousins, the unit has generally been effective. The run game remains a work in progress, though, ranking only 29th in EPA per play and 32nd in yards per attempt. Defensively, there is no such split: the unit is stout both in the passing game and against the run, generates plenty of pressure, and has taken the ball away more than any other team in the league through four games. It has struggled a bit in the red zone (29th) but overall has been very good and a key reason why Las Vegas is 3-1 in the first place. Raiders 2026 season As noted above, the Raiders are in the midst of their best start since 2021 — an impressive feat given that they are a) led by a first-team head coach and b) picked first overall in April. That said, the record requires some context. Week 1: 27-13 win vs. Miami Dolphins (1-0) Week 2: 26-14 win at Los Angeles Chargers (2-0) Week 3: 35-27 win at New Orleans Saints (3-0) Week 4: 30-27 loss vs. Kansas City Chiefs (3-1) Teams don’t go 3-1 by accident, but it needs to be pointed out that the Raiders’ opponents during their 3-0 start have all underwhelmed this season. If we remove their games against Las Vegas from the equation, the Dolphins, Chargers and Saints are a combined 1-8 this year. Among the 14 teams in the current playoff picture , none has as low a strength of victory as the Raiders’ .083. This begs the question: are they a paper tiger? So far the evidence is inconclusive, but a second straight game against a playoff-caliber opponent could provide a preliminary answer. So far, however, that placeholder has done his job well. In his four starts, Cousins has completed 93 of 144 passes (64.6%) for 1,026 yards, a league-best 11 touchdowns and four interceptions. He also has taken just five sacks and ranks 10th among all NFL QBs in EPA per play (0.214). The story of Cousins’ supporting cast starts at tight end, where Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer are as formidable a 1-2 as any in football. Bowers is ranked first on the team with 25 targets, catching 16 of them for 202 yards and a pair of touchdowns. Mayer leads the team with 20 catches of 24 targets, gaining 169 yards and also scoring once. Also regularly targeted are multi-purpose running back Ashton Jeanty, whose 429 scrimmage yards — 264 on the ground plus 165 through the air — lead the team. At wide receiver, Tre Tucker’s 15 catches for 233 yards and one touchdown lead the way, while third option Cody White tops the Raiders with three scores thus far. The group is anchored by an offensive line that made free agency pickup Tyler Linderbaum the highest-paid center in NFL history this offseason. On the other side of the line of scrimmage lies the real strength of this team. While the interior is relatively solid, and featuring former Patriot Adam Butler as its third option, the edge is one of the deepest in all of football. It is led by Maxx Crosby, whose offseason drama involving a near-trade to the Baltimore Ravens has seemingly had no effect on his output: his 25 total pressures are ranked fourth in the league through four weeks, while he also registered 2.0 sacks, a forced fumble, and a recovery. Crosby is the big name, but Kwity Paye and Malcolm Koonce have also been productive opposite him, picking up nine and 12 pressures, respectively; Koonce also forced a pair of fumbles. Speaking of fumbles, off-ball linebacker Nakobe Dean has forced three of them, the most in football so far. The Raiders also have the league leader in interceptions on their roster, with fifth-round draft pick Hezekiah Masses picking off three passes in four games to start his NFL career. Masses’ play has been one of the big stories for a team whose secondary is quite experienced elsewhere: Eric Stokes, Taron Johnson and Jeremy Chinn are all established players. The only other question mark from that perspective is No. 2 safety Treydan Stukes, who also arrived during this year’s draft. In the kicking game, the Raiders are relying on experience as well. Kicker Matt Gay and punter A.J. Cole are both in their eighth seasons in the league. Gay has made all 10 of his field goals and all nine of his extra points thus far. His afternoon there spanned 47 rushing yards, 27 receiving yards, a touchdown and a two-point conversion. And a knee injury. Yet the starting running back was officially among nine partial participants to begin the new week. So was Barmore across the line of scrimmage. A shoulder injury had kept No. 90 out for three straight practices on the way to landing among New England’s inactives . The defensive tackle was back on hand Wednesday after head coach Mike Vrabel hinted he “may do some things.” The same availability went for an undrafted rookie corner in Canada, who had been downgraded from questionable on the eve of the 1 p.m. ET divisional kickoff because of a hamstring injury. New England’s quarterback did not carry a game designation before becoming AFC Offensive Player of the Week . title: Mike Vrabel gives a status update on Patriots WR Kyle Williams
summary: Kyle Williams seemed poised for a bigger role this season. The New England Patriots’ second-year wide receiver had flashed in preseason, been on the receiving end of some considerable praise from his head coach, and saw fellow wideout Kayshon Boutte get traded to the Houston Texans. The stage therefore appeared set for Williams to take […]
full_text: Kyle Williams seemed poised for a bigger role this season. The New England Patriots’ second-year wide receiver had flashed in preseason , been on the receiving end of some considerable praise from his head coach, and saw fellow wideout Kayshon Boutte get traded to the Houston Texans. The stage therefore appeared set for Williams to take a leap in Year 2. Four games in, he hasn’t. Even with the Patriots struggling with availability at his position, Williams has caught just two passes for 44 combined yards, tying for ninth and sixth on the team in the respective categories. And yet, Mike Vrabel is still feeling good about his development. “He continues to improve,” New England’s HC told reporters on Wednesday. “Sometimes, it’s hard to hear that or believe that when you have to be able to see the football and to be able to get it. He has helped us out on the kickoff returns. I would’ve liked for us to have thrown a better ball to him down in the end zone [against the Buffalo Bills], but that didn’t happen.” Williams’ lack of production is not necessarily due to a lack of opportunities. Including the play against the Bills mentioned by Vrabel — a fourth-quarter go ball down the right sideline that fell incomplete — he has been targeted seven times in 64 offensive snaps. Even though that is not a monumental number, it still puts him on track to surpass his 21-target rookie regular season in 2025. The stats just don’t look the part just yet, something that also holds true for his role as New England’s primary kickoff returner. On 11 runbacks, the same number he had all of last season, Williams is averaging only 24.8 yards so far. Will something change with A.J. Brown still on injured reserve and Mack Hollins’ injury outlook also unclear this season? Time will tell, but his usage so far suggests that no major change should be expected. Mike Vrabel nonetheless remains in Williams’ corner. “I would say that he’s committed to working and improving and understanding more than one spot”, he said about Williams. “We’re excited about where he’s going to go.”

title: Efton Chism focused on opportunity ahead, not Bills trash talk
summary: New England Patriots wide receiver Efton Chism III was asked about Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson’s postgame comments on Wednesday. The wide receiver decided not to jab back.  “He’s a great player. They’re a great team. I got a bunch of respect for him, but we’re excited for this week, looking forward to the Raiders,” Chism […]
full_text: New England Patriots wide receiver Efton Chism III was asked about Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson’s postgame comments on Wednesday. The wide receiver decided not to jab back. “He’s a great player. They’re a great team. I got a bunch of respect for him, but we’re excited for this week, looking forward to the Raiders,” Chism said at his locker. Chism submitted one of the early catch-of-the-year candidates last Sunday in Buffalo, fully extending with one hand to haul in the game-winning touchdown. Gardner Johnson, however, wasn’t impressed. “An elevated guy made a hell of a catch — probably won’t hear from him again,” Gardner-Johnson said. “A practice squad player made a hell of a play. That’s all I’m going to tell you. You do it again, and he probably won’t make it again.” The Patriots are expecting to hear more from Chism, who — unlike Gardner-Johnson — has never been on a practice squad in his career. With A.J. Brown remaining on injured reserve through at least next week and Mack Hollins (calf) sidelined from Wednesday’s practice, Chism is set to see increased opportunities. “For me, it’s just reset. The good, the bad, whatever it is, it’s getting back to my work and our work as a team. Try to stack another one,” Chism said. “You never know when you’re going to get those opportunities. Just trying to take advantage of them. Nobody ever wants to see people get hurt. I want those guys back, I know everyone else wants those guys back. But continue to prepare like a starter.” Beyond the injuries, Chism’s performance on Sunday and work ethic behind the scenes could also earn him more opportunities in the offense. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye complimented how smart Chism is as a player and how he’s always in the right spot, a trait Maye described as reassuring for a quarterback. The duo stay after practice nearly everyday to bank reps, and now Maye is ready to see what Chism can do with a bigger role. “It’s been awesome just seeing Chis come in here and be the same guy,” Maye said. “From Day 1, you saw. You can tell when a guy from my experience, a receiver, who has a chance at making plays. You see that with Chis. He’s fearless. “He’s doing a lot of the little things. He’s just showing up. He comes in everyday and always tries to see my side of things and ask questions and try to get on the same page. And that’s what happens: you start seeing the results.”

summary: Drake Maye has been named AFC Offensive Player of the Week following his resurgence at Highmark Stadium. He added a team-high and season-high 54 rushing yards to lead the conference’s […]

(Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images Drake Maye has been named AFC Offensive Player of the Week following his resurgence at Highmark Stadium. The New England Patriots captain completed 22-of-37 passes for 269 yards and three touchdowns in last Sunday’s 29-26 AFC East upset against the Buffalo Bills. He added a team-high and season-high 54 rushing yards to lead the conference’s quarterbacks by the end of Week 4. Week 4 belongs to @DrakeMaye2 🙂‍↕️ pic.twitter.com/ifqG8dU3mI — New England Patriots (@Patriots) October 7, 2026 Jacksonville Jaguars linebacker Foyesade Oluokun and Kansas City Chiefs punter Matt Araiza joined the QB as AFC Defensive Player of the Week and AFC Special Teams Players of the Week, respectively. Entering last Sunday’s divisional matchup with one touchdown and seven turnovers on the campaign, Maye was intercepted once and lost a fumble on the lone occasion he was sacked in Orchard Park. But the 24-year-old delivered two scoring strikes to Romeo Doubs and hit the right glove of Efton Chism III for the game-winning TD with 1:50 remaining in the fourth quarter. And with that, the unbeaten Bills went to 3-1 while the Patriots went to 2-2. “It’s great. It’s great to see him be recognized for his performance and helping us win,” head coach Mike Vrabel said during his Wednesday press conference . “I want us to win those awards every single week, whether that’s Drake or anybody on offense or the performances that we could have on defense or special teams.” For the No. 3 overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft, it marks the second career AFC Offensive Player of the Week honor. Maye finds himself the fifth quarterback in franchise history to get the call multiple times, joining 30-time winner Tom Brady, six-time winner Drew Bledsoe as well as two-time winners Matt Cassel in Tony Eason. The North Carolina product also joins running back Willie Parker and tight end Alge Crumpler as the only Tar Heels to twice be named AFC Offensive Player of the Week during their careers. A reigning second-team All-Pro who paced the NFL in passer rating and completion percentage on the way to Super Bowl LX, Maye will cross paths with the Las Vegas Raiders next Sunday. Kickoff at Gillette Stadium is set for 1 p.m. ET.

title: Patriots strength of schedule talk is back on the menu
summary: One of the biggest talking points surrounding the New England Patriots last season was the supposedly easy schedule they played on their way to a division title, playoff berth, and ultimately the Super Bowl. While some of it was naturally hyperbole, there was some truth to the fact that the team benefitted from its fourth-place […]
full_text: One of the biggest talking points surrounding the New England Patriots last season was the supposedly easy schedule they played on their way to a division title, playoff berth, and ultimately the Super Bowl. While some of it was naturally hyperbole, there was some truth to the fact that the team benefitted from its fourth-place schedule and a generally weak year in the AFC. This season was supposed to be different. Entering 2026, the team was set to go up against an above-average slate of opponents. Based on win-loss totals from a year ago, their scheduled ranked as the sixth-hardest; based on projected win totals, they ranked 10th. Turns out, their schedule might be a lot easier than that if we use the first four weeks of the season as an indication. Using traditional win-loss rate, only three other clubs have it easier down the stretch than the current 2-2 team. And here we go — Ben Baldwin (@rbsdm.com) 2026-10-05T14:09:03.560Z Even if we use a more complex methodology — Pro Football Focus’ point spread rating — we can see that New England’s schedule from here on out becomes a lot more manageable. Strength of schedule data via PFF. Lower number is tougher opponents. So for instance, the Raiders, Chiefs, and 49ers have had the easiest schedule so far, will have the toughest going forward (they all play each other). The Lions had easy so far, will stay that way. pic.twitter.com/uYARXVWqTB — Shaun Newkirk (@Shauncore) October 6, 2026 That does not mean the Patriots’ remaining 13 games won’t have their pitfalls and potential for problems. Whether it is teams getting healthier at key positions (i.e. Chicago Bears) or hitting their stride at the right time (i.e. Green Bay Packers), or challenging circumstances due to scheduling (i.e. two Thursday night games) or location (i.e. Detroit Lions in Germany), anything can happen even if the projection works in New England’s favor at the moment. Still, what this shows more than anything is that the Patriots have a chance to build some momentum after a challenging four-game stretch to open the season. Given that they are 2-2 and currently inside the AFC playoff picture , they have the potential to keep making some noise. It starts with internal improvement both performance- and health-wise, but the schedule certainly could help with that as well. Again.

title: Examining the roster ties between Patriots, Raiders ahead of Week 5
summary: There’s the Josh McDaniels connection. There’s the Tom Brady connection. And then there’s those in the AFC East and AFC West locker rooms. Between the active rosters, practice squads and reserve lists, eight players in the fold for Sunday have been both New England Patriots and Las Vegas Raiders during the NFL journeys. Here’s a […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 13: Adam Butler #69 of the Las Vegas Raiders enters the field during player introductions prior to an NFL football game against the Miami Dolphins at Allegiant Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images There’s the Josh McDaniels connection. There’s the Tom Brady connection. And then there’s those in the AFC East and AFC West locker rooms. Between the active rosters, practice squads and reserve lists, eight players in the fold for Sunday have been both New England Patriots and Las Vegas Raiders during the NFL journeys. Here’s a glance through the list of the formers leading up to the 1 p.m. ET kickoff at Gillette Stadium. LAS VEGAS Phillip Dorsett II, wide receiver — Dorsett has not made appearance beyond the preseason since 2023. But the No. 29 overall pick in the 2015 NFL draft has continued his career in Las Vegas as a member of the practice squad over the past two campaigns. That’s after making a previous stop there when New England’s current offensive coordinator held the title of head coach. The 33-year-old wide receiver has caught 151 passes for 2,001 yards and 12 touchdowns since entering the league out of the University of Miami more than a decade ago. In 2017, he landed in Foxborough at the 53-man roster deadline as the Indianapolis Colts landed quarterback Jacoby Brissett. From there, Dorsett reeled in 73 passes for 881 yards and eight touchdowns across 45 games in the regular season. The playoffs stretched additional 126 yards and two trips to the end zone. A Super Bowl LIII ring followed. Adam Butler, defensive tackle — Butler entered the league at Gillette Stadium as an undrafted free agent in 2017. The former Vanderbilt convert from the offensive line to the defensive line went on to appear in 63 games, starting 12, while having a hand in 96 tackles, 15 sacks and nine batted passes. After being retained on a restricted tender in 2020, the Super Bowl LIII champion moved on to another corner of the AFC East. Yet Butler was released by the Miami Dolphins with a failed physical designation in 2022 and spent the year out of football. The 32-year-old defensive tackle has since found his footing in Las Vegas over the past four seasons. Butler’s time in silver and black has spanned 53 games, 32 starts, 152 tackles and 11.5 sacks. He’s also knocked down six passes, forced two fumbles and recovered two fumbles. Patrick Johnson, defensive end — Now on the 53-man roster for the Raiders, Johnson had seen his agreement in Foxborough expire in February. The 28-year-old edge rusher joined the practice squad of the 2025 AFC champions during preparations for Super Bowl LX. Originally entering entering the NFL in the seventh round of the 2021 draft at No. 234 overall, Johnson was a member of the Philadelphia Eagles’ Super Bowl LVII team and has also spent time with the New York Giants as a waiver claim. The Tulane product has checked into 74 games in the regular season while totaling 50 tackles, one sack, one forced fumble and one recovery as well as a pair of starts. Cameron McGrone, linebacker — The Patriots called McGrone’s name in the fifth round of the 2021 class at No. 177 overall. But with a redshirt year on deck after the Michigan product sustained a second torn ACL during his final Big Ten season. McGrone started and finished his rookie campaign on the non-football injury list despite having his 21-day practice window open. After going through the waiver wire unclaimed at the end of the 2022 preseason, McGrone was brought back on New England’s practice squad. He’d depart for a 53-man roster spot in Indianapolis that winter, however, and the 26-year-old linebacker’s stay in the AFC South stretched into 2025. A stint with the Cleveland Browns followed before heading to the desert in May. McGrone then joined the Raiders’ practice squad at its formation. His NFL career includes 27 appearances and 13 tackles through 51 snaps on defense and 390 snaps on special teams. NEW ENGLAND Mack Hollins, wide receiver — The 33-year-old Hollins agreed to terms with the Patriots on a two-year deal as an unrestricted free agent in 2025. The move reunited the veteran wide receiver with his head coach from 2022. Hollins found four touchdowns and career highs with 94 targets, 57 receptions and 690 yards while a member of McDaniels’ Raiders that season. He now stands 131 games, 56 starts, 223 catches, 2,828 yards and 17 touchdowns into an NFL run that began in the fourth round of the 2017 draft at No. 118 overall. The former North Carolina Tar Heel won a Super Bowl LII while a rookie in Philadelphia. Tours with six different NFL clubs have been logged. He leads his current club in receptions and receiving yards while also being tied with Romeo Doubs in targets, but did not finish the first game of October due to a calf injury. Ben Brown, guard — Back in the starting lineup amid attrition, Brown has appeared in 30 games since New England signed him to the 53-man roster off the practice squad of Las Vegas in the fall of 2024. Taking the field at center, left guard, right guard and jumbo tight end, the 28-year-old offensive lineman has handled 1,086 downs on offense for the organization. He’s also gotten the nod for 15 starts, with the first of his NFL career coming same week he left Las Vegas and the latest in place of two veterans on injured reserve. Brown made his initial stops with the Cincinnati Bengals, Seattle Seahawks and Arizona Cardinals after going undrafted in 2022. The Ole Miss product reached a contract extension in December and returned to the active roster shortly after being released in a procedural move in August. Greg Van Roten, guard — The 36-year-old Van Roten visited Gillette Stadium during training camp and circled back to sign a one-year deal after the aforementioned backup interior lineman suffered a multiweek injury. He started at right guard in New England’s first game without incumbent Mike Onwenu. But a thigh injury has since sent the NFL veteran of 147 games and 106 starts to IR, as well. Van Roten began his career as an undrafted rookie with the Green Bay Packers in 2012. The All-Ivy League offensive tackle out of Penn has been a member of nine different NFL teams as well as the CFL’s Toronto Argonauts over the years since then. And in 2023, his lone year in Las Vegas, he started all 17 games before going wire-to-wire in 2024 and 2025 with the New York Giants. Robert Spillane, linebacker — Spillane finds himself a back-to-back team captain for the Patriots after reaching a three-year pact entering the 2025 league year. The 30-year-old Western Michigan alum has appeared in 103 games, starting 67, since entering the NFL in 2018 as an undrafted tryout at rookie minicamp with head coach Mike Vrabel’s former Tennessee Titans. Spillane went on to spend four seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers before heading to Las Vegas in 2023. From there, the linebacker became a Raiders captain and started every game across two campaigns, respectively posting 148 and 158 tackles as well as 1,101 and 1,095 defensive snaps. A veteran of 623 tackles and 9.5 sacks, Spillane’s NFL odometer includes three forced fumbles, two fumble recoveries, eight interceptions and one touchdown return.

title: Chris Olave continues to shine despite Saints’ ugly loss
summary: The New Orleans Saints had very little go right in Monday night’s 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons, but Chris Olave continued to show why he should be considered one of the best wide receivers in the NFL. Olave finished the night with eight receptions for 116 yards on 12 targets. with a long reception […]
full_text: The New Orleans Saints had very little go right in Monday night’s 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons, but Chris Olave continued to show why he should be considered one of the best wide receivers in the NFL. Olave finished the night with eight receptions for 116 yards on 12 targets. with a long reception of 44 yards, leading the Saints in all three categories. This marked Olave’s third 100-yard receiving game through the first four weeks of the season and his second consecutive game surpassing that mark. He has now recorded at least eight receptions in all four games this season while reaching double-digit targets in each contest. That consistency has made Olave one of the few dependable pieces of the Saints’ offense that has had a difficult start. Through four games, Olave has 35 receptions for 491 yards (second league-wide) and one touchdown. He is averaging 14 yards per reception and has already established himself as the focal point of the Saints’ passing attack. Against Atlanta, Olave’s 116 receiving yards accounted for more than one-third of New Orleans’ 320 total yards. While the Saints ultimately could not keep pace with Atlanta, Olave’s performance was another reminder that New Orleans should feel comfortable with their investment in the wideout. For a team searching for answers after falling to 1-3, Olave has been one of the few constants. His production has not slowed despite the Saints’ struggles, and Monday night was the latest example.
author: Nic Jennings

title: Is Kellen Moore’s seat hot after loss to the Falcons?
summary: The New Orleans Saints’ 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons on Monday night felt different. It was completely embarrassing. It was not just another loss. It was a total failure across all three phases on a night that was so special to the city and the fanbase. The Saints had an opportunity to make a […]
full_text: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-SEPTEMBER 13: Head coach Kellen Moore of the New Orleans Saints reacts to a call during the second half of an NFL football game between the New Orleans Saints and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Sunday, September 13, 2026 (Photo by Jorge Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images The New Orleans Saints’ 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons on Monday night felt different. It was completely embarrassing. It was not just another loss. It was a total failure across all three phases on a night that was so special to the city and the fanbase. The Saints had an opportunity to make a statement in front of a nationally televised audience, and they blew it. And now, it’s fair to ask how hot Kellen Moore’s seat is after a 1-3 start. Moore did not hide from the performance afterward. He repeatedly acknowledged that the Saints were not prepared for Monday night’s game, which is frustrating to hear after knowing how important this game was and how much it meant to the organization. It would be easier to accept if it were an isolated occurrence. But it hasn’t been. The Saints under Kellen Moore have now trailed by double digits 16 times since the start of the 2025 season, the most in the NFL over that span. Monday night was another example, as Atlanta jumped out to a 14-0 lead in the first quarter and extended it to 24-7 by halftime. The problem isn’t simply that New Orleans has fallen behind. It’s that Moore has been asked repeatedly why his team continues to struggle to open games, and his answers have consistently come back to some version of needing to look at things, make adjustments and figure out what went wrong. At some point, those answers have to turn into results. The Saints scored just six total first-quarter points through their first four games and have been forced to play from behind in every game this season. Under Moore, New Orleans has failed to score in the first quarter 14 times. That puts immense pressure on Moore to fix the preparation and execution issues that have followed his team into another season. There is still plenty of football left to play, and firing a head coach after four games would be an extreme move. But this is also Year 2 for Moore, so there’s no excuse of this being his first rodeo. The Saints expected progress after a six-win first season, and instead they are 1-3 after getting embarrassed by their biggest rival on Monday night. Moore has repeatedly said the Saints need to look at themselves. Now, the question is how long the organization will continue waiting for the answers to translate onto the field before they take a look at him.

Tyler Shough did his best to try to keep the Saints in the game and ripped a handful of excellent throws, but the offensive onslaught and the relentless pressure generated by Atlanta’s pass rush was simply too much to overcome, exposing New Orleans’ mortality and dampening its outlook after four weeks.“ Fox Sports – 23 (-7) “They had a real shot to win each of their first three games before getting blown out by the Falcons on Monday night, and there are two big reasons why they’re in a bit of trouble. One is the injury to RB Travis Etienne, because it’s pretty clear Alvin Kamara can’t lead their rushing attack anymore. The other is that their rushing defense is terrible. The Falcons ripped through them for more than 200 yards and they’ve given up almost 600 rushing yards in four games. It’s a pretty good bet the Vikings, Giants and Steelers are going to try to take advantage of both those things over the next three weeks before the Saints’ bye.“ Bleacher Report – 24 (-8) “Maybe the New Orleans Saints are who we thought they were entering the season. That is forcing Tyler Shough to try to win with his arm, and while the second-year signal-caller has exceeded expectations, he’s not that guy. Not yet. title: State of the NFC South: Week 4 recap
summary: A new battle at the top of the division. Tampa Bay Buccaneers At the bottom of the NFC South, the Buccaneers have been bad. Another winnable game was in front of them, but they basically gave it away. This team is 0-4 going into Week 5 with Baker Mayfield injured, bad coaching, roster issues everywhere, […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 05: Bijan Robinson #7 of the Atlanta Falcons runs the ball for to score a 59 yard touchdown against the New Orleans Saints during the first quarter of the game at Caesars Superdome on October 05, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) | Getty Images A new battle at the top of the division. Tampa Bay Buccaneers At the bottom of the NFC South, the Buccaneers have been bad. Another winnable game was in front of them, but they basically gave it away. This team is 0-4 going into Week 5 with Baker Mayfield injured, bad coaching, roster issues everywhere, and a lack of run game. Green Bay also looked like they wanted to lose this game, and maybe if Mayfield was playing, they would have, but hope is lost with this team. Tampa Bay has a tough matchup against the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday Night Football, so it looks like this team is going 0-5. Carolina Panthers On the opposite end of the division, Carolina did really well on Sunday Night Football against the Detroit Lions. The offense was really consistent and picked the Lions apart all night, with Tetairoa McMillan having a career night, and the run defense did really well against Jahmyr Gibbs. That same defense allowed Jared Goff to throw for more than 400 yards, so it wasn’t perfect, but it was impressive nonetheless. In Week 5, the Panthers have a winnable game, but the defense will need to do a bit better against the Jalen Hurts-led offense. Atlanta Falcons Now to our NFC South matchup of the week. The Falcons came into this game as an unknown, and they left fighting for first place in the division. Atlanta’s offense had the easiest day of their life, basically seeing zero resistance in the run and pass game, and the defense didn’t have to worry about the Saints’ rushing attack once. The Falcons have not seen a challenge in the past two weeks; maybe that will change in Week 5 against the Baltimore Ravens. New Orleans Saints On the other side of the matchup, the Saints were embarrassing in this one. Just a horrible loss in a game with so much emotion, and now, the team is 1-3 with hope ripped away from the fan base. Tyler Shough, Chris Olave, Chase Young, and Juwan Johnson are still the top guys on this team and it’s clear, but besides that group, it has not been great and now the Saints will have to go up against the Minnesota Vikings. NFC South standings: Carolina Panthers (1-2) Atlanta Falcons (2-2) New Orleans Saints (1-3) Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-4)
