title: Giants Malik Nabers explains emotional outburst vs. Cardinals
summary: Malik Nabers was not happy about his lack of second-half targets Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals, and the New York Giants star wide receiver let the sideline know it during the game. “I felt like I didn’t get targeted much after halftime. So, that was just a thing,” Nabers said. “It’s just – I felt […]
full_text: Malik Nabers | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Malik Nabers was not happy about his lack of second-half targets Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals, and the New York Giants star wide receiver let the sideline know it during the game. “I felt like I didn’t get targeted much after halftime. So, that was just a thing,” Nabers said. “It’s just – I felt like creating explosives down the field was just helping us get in a better position to score touchdowns. Some of those plays didn’t come my way, so just trying to figure out why.” Nabers caught five passes on five targets in the first half for 84 yards. He caught one pass for 28 yards on just two targets in the second half. Nabers and head coach John Harbaugh talked about the receiver’s frustration after the game. “I talked to him just about – just trying to clarify on – I think we need to implement more things after halftime,” Nabers said. “Just also trying to give me the ball down the field to create some of those opportunities for us to gain more points. It felt like during the first half when we did that, it kind of led into the right direction with scoring touchdowns in the red zone. And just – after that, we just couldn’t get going. So, I felt like the offense was needing a spark and I wanted to be that spark, so I was just trying to figure out what was going on, and what was the thought process on going into after halftime and coming out, what was the talk that he had with the coaches on implementing things down the field – we had a talk about it.” Harbaugh said that Nabers is “emotional.” “I don’t even know what he was saying because I didn’t hear it – I couldn’t hear. But he’s emotional, he’s a competitor,” Harbaugh said. “I do think that – he and I talked after the game just like we always do, and one of the things that comes through in getting to know Malik is that he’s definitely a high-energy, emotional self-motivator. I think that’s kind of how he gets his energy riled up. So, if it helps him play better, great. If it gets in his way at some point in time and we think it’s hindering him in some way, then I’d like to see less of whatever. “We always talk all the time about (it to the) guys. If it’s helping us, we want more of it and if it’s hurting us, we want less of it. So, I don’t think it was hurting him in any way, whatever that was, and we had a great conversation after and I think I understand that part of him. I’m getting to know him a little better that way.” Nabers said veteran running backs coach Willie Taggart had a chat with him after the game about how to “use his voice. “He was just telling me how to just use my voice. I have a huge voice in the offense, so the more and more I’m reserved and not really saying a lot, it kind of can be either taken as the wrong way or a positive way. Like I say, I’m really quiet and I stay to myself, so everybody can take that which way they want – but just using my voice and just knowing how to use my voice the right way,” Nabers said. “I would say everything doesn’t have to be an outburst or anything like that. Just simply having a one-on-one conversation or getting the offense going like, ‘Let’s go.’ Just using my voice as a leader and being that guy that everybody wants me to be. Right now, since we’re down a couple of people, I’m just trying to lead the team to get more wins.”

title: NY Giants’ CB Deonte Banks is NFC Defensive Player of the Week
summary: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — Deonte Banks has been named NFC Defensive Player of the Week after his game-saving interception for the New York Giants in Sunday’s 36-24 victory over the Arizona Cardinals. Banks intercepted Arizona quarterback Jacoby Brissett on fourth-and-goal at the 4-yard line, returning the ball 98 yards for a touchdown. Banks said after […]
full_text: Deonte Banks | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — Deonte Banks has been named NFC Defensive Player of the Week after his game-saving interception for the New York Giants in Sunday’s 36-24 victory over the Arizona Cardinals. Banks intercepted Arizona quarterback Jacoby Brissett on fourth-and-goal at the 4-yard line, returning the ball 98 yards for a touchdown. Banks said after the game that he had called his shot during the week . “They was giving me a tight end and a receiver set all day. I’ve been thinking a slant all day and they haven’t been giving it to me,” Banks said. “That time I just knew they were going to give it to me. It was just a matter of time because they kept running it. “I knew I was going to take it. I’ve been calling it all week. I’m going to pick a slant this week.” “My guy. Tae Banks!” Wink Martindale’s belief in Deonte Banks never wavered. He talks about the Giants’ excellent “cat coverage” corner & breaks down his Pick-6 “Wednesdays with Wink” is up NOW on the Talkin’ Ball with Pat Leonard @YouTube Channel 👀 Brought to you by… pic.twitter.com/M8uCHu0g9K — Pat Leonard (@PLeonardNYDN) October 7, 2026 Banks also had four passes defensed, tied for the most in a game by any player this season. A first-round pick in 2023, Banks had a promising rookie season. The last two seasons, though, have been difficult, and there were questions entering the season about what role Banks might have. He has, though, responded to the opportunity given to him by head coach John Harbaugh. “We just taught the defense really and talked to him about playing technique the right way, and he was just really amenable to it,” Harbaugh said. “We didn’t really have any kind of an in-depth conversation about the past. You know, that really wasn’t part of it. Just said, ‘Hey, man, we know what you’re capable of, let’s go play some good football.’ And maybe that was just all it took, maybe that’s all that was really needed. I do think he felt the confidence. I think he felt happy about the opportunity, maybe. Maybe he was freed up a little bit from the past, whatever happened. I mean, he had a great year his first year. So, maybe he leaned into that a little bit more. I’m not really sure, but it just wasn’t something we thought too much about. We just made it about the football, probably, more than anything.”

title: NY Giants sign QB Jake Haener to their 53-man roster, per report
summary: The New York Giants are signing backup quarterback Jake Haener to their 53-man roster, per a report from Mike Garafolo of the NFL Network. This fills the roster spot opened by the loss of wide receiver/kick returner Braxton Berrios. The Giants singed Haener on Aug. 17 following some disastrous preseason performances by Brandon Allen. Haener, […]
full_text: Jake Haener | Getty Images The New York Giants are signing backup quarterback Jake Haener to their 53-man roster, per a report from Mike Garafolo of the NFL Network . This fills the roster spot opened by the loss of wide receiver/kick returner Braxton Berrios . The Giants singed Haener on Aug. 17 following some disastrous preseason performances by Brandon Allen. Haener, 27, is a former fourth-round pick by the New Orleans Saints in the 2023 NFL Draft. He spent time as the Saints’ starting quarterback in 2024 after Derek Carr’s Week 14 injury, but was waived and signed to the Saints’ practice squad in 2025. Haener played well enough for the Giants in the final preseason game and was ultimately signed to the practice squad instead of Allen. Haener now likely becomes the Giants’ primary backup while J.J. McCarthy gets up to speed. This does raise the question as to whether or not the Giants will employ their “McCarthy package” against the Washington Commanders. This also opens up a spot on the Giants’ practice squad. The Giants did have a visit on Tuesday from wide receiver Dontae Fleming , who spent last season on the Minnesota Vikings’ practice squad.
author: Chris Pflum

title: Odell Beckham Jr. signs with the Vikings practice squad
summary: The Minnesota Vikings announced Thursday morning that they’ve signed former New York Giants star wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. to their practice squad. The Giants originally signed Beckham to their 90-man roster back on June 1, and while the ball didn’t find Beckham in games, he looked solid in practice and preseason. He ultimately made […]
full_text: Wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings announced Thursday morning that they’ve signed former New York Giants star wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. to their practice squad. The Giants originally signed Beckham to their 90-man roster back on June 1, and while the ball didn’t find Beckham in games, he looked solid in practice and preseason. He ultimately made the Giants’ initial 53-man roster after final cutdowns. However, he only saw 20 snaps over the first three games with the Giants before being released prior to Week 4. Beckham remained a fan favorite in New York, receiving ovations every time he got on the field, but his second stint as a Giant ended with no catches. It was reported that Beckham had no interest in signing with the Giants’ practice squad and wanted to go somewhere where he had a better chance to play. The Vikings are looking for a spark on offense, and head coach Kevin O’Connell is familiar with Beckham from their time together with the Los Angeles Rams.

title: Cornerback Greg Newsome explains the Giants’ ballhawking ways
summary: There were plenty of stories that came out of the New York Giants 36-24 win over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 4. One of the biggest was how the Giants’ defense transformed itself after the Cardinals’ second drive. The story of the game has been how the Giants’ front seven took over the game, but […]
full_text: New York Giants cornerback Greg Newsome II intercepts a pass against the Arizona Cardinals. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images There were plenty of stories that came out of the New York Giants 36-24 win over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 4. One of the biggest was how the Giants’ defense transformed itself after the Cardinals’ second drive. The story of the game has been how the Giants’ front seven took over the game, but the development of the secondary was just as important. Veteran cornerback Greg Newsome II has been a steady presence on the outside for the Giants, and was one of three players to intercept Jacobi Brissett on Sunday. His experience and demeanor has led to him becoming one of the leaders on the back end of the Giants’ defense. He was careful, though, to credit front seven players like Abdul Carter, Brian Burns, Tremaine Edmunds, and D.J. Reader. “Guys are hunting,” Newsome said. “Guys are giving us chances to get our hands on footballs. It’s also great in the secondary that we’re playing tight coverage. We’re getting our heads around and just trying to find the football. But, like I said, once again, it’s rush and coverage working together, so without those guys up front, we wouldn’t have 14. Shout out to those guys up front.” We anticipated before the season that Dennard Wilson would want to base his defense on “Step” coverage — that is, coverage with the cornerback within a step of the receiver. The philosophy is to challenge quarterbacks to consistently make tight window throws. Each of the Giants’ corners has upside in press-man coverage, and Newsome has been one of the best in the NFL in playing tight coverage. Here's a look at how cornerbacks have been in coverage through the first three games of the season. Trent McDuffie on another planet right now in his first season with the Rams. — Ben Baby (@bbaby41.bsky.social) 2026-10-01T17:06:17.213Z The tight coverage combined with the pressure generated by the Giants’ front seven has the Giants among the league leaders in takeaways. The Giants are tied for third with eight total turnovers and tied for first in the NFL with six interceptions. Newsome explained that the Giants’ secondary makes a point of practicing taking the ball away during the week. “First, our coaches. Just how we structure practice,” he said. “We’re always doing takeaway things before we get into team activities and things like that. Obviously, I think our d-line, our front seven, the guys that are blitzing. I think they’re doing a great job of just pressuring the quarterback, affecting the quarterback, and just giving us a chance to make plays out there.” It didn’t look so good to start the game against the Cardinals. The Giants’ defense made some plays, but were ultimately little more than a speedbump on the Cardinals’ first two drives. While the interior of the Giants’ defense was stout against Arizona’s runs, the perimeter proved vulnerable to well-schemed off-tackle runs. The game was flipped on its head when Dennard Wilson began to call a much more aggressive defense and used the Giants’ speed to disrupt the Cardinals’ running game as well as their passing attack. That put the ball in Brissett’s hand and Brissett in less advantageous positions. “Them stopping the run makes teams one-dimensional,” Newsome said. “It helps us out on the back end. It helps the linebackers not have to bite up on play fakes and things like that. I think with them doing such a great job up there with the front seven, it definitely helps our job, and just getting them on passing downs, allowing our guys to go up there and attack, so I think they’ve been doing an amazing job.” This Giants team is playing with much more confidence and tenacity than fans are used to seeing from their squad. It shows in how they’ve won their last two games: Walk-off interceptions in the closing seconds of the game. However, John Harbaugh seems to be channeling Han Solo and is coaching his players to not let their confidence turn into cockiness. “We’re underdogs every week, so that’s enough humbling for us,” Newsome said. “We’ve got to continue to keep going 1-0 each week. We don’t get too high, we don’t get too low. It’s a long season, so it’s great to be 3-1, but we have a lot of football left to play.” Newsome mentioned “going 1-0”, which has been the message from the Giants’ front office and coaches. Observers noticed that the Giants’ brass was wearing tee shirts emblazoned with a “1-0” prior to Sunday’s game. The message is that the players need to focus on getting to a 1-0 record each week. The team seems to have bought into the mantra while they embrace the underdog mentality. “I think we have a lot of vets in here that have played meaningful football that know how much each win matters,” Newsome said. “So we just focus on the next opponent. We don’t really care too much about the last game. It’s in the past, and now we’ve got to find a way to go 1-0 this week.” The Giants have a 3-1 record and lead the NFC East, but you wouldn’t know it from how Newsome says the team is carrying itself. “For sure you can play with an underdog mentality,” he said. “3-1 can easily turn into 3-14. That can easily do that. If you’re not careful enough, and if you have too much – if you’re not humble, you will get humbled. So, at the end of the day, we have to continue to have that mindset that we had in the beginning of the season, and we’re going to carry it the entire way. We definitely will keep that mindset.”
author: Chris Pflum

title: NFL power rankings: Nick’s picks for how teams stack up before Week 5
summary: No. 1 — San Francisco 49ers (4-0) | (2nd) 📈 1 spot The 49ers went into Denver and defeated the Broncos, 24-14. It was a defensive 3-3 game until the end of the third quarter, when Brock Purdy led a nine-play, 28-yard drive that ended in a one-yard touchdown to Deebo Samuel. The 49ers are […]
full_text: Has Bryce Young turned a corner? | Getty Images No. 1 — San Francisco 49ers (4-0) | (2nd) 📈 1 spot The 49ers went into Denver and defeated the Broncos, 24-14. It was a defensive 3-3 game until the end of the third quarter, when Brock Purdy led a nine-play, 28-yard drive that ended in a one-yard touchdown to Deebo Samuel. The 49ers are now undefeated at 4-0, with wins against the Rams, Dolphins, Cardinals, and Broncos. No. 2 — Kansas City Chiefs (4-0) | (3rd) 📈 1 spot The Chiefs scored 21 points in the fourth quarter to secure a victory over Las Vegas in Week 4. The defense held the Raiders to two field goals in the fourth quarter, while forcing a special teams fumble and an interception. It was a complementary win where all three phases did their duty, and Patrick Mahomes only had to complete 15 passes ( of 30 attempts ). Kansas City may reunite with Tyreek Hill too after the terrible injury to Tyquon Thornton. This was a strange, but important, win for the Chiefs against a quality 3-1 Raiders team. No. 3 —Buffalo Bills (3-1) | (1st) 📉 2 spots The New England Patriots came to play! The Bills’ defense surrendered 405 yards in the game, but a late Josh Allen interception, followed by a 12-yard Hunter Henry catch on third-and-ten, secured the victory for New England. The 49ers jump the Bills here, but Buffalo is still a top-three team in the NFL. No. 4 — Seattle Seahawks (3-1) | SAME The Seattle Seahawks defeated the Chargers, 30-23, with Emmanuel Wilson as the number one running back as Jadarian Price was placed on I.R. Seattle was up 27-3 and 30-13 in the game at the start of the fourth quarter, and Los Angeles was able to score 10 points to make the game slightly more interesting, but the Super Bowl champions controlled the game. No. 5 — Los Angeles Rams (2-2) | SAME The Rams went into Philadelphia and scored two fourth-quarter touchdowns while forcing two turnovers on downs from the Eagles. The Rams won 24-20 in a game with 10 punts. Puka Nacua caught nine passes for 125 yards on 12 targets. No. 6 — Minnesota Vikings (4-0) | (7th) 📈 1 spot The Vikings took down the Miami Dolphins, 15-10, in an uninspiring win led — of course — by Brian Flores’ defense. Kyler Murray threw for 247 yards, but it still left so much to be desired. The Vikings kicked five field goals to win the game. I don’t love having this team in the top-six, to be honest, but their defense is elite, and they’re a well-coached team that just needs more from their quarterback position. No. 7 — Chicago Bears (3-1) | (9th) 📈 2 spots Ben Johnson is fun! The Bears possessed the football for more than 42 minutes; the Jets had 157 total yards on just 32 plays! New York wasn’t disciplined, committing 12 penalties for 76 yards. Quarterback Tyson Bagent did enough to secure the win, but former Rutgers running back Kyle Monangai led the offense with 146 yards on 30 rushes and two scores. A funky, rainy Week 2 loss is the only thing keeping the Bears undefeated. No. 8 — Jacksonville Jaguars (3-1) | (11th) 📈 3 spots The Jaguars’ defense forced two turnovers and a turnover on downs for Cincinnati to end the game, but allowed 437 total yards, while Joe Burrow threw the ball 54 times without Ja’Marr Chase. Jacksonville had a long Bhayshul Tuten touchdown called back for a dubious penalty. Overall, Jacksonville is now 3-1, and they’re playing well under Liam Coen. No. 9 — Baltimore Ravens (3-1) | (6th) 📉 3 spots Baltimore handled its business against the Tennessee Titans, 24-18, with the Titans scoring 11 points in the second half; the story of the game, however, was Lamar Jackson leaving the game at halftime with an ankle injury. The severity of the injury is still unknown, which is why the Ravens fell in the rankings. If it’s an extended absence, they more than likely will continue to fall, asthe offense looked poor with Tyler Huntley at quarterback. No. 10 — Dallas Cowboys (2-2) | (15th) 📈 5 spots Dallas’ defense remains a problem. C.J. Stroud performed well, throwing for 347 yards and two touchdowns against Dallas, but Dak Prescott matched him with 335 yards and a score, while also completing 17 passes to CeeDee Lamb. Javante Williams punched in three rushing touchdowns. Dallas is 2-2, but they’re a solid team; if they can fix that defense, they’d be a threat in the NFC. No. 11 — Las Vegas Raiders (3-1) | (14th) 📈 3 spots Sure, they lost, but Kirk Cousins has the Raiders playing well, and defensive coordinator Rob Leonard has done well all season. Patrick Mahomes only completed 15 passes, and the Raiders had one too many errors in the second half, but they played well. Klint Kubiak has this team sitting at 3-1. No. 12 — Cincinnati Bengals (2-2) | (10th) 📉 2 spots The Bengals lost to the Jaguars at home and also lost Ja’Marr Chase to a head injury. The Bengals still had a 437-yard offensive performance. Cincinnati just could not run the football; Chase Brown gained 10 yards on nine carries — abysmal! Tee Higgins caught 11 passes for 157 yards on 16 targets without Chase. The Bengals defense was solid again, but Zac Taylor’s squad didn’t do enough to secure the home win. No. 13 — Denver Broncos (2-2) | (10th) 📉 3 spots The Broncos’ offense looks inept for far too long in these games. Bo Nix’s team had three points until the fourth quarter, and San Francisco was able to put 21 fourth-quarter points on the Broncos. There’s no denying Denver’s talent level, but the Broncos disappear offensively too much. No. 14 — New England Patriots (2-2) | (27th) 📈 13 spots The Patriots are moving all over this board. New England looked terrible for three weeks, despite defeating the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 2, but they went into Buffalo and defeated the Bills 29-26. Drake Maye still made mistakes, but he found Romeo Doubs for two touchdowns, and Mike Vrabel’s defense did enough to stop the Josh Allen train. They host the Raiders next week. No. 15 — Carolina Panthers (2-2) | (22nd) 📈7 spots Am I being fooled by the prime-time victory — maybe! But the Panthers’ free-agent defensive additions are proving successful. They’re 2-2, and just beat the Lions 32-26, with Bryce Young throwing for 329 yards and two scores. Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards. The Panthers are looking solid early in 2026. No. 16 — Detroit Lions (2-2) | (12th) 📉 3 spots The Lions are 2-2 with losses against the Panthers and Bills. They won their two home games against the Jets and Saints. Kelvin Sheppard’s defense is an issue, but the offensive firepower is undeniable. Brighter days are ahead for Detroit, with the Packers, Cardinals, Dolphins, and Buccaneers on the schedule over the next six games. No. 17 — Atlanta Falcons (2-2) | (25th) 📈 8 spots The Falcons have won two in a row after a 0-2 start where Cooper Rush was their starting quarterback. Michael Penix Jr. didn’t do much against the Saints, but he provides the Falcons with a much-needed level of competency at quarterback. Atlanta has a strong defense and a solid offensive line, so they jumped up the rankings significantly after their Week 4 road victory against the Saints. No. 18 — Cleveland Browns (3-1) | (24th) 📈 6 spots The Browns are on a three-game winning streak, and Todd Monken has this team playing a physical style of football that suits the NFC North. Deshaun Watson is playing competent football, and the offensive line is doing a solid job up front. Defensively, the Browns forced two interceptions. The Browns defeated Pittsburgh, 27-24. I feel strange putting the Browns this high, but they defeated Carolina and Pittsburgh at home over the last two weeks. No. 19 — New York Giants (3-1) | SAME The Giants are a resilient team. They went down 14-3 and adjusted on defense to stop the Cardinals’ rushing attack. They also received the Jameis Winston Experience: a three-touchdown, two-interception affair full of inaccurate throws and incredible efforts that helped move the chains. Winston had above a 12% big-time throw rate in Week 4. My concerns, though, are the Giants’…

title: 6 storylines for NY Giants-Washington Commanders: Prepping for Jayden Daniels
summary: The NFC-East leading New York Giants (3-1) travel to Landover, Md. Sunday to face the 1-3 Washington Commanders. What are the storylines to watch this week, beyond the Giants trying to defend a solo grip on first place for the first time since November of 2015? Let’s take a look. Jayden Daniels: ‘Looks like we’re […]
full_text: Jayden Daniels | Getty Images The NFC-East leading New York Giants (3-1) travel to Landover, Md. Sunday to face the 1-3 Washington Commanders. What are the storylines to watch this week, beyond the Giants trying to defend a solo grip on first place for the first time since November of 2015? Let’s take a look. Jayden Daniels: ‘Looks like we’re going to get him’ Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels has not played since dislocating his left, non-throwing, elbow in Week 2 against the Philadelphia Eagles. That is the second time in two seasons Daniels has suffered that injury. Head coach John Harbaugh and the Giants are expecting to see Daniels behind center on Sunday. “We’re going to have to prepare for Jayden. I mean, that’s got to be, until they say he’s not playing, we’re assuming he’s playing and we’ll be preparing for all the things he does, as if he was 100 percent healthy,” Harbaugh said. “They’re not going to put him out there if he’s not ready to play. So, that’s the way we’ll approach it. The Commanders have used now-injured veteran Marcus Mariota and seventh-round pick Athan Kaliakmanis, formerly of Rutgers, at quarterback in Daniels’ absence. They surprisingly won a game against the Seattle Seahawks with Mariota at quarterback, but Daniels, the 2024 AP Offensive Rookie of the Year, is a difference-maker. “He’s different. He’s a premier quarterback who can operate just in all those modalities. Is that a good word? I mean, he can RPO. He’s quarterback driven. It’s drop back pass. It’s under center. It’s under center, play-action, downhill run game. He does it all. He’s a very accurate passer. Outside throwing lanes, especially accurate, which is tough. Nice touch underneath,” Harbaugh said. “I mean, he’s proven himself to be a very, very dangerous quarterback, obviously. So, yeah, premier guy and it looks like we’re going to get him, so we’re going to have to be at our best.” Who’s at center? Bryan Hudson made his first NFL start on Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals after John Michael Schmitz missed a couple of late-week practices due to the birth of a child. Hudson played well in what was his first meaningful NFL action. So, now the question is whether or not he played well enough to displace Schmitz, a decent player but one who has never lived up to his status as the 57th overall player taken in the 2023 NFL Draft. Harbaugh was non-committal on Monday. “We’ll see. We haven’t really talked about it yet today,” Harbaugh said. “So, we haven’t had that personnel meeting yet, but I’ll say Huddy (played really well, and we were excited about him going in. So, maybe create some options for us, but JMS was playing really well too. So, a very good problem to have.” How will the Giants solve it? I think Hudson starts against the Commanders. Why? I believe the Giants know that Schmitz, in the final year of his rookie contract, is not their answer at center beyond this season. Unless something changes drastically, I can’t see Schmitz getting a second contract from New York. They will almost certainly need a new center for 2027, and it would be a shame if they didn’t give Hudson an extended run to determine if they already have their answer in place. Harbaugh said something interesting on Monday that applies to the center position, even though he was responding to a question about potentially having to fill Braxton Berrios’s roster spot. “We’ll turn over every stone,” Harbaugh said. “But sometimes the best stones are right under your feet.” That, I think, is the best explanation for why Hudson needs an opportunity to play. Hitting the road The Giants are 3-0 at home, and establishing a home field advantage is an important step in becoming a truly good football team. You do, though, have to win some games on the road. The Giants have gone 3-14 on the road the past two season, including 1-8 in 2025. They got manhandled by the Los Angeles Rams on the road in their only loss so far this season. Showing the ability to win games that matter on the road would be another step in the evolution of a team still trying to transition from down-trodden loser to truly dangerous contender. Are the Giants ready to take that step? ‘Protect the football at all times’ The Giants have already fumbled the ball seven times this season, but have been fortunate enough to lose only two of those. Cam Skattebo has three of those fumbles in 76 touches. That kind of sloppiness with the ball will eventually cost the Giants games “Sometimes you try too hard. Sometimes you try too hard to get the extra couple yards, to break out of the pile, to get the run game going. And then the ball becomes a little bit vulnerable in there and I just think we just stick (to it),” Harbaugh said. “You watch what Skatt and Najee have been doing, too. But protect the ball at all costs. The yards are going to come. Make that the first priority. Don’t forget that. Play to play. Keep reminding each other of that.” Harbaugh said holding on to the ball is a priority for everyone. “We have these heavy balls now that we bring in, and they carry this. But it’s not really punishment. They do it all anyway. They carry them around. We punch them out. They’ve got to hold them behind the line. But that’s what all the guys do anyway,” Harbaugh said. “So even our managers have to not fumble the ball. They’ll punch it out if they’re holding it loose. So, it just kind of needs to be like an organizational priority. You protect the football at all times if it’s in your hands.” Something else Harbaugh said might be considered a warning shot for quarterback Jameis Winston , who has three touchdown passes and three interceptions since taking over for the injured Jaxson Dart . “It’s definitely a priority for us. The priority for us,” Harbaugh said. “Not turning the ball over, whether it be fumbles or interceptions. If we’re going to accomplish the things we want to accomplish, that has to get done. That is the number one priority offensively. Everybody knows it. We all know it. We have to know it and do it.” ‘3 yards and a cloud of dust’ That has, more or less, been the Giants’ rushing attack so far this season. Skattebo is averaging 3.5 yards per carry. On 68 rushing attempts, his longest gain is 13 yards. Over the last three games, he has gained just 154 yards on 50 carries, 3.08 yards per attempt. Najee Harris is averaging 4.0 yards per carry (22 rushes, 88 yards). His career average, though, is just 3.9 yards on more than 1,100 attempts. The Giants want to grind teams down with their running game, but overall they are 23rd in the league at 3.7 yards per rush. The Giants’ rushing Expected Points Added (EPA) is -15.6, 26th, per NextGenStats. Their 37.8% success rate is 22nd. The Giants are at -45 in rushing yards over expected, 26th in the league. Remember when the Giants were flirting with Super Bowl MVP running back Kenneth Walker in free agency, or considered a legitimate landing spot in the draft for Jeremiyah Love ? This is why. They don’t have a home run hitter in their backfield. The closest that they have is Tyrone Tracy , who has a career average of 4.3 yards per carry, but he has carried only four times for 16 yards this season. In an effort to create some chunk plays, the Giants might need to give the ball to Tracy more often. They might also have to turn to this: The J.J. McCarthy package The Giants manipulated their roster against the Arizona Cardinals is such a way that McCarthy was QB3, with Harbaugh saying it was “unrealistic” for J.J. McCarthy to be able to function in a full backup role. Harbaugh, though, admitted that there were “certain plays that we had prepared for” McCarthy. They ended up choosing not to use them. That could change this Sunday. Harbaugh said on Monday that McCarthy being the No. 2 quarterback behind Jameis Winston this week is “definitely on the table.” McCarthy is not the runner Jaxson Dart is. In 10 games, he has averaged 3.7 rushes per game for 4.9 yards per carry. Dart, an…

title: NY Giants news: Braxton Berrios to IR, Dominic Zvada on early success, more
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know as the Giants get set to hit the road to Washington this week. Season is over for Braxton Berrios Giants’ John Harbaugh forecasts QB move that could change course of season | NJ.com But he did say that J.J. McCarthy — […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know as the Giants get set to hit the road to Washington this week. Season is over for Braxton Berrios Braxton Berrios announced on Instagram that he needs surgery on his foot/ankle and is out for the season. pic.twitter.com/vYhObO1Ukk — Jordan Raanan (@JordanRaanan) October 6, 2026 Giants’ John Harbaugh forecasts QB move that could change course of season | NJ.com But he did say that J.J. McCarthy — an intriguing third-year quarterback just acquired via a trade — could be the backup for the game, rather than the third stringer. “I think that’s a possibility,” Harbaugh said. “We’ll see how it goes during the week, but that’s definitely on the table.” For all of McCarthy’s flaws — and he has plenty — his mobility would let the Giants run the offense they envisioned running with Dart. And perhaps coordinator Matt Nagy could turn McCarthy into more of a game manager — within a run-focused offense — than Winston can be. John Harbaugh during the final play of Sunday’s game "You want the pressure?" John Harbaugh was ready for somebody to make a play, and then Deonte Banks did just that. @insidetheNFL Week 4 Mic'd Up on X pic.twitter.com/9ygrscqeE2 — NFL (@NFL) October 6, 2026 John Harbaugh set a Giants standard everyone is already meeting | New York Post It is quite something that Deonte Banks made a game-sealing interception and en route to turning it into an emphatic pick-6, he reached a speed of 21.85 mph on his 98-yard return. No ball carrier in the NFL has run faster than that this season, according to NextGen Stats. John Harbaugh says New York Giants’ backs must clean up fumbling issues | USAToday.com Still, that’s too many times for Harbaugh’s liking. This past Sunday against Arizona, it was running back Najee Harris who coughed up the ball on the Cardinals’ 43 yard-line, killing a second-half drive. It amounted to nothing in the end, as Arizona ended up punting the ball back to the Giants, but it could have been a game-changer. “Najee’s never been a guy that fumbles too much,” Harbaugh explained to reporters on Monday. “And sometimes you try too hard. Sometimes you try too hard to get the extra couple yards, to break out of the pile, to get the run game going. And then the ball becomes a little bit vulnerable in there, and I just think we just stick (to it). You watch what Skatt and Najee have been doing, too. But protect the ball at all costs.” Early NFL All-Rookie Team: Which 2026 draft picks have excelled so far? | The Athletic First team: Arvell Reese, Giants (Round 1, No. 5); Jacob Rodriguez, Dolphins (Round 2, No. 43). This is a crowded position for rookies, but Reese’s dominant performance against the Cardinals on Sunday clinched his spot on the first team. The No. 1 prospect for me this past draft, Reese finished with nine tackles (all solo) and now leads the NFL (not just rookies) with 27 solo tackles. Reese also had a tackle for loss, three passes defended and his first career interception in Week 4. He is the NFL’s only non-defensive back with at least four passes defended and one interception this season. Arvell Reese nominated again for Pepsi NFL Rookie of the Week | Giants.com The linebacker was nominated for Pepsi NFL Rookie of the Week, the second time he has been up for the award in as many games, after he led the Giants with nine solo tackles, three passes defensed, one tackle for loss and his first career interception. Fans can vote for Reese on Instagram or X ( @NFL ) through Thursday at 11 a.m. ET to determine who will bring home the championship belt for Week 4. The winner will be announced later that day. After the regular season, four players will be nominated for Pepsi NFL Rookie of the Year honors. New York Giants (3-1). New York’s schedule isn’t daunting, but with a backup quarterback like Winston (or J.J. McCarthy), no game is guaranteed, which opens the doors for division rivals. Dallas is currently the betting favorite to win the division at +134 and does feel like the most complete team in the NFC East at the moment. The offense is tied for the second-highest scoring unit in the league, averaging 30.5 points per game. The Cowboys are also the fourth-best on third down (51.02%) and the third-best in the league in the red zone (81.25%) through the first month. Their defense is still a major question, but the addition of corner Joey Porter Jr. should help improve the secondary. Buyers or Sellers for the NFL’s Most Surprising Teams 1 Month From Trade Deadline | Bleacher Report New York Giants: Buyers. With quarterback Jaxson Dart on season-ending injured reserve, the New York Giants are going through the Jameis Winston experience and still winning games. Currently atop the NFC East, Big Blue should bring in a veteran quarterback in case Winston implodes with turnovers. Keep in mind that J.J. McCarthy struggled in his second season, which was his first year as a starter with the Minnesota Vikings. He may not be equipped to take over on short notice in New York. Because of Brian Burns’ season-ending knee injury, the Giants should also look to add an edge-rusher, which is ironic given all the trade buzz around Kayvon Thibodeaux this past offseason. summary: Normally, when we’re talking about mock drafts for the New York Jets in October, it’s for an obvious bad reason. Arch Manning is a talented quarterback prospect who could be available in the 2027 NFL Draft. With […]
full_text: Sep 26, 2026; Knoxville, Tennessee, USA; Texas quarterback Arch Manning (16) celebrates after a college football game between Tennessee and Texas at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn. on Sept. 26, 2026. Mandatory Credit: Brianna Paciorka-USA TODAY Network via Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Normally, when we’re talking about mock drafts for the New York Jets in October, it’s for an obvious bad reason. However, today’s discussion will destroy a stupid narrative that people have been peddling for months, if not years. Arch Manning is a talented quarterback prospect who could be available in the 2027 NFL Draft. With the Jets being recently terrible and having multiple first-round picks, there has been a chance for a while that these two could join forces. Whenever that conversation has been brought up, a swarm of people has been quick to say that would never happen because the Manning family wouldn’t allow it. Interesting. Well, when Uncle Eli Manning was asked where he’d prefer his nephew to play football at the NFL level, he brought up the green and white. “There’s two ways I look at this,” Manning said via Grace McCarron of the New York Post. “For purely selfish reasons, I wouldn’t mind if he went to the [New York] Jets, just because I live right there, I could go to games, I could have dinner with him during the week a little bit. I think it’d be great for him to have some family nearby, so I wouldn’t mind him going to the Jets, being up in New York…that’s just my selfish reasons, and I think he could help them.” Well, well, well, isn’t that a fun plot twist. So it sounds like if the Jets were in a position to select the young Manning, there wouldn’t be any roadblocks to making that a reality. I’m not sure how the LOL Jets crowd is going to take this one, but… Full stop. The New York Jets are one of, if not the best, landing spots for a young quarterback next year. Their roster is overflowing with offensive talent, talented pieces on the offensive line, pass catchers, running backs, and all the rest. If Manning or any other QB prospect lands with the green and white, they have a path to immediate success. We haven’t been able to say that for a long time. J-E-T-S! title: Scouting Jets linebacker Troy Reeder
summary: The Jets recently acquired former Rams linebacker Troy Reeder, who has already been active a few times due to injuries at linebacker. Today, we break Reeder down in detail. The 32-year old Reeder is listed at 6’3” and 245 pounds and was undrafted out of Delaware in 2019. He has started 38 games in his […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - SEPTEMBER 21: Los Angeles Rams linebacker Troy Reeder (51) looks on during the game between the Los Angeles Rams and the Philadelphia Eagles on September 21, 2025 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA.(Photo by Andy Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Jets recently acquired former Rams linebacker Troy Reeder, who has already been active a few times due to injuries at linebacker. Today, we break Reeder down in detail. The 32-year old Reeder is listed at 6’3” and 245 pounds and was undrafted out of Delaware in 2019. He has started 38 games in his NFL career, along with another five in postseason action. Background Reeder was a three-star high school recruit, and headed to Penn State in 2014 whereupon he redshirted his first season. In 2015, he started all 11 games and generated 67 tackles, 5.5 tackles for loss, and an interception. At the end of a pretty successful first season, it was perhaps surprising that he opted to transfer to Delaware but this was partly because he wanted to be closer to his family and his brother was also at Delaware. He was also expected to move into a backup role behind players such as Jason Cabinda if he stayed with the Nittany Lions. Reeder was immediately successful with the Fightin’ Blue Hens, as he had 63 tackles, two interceptions and two forced fumbles to earn second-team all-CAA recognition in 2016. In 2017, Reeder went a step further as he earned first team recognition by registering 89 tackles, 2.5 sacks and an interception. His final season saw him named as a second-team all-American and he was once again a first-team all-CAA selection. He set career marks in multiple categories with 127 tackles, 13.5 tackles for loss and 2.5 sacks. Despite this success, Reeder was unselected in the 2019 NFL draft, but he made the Rams’ roster as an undrafted rookie and ended up making eight starts as he recorded 58 tackles and two forced fumbles. In 2020, he once again played a significant role with seven starts, and was second on the team with 81 tackles, adding three sacks. 2021 was the best season of Reeder’s career, as he played a major role in the Rams’ Super Bowl success. He started 10 regular season games and had 91 tackles, six pass breakups, two sacks and two interceptions. Reeder moved on at the end of the 2021 season, to join the Chargers, but he ended up in a rotational role with them. He had 11 tackles, a forced fumble and a pass breakup, with zero starts. In 2023, he initially joined the Vikings, but failed to make their roster and ended up back with the Rams having signed to their practice squad after final cuts. He was added to the active roster before the season and ended up playing in every game with 23 tackles and six starts. Reeder began 2024 as a starter and was productive in the first five games only to then suffer a season-ending injury in the sixth. He ended up with 46 tackles, a tackle for loss and a pass breakup. Last season, he was back with the Rams but started just one game, although he played a major role on special teams. He ended up with 25 tackles and two pass breakups. This year, Reeder had been without a team until early on in training camp when he was picked up by the Lions. However, they released him at the end of preseason. The Jets acquired Reeder and signed him to their practice squad after final cuts and have since signed him to the active roster after Marcelino McCrary-Ball went onto injured reserve. Let’s move onto some more in-depth analysis of what Reeder brings to the table, based on in-depth research and film study. Measurables/Athleticism Reeder has good size in terms of his height and weight, but his arm length is below 30 inches. That’s incredibly rare for an NFL linebacker as only six players in combine history have had a measurement of under 30 inches and most of them didn’t have much of a pro career. This was probably the main reason he went undrafted. His other measurables are excellent though. He ran a 4.63 in the 40-yard dash at his pro days and managed 27 bench press reps with solid explosiveness and agility numbers. Usage Reeder has always been an off-ball linebacker, matching up in the slot or creeping up to the edge on rare occasions. He has played both as an outside linebacker and as a Mike. He also played running back in high school. Run defense Reeder is a productive run defender, whose performance grades on analytical sites such as Pro Football Focus have steadily improved over the course of his career from poor to about average. He is adept at plugging gaps between the tackles but can take over-aggressive angles in pursuit from time to time. Coverage skills Reeder has been exposed to a lot of coverage situations over the course of his career, which has inevitably led to him giving up some key plays at times. He has given up a catch on 80 percent of his targets during his career and, although that percentage has been lower in recent years, he’s given up more yards per catch. However, it says something about his coaches’ belief in him that he was trusted in these situations and he has shown some playmaking ability too. The only two interceptions of his career came in the Rams’ Super Bowl winning season, during which he also had a career-high six pass breakups. Tackling Reeder missed a ton of tackles during his first three seasons, with his tackle radius and range clearly being affected by his lack of arm length. However, he’s really improved his tackle efficiency in recent seasons and can close fast on the ball and stop a runner in their tracks. He only has one forced fumble at the NFL level but he had five in college. Blitzing Reeder hasn’t blitzed that much during his career, but did have one game in 2020 where he racked up three sacks. That was a bit of an anomaly, though, as he only had two other sacks in his other six NFL seasons combined, and five in his college career. His pressure rate was pretty good in college and early on in his NFL career, but it’s been low since 2021 and he’s rarely been used as a blitzer since then. Special teams Reeder brings a lot of special teams experience to the table and that has already made an impression with the Jets as he had four special teams tackles in his first two games with them. He has played on every unit apart from the placekicking unit and racked up 45 special teams tackles in his career, including 15 last year. He has had four special teams penalties, though. At Delaware, Reeder blocked a kick in each of his three seasons and he has contributed in the punt rush at the NFL level. He also had a big recovery of a muffed punt in a postseason game with the Rams. Physicality Reeder has good size and can make some impressive hits as a tackler and in coverage. He also shows a willingness to take on lead blockers and can be aggressive when setting up stunts. Reeder has only ever had one defensive penalty at the NFL level, although he had five in his final season at Delaware. The lone NFL penalty was for unnecessary roughness though. He was ejected from a preseason game for a late hit on a sliding quarterback though. Instincts/Intelligence Reeder has good smarts and football IQ, as evidenced by him having to take over the green dot for the Rams in the middle of their postseason run. Having done that successfully, Reeder would take on those responsibilities full-time in 2024 but the team started 1-4 and then went on an 8-3 run after he got hurt. He has shown that he can make good reads and communicate before the snap, as well as showing instincts in terms of avoiding blockers. However, he can make mistakes in terms of mis-reading play fakes and misdirection. He had plenty of academic honors in college, both while he was at Penn State and at Delaware. Attitude Reeder has been regarded as a good leader with coaches on the Rams’ coach at one stage referring to him as a “pseudo-coach”. He has also been a good mentor, taking young players under his wing on a…

summary: The Philadelphia Eagles issued their first official injury report of the week on Wednesday in advance of their Week 5 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. The Eagles listed seven players under DID NOT PARTICIPATE: Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith, Drew Kendall, Jonathan Greenard, Jihaad Campbell, Marcus Epps, and Hollywood Brown. Barkley suffered a hamstring […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 09: Saquon Barkley #26 of the Philadelphia Eagles talks with Devonta Smith #6 during the second quarter of the game against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium on October 09, 2025 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles issued their first official injury report of the week on Wednesday in advance of their Week 5 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. The Eagles listed seven players under DID NOT PARTICIPATE: Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith, Drew Kendall, Jonathan Greenard, Jihaad Campbell, Marcus Epps, and Hollywood Brown. Barkley suffered a hamstring injury during the Eagles’ Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. He’s reportedly “ week-to-week .” Barkley figures to be unavailable against the Jags but he’s not expected to be placed on injured reserve, meaning the Eagles are expecting to have him back before he has to miss four games. With Barkley likely out and Tank Bigsby going on injured reserve, the Eagles have two running backs on the roster: Will Shipley and Dameon Pierce, who was called up from the practice squad on Wednesday. They also still have Carson Steele and Jaydon Blue on the practice squad. Smith was seen stretching on the sideline as the rest of the team warmed up together. Seems like he’ll miss this game but maybe he has a chance to return in Week 6? We’ll see. Kendall’s knee injury is a new development. If he can’t play, the Eagles will have to go with their third different starting center through five games this season. Willie Lampkin could get the nod at the pivot with … Fred Johnson? Jake Majors? Micah Morris? … at left guard. Not exactly ideal. Greenard suffered an ankle injury in Week 4. He’s reportedly “ day-to-day ,” which is typically less serious than “week-to-week.” We’ll see if he’s able to practice at all on Thursday. If not, he’ll probably miss Sunday. But he might then be able to return in Week 6. Campbell is listed with a knee injury. If the second-year linebacker can’t suit up, look for Jeremiah Trotter Jr. to start in his place. There have been calls for the Eagles to bench Campbell in favor of Trot Jr. When asked about Trot Jr. earlier this week, Fangio said he “played very well.” Then asked if Trot Jr. warrants more playing time, Fangio said: “Possibly, yeah.” Epps could miss a second straight game. If that’s the case, look for Michael Carter II to play safety in the Eagles’ nickel packages next to Andrew Mukuba. Cooper DeJean is still starting at safety in Philly’s base defense. Kenny Moore II will provide depth on the back end as he gets more acclimated to playing a new position. Brown is on track to miss his third game in a row. If he’s not ready to play in Week 6, the Eagles will have wasted his roster spot when they could’ve just put him on IR to miss four games. If Brown and Smith both don’t play, the Eagles will roll with the following five receivers: Dontayvion Wicks, Darius Cooper, Makai Lemon, Britain Covey, and Elijah Moore. The Eagles listed four players under LIMITED PARTICIPATION: Quinyon Mitchell, Zack Baun, Dallas Goedert, and Fred Johnson. Mitchell suffered a knee injury in Week 4 that prevented him from returning to the game after he left. Seems like he might be able to suit up this week. Or next week at the latest. If not, it’ll be seasoned veteran Jonathan Jones starting in his place. Baun miss Week 4 while in the concussion protocol. That he’s progressed to the point where he can be limited in practice is a good sign for his chances of playing this weekend. It could be Baun and Trot Jr. starting at off-ball linebacker. Big boost for the Eagles’ defense to get Baun back. Goedert returned to practice for the first time suffering a knee injury in Week 2. He might be able to play against the Jags. If so, the Eagles could have four tight ends active for Sunday: Goedert, Johnny Mundt, Zach Ertz, and E.J. Jenkins. Will be interesting to see how that snap count plays out. Fred Johnson returned to practice after missing the Eagles’ last two games. With Markel Bell seemingly in line to start for the recently retired Lane Johnson, Fred Johnson could serve as the Eagles’ swing tackle behind Bell and Jordan Mailata. Or Fred Johnson could potentially start at guard if Kendall can’t play and they need him to fill in with Lampkin moving to center. title: Is the Nick Sirianni era already over?
summary: “How did you go bankrupt?”“Gradually, then suddenly.”  Ernest Hemingway’s iconic line can be applied to many lines of work. When you look at the final seasons of the head coaches under Jeffery Lurie, this feels like it could be it for Nick Sirianni. Andy Reid’s Dream Team went 7-1 over the final 4 games of […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Head Coach Nick Sirianni of the Philadelphia Eagles stands on the field prior to an NFL football game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images “How did you go bankrupt?” “Gradually, then suddenly.” Ernest Hemingway’s iconic line can be applied to many lines of work. When you look at the final seasons of the head coaches under Jeffery Lurie, this feels like it could be it for Nick Sirianni. Andy Reid’s Dream Team went 7-1 over the final 4 games of 2011 and first 4 of 2012. He then went 1-11. Chip Kelly was 19-9 entering December 2014, he went 7-12 and didn’t finish 2015. Doug Pederson needed a 4 game win streak at the end of 2019 to make the playoffs, in 2020 he won 4 games all season. Since starting last season 8-2, Sirianni is 5-7. When a head coach fails, there’s plenty of organizational blame to go around, it doesn’t happen in a vacuum. But the owner isn’t going anywhere, and the GM isn’t going anywhere either. The 2026 Eagles are looking like what the end of a coaching tenure looks like. Injuries have not saved an Eagles coach before In only four games the injuries have piled up on the Eagles. That’s out of the head coach’s control, but they have not been a get out of jail free card. Doug Pederson’s final season was a graveyard on offense: Miles Sanders, every OL but Jason Kelce, every WR but Greg Ward, and every tight end but Richard Rodgers missed at least four games. The defense was decimated too, with only 5 players starting 12+ games, and 8 starting 8+. Nor did injuries save Andy Reid in 2012, when LeSean McCoy, DeSean Jackson, and three OL starters missed at least 4 games. Michael Vick lost his starting job to a concussion, then gained it back for the season finale after Nick Foles broke his hand. Bad drafts have wiped out the cupboard From 2016 to 2018, the Eagles had some really good drafts: Carson Wentz, Isaac Seumalo, Hal Vaitai, Derek Barnett, Rasul Douglas, Mack Hollins, and then Dallas Goedert, Avonte Maddux, Josh Sweat, Matt Pryor, and Jordan Mailata in 2018. Then in 2019 the Eagles drafted Miles Sanders, in 2020 Jalen Hurts. Their other 13 picks over those two years were a waste, highlighted by Andre Dillard, JJ Arcega-Whiteside, Jalen Reagor, and Davion Taylor rounding out their first and second day selections those years. The back of the draft provided no gems. Quez Watkins, K’Von Wallace, and Jack Driscoll hung around for a few years. John Hightower, Shaun Bradley, Prince Tega Wanogo, Casey Toohill, and Shareef Miller gave the Eagles nothing. Clayton Thornton didn’t make the roster as a rookie, but the next QB drafted in 2019, just 11 picks later, was Gardner Minshew. The 2014 and 2015 drafts were pretty empty. Jordan Matthews was fine, while Jordan Hicks (3rd round) and Beau Allen (7th) were good value; Nelson Agholor had a great season in 2017. But the rest of those drafts left nothing behind: Eric Rowe was taken 47th overall in 2015 and a year later was traded for what would be the 131st pick. That’s still a better return than Marcus Smith, Josh Huff, Jaylen Watkins, Taylor Hart, Ed Reynolds, JaCorey Sheppard, Randall Evans, and Brian Mihalik. It’s a similar story in 2010 and 2011. Brandon Graham was a great pick in the 1st round in 2010, and Jason Kelce was a steal of steals in the 6th round in 2011, but the rest of those drafts were a wasteland. The third best player the Eagles drafted was Dion Lewis, who barely played for the Eagles, with Kurt Coleman, Nate Allen, and Riley Cooper the best of the rest. The Eagles had 24 total picks in that two year span, and landed just two of them. It is early, but after an incredible run from 2021 to 2024, the past two Eagles drafts are looking closer to the end of era hauls than they are depth providers. Makai Lemon hasn’t shown anything and the coaching staff doesn’t know what to do with him. Jihaad Campbell is still more theory than reality. Drew Kendall has done a nice job in a couple of games but already 4 of the 8 day three picks from 2025 are on other teams or out of the league. New play caller failure This has doomed Eagles coaches. A coach can’t really control injuries and bad draft picks, but coaching is coaching. In 1998 to replace Jon Gruden, who was hired as Raiders head coach, Ray Rhodes brought in Dana Bible. The Eagles offense was such a disaster that Bible was replaced after six games by Bill Musgrave, who had one year of experience as a coach and actually was in Colts training camp as a player earlier that season. The Eagles not only finished the season dead last in scoring with 161 points (10.1 per game), they were so bad that no team has scored fewer points or points per game in a season since. In a slight parallel to this season, the Eagles also replaced their excellent OL coach, as Gruden took Bill Callahan with him to Oakland. His replacement turned out alright over the long run: Juan Castillo. Castillo takes us to our next disastrous play caller hire. In 2011 Andy Reid made two horrible decisions: first, he wanted the wide nine defensive front that was in vogue to be the basis of his defense, so he hired his defensive line coach, Jim Washburn, to install it then hired his defensive coordinator, rather than the other way around. Then he made an even worse decision to make his offensive line coach, one Juan Castillo, his defensive coordinator. Nothing about this worked. The 2020 season also has some parallels. After promoting Super Bowl winning assistant Mike Groh in 2018, Doug Pederson had to fire him ahead of the 2020 season. Pederson, with more than a gentle nudge from the front office, then went with a college of coaches , bringing in former Kyle Shanahan assistant Rich Scangarello, former Dan Mullen assistant Andrew Breiner, and former Kevin Sumlin (who the Eagles had considered for their head coach opening in 2013) assistant Aaron Morehead. In the end though it was still Doug Pederson’s offense, just with too many lousy cooks in the kitchen. Bringing in accessory pieces from top (or supposed top) offensive minds didn’t get the job done. It was apparent early on that Brian Johnson wasn’t up to the job, it was apparent early on that Kevin Patullo wasn’t up to the job, and it sure looks like Sean Mannion isn’t either. The decision to move on from Jeff Stoutland has backfired. There’s only so many bad coaching hires one can make before their credit runs out. Jeffrey Lurie has a quick hook Maybe the Eagles circle the wagons and start to turn things around. The unintentional accelerated offensive line replacement might improve the situation as the season progresses. Maybe the leaders of the team, who have previously shown the ability to bounce back, find it again. This team is trending down, but they haven’t yet sunk. There is still time to bail enough water out. Or maybe they are headed to rock bottom. The Eagles offense has been built on the line, it has fallen apart. The defense is less than the sum of its parts. A depleted roster, one that wasn’t nearly as good as originally thought, a limping defense, and a broken offense. These are all key ingredients of the end of an era. This is the 32nd full season under Jeffrey Lurie. Only twice has a head coach survived a losing season that wasn’t his first: Ray Rhodes’ 6-9-1 in 1997, he would be fired the next year; and Andy Reid’s miserable 2005. That’s a very short leash by Lurie, but none of the firings were mistakes. Ray Rhodes (Packers) and Chip Kelly (49ers) were immediately hired as head coaches but were one and done. Doug Pederson was fired after three seasons in Jacksonville. The Eagles won a Super Bowl before Andy Reid did. Sirianni has never been beloved by his players. The heavier the hand he’s had in the coaching staff the worse the results, and not just on offense. His in-game coaching has been inconsistent at best. The Eagles started taking on water last season. If they…

title: Eagles-Rams Film Review: Good, not great defense
summary: I thought the Eagles’ defense was similar against the Rams as it was against the Bears. For a long time, this looked like a performance that should have been enough to win. Then the last two meaningful Rams possessions happened, and it all fell apart. That is where I am with this defense right now. […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 4: Cooper DeJean #33 of the Philadelphia Eagles breaks up a pass intended for Jordan Whittington #88 of the Los Angeles Rams during an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on October 4, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images I thought the Eagles’ defense was similar against the Rams as it was against the Bears. For a long time, this looked like a performance that should have been enough to win. Then the last two meaningful Rams possessions happened, and it all fell apart. That is where I am with this defense right now. Good, not great. There is enough talent to compete with a very good Rams offense, but this group cannot keep carrying an offense that went 0-for-12 on third down. I think fatigue mattered again. But that can’t excuse every clean pocket, missed tackle, or coverage mistake. The defense still had a chance to close this game out and failed. There was plenty of soft zone and a lot of completions that felt a little passive. There was a weird amount of Cover 2 in this game. I understand trying to make Matthew Stafford sustain drives rather than giving him easy explosives, and that approach worked for stretches. But if you are going to play that way, you need to tackle well and eventually make the quarterback uncomfortable. The Eagles did neither consistently enough. Let’s get into it. Defense We may as well start with an interception! We need some positivity in our lives. Last week, I wondered whether Vic Fangio might lean into a little more man coverage with this personnel, and this was an example of why I could see the appeal. The Eagles begin with a single-high safety and play man underneath. This is a different starting picture from the two-high structures we usually associate with Fangio. Jonathan Greenard does an excellent job creating pressure. Stafford overthrows the receiver, and Andrew Mukuba takes advantage by making a great play on the ball. That is a pretty good way to help an offense that cannot move the ball! Eagles' Defense All22 Thread vs. Rams. 1) We may as well start with the interception! I wondered last week if we might see a bit more man coverage, and we saw it here! This is not a very 'Fangio defense' rep, considering they start with a single-high safety, but I can see the… pic.twitter.com/ATmlvSqHEI — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 6, 2026 Jeremiah Trotter Jr. makes it difficult to watch these games without wondering whether he should be playing more. His awareness is excellent. He recognizes the receiving threat quickly, gets into position before the throw, and limits the opportunity for yards after the catch. There is very little hesitation. That is the difference between Trotter and Jihaad Campbell for me right now. Campbell has the athletic ability to cover in space, but Trotter is quicker to understand where he needs to be. I am not ready to scream that Campbell should be benched. He is a second-year, first-round linebacker, and there is a development question here as well as an immediate performance question. But Trotter has earned meaningful snaps. If the choice is this close, I would seriously consider rotating them within games rather than treating it as an all-or-nothing decision. You can keep developing Campbell while acknowledging that Trotter is playing good football. 2) I'm not going to scream that Jeremiah Trotter should start over Campbell yet (I'll get into it in the article), but it's hard not to be impressed by Trotter every time he plays. The difference is the awareness and instincts that Trotter shows. He's good at limiting YAC by… pic.twitter.com/EpDDVnyu6C — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 6, 2026 The Quinyon Mitchell vs. Davante Adams matchup was awesome. Adams wins this rep with a cheeky little push-off, but there is more to it than that. Watch the route. He sells the possibility of coming back, creates just enough hesitation, and then breaks back toward Stafford. Against a corner as good as Mitchell, that tiny pause matters. Adams is still a fantastic receiver, and these two gave as good as they got. The more frustrating part is the time Stafford has in the pocket. The Eagles send five rushers and still do not make Stafford uncomfortable. Jalyx Hunt is being used as a stand-up rusher here, which was one of several different things Fangio tried. I understand why he was searching for answers. The front simply is not winning enough on its own. There were a lot of stunts, but those take time to develop, and Stafford is very capable of finding an answer before the rush gets there. You cannot ask Mitchell to win every rep against Adams while the quarterback stands there comfortably. That’s a tough ask for any cornerback. 3) Man, I loved watching the Quinyon Mitchell vs. Davante Adams battle. It was a great contest. Adams wins this one with a cheeky little push-off, but his route is still so good. Watch how he pretends to come back before actually breaking it back to the QB, forcing Q to… pic.twitter.com/s3XlpuvAJG — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 6, 2026 Here is another changeup. The Eagles drop both edge defenders into coverage and bring both off-ball linebackers. We had not seen this from them this year, and I liked seeing Fangio try something different. Campbell takes on the running back and does a good job as a rusher. I think he is being held, too, although Stafford gets the ball out quickly enough to prevent the pressure from becoming decisive. Unfortunately, Tariq Woolen loses to Puka Nacua on the outside. Woolen was better than he was against the Bears, but he still wasn’t that good. Nacua won against him several times. 4) This is an interesting rep. Fangio definitely threw some unique looks at the Rams this week. The Eagles drop both edge defenders into coverage (which we haven't seen this year) and blitz both off-ball linebackers. Campbell takes on the back and does a great job (I think he's… pic.twitter.com/MgY5HhRJK9 — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 6, 2026 The run defense was a mixed bag, but I do not think it was the main reason the Eagles lost. The Rams finished with 106 yards on 25 carries, averaging 4.2 yards per attempt. I thought the linebackers and secondary were a little more patient coming downhill, which helped them avoid being pulled out of position by play action as often as they were against the Bears. Personally, I’m OK giving up 4.2 yards per rush if it means they don’t get killed by play action as they did against the Bears. Trotter deserves another mention here. He is so clever at avoiding the offensive linemen trying to climb up to him. He finds his way through without getting swallowed by a block, stays involved, and finishes the play. This is what I liked about him before the Eagles drafted him. He won’t always produce a spectacular athletic rep, but he knows how to get to the football. Sometimes the evaluation really is that simple. He is a good player. He always has, and I think he will be for a long time in this league. 5) The Eagles' run defense was a mixed bag (a bit like the Bears' game), but I don't think it was the reason they lost the game. I thought they were a bit more hesitant coming downhill, which helped against play action. I had to shout out Trotter because he's just so good at… pic.twitter.com/pelBMHhbb4 — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 6, 2026 Moro Ojomo makes a huge stop on 3rd-and-1 to force a punt. This is how you avoid a double team! Instead of sitting there and letting the blockers get their hands on him, he attacks across the front and gets into the play before they can establish control. I have complained about Fangio slanting his defensive linemen because of the boom-or-bust nature of it, especially when the movement can open a lane elsewhere. But 3rd-and-1 is exactly the kind of situation where I like taking that chance. You need immediate penetration, and Ojomo provides it. The call and the execution work together here. This defense…

title: Cam Jurgens trade: Eagles send center to Ravens for draft picks
summary: Well, here’s a massive Eagles offensive line development for the second day in a row: Philadelphia is trading Cam Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens in exchange for multiple draft picks. The full terms of the deal, as first reported by NFL insider Adam Schefter: EAGLES RECEIVE — 2027 fifth-round pick, 2028 second-round pick RAVENS RECEIVE […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - JANUARY 04: Philadelphia Eagles offensive lineman Cam Jurgens (51) warms up before the game between the Washington Commanders and Philadelphia Eagles on January 04, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Kyle Ross/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Well, here’s a massive Eagles offensive line development for the second day in a row: Philadelphia is trading Cam Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens in exchange for multiple draft picks. The full terms of the deal, as first reported by NFL insider Adam Schefter: EAGLES RECEIVE — 2027 fifth-round pick, 2028 second-round pick RAVENS RECEIVE — Cam Jurgens, 2027 seventh-round pick Wow. Safe to say no one saw this coming. Coming off a down season in 2025 where he inexplicably still made the Pro Bowl, the Eagles were hoping Jurgens would bounce back in 2026. Along with fellow starting offensive lineman Landon Dickerson, Jurgens made an offseason trip to Medellín, Colombia for stem cell therapy. After beginning the season at his normal center position, the Eagles decided to move Jurgens to left guard with Dickerson massively struggling and landing on injured reserve after Week 1. To no surprise, Jurgens massively struggled at a new position where he had no previous experience. There were calls for the Eagles to bench him in favor of Willie Lampkin. Jurgens was expected to miss Week 5 after self-reporting a concussion. But no one expected him to be off the Eagles’ roster entirely. Howie Roseman clearly saw an opportunity to get good draft pick compensation in return for a player with a questionable outlook moving forward. The Ravens were clearly desperate for center help after losing Tyler Linderbaum in free agency and seeing their next three replacement options get injured. Kudos to the Eagles’ general manager for taking advantage of this opportunity. It is a shame that Jurgens’ Eagles career came to such an abrupt end. He was drafted to be Jason Kelce’s successor and it once looked like he was going to have a long career in Philly. Jurgens should always be remembered fondly for toughing it out through a back injury in an NFC Championship Game win over the Washington Commanders and the team’s Super Bowl LIX victory during the 2024 season. With Jurgens gone and Lane Johnson retiring, the Eagles’ offensive line is clearly in flux . That’s not really ideal in the short-term. But Roseman’s trade signals that the team has a long-term focus in mind. While I don’t think the Eagles are ready to completely throw in the towel on the 2026 season, the Jurgens trade seems like an acknowledgement that 2026 might just be a down year for this franchise. The Eagles are now set to have four picks in the first two rounds of the 2028 NFL Draft: their own first-round pick, the New England Patriots’ first-round pick (via the A.J. Brown trade), their own second-round pick, and the Ravens’ second-round pick.

title: Eagles reportedly calling up Dameon Pierce to the roster
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are calling practice squad running back Dameon Pierce up to the active roster, according to a report from NFL insider Jeremy Fowler. The Eagles are currently short-handed in the backfield. Saquon Barkley is expected to miss at least one game, if not multiple, due to a hamstring injury. Tank Bigsby was placed […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JUNE 2: Dameon Pierce #39 of the Philadelphia Eagles runs with the ball during OTA offseason workouts at Jefferson Health Training Complex on June 2, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are calling practice squad running back Dameon Pierce up to the active roster, according to a report from NFL insider Jeremy Fowler . The Eagles are currently short-handed in the backfield. Saquon Barkley is expected to miss at least one game, if not multiple, due to a hamstring injury. Tank Bigsby was placed on injured reserve . Will Shipley was the only healthy running back on the roster … and he’s missed time in practice over the past few weeks due to a foot injury. Pierce was one of three Eagles running backs on the practice squad. The other two: preseason standout Carson Steele and former Dallas Cowboys draft pick Jaydon Blue. Why Pierce over Steele? Pierce is clearly the more accomplished player in terms of regular season production. He also looked good early in training camp before getting banged up. He flashed again upon returning from injury. As an added bonus, Pierce has experience returning kickoffs with a strong 32.8 career average. At this point in time, it looks like Shipley will start at running back for the Eagles in Week 5 with Pierce rotating in. We’ll see if the team rides with just two backs or if they end up adding another to the game day roster. The Eagles are expected to officially announce more roster moves within the next few days.

title: Eagles News: Reflecting on Lane Johnson’s legendary career
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Lane is a legend. While I do think he’s properly getting his flowers following his retirement announcement, I do wish the damper of “How do the Eagles replace him?” wasn’t also a necessary discussion right now. Wish he could’ve made the […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - FEBRUARY 09: Lane Johnson (65) of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrates with owner Jeffrey Lurie after Super Bowl LIX against the Kansas City Chiefs at Caesars Superdome on February 09, 2025, in New Orleans, Louisiana. The Eagles defeated the Chiefs 40-22. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Lane is a legend. While I do think he’s properly getting his flowers following his retirement announcement, I do wish the damper of “How do the Eagles replace him?” wasn’t also a necessary discussion right now. Wish he could’ve made the decision back in the offseason to allow more space for celebrating him without interruption. To be clear, this isn’t to criticize Lane. He clearly wasn’t ready to make the call back then. That’s understandable. Things change. You can’t always anticipate how you’re going to feel down the road. In any case, here’s to one of the greatest Eagles players we’ll ever see. Glad we all got to witness his excellent career and come to know him as a fellow human. I know offensive linemen aren’t the most popular jersey choices for fans but I do hope to see more No. 65s out in the wild. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Eagles legend Lane Johnson retires: Five thoughts on the announcement – PHLY Eagles 1) Lane Johnson is the best player I’ve covered in my eight years reporting on this team. He was the type of ruthlessly efficient offensive tackle that didn’t always grab your attention on a down-in, down-out fashion, but the consistency with which he singlehandedly erased even the league’s top edge rushers solidified his status as one of the best offensive linemen in modern NFL history. Johnson went whole seasons without allowing not only sacks, but pressures during his career. And he did so in a way the Eagles built an entire offensive philosophy around. They’d have two of the league’s best offensive tackles, and they’d leave them both isolated on islands in pass protection as a result. Perhaps that arrangement didn’t get the recognition it deserved throughout Johnson’s career; his five All-Pro honors somehow feel insufficient for the player he was and the impact he had on the game. So did his omission from the NFL’s Top 100 players going into this season (something that didn’t seem lost on him upon his return to training camp a few months ago). None of this should change what most in Philadelphia already know: Johnson was one of the best players of a generation and belongs in the Hall of Fame. Lane Johnson gave the Eagles greatness.
